signals.title: `cast_keep_nullable` fails to preserve nullability when target type is `LowCardinality` because `canBeInsideNullable` returns false for LC types
signals.text: _Found via ClickGap automated review. Please close or comment if this is incorrect or needs adjustment._ _Retrospective finding from a historical scan of [PR #95747](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747) (merged 2026-02-02). Confirmed on current codebase — close with a note if already fixed._ ### Describe what's wrong With `cast_keep_nullable = 1`, casting from any nullable source (both `Nullable(T)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`) to a `LowCardinality(U)` target throws `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` on NULL values instead of producing `LowCardinality(Nullable(U))` **Root cause:** CastOverloadResolver.cpp:176-177: `type->canBeInsideNullable()` returns false for `LowCardinality` types, preventing `makeNullable` from being called. Should use `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(type)` (DataTypeNullable.cpp:186) which handles LC targets by wrapping the inner dictionary type in Nullable. **Why we believe this is a bug:** CastOverloadResolver.cpp:174-177 → `getReturnTypeImpl` checks `type->canBeInsideNullable()` before calling `makeNullable(type)`. `DataTypeLowCardinality` inherits the default `canBeInsideNullable()` which returns false (IDataType.h:325). So the nullable wrapping is skipped for LC targets, and the return type stays `LowCardinality(U)` without nullability. **Affected locations:** - `src/Functions/CastOverloadResolver.cpp:176` — canBeInsideNullable guard blocks LC target nullability preservation - `src/Functions/CastOverloadResolver.cpp:177` — makeNullable cannot create LowCardinality(Nullable(T)) — only Nullable(LowCardinality(T)) which is invalid **Impact:** Any user with `cast_keep_nullable = 1` casting nullable data to a `LowCardinality` target type gets an exception. This is the same class of bug that PR #95747 intended to fix but only addressed for non-LC targets. ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `596eb6de5409`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test: cast_keep_nullable should preserve nullability when target type is LowCardinality -- Bug: makeNullable + canBeInsideNullable guard fails for LowCardinality targets -- because LowCardinality.canBeInsideNullable() returns false. Should use -- makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullable to get LowCardinality(Nullable(T)) instead. SET cast_keep_nullable = 1; -- Baseline: these work correctly (PR fix for non-LC targets) SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::String AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::String AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Bug: Nullable source to LowCardinality target throws instead of preserving nullability SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Bug: LowCardinality(Nullable) source to LowCardinality target also throws SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Non-null should work regardless SELECT 'hello'::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; ``` [Try it on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/0120ba7d-ce2f-4594-bfa7-9bb806259746) ### Expected behavior ``` \N Nullable(String) \N Nullable(String) \N LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) \N LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) hello LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` \N Nullable(String) \N Nullable(String) Code: 349. DB::Exception: Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type (CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN) ``` ### Additional context **Open risks:** - The `accurateCastOrNull` path (CastOverloadResolver.cpp:159-168) has a similar issue — it rejects LC targets entirely via validateNestedTypesForAccurateCastOrNull **Suggested fix:** Replace lines 174-177 with: `if (keep_nullable && (arguments.front().type->isNullable() || arguments.front().type->isLowCardinalityNullable() || isDynamic(*arguments.front().type))) return makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(type);` — this uses the existing `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe` (DataTypeNullable.cpp:186) which handles both regular types and LC types correctly. **Analysis details:** Confidence HIGH | Severity P1 | Testability: `STATELESS_SQL` Found during automated review of [PR #95747](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747). --- _ClickGapAI · Confidence: HIGH · Severity: P1 · Finding: `h_pr95747_001`_

signals.title: ARM performance regression: `string_similarity` query `0` is slower
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the situation ## Summary `string_similarity` query `0` regressed on ARM/aarch64 for `client_time`. - Controlled baseline → affected shift: **+12.66%** (0.047351s → 0.053347s, 20 / 20 runs). - Baseline → latest shift: **+12.80%**; latest still shows the slowdown. - Historical public signal: **+12.63%** in ClickHouse performance history. - Reproduction class: `reproduced`. - Public history: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/history/string_similarity/0?metric=client_time&arch=arm ## Builds and environment Measured on ARM/aarch64, Neoverse-V2 class CPU, 32 logical CPUs, about 123 GiB RAM. Hostname and private workspace paths are intentionally omitted. | Role | Revision | Public ARM binary | Note | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 3dadc439d799 | https://clickhouse-builds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/REFs/master/3dadc439d7993eb60da8c4cc0be97e2c3e8de871/build_arm_release/clickhouse | nearest available first-parent build was used | | affected | 2ab3ce2270a4 | https://clickhouse-builds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/REFs/master/2ab3ce2270a47f248d2c4f869eb05277546b6d72/build_arm_release/clickhouse | — | | latest | 4f8c03e43e3e | https://clickhouse-builds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/REFs/master/4f8c03e43e3ed34e6dd44a2a6d96ef11de46228e/build_arm_release/clickhouse | — | ## Reproduction Performance test: `string_similarity` Query index: `0` Metric: `client_time` SQL: ```sql SELECT avg(levenshteinDistance(randomString(300), randomString(300))) FROM numbers(10000) ``` Datasets / inputs: Not captured. This is intentionally independent of the private investigation workspace: 1. Use an idle ARM/aarch64 host with similar CPU class if possible; the measurements below were taken on Neoverse-V2. 2. Download the public ARM ClickHouse binaries listed in the build table for the baseline and affected revisions. 3. Load the datasets/fixtures listed below using the normal ClickHouse performance-test data setup. 4. Run the SQL below at least 21 times for each revision and compare median `client_time`. 5. A valid reproduction should show the affected revision slower by approximately the measured shift, while same-revision reruns stay near zero shift. A minimal manual loop, after starting each revision as a local server and loading data, is: ```bash for i in $(seq 1 9); do clickhouse-client --time --query "$QUERY" done ``` ## Measurements | Comparison | Builds | Runs | Left median | Right median | Shift | Left range | Right range | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before→after | baseline vs affected | 20 / 20 | 0.047351s | 0.053347s | +12.66% | 0.047154s–0.047576s | 0.053204s–0.053867s | | before→latest | baseline vs latest | 20 / 20 | 0.047401s | 0.053466s | +12.80% | 0.047241s–0.047619s | 0.053258s–0.053705s | | before→before | baseline vs baseline | 21 / 21 | 0.047304s | 0.047433s | +0.27% | 0.047174s–0.047617s | 0.047276s–0.063973s | | after→after | affected vs affected | 19 / 19 | 0.053417s | 0.053380s | -0.07% | 0.053227s–0.053772s | 0.053209s–0.053633s | | latest→latest | latest vs latest | 19 / 19 | 0.053445s | 0.053474s | +0.05% | 0.053283s–0.054145s | 0.053356s–0.053800s | Stability checks: before→before +0.27%, after→after -0.07%, latest→latest +0.05%. Same-build comparisons are included above so reviewers can distinguish a regression from benchmark noise. ## Approximate introduction window Controlled reproduction compares baseline revision `3dadc439d799` with affected revision `2ab3ce2270a4`. No narrower self-contained localization window was captured. ## Code areas and mechanism clues - Files changed in the bounded window: `ci/jobs/scripts/check_style/check_cpp.sh`, `src/Access/IAccessStorage.cpp`, `src/Access/IAccessStorage.h`, `src/Access/SettingsProfileElement.cpp`, `src/Access/SettingsProfileElement.h`, `src/Common/Dwarf.cpp`, `src/Common/Dwarf.h`, `src/Common/MapWithMemoryTracking.h`, `src/Common/SetWithMemoryTracking.h`, `src/Common/StackTrace.cpp`, `src/Common/Volnitsky.h`, `src/Common/examples/symbol_index.cpp`. - Shortstat for that window: 191 files changed, 856 insertions(+), 714 deletions(-). - Static code/query review: The query repeatedly calls levenshteinDistance; PR patches FunctionsStringDistance buffers from std::vector to VectorWithMemoryTracking. - Suspect area from static review: Levenshtein/string-distance hot buffers now use VectorWithMemoryTracking. These are investigation leads only; the issue should not assign blame to a change without a validating patch or rollback measurement. - Server query duration: baseline 49.0 ms → affected 55.0 ms (+12.24%). ## Fix or validation status A local benchmark-backed prototype validation improved the affected build. This is measured working evidence for a fix direction, not a reviewed upstream patch and not a final root-cause/blame claim. - Validation status: `POSITIVE_BUILD_VALIDATED` - Validated strategy: stack scratch for small ASCII blocked Myers edit distance - Report summary: positive: stack scratch avoids per-row heap churn for 300-byte ASCII strings (-20.0%) - Controlled regression context: before→after +12.663%; before→latest +12.796%. - Validation artifact: `data/runs/fix_validation_string_similarity_0_stack_scratch/controlled_repro_summary.json` - Source/prototype diff: `data/builds/patched_044a9bb55475_string_similarity_stack/source.diff` - Prototype touched production source: `src/Functions/FunctionsStringDistance.cpp`. - Report diff excerpt summary: +36 / -9 lines; key validation shift: before_after -20.02%. Validation shifts from the report: | Comparison / metric | Shift | | --- | --- | | `controlled_before_after` | +12.663% | | `controlled_before_latest` | +12.796% | | `after_after` | +0.109% | | `before_after` | -20.017% | | `before_before` | +0.023% | | `latest_latest` | -0.099% | How to recreate the idea for review: 1. Check out the affected revision from the build table. 2. Apply or reimplement the validated prototype/source diff from the report, starting with the touched production files listed above, then narrow it to the smallest semantic change that preserves the measured improvement. 3. Build ClickHouse for ARM release and rerun the benchmark above. Accept only if the affected-vs-patched comparison improves and same-build self checks stay near zero. <details><summary>Patch excerpt used for the local validation</summary> ```diff diff --git a/src/Functions/FunctionsStringDistance.cpp b/src/Functions/FunctionsStringDistance.cpp index 686237eb7b8..8bf9fea62a4 100644 --- a/src/Functions/FunctionsStringDistance.cpp +++ b/src/Functions/FunctionsStringDistance.cpp @@ -325,18 +325,30 @@ struct BlockMyersEditDistance struct PatternMasksASCII { static constexpr size_t W = sizeof(Word) * 8; + static constexpr size_t stack_blocks = 8; UInt32 num_blocks = 0; - VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> tbl; // flat: tbl[c * num_blocks + k] = bitmask of positions of char c in block k + Word stack_tbl[256 * stack_blocks]; + VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> heap_tbl; // flat: tbl[c * num_blocks + k] = bitmask of positions of char c in block k + Word * tbl = nullptr; void build(const UInt8 * needle, UInt32 m) { num_blocks = (m + W - 1) / W; - tbl.assign(256 * num_blocks, Word(0)); + if (num_blocks <= stack_blocks) + { + tbl = stack_tbl; + std::fill_n(tbl, 256 * num_blocks, Word(0)); + } + else + { + heap_tbl.assign(256 * num_blocks, Word(0)); + tbl = heap_tbl.data(); + } for (UInt32 i = 0; i < m; ++i) tbl[needle[i] * num_blocks + i / W] |= Word(1) << (i % W); } - const Word * operator[](UInt8 c) const { return tbl.data() + c * num_blocks; } + const Word * operator[](UInt8 c) const { return tbl + c * num_blocks; } }; struct PatternMasksUTF8 @@ -404,13 +416,28 @@ struct BlockMyersEditDistance // As in the non-blocked version, but this time per block: // VP all ones, VN all zeros encodes that the first column's edit distances equal the row index (0,1,2,...,m). - VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> VP(num_blocks, ~Word(0)); - VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> VN(num_blocks, Word(0)); - UInt32 score = needle_len; - - // 3 * 128 * sizeof(Word) bytes of stack (3 KB for Word=UInt64). - // Covers needles up to 128*64 = 8192 chars + // 5 * 128 * sizeof(Word) bytes of stack (5 KB for Word=UInt64): VP/VN plus HP/HN/D0. + // Covers needles up to 128*64 = 8192 chars and avoids per-row heap churn for common medium strings. constexpr size_t stack_limit = 128; + Word vp_scratch[stack_limit]; + Word vn_scratch[stack_limit]; + VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> vp_heap; + VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> vn_heap; + Word * VP = vp_scratch; + Word * VN = vn_scratch; + if (num_blocks > stack_limit) + { + vp_heap.assign(num_blocks, ~Word(0)); + vn_heap.assign(num_blocks, Word(0)); + VP = vp_heap.data(); + VN = vn_heap.data(); + } + else + { + std::fill_n(VP, num_blocks, ~Word(0)); + std::fill_n(VN, num_blocks, Word(0)); + } + UInt32 score = needle_len; VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> hp_heap; VectorWithMemoryTracking<Word> hn_heap; ``` </details> ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? latest ### How to reproduce ## Reproduction Performance test: `string_similarity` Query index: `0` Metric: `client_time` SQL: ```sql SELECT avg(levenshteinDistance(randomString(300), randomString(300))) FROM numbers(10000) ``` This is intentionally independent of the private investigation workspace: 1. Use an idle ARM/aarch64 host with similar CPU class if possible; the measurements below were taken on Neoverse-V2. 2. Download the public ARM ClickHouse binaries listed in the build table for the baseline and affected revisions. 3. Load the datasets/fixtures listed below using the normal ClickHouse performance-test data setup. 4. Run the SQL below at least 21 times for each revision and compare median `client_time`. 5. A valid reproduction should show the affected revision slower by approximately the measured shift, while same-revision reruns stay near zero shift. A minimal manual loop, after starting each revision as a local server and loading data, is: ```bash for i in $(seq 1 21); do clickhouse-client --time --query "$QUERY" done ``` ### Expected performance _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #108185 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1883` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Lazy materialization OOB: cols.size() mismatch (debug) + release vector<bool> out-of-bounds read with Map subscript + two text indexes
signals.text: # Lazy-materialization OOB — `cols.size()` mismatch and release `vector<bool>` out-of-bounds read with Map subscript + text indexes ## Summary A `MergeTree` `SELECT` with **two `text` skip indexes** on `mapValues(map)` and `mapKeys(map)`, plus `PREWHERE` and `WHERE` clauses each referencing a **different** Map subscript, plus `LIMIT` (which triggers the lazy-materialization pass), aborts on both build modes: - **Debug/sanitizer:** `Logical error: 'cols.size() == required_columns.size()'` at `src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeLazyMaterialization.cpp:544` (`optimizeLazyMaterialization2`). - **Release:** libc++ hardening detects `vector<bool>::operator[] index out of bounds` at `contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__vector/vector_bool.h:297` — a **genuine out-of-bounds read**, not masked. Both symptoms are the same underlying bookkeeping bug in the lazy-materialization pass: the optimizer's column-count arithmetic desynchronizes from the actual `required_columns` set when the plan mixes Map subscripts with text-index-covered predicates, then indexes a `vector<bool>` past its end. Found by the AST-fuzzer-oracle campaign (PR #99980), snapshot `runs/merged15/crashes/inst-02-20260720-200503` (old master, surfaced as `verbose_abort:62`); rechecked + reduced on current master **`4c1b7ef9edcd`** (2026-07-22). ## Reproduction — self-contained, verified on both debug and release ```sql CREATE TABLE tab ( id UInt32, map Map(String, String), INDEX idx_mv mapValues(map) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'array') GRANULARITY 100000000, INDEX idx_mk mapKeys(map) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'array') GRANULARITY 100000000 ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 1, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, {'127.0.0.1':'a', '::1':'b'}), (2, {'x':'y'}), (3, {'(':'z'}); SELECT id FROM tab PREWHERE '(' IN (map['127.0.0.1']) WHERE map['::1'] IN '(' ORDER BY ALL LIMIT 681; ``` Debug output: ``` Logical error: 'cols.size() == required_columns.size()' src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeLazyMaterialization.cpp:544 ``` Release output (with libc++ hardening enabled, as in the release fuzz build): ``` vector<bool>::operator[] index out of bounds contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__vector/vector_bool.h:297 ``` ## Path ``` InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer::buildQueryPipeline → QueryPlan::optimize → optimizeTreeSecondPass → optimizeLazyMaterialization2 (optimizeLazyMaterialization.cpp:544) ``` The optimizer's column-count bookkeeping desynchronizes: it computes a `required_columns` set of size N based on the pre-optimization plan (Map-subscript virtual columns + text-index synthetic columns), but produces a `cols` vector of size ≠ N when it walks the actual index-read plan. The subsequent `cols[i]` accesses index a `vector<bool>` past its end — caught by the assert on debug and by libc++ hardening on release. ## Minimization / load-bearing conditions - **BOTH text indexes are required.** With only `idx_mv` (mapValues) or only `idx_mk` (mapKeys) the query runs clean. - **PREWHERE and WHERE must reference DIFFERENT Map subscripts.** Dropping either the PREWHERE or the WHERE — or using the same subscript in both — makes it clean. - **`LIMIT` is required** (it's what triggers the lazy-materialization pass). Removing `LIMIT` is clean. - **The three-row dataset shown is sufficient** (a Map with 2 entries, one with 1 entry, one with the `'('` key). The `'('` value/key in row 3 is what the PREWHERE / WHERE constants match against. - `GLOBAL` is not needed (plain `IN` works). Any constant `SELECT` decoration is not needed either. - `index_granularity = 1` reproducibly triggers the mark bookkeeping; larger granularity may not. ## Environment - ClickHouse `26.7.1.1`, git hash `4c1b7ef9edcd` (master + 868 commits over the fuzz base), aarch64. - Reachable via ordinary user SQL — `text` skip index and `Map` are supported features, no experimental gate needed at the SQL level. ## Suggested fix direction `optimizeLazyMaterialization2` must reconcile its `required_columns` vs. `cols` arithmetic when the plan includes text-index-covered Map subscripts. Either (a) exclude text-index-covered virtual columns from the lazy-materialization eligibility, or (b) recompute the bit-vector size to match the post-optimization column layout. The release out-of-bounds read is only visible because our release build has libc++ hardening enabled. Downstream users on release builds without hardening would see silent undefined-behavior reads (potentially returning garbage rows), so a fix on release is more urgent than the debug assertion alone would suggest.

signals.title: JSON object traversal pays duplicate-key bookkeeping on every key of every object — a no-duplicate fast path removes it (json_type_parsing q3 +33%, 26.6 → 26.7, aarch64)
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the situation The JSON object-traversal loop in `src/Formats/JSONExtractTree.cpp` (`ObjectJSONNode::traverseAndInsert`) now spends a hash-map node, a nested `std::unordered_set` node and a duplicate `getJSONElementType()` call on **every key of every traversed object**, whether or not any key actually repeats. Duplicated keys inside one JSON object are rare, so for the common case this bookkeeping is provably dead work: a cheap single key-only probe per object ("does any key repeat at all?") makes the entire cost skippable with observably identical behaviour. A patch implementing that fast path is attached below; on the no-duplicate path it does strictly less work than both the current two-pass loop and the single-pass loop it replaced. The cost was found while investigating a CI dashboard step: `json_type_parsing` query 3 regressed by **+33.23%** (CI sweep step ratio **1.327**) between 26.6 and 26.7 on aarch64. Local confirmation on exact release binaries, paired interleaved A/B (client wall time), two independent sessions of 7 runs/side each: | Session | ratio (26.7 / 26.6) | bounds | median 26.6 | median 26.7 | randomization p | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | run-20260803-4cb7 | 1.2408151248527945 | [1.1495680928835508, 1.2580533451920255] | 0.53325925 s | 0.6623717499999999 s | 0.011655011655011656 | | run-20260803-34b6 | 1.2346288618234684 | [1.1209754845334359, 1.292740403757532] | 0.5427225 s | 0.67041575 s | 0.011655011655011656 | Combined significance across sessions p = 1.35e-03, direction stable. Server-side, the effect is pure CPU on the traversal path: - q3 `UserTimeMicroseconds`: 383649 → 509470 (**ratio 1.328**, delta 125821 µs); `query_duration_ms`: 390 → 516 (ratio 1.3231); client wall ratio 1.226. - Work counters are byte-identical between the binaries on q3: `SelectedRows` 100, `SelectedBytes` 24039500, `ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadBytes` 13044600, `IOBufferAllocBytes` 14093364, `FileOpen` 1, `ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorRead` 15, peak memory 28620878. Same work, more CPU. - q1 (same test, many-key file, dynamic paths disabled) `UserTimeMicroseconds`: 4369465 → 5976239 (ratio 1.3677). Mechanism localisation — the cost scales with the number of traversed object keys, not with input bytes: - Equal-byte-volume discriminator (~28 MB on both sides): 1000 keys per object → ratio **1.3514** [1.2685, 1.4378] (regression); 10 keys per object → ratio **0.968** [0.8434, 1.132] (no regression). A global binary slowdown cannot move two equal-byte workloads in opposite directions. - Certified controls (15 runs/side, equivalent within the ±0.05 practical band): pure-CPU long workload ratio 0.9959438444128179 [0.9828378461874818, 1.003067097796909]; reading the very same bytes as q3 but as `JSONAsString` (no object traversal) ratio 1.0102915052855355 [0.9809724047306175, 1.0428511875123037]. Stage-isolating probes: `LineAsString` 1.0248, `JSONAsString` 1.0065, pure CPU 0.9996. The culprit change rewrote the traversal into two passes: a new first pass building `key_element_types` (v26.7.1.1315-stable `src/Formats/JSONExtractTree.cpp:1952-2005`, declaration at `:1957`), plus the retained second pass with `visited_keys` at `:2010`, a duplicate `getJSONElementType` at `:2014`, and `key_element_types` lookups at `:2024` and `:2039`. All cited lines were independently re-verified at tag v26.7.1.1315-stable; the pre-PR parent had one loop with one `getJSONElementType` per key. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? - Measured: **v26.7.1.1315** regressed vs **v26.6.1.1193** (aarch64, official release binaries; binary sha256 attested in the investigation ledger). - The culprit PR was merged 2026-07-09 (merge commit `797a5a9e447305dd4d54f23f545a2d9c8266776b`); the CI series change point is 2026-07-09T22:54:43Z, so 26.7 and later. - Backport exposure: the PR carries `pr-must-backport` and `v26.2-must-backport`, and a bot comment confirms the fixed bug reproduces on 26.3/26.4/26.5/26.6 — so the fix, and this cost, are destined for those branches too. - x86_64 was not measured in this investigation; the mechanism (per-key hashing work) is not architecture-specific. ### How to reproduce Perf test `json_type_parsing`, query index 3. Setup (generates its own input under `user_files`; no CI dataset needed): ```sql INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(test_json_parsing_1.txt, Raw) SELECT toJSONString(arrayMap(x -> tuple('a' || x, multiIf(x % 6 == 0, x::UInt32, x % 6 == 1, x / 3.333333, x % 6 == 2, randomStringUTF8(16), x % 6 == 3, '2020-01-01', x % 6 == 4, '2020-01-01 10:00:00', '2020-01-01 10:00:00.000')), range(1000))::Map(String, Dynamic)) FROM numbers(10000) SETTINGS use_variant_as_common_type = 1, engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(test_json_parsing_2.txt, Raw) SELECT toJSONString(arrayMap(x -> tuple('a' || x, [arrayMap(y -> tuple('b' || y, 'Data'), range(20))::Map(String, String)]), range(1000))::Map(String, Dynamic)) FROM numbers(50) SETTINGS use_variant_as_common_type = 1, engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; ``` Target query (q3): ```sql SELECT * FROM file(test_json_parsing_2.txt, JSONAsObject, 'json JSON(max_dynamic_paths=0)') FORMAT Null; ``` Compare 26.6.1.1193 vs 26.7.1.1315 with paired, strictly interleaved ABAB runs (we used 7 runs/side per session, two independent sessions with fresh server pairs and freshly generated input). The key-count discriminator, if you want the mechanism signature (equal bytes, opposite verdicts): ```sql -- many keys per object (regresses, ratio 1.3514) INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(disc_many.txt, Raw) SELECT toJSONString(arrayMap(x -> tuple('k' || x, 'abcd'), range(1000))::Map(String, String)) FROM numbers(2000) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; -- few keys per object, same byte volume (does not regress, ratio 0.968) INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(disc_few.txt, Raw) SELECT toJSONString(arrayMap(x -> tuple('k' || x, repeat('a', 1400)), range(10))::Map(String, String)) FROM numbers(2000) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; SELECT * FROM file(disc_many.txt, JSONAsObject, 'json JSON(max_dynamic_paths=0)') FORMAT Null; SELECT * FROM file(disc_few.txt, JSONAsObject, 'json JSON(max_dynamic_paths=0)') FORMAT Null; ``` ### Expected performance Parsing JSON objects that contain no duplicated keys — the overwhelmingly common case — should cost what it did in 26.6: on this workload, q3 at ~0.533 s client wall / 383649 µs user time rather than ~0.662 s / 509470 µs. When no key repeats, the duplicate-key bookkeeping cannot change the outcome (`visited_keys` can never report a repeat, `key_element_types[key].size() > 1` requires a repeated key, and every duplicate error/skip branch is unreachable), so it should not be paid. ### Related issues and pull requests - Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108218 ("Fix `type_json_allow_duplicated_key_with_literal_and_nested_object` not working with typed paths in JSON") - Related: query 0 of the same test (`test_json_parsing_1.txt` as plain `JSON`) also regressed in both local sessions (ratios 1.1598344332180672 and 1.157688931229005) although the CI sweep never flagged it; it is tracked as its own follow-up and not claimed here. ### Additional context **Culprit-PR intent.** PR #108218 is labelled `pr-bugfix`; its body and review discussion contain no performance statements, and its CI Performance Comparison summary was green. The measured cost is therefore undisclosed, not an intended trade-off — this issue asks to keep the bug fix and drop the constant overhead, not to revert the fix. **Proposed fix.** Probe each object once, keys only; take a fast path with zero duplicate bookkeeping when no key repeats, fall through to the current two-pass logic otherwise. The candidate improvement was measured only on two locally built binaries, so it is deliberately **not** established by this investigation (blocked at the exact-provenance gate until repeated on official builds); it is carried on a linked candidate-fix work item with its full validation bundle. The adversarial audit of the investigation confirmed the patch is one file, one hunk, purely additive (+41/−0), contains no numeric or string literals, nothing benchmark-shaped (its sole conditional keys on `!has_duplicated_key`, a universal JSON property), touches no tests or CI files, and that the culprit PR's own regression suite (`04331_*`) routes entirely through the untouched general path. Smoke on the patched build: 17/17 result-hash equality including five positive duplicate-key cases, plus 5/5 error parity on `INCORRECT_DATA`. <details> <summary>Proposed patch: skip per-key duplicate-key bookkeeping for objects with no repeated key (validated: improvement measured on locally built binaries only — G2-blocked pending official builds, not established by this report; smoke 17/17 result-hash equality + 5/5 error parity)</summary> ```diff --- a/src/Formats/JSONExtractTree.cpp +++ b/src/Formats/JSONExtractTree.cpp @@ -1949,6 +1949,47 @@ if (element.isObject() && (skip_typed_path_check || !typed_path_nodes.contains(current_path) || (format_settings.json.type_json_allow_duplicated_key_with_literal_and_nested_object && hasTypedPathWithPrefix(current_path + ".")))) { + /// Duplicated keys inside one JSON object are rare, but the bookkeeping required to + /// handle them is not free: the passes below spend a hash-map node, a nested + /// std::unordered_set node and a getJSONElementType() call on EVERY key of EVERY + /// object, whether or not any key repeats. That cost is paid per traversed key, so it + /// scales with the key count of the document and hurts wide/deeply nested JSON most. + /// + /// So first answer the much cheaper question "does this object have a duplicated key + /// at all?" with a single key-only probe (no element types, no per-key nested set). + /// When the answer is no, none of that bookkeeping can change the outcome: + /// - visited_keys can never report a repeat, so its inserts and lookups are dead; + /// - key_element_types[key].size() > 1 requires a repeated key, so skip_typed is + /// always false; + /// - every duplicate error/skip branch is unreachable. + /// The fast path below is therefore observably identical to the general path, and does + /// strictly less work than it (and than the single-pass version this replaced). + bool has_duplicated_key = false; + { + std::unordered_set<std::string_view> probed_keys; + for (auto [key, value] : element.getObject()) + { + (void)value; + if (!probed_keys.insert(key).second) + { + has_duplicated_key = true; + break; + } + } + } + + if (!has_duplicated_key) + { + for (auto [key, value] : element.getObject()) + { + String path = buildChildPath(current_path, key, insert_settings, is_root); + if (!traverseAndInsert(column_object, value, path, insert_settings, format_settings, paths_and_values_for_shared_data, current_size, error, false)) + return false; + } + + return true; + } + /// First pass: collect the set of distinct element types (LITERAL/OBJECT) per key. /// This lets us detect all duplicates upfront so we can: /// - throw errors immediately for invalid duplicates (before any data is inserted), ``` </details> **Caveats and disclosed limitations.** - All measurements are from a single dedicated aarch64 host (Linux VM); x86_64 is unmeasured. - Regression and mechanism numbers are from official release binaries (exact-release provenance, sha256-attested: 26.6.1.1193 `962fd0cc…`, 26.7.1.1315 `3057f9ff…`). Only the candidate-fix improvement involves locally built binaries, and it is explicitly not claimed here. - Unexplained observation, recorded but not claimed: `MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheckBytes` on q3 moved 183472 → 33738480 while the allocation count moved only 20 → 28; on the patched build both return to their 26.6-like values (183664 / 20). Eight extra large allocations cannot be one hash node per traversed key, so no per-key-allocation arithmetic is claimed from this counter.
signals.author: egor-click

signals.title: Keyed aggregations over huge constant-folded literals still pay a per-execution O(N) content-hash in the hash-table-stats cache key (bounded residual of #107643; ~9ms per execution for a 5M-element literal)
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the situation There is a small, result-preserving win available here: bounding how many bytes of a constant may be hashed into the cache-key fingerprint (a ~30-line patch, below) removes the last per-execution cost that grows with a constant-folded literal's size from the aggregation hash-table-stats cache key. On the fixed build the key costs 89–93us regardless of literal size (vs 8.8ms at 5M elements / 35.3ms at 20M elements before), a plan with many keyed aggregations over large folded constants runs about 2x faster end to end, every smoke query returns byte-identical results (including a deliberately constructed collision pair), and peak memory is byte-identical. **Background — the parent finding.** The aggregation hash-table-statistics cache key introduced by merge `49dc83c610c4fb82ee468e61b7f82a1968123027` (PR #107643) serializes the aggregation's input plan subtree — including full constant column data — during query plan optimization, on every execution. That caused the `quantile_merge` +78.5% CI regression documented in the parent finding — filed as https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113037 — whose proposed patch has two parts: (1) skip the key entirely for keyless aggregations (the key is never consumable there), and (2) represent constants larger than 64 KiB in the hash-input-only stream by an identity fingerprint — marker + row count + **whole-column SipHash** — instead of their full binary data. **The residual (keyed case).** For *keyed* aggregations the key is still computed, and part (2)'s fingerprint calls `data.updateHashFast(column_hash)`, which for an array constant recurses into offsets and data and ends in a single hash update over the entire element buffer — every byte of the literal, per execution. The parent fix reduced the constant factor (full binary serialization → one hash pass) without removing the linear term. Per the investigation objective: the measured residual is ~9ms plan-optimize per execution for a 5M-element folded literal on the parent-fixed build, vs ~44ms unpatched and ~0.07ms on 26.6. The serialized stream exists only as SipHash input inside `calculateHashFromStep(const ITransformingStep &)` (`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp`), which is why the cost appears only on plan steps that do not preserve row count[^rowcount], and vanishes entirely when `collect_hash_table_stats_during_aggregation = 0` short-circuits `setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys`. Hash path: `serializeConstant` in `src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp` (the `updateHashFast` call sits at line 4165 at our base ref; the originally cited :4148 was the diff hunk header) → `ColumnArray::updateHashFast` (`src/Columns/ColumnArray.cpp:360-363`) → `ColumnVector::updateHashFast` (`src/Columns/ColumnVector.cpp:108-111`, one `hash.update(data.data(), size()*sizeof(T))`). **Linearity, measured** (parent-fixed local build at the `v26.7.1.1315-stable`-era base ref, arm64, `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` per execution): | Folded literal | Counter per execution (us, raw series) | Verified median (us) | | --- | --- | --- | | `range(1000000)` | 1792, 1853, 1840, 1830 | 1840 | | `range(5000000)` | 8797, 8835, 8746, 8792, 8794 | 8794 | | `range(20000000)` | 35625, 35277, 35171, 35256 | 35277 | Floor-subtracted cost is 1742.0 / 1743.1 / 1762.8 us per million elements at 1M/5M/20M (max deviation 0.77%), while the setting-off floor stays size-invariant ([79, 76, 74, 79, 79] us at 5M). An integer literal is narrowed by `FieldToDataType`, so `range(N)` folds to `Array(UInt32)` at 4 bytes/element: hashed content is 4/20/80 MB and implied throughput is 2.27–2.30 GB/s — consistent with a single-pass SipHash, i.e. the residual is linear in literal bytes at hash throughput, not a fixed overhead. **The fix.** A new registry cap, `max_constant_bytes_to_hash` (set to 1 MiB where the cache key is computed), makes `serializeConstant` write only the constant's *shape* once the constant exceeds the cap — marker, row count, data byte size, and a flag recording whether content was hashed — so the cost stops growing with the literal. Validation (parent-fixed baseline vs cap-fixed candidate, sole A→B code delta is the cap — verified by patch diffing): - Objective query (single keyed aggregation, 5M-element folded constant): plan-optimize counter [8912, 8745, 8874, 8935, 8934] → [93, 89, 92, 92, 91] us — 8.9ms → 0.09ms, two orders of magnitude. - Post-fix cost is size-invariant: 91.4us at 5M vs 91.8us at 20M elements — slope 0.027us per million elements against a pre-fix 1743us per million; exactly the linear term is removed and nothing more. - Amplifier `q_union16_20m` (sixteen keyed aggregations, each over its own distinct large folded array constant, each producing one row): wall verdict **improvement** in two interleaved sessions — ratio 0.4909, bounds [0.4476, 0.6457], and ratio 0.4913, bounds [0.4313, 0.566] (n=9/side each); causal counter [141750, 141497, 141676, 140992, 140930] → [1344, 1339, 1363, 1324, 1387] us. A 32-aggregation variant also roughly halves (ratios 0.5485 / 0.5288) but its verdicts are labelled unstable at this rig's variance. - Smoke: 14 queries, 100% result-hash equality — including a deliberately colliding pair, `range(2000000)` vs `arrayMap(y -> y + 1, range(2000000))`: same type, same element count, same byte size, different content, therefore sharing a shape-only key. Peak memory byte-identical on all three probe workloads. **Positioning against the culprit PR's intent.** PR #107643's own stated goal was to remove per-query overhead (the eager query-tree-to-AST conversion was "a noticeable cost during query analysis even though that AST is otherwise unused on the common `SELECT ... FROM <MergeTree>` path"). The one performance tradeoff its cloud benchmark report declared is unrelated to this mechanism: clickbench Q31 +11.9%, described there as "the expected flip side: preallocation can overshoot and cost cache locality when the estimate is off." Nothing in the PR discussion declares or prices a plan-optimization cost proportional to the size of a constant-folded literal. This residual therefore cuts *against* the PR's stated intent, and removing it is aligned with that intent — not a reversal of a deliberate tradeoff. **Disclosed costs of the fix:** - Above the cap, the cache key no longer distinguishes two constants that share type, element count and byte size; such plans share one hash-table-statistics entry. That entry supplies a preallocation size hint to the aggregator (`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:117-121`) — and, via `initDataVariantsWithSizeHint`, feeds the single-level→two-level pre-conversion decision — so a collision can mis-size a preallocation or flip that pre-conversion, but cannot change a query result. The colliding-pair smoke verifies this. - Bounded, not eliminated: the post-fix residual is 92us [89, 93] against a setting-off floor of 79us [74, 79] — non-overlapping, +16% (the key path still runs; the mechanism predicts exactly this). - Binary size +128 bytes (947296264 → 947296392). - On a sub-threshold plan whose code path is unchanged (eight keyed aggregations over ~8KB folded constants, below the 64KB fingerprint threshold), plan-optimize time was consistently a few tens of microseconds higher on the candidate — [828, 782, 788, 780] vs [857, 841, 830, 873] us, about +7 percent of a sub-millisecond time — most likely code layout in the recompiled translation units; far below wall-clock resolution. - No-effect controls clean: a keyed aggregation over a `numbers` source with no folded constant is inside-band in both sessions (ratios 1.0104 [0.9861, 1.0277] and 1.011 [0.9962, 1.0374]); a below-threshold constant is counter-indistinguishable ([132, 130, 134, 133] vs [130, 145, 130, 137] us); the `hash_table_sizes_stats` perf-test sweep shows ratios 0.9064–1.0429 with no query beyond run-to-run noise (4 of its queries need the external `hits_100m_single` dataset and were skipped, disclosed). ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? The linear per-execution term exists wherever the #107643 cache-key path serializes or hashes constant data for keyed aggregations: - Stock `v26.7.1.1315-stable` pays it as full constant serialization (~44ms per execution at 5M elements — the parent issue's keyed case). - A build carrying the parent fingerprint fix pays it as a whole-column hash (~9ms per execution at 5M elements — this issue). - `v26.6.1.1193-stable` is unaffected (~0.07ms). Measured builds: base ref `a6156303df65c307bdb8b66e9e9cc5637346a6b8` plus the parent patch (baseline, binary sha256 `e70346392b04328a18a1ace47e625f905b2191287f7967cd3b9e392eeeb1f0a4`) vs plus this patch (candidate, `ff69830ad339970a50b950caf11a2381845c669cce4c559038a3b54b4bc678e0`), both locally built, attested as 26.7.1.1. Current master was not measured. ### How to reproduce On any affected build, take a keyed (`GROUP BY`) aggregation whose plan contains a constant-folded array literal well above the 64 KiB fingerprint threshold (e.g. a folded `range(5000000)` — the parent issue's `quantile_merge` query with a grouping key is the original shape) and watch `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` per execution. 1. On the parent-fixed build the counter medians are 1840 / 8794 / 35277 us for 1M / 5M / 20M-element literals — linear in the literal. 2. Discriminator — `SET collect_hash_table_stats_during_aggregation = 0`: the counter drops to the 74–79us floor and becomes size-invariant, because `setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys` is short-circuited. 3. Discriminator — scale the literal: cost per million elements is flat (1742.0–1762.8 us floor-subtracted), i.e. a linear term, not fixed overhead. 4. On stock 26.7 (no parent fix) the same query shape pays the ~5x larger full-serialization cost (~44ms at 5M elements) through the same code path. Note: the single-aggregation objective query's wall-clock gain is **not** resolvable on our rig (ratios ~0.96, labelled unstable in both attempts) — its ~9ms gain is counter-level only. The wall-clock improvement was demonstrated on a synthetic amplifier (16 keyed aggregations over distinct large folded constants in one plan, `UNION`-combined) built to expose the same mechanism above wall-clock noise. ### Expected performance The cache-key cost for a keyed aggregation should be O(1) in the size of any folded literal in its subtree: with the cap, 89–93us at 5M elements and size-invariant to 20M (slope 0.027us per million elements vs 1743us per million without), against a 74–79us floor with the stats path disabled entirely. End to end, a many-aggregation plan over large folded constants runs ~2x faster (ratios 0.4909 / 0.4913 in two sessions); a single-aggregation query recovers ~9ms → ~0.09ms of plan-optimize time per execution, below wall-clock resolution for the query we measured. ### Related issues and pull requests - Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107643 — the residual persists (in reduced form) even with our parent-finding patch applied. - Parent finding: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113037 — aggregation hash-table-stats cache key serializes large constant-folded literals on every execution (`quantile_merge` +78.5%). Its patch covered the keyless-aggregation skip and constant fingerprinting; this issue is the remaining keyed case that patch left bounded but linear. - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113333 (open, groeneai) — implements the keyless-skip fix and closes #113037. Its description explicitly reserves this issue's topic: "Constant serialization is still costly for keyed aggregations, about 62 ms here, and is left to a separate fix." This issue is the problem statement for that separate fix. - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106137 — the plan-node hashing infrastructure that #107643 reuses (per the PR description). ### Additional context groeneai raised four objections on the #113037 thread that bear on this proposal; each is addressed with what we measured: 1. *"SerializedSetsRegistry ... not a serialization-policy holder, threshold would sit in the wrong layer."* — Since PR #106073 merged (2026-08-05), the registry does carry a cache-key serialization-policy flag: `bool for_cache_key` in `src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h`. On master this layer already holds exactly this kind of policy; the proposed cap fields would sit next to an existing one. 2. *"64 KiB is an unmotivated constant ... thresholds become settings unless justified."* — Conceded. We propose the threshold as a setting rather than a hard-coded constant. 3. *"updateHashFast is not universally implemented: ColumnBLOB, ColumnCompressed, ColumnLazy all throw ... would LOSE preallocation for plans that serialize fine today."* — Conceded for the 64 KiB–1 MiB band, where the fingerprint hashes content via `updateHashFast` while full serialization would have succeeded; that band is exactly the already-disclosed smoke coverage gap (see the validation caveats below). Above the 1 MiB cap the shape-only branch does not call `updateHashFast` at all. 4. *"Streaming it through a hashing write buffer removes the allocation with no cache-key identity change."* — Agreed on the allocation: streaming removes the 379MB allocation. It does not remove the O(N) serialize+hash term, which our gated numbers put at ~1.74ms per million elements (floor-subtracted 1742.0 / 1743.1 / 1762.8 us per million at 1M/5M/20M). The cap/fingerprint targets that linear term itself, which streaming cannot touch. The patch adds one field to `SerializedSetsRegistry` (`max_constant_bytes_to_hash`, default 0 = "always hash the whole content", so plan-shipping serialization is untouched) and sets it to 1 MiB at the single hash-input-only call site. Above the cap the fingerprint keeps the constant's shape only — marker, row count, data byte size, hashed-content flag. The touched code is the generic hash-input-only serialization stream, so every large constant in any such stream benefits, not only the triggering query's shape. 1 MiB of content hashing is ~0.2ms; the cap sits 8x–160x below every constant measured in this investigation, so it is not tuned to the benchmark. <details> <summary>Proposed patch (cumulative over the parent-finding patch): bound fingerprint content-hashing at 1 MiB — above the cap the cache key records only the constant's shape (validated: objective-query plan-opt 8.9ms → 0.09ms and size-invariant to 20M elements; amplifier wall ~2x, ratios 0.4909/0.4913; smoke incl. deliberate shape-collision pair 100% result equality; peak memory byte-identical)</summary> ```diff diff --git a/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp b/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp index f12b3152794..e3752bb42f9 100644 --- a/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp +++ b/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp @@ -4148,6 +4148,43 @@ static void serializeConstant(const IDataType & type, const IColumn & value, Wri "Cannot serialize non-constant column {} as constant", value.getName()); const auto & data = const_column->getDataColumn(); + + /// Hash-input-only streams (see SerializedSetsRegistry::max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint): + /// represent large constants by an identity fingerprint instead of their full binary data. + /// A constant-folded literal can be arbitrarily big (e.g. `range(5000000)` folds into a + /// 5M-element array), and serializing it in full on every query execution just to compute + /// a hash-table-stats cache key costs more than the aggregation it is meant to help. + /// The fingerprint keeps the key's identity (type is encoded by the caller; size and a + /// whole-column hash are written here) at a bounded cost. This stream is never deserialized. + if (registry.max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint + && data.byteSize() > registry.max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint) + { + const size_t data_bytes = data.byteSize(); + writeStringBinary("__constant_fingerprint", out); + writeVarUInt(data.size(), out); + writeVarUInt(data_bytes, out); + + /// Hashing the content is itself O(data_bytes): SipHash over a constant-folded + /// literal runs at a few GB/s, so a 40MB folded `range(5000000)` array still costs + /// ~9ms on EVERY execution of the query — the same linear per-execution cost this + /// fingerprint exists to remove, only with a smaller constant factor. Above + /// max_constant_bytes_to_hash keep the constant's shape only (its type is written by + /// the caller, its row count and data size just above), which is O(1) in the + /// literal's size. Two distinct constants that share a type and a shape then also + /// share a cache key; that key selects a hash-table SIZE HINT for preallocation, so a + /// collision can only mis-size a preallocation and can never change a query result. + const bool hash_content = !registry.max_constant_bytes_to_hash + || data_bytes <= registry.max_constant_bytes_to_hash; + writeVarUInt(hash_content ? 1 : 0, out); + if (hash_content) + { + SipHash column_hash; + data.updateHashFast(column_hash); + writeBinary(column_hash.get64(), out); + } + return; + } + type.getDefaultSerialization()->serializeBinary(data, 0, out, FormatSettings{}); } diff --git a/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h b/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h index 1413aa556da..4beb1f15618 100644 --- a/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h +++ b/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h @@ -15,6 +15,25 @@ struct SerializedSetsRegistry }; std::unordered_map<FutureSet::Hash, FutureSetPtr, Hashing> sets; + + /// When non-zero, constant column values whose data is larger than this many bytes are + /// serialized as an identity fingerprint (marker + row count + data size + a bounded + /// content hash) instead of full binary data (see serializeConstant in ActionsDAG.cpp). + /// Such a stream CANNOT be deserialized; this mode is only for streams that are used as + /// hash input (aggregation hash-table stats cache keys, see calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp), + /// mirroring how Set constants are represented by their precomputed hash there. + /// 0 (default) keeps full serialization for shipping plans between servers. + size_t max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint = 0; + + /// Upper bound on how many bytes of a constant's data may be hashed INTO that fingerprint. + /// Writing the fingerprint is cheap, but hashing the column content is itself O(bytes): + /// a constant-folded literal is unbounded (`range(5000000)` folds into a ~40MB array + /// constant, `range(50000000)` into ~400MB), so a whole-column hash keeps a linear + /// per-execution cost in the plan-optimize path. Above this size the fingerprint keeps + /// only the constant's shape and the cost becomes O(1) in the literal's size. + /// Only meaningful together with max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint. + /// 0 (default) means "always hash the whole content". + size_t max_constant_bytes_to_hash = 0; }; class ColumnSet; diff --git a/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp index 03ed735d700..89af78827cf 100644 --- a/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp +++ b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp @@ -58,6 +58,16 @@ UInt64 calculateHashFromStep(const ITransformingStep & transform) { WriteBufferFromOwnString wbuf; SerializedSetsRegistry registry; + /// This stream is only SipHash input (never deserialized), so large constant columns may be + /// written as identity fingerprints instead of full binary data. Without this, a plan that + /// contains a big constant-folded literal (e.g. `range(5000000)` becomes a 5M-element array + /// constant) would be serialized in full on EVERY execution of the query, which is easily + /// more expensive than the aggregation the cache key is meant to speed up. + registry.max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint = 64 * 1024; + /// ... and above this size do not even hash their content: the hash itself is linear + /// in the constant's size, which is exactly the per-execution cost being removed here. + /// 1MB of content hashing is ~0.2ms, an acceptable upper bound for a preallocation hint. + registry.max_constant_bytes_to_hash = 1024 * 1024; IQueryPlanStep::Serialization ctx{.out = wbuf, .registry = registry, .skip_final_flag = true, .skip_cache_key = true}; writeStringBinary(transform.getSerializationName(), wbuf); ``` The remaining hunk of the validated diff (same file, `setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys`) is the parent finding's keyless-aggregation skip — already carried by PR #113333, shown for context only: ```diff @@ -225,7 +235,13 @@ void setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys(const QueryPlanOptimizationSettings & opti { auto * node = stack.back(); stack.pop_back(); - if (typeid_cast<AggregatingStep *>(node->step.get())) + /// Skip aggregations without GROUP BY keys: they use the `without_key` method + /// (see AggregatedDataVariants::chooseMethod), which has no hash table, so + /// HashTablesStatistics can never be consumed for them. Hashing their input + /// subtree would be pure per-execution overhead (it serializes every + /// non-rows-preserving step below the aggregation). + if (const auto * aggregating = typeid_cast<AggregatingStep *>(node->step.get()); + aggregating && !aggregating->getParams().keys.empty()) aggregating_nodes.push_back(node); for (auto * child : node->children) stack.push_back(child); ``` </details> Validation caveats, disclosed: - The comparison uses locally built binaries at base ref `a6156303df65c307bdb8b66e9e9cc5637346a6b8` (baseline = base + parent patch, candidate = base + this cumulative patch), not CI/release binaries — the same local-build convention as the parent finding. - The objective query's own wall-clock gain is not resolvable on this host (ratios ~0.96, unstable in both attempts); its gain is counter-level only, and the wall-clock ~2x comes from a synthetic amplifier built to expose the same mechanism above wall-clock noise. - The "two independent sessions" are same-host repeats started 39 seconds apart with the same binaries; the within-session A/B interleaving, not the repetition, is what controls environment drift. - The patch shown is cumulative versus the base ref (it includes the parent fix). The residual-specific A→B delta validated here is only the `max_constant_bytes_to_hash` registry field, its 1 MiB setting at the cache-key call site, and the shape-only branch (plus two varints in the fingerprint stream). - Rebase note: the patch is against base ref `a6156303`. PR #106073 (merged 2026-08-05) renamed `skip_cache_key` → `for_cache_key` and folded `skip_final_flag` (see `calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp:98-107` on master) — a trivial rebase is required.

signals.title: UNIQUE KEY accepts a subcolumn, making the table permanently un-insertable
signals.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong A `UNIQUE KEY` element that names a **subcolumn** (`` `c.1` ``, `` `c.null` ``, `` `c.keys` ``, ...) is accepted at `CREATE TABLE`, but every `INSERT` into the resulting table then fails with: ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column c1.1 in block. There are only columns: c0, c1, c2, c3, c4. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` The table is otherwise healthy — it persists across restart, `SELECT` works, `DROP` works — it just can never be written to. Since `UNIQUE KEY` cannot be altered, the only remedy is to recreate the table. This is the exact failure mode the DDL guard added in #107986 was written to prevent. Its comment says so verbatim (`registerStorageMergeTree.cpp`): > Reject expression-style elements at parse time: runtime consumers look up keys via > `block.getByName(<column name>)`, so an expression-style UK passes DDL but crashes the first INSERT. Subcolumns slip past that guard through a three-step gap: 1. **Backticks change the parse.** Bare `c.1` parses as `Function tupleElement(c, 1)` and is correctly rejected as expression-style. Backticked `` `c.1` `` is a plain `ASTIdentifier` whose *name* is the string `"c.1"`, so `is_plain_identifier` accepts it. 2. **`reject_non_physical` looks in the wrong index.** It tests `metadata.columns.has(name) && !hasPhysical(name)`, but `ColumnsDescription::has` searches only the top-level column index; subcolumns live in a separate `subcolumns` index reached via `hasSubcolumn`. So `has("c.1")` is `false` and the check short-circuits. 3. **The fallback assumption does not hold.** The guard's comment ends with *"A name that matches no column at all (not physical, not virtual) is left for `getKeyFromAST` (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)."* But a subcolumn name is not "no column at all" to the `TreeRewriter` — it resolves fine, so `unique_key.column_names` becomes `["c.1", ...]` and no error is raised. At `INSERT`, `SSTIndexWriter::write` does `block.getByName("c.1")` against a block that contains only physical columns → `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. Found by BuzzHouse. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on `master` — version `26.8.1.1154`, commit `59f0c881f8088762625627e14a0434d8db966566`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`. Deterministic. ## How to reproduce Run Fiddle: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/fcb27b57-281c-4b90-81ca-65ea02c2790e Five subcolumn families reach the same end state: | UNIQUE KEY element | column type | result | | --- | --- | --- | | `` `c.1` `` | `Tuple(String)` | `Not found column c.1 in block` | | `` `c.x` `` | `Tuple(x String)` | `Not found column c.x in block` | | `` `c.null` `` | `Nullable(String)` | `Not found column c.null in block` | | `` `c.size0` `` | `Array(Int32)` | `Not found column c.size0 in block` | | `` `c.keys` `` | `Map(String, String)` | `Not found column c.keys in block` | The neighbouring cases are all rejected correctly at `CREATE`, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a deliberate allowance: | UNIQUE KEY element | result | | --- | --- | | `c.1` (no backticks) | Code 36 — "Expression-style elements ... are not yet supported" | | `` `nosuch` `` | Code 47 — missing column | | `` `_part` `` | Code 36 — "virtual columns ... are not allowed" | | `` `c.a` `` on a `JSON` column | Code 549 — rejected by the key-expression type check | A `Nested` subcolumn such as `n.x` is unaffected: it is a genuine top-level physical column, so `has()` finds it and the guard behaves. ## Expected behaviour `CREATE TABLE` rejects a subcolumn in `UNIQUE KEY` with a clear `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, in line with the existing rejections for virtual / `ALIAS` / `EPHEMERAL` / expression-style elements — rather than producing a table that accepts no writes. ## Suggested fix One check next to the existing virtual-column check in `reject_non_physical` (`src/Storages/MergeTree/registerStorageMergeTree.cpp`): ```cpp if (!metadata.columns.has(name) && metadata.columns.hasSubcolumn(GetColumnsOptions::All, name)) throw Exception(ErrorCodes::BAD_ARGUMENTS, "UNIQUE KEY column `{}` is a subcolumn; UNIQUE KEY must name whole stored columns", name); ``` The leading `!metadata.columns.has(name)` keeps real `Nested` columns working, and placing the check before `getKeyFromAST` preserves the existing `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` path for names that match nothing at all. `GetColumnsOptions` is not currently referenced in that file, so this may need `#include <Storages/ColumnsDescription.h>`. If subcolumn keys are meant to be supported eventually, the alternative is to resolve the key expression into the block on the write path instead of rejecting it — but the interim guard's own stated contract ("only bare column names are allowed") argues for rejecting now. ## Additional context Related, same feature, both distinct from this: #110854 (`ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` on a UNIQUE KEY table rewrites metadata before validation and poisons startup) and #104963 (inconsistent AST formatting with `UNIQUE KEY`). Umbrella: #103486.

signals.title: optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq changes results: uniq*(tuple(nullable)) drops NULLs and depends on constant folding
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq` (default `true`) strips injective functions from `uniq*` arguments. When the stripped function is `tuple()` and its argument is `Nullable`, the rewrite is not semantics-preserving: `tuple(NULL)` is a value that `uniq*` counts, but a bare `NULL` is skipped by `uniq*`. So the optimization silently changes the result. ```sql SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL); -- 2 (with the optimization, i.e. by default) SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL) SETTINGS optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq = 0; -- 3 (correct: (1), (2) and (NULL) are three distinct tuples) ``` `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` shows the rewrite dropping the tuple: ```sql EXPLAIN SYNTAX SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- SELECT uniqExact(arrayJoin([NULL])) ``` A second, related symptom: with the analyzer, whether the optimization applies at all depends on whether the argument happens to be constant-foldable, so semantically identical expressions disagree with each other: ```sql SELECT countDistinct(tuple(NULL)); -- 1 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- 0 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin( emptyArrayToSingle([]::Array(Nullable(Int32)))))); -- 0 ``` `tuple(NULL)` has all-constant arguments, so it is folded into a `ConstantNode` during query analysis, and the pass no longer recognises it as a function to unwrap. The `arrayJoin` variants are not folded , so there the `tuple()` is stripped. With `enable_analyzer = 0` all three return `0`, because the legacy `TreeOptimizer` does the same rewrite on the un-folded AST. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/718dd23f-a726-4218-92f5-7b78048bda57 Also reproduces with `uniq`, `uniqHLL12`, `uniqCombined64` and `uniqTheta` (every function listed in `isUniqFunction`), and with `countDistinct` via `count_distinct_implementation`. ### Expected behavior `uniqExact(tuple(x))` should not depend on `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq`, on whether the argument is constant-foldable, or on `enable_analyzer`. `tuple()` is injective on the values it receives, but it also removes nullability, and `uniq*` treats NULL specially — so it must not be eliminated when its argument is `Nullable` and its own result type is not. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115466 - Backported to: `26.7.5.8`, `26.6.4.8`, `26.5.8.9`, `26.3.21.7`, `25.8.33.3` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)

signals.title: DeltaLake: trivial `SELECT count()` over a table with deletion vectors counts the deleted rows (`numRecords` summed, DV cardinality ignored)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** A Delta table where a `DELETE` was persisted as a deletion vector (the default for Spark/Databricks-written tables with `delta.enableDeletionVectors = true`) returns a wrong `SELECT count()`: the trivial-count path answers from file-level `numRecords` statistics and never subtracts the deletion vector's `cardinality`, so every DV-deleted row is still counted. Any query that actually scans the data (`sum`, `min`/`max`, a selective predicate) returns the correct result — the deletion-vector *scan* path works — which makes the wrong `count()` inconsistent with every other answer the same table gives. Version-pinned reads via `delta_lake_snapshot_version` have the same wrong count. `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` is a workaround. `optimize_count_from_files = 0` does **not** help — the shortcut is the storage's `totalRows`, not the files-count path. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1448 (also checked master snapshots back to 26.8.1.820). **How to reproduce** Write a table with a deletion vector using Spark (`pip install pyspark==3.5.3 delta-spark==3.2.1`, needs a JRE): ```python from delta import configure_spark_with_delta_pip from pyspark.sql import SparkSession b = (SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]") .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")) spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(b).getOrCreate() spark.sql("CREATE TABLE t (k BIGINT, v BIGINT) USING delta LOCATION '/tmp/dv_table' TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableDeletionVectors = true)") spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300)") spark.sql("DELETE FROM t WHERE k < 50") # persisted as a deletion vector, cardinality 50 spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300, 310)") ``` The table now holds 260 rows (Spark: `SELECT count(*)` → 260, `VERSION AS OF 2` → 250). Then: ```bash clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table')" # 310 <- wrong, counts the 50 DV-deleted rows clickhouse local -q "SELECT count(), sum(k), min(k) FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table')" # 260 46670 50 <- scan path, correct clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0" # 260 <- workaround clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_version = 2" # 300 <- wrong; Spark's VERSION AS OF 2 says 250 (a scanning query with the same pin correctly returns 250) ``` An `strace` of the wrong read shows neither the data files nor the `deletion_vector_*.bin` file is ever opened — only the `_delta_log` JSON files. **Expected behavior** `SELECT count()` returns 260 (and 250 at `delta_lake_snapshot_version = 2`), matching what the same queries return when they scan. **Actual behavior** 310 and 300: the count is answered from metadata as the plain sum of `numRecords` across add actions, ignoring each file's `deletionVector.cardinality`. **Mechanism** `DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel::totalRows` serves the trivial-count from `TableSnapshot::getTotalRows`. Both row-accumulation sites in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/DeltaLake/TableSnapshot.cpp` (the scan callback that fills `data_files`, and the `StatsVisitor` stats-only path) receive the file's `dv_info` handle from delta-kernel, yet unconditionally do `total_rows.value() += stats->num_records`. Fail-close would be setting `total_rows = std::nullopt` whenever `dv_info` is present (forcing the scan path); the precise fix is subtracting the deletion vector's cardinality. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/93852 --- Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: DataLakeCatalog: aws_external_id setting leaks in plaintext in SHOW CREATE DATABASE / system.databases.engine_full (masked everywhere else)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** A `DataLakeCatalog` database masks every credential-bearing setting in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` and `system.databases.engine_full` **except `aws_external_id`**, which is shown in plaintext — at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Any user who can run `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` or read `system.databases` sees it. `aws_external_id` is the external ID passed to AWS STS `AssumeRole`, matching the `sts:ExternalId` condition on the role's trust policy (its own setting description in `src/Databases/DataLake/DatabaseDataLakeSettings.cpp` notes it is for roles owned by a third party, such as ClickHouse Cloud). ClickHouse already treats this value as a secret in the *inline* `s3()` / `extra_credentials` form: `external_id` is a member of `s3_secret_keys` in `src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.h`, whose own comment calls it "the shared secret of the assume-role triple". So the identical value is masked in one surface and leaked in another. The cause is that the `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE` masking map in `src/Databases/DataLake/DataLakeConstants.h` lists `catalog_credential`, `auth_header`, `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, the `storage_*` variants, `onelake_*`, `google_adc_client_secret` / `google_adc_refresh_token`, and `dlf_*`, but has no entry for `aws_external_id`. (`aws_role_session_name` is likewise absent from the map, but that is an operator-chosen session label rather than a secret; the concern here is `aws_external_id`.) **How to reproduce** Any ClickHouse build with the Glue `DataLakeCatalog` backend. The Glue catalog is constructed lazily, so no live endpoint is needed to observe the masking: ```sql SET allow_database_glue_catalog = 1; CREATE DATABASE ge ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://glue.us-east-1.amazonaws.com') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'glue', region = 'us-east-1', aws_access_key_id = 'AKIAEXAMPLE', aws_secret_access_key = 'SECRET', aws_role_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/r', aws_external_id = 'my-external-id-value'; SELECT engine_full FROM system.databases WHERE name = 'ge'; ``` Output (note `aws_secret_access_key` is `[HIDDEN]` but `aws_external_id` is verbatim): ``` DataLakeCatalog('https://glue.us-east-1.amazonaws.com') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'glue', region = 'us-east-1', aws_access_key_id = '[HIDDEN]', aws_secret_access_key = '[HIDDEN]', aws_role_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/r', aws_external_id = 'my-external-id-value' ``` `SHOW CREATE DATABASE ge` shows the same unmasked value. **Expected behavior** `aws_external_id` should be masked as `'[HIDDEN]'` in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE`, `system.databases.engine_full`, and any other formatted-with-secrets-hidden surface, consistent with how the inline `external_id` argument is masked via `s3_secret_keys` and with the other credential settings in `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE`. **Which ClickHouse server versions are incompatible** Reproduced on master (26.8). By code inspection the gap exists on every version whose `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE` map omits `aws_external_id`.
