signals.title: optimizeExchanges throws Unknown identifier for an ActionsDAG pass-through sort column
signals.text: ## Description `optimizeExchanges` can throw during `QueryPlan::optimize` when it tries to move a sorted Gather across an `ExpressionStep` or `FilterStep` whose maintained sort column is passed through implicitly: ```text Code: 47 Unknown identifier: '__table2.state' ``` One triggering plan shape contains a partitioned window followed by an outer filter: ```sql SELECT * FROM ( SELECT state, season, dense_rank() OVER ( PARTITION BY state, season ORDER BY total_sales DESC ) AS category_rank FROM ... ) WHERE category_rank <= 3 ORDER BY state, season, category_rank ``` The failure occurs during query-plan optimization, before plan splitting or execution, and does not depend on Stateless Workers. ## Root cause `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` builds a step's output header from both explicit DAG outputs and unconsumed input columns copied through unchanged. A pass-through sort column can therefore exist in the output header without having a corresponding node in `dag.outputs`. After confirming that the output header contains the sort column, `isSortColumnPreserved` unconditionally calls: ```cpp dag.findInOutputs(column_name) ``` `findInOutputs` searches only explicit DAG outputs and throws Code 47 when the column is an implicit pass-through. The lookup therefore treats a valid unchanged column as missing. ## Introduction and exposure The unsafe lookup was introduced by #106020. The distributed `PARTITION BY` window placement added by #114111 allows this plan shape to reach the pre-existing defect.
signals.author: XuJia0210

signals.title: CHECK TABLE returns 0 instead of failing when the check is aborted by a partial shutdown (Keeper session loss) — a false corruption alarm on healthy data
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe what's wrong When a `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica has lost its Keeper session and entered partial shutdown, `CHECK TABLE t SETTINGS check_query_single_value_result=1` returns `0` — the result that is documented to mean "the check detected an error in the table data" — even though the data is perfectly healthy and nothing was actually checked. The window is deterministic. In the first seconds of a Keeper outage (session still alive but unresponsive), the query correctly fails with `KEEPER_EXCEPTION` / `Connection loss`. Once the session expires and the restarting thread calls partial shutdown, the same query flips from erroring to *certifying failure*: the storage check throws `ABORTED` ("Table shutdown was called"), and `TableCheckTask::checkNext` in `src/Interpreters/InterpreterCheckQuery.cpp` deliberately refuses to rethrow `ABORTED`, converting it into a `CheckResult` row with `success=false` and an empty `part_path`, and marks the task finished — so the remaining parts are never checked and the single-value aggregation latches `0`. With `check_query_single_value_result=0` the output is a single row with an empty part path and the message `Table shutdown was called` — clearly not a per-part data verdict, yet in the single-value form it is indistinguishable from real corruption. Any monitoring or automation that runs `CHECK TABLE` and alerts (or quarantines, or re-replicates) on `0` fires a false alarm on every Keeper flap. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduces on 26.8.1.1068 (official build) and on current master 26.8.1.1833 (official build). ### How to reproduce 1. Start a ClickHouse server with a standalone (or embedded) Keeper and create a small `ReplicatedMergeTree` table with a few parts: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, val UInt64, part UInt16) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/t', 'r0') PARTITION BY part ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number, number % 4 FROM numbers(1000); ``` 2. Verify the baseline: `CHECK TABLE t SETTINGS check_query_single_value_result=1` returns `1`. 3. Pause the Keeper process (`kill -STOP <keeper pid>`) and wait for the session to expire so the replica enters partial shutdown (the table becomes readonly). 4. Run the check repeatedly. Observed timeline: ``` t+30s CHECK -> Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: ... Connection loss ... (KEEPER_EXCEPTION) -- correct: the query fails t+35s CHECK -> 0 -- wrong: certifies data failure ``` With `check_query_single_value_result=0` the `0` case returns one row: empty part path, `is_passed=0`, message `DB::Exception: Table shutdown was called`. 5. Resume the Keeper (`kill -CONT <keeper pid>`); after the session is re-established, `CHECK TABLE` returns `1` again. ### Expected behavior `CHECK TABLE` should fail with an error (as it already does for the session-loss window) whenever the check could not be executed. A result of `0` should only ever mean that at least one part actually failed its data check. ### Error message and/or stacktrace `is_passed=0` row produced without any part being read: ``` 0 DB::Exception: Table shutdown was called ``` ### Additional context The conversion happens in the `catch` block of `TableCheckTask::checkNext` (`src/Interpreters/InterpreterCheckQuery.cpp`): `ABORTED` is excluded from the retryable-exception rethrow, turned into a failed `CheckResult` with an empty path, and `is_finished` is set so the remaining parts are skipped. The same window also reproduces on `SharedMergeTree`.
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: `CI Tests` fails on master for any PR touching `ci/`: `test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data` broken by the #115221 + #104631 combination
signals.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115221 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104631 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 ### Describe what's wrong `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py::test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data` fails on current master (verified on `590a91de69b`), so the `CI Tests` job is red for every pull request whose changes select it (anything touching `ci/`). The test (added in #115221, merged 2026-08-21 01:27 UTC) asserts that changing only `ci/defs/job_configs.py` or `ci/defs/defs.py` does not schedule `Build (arm_release)`. Meanwhile #104631 (merged 2026-08-20) added `Parser memory check` to the PR workflow with - `digest_config` including `./ci/defs/defs.py`, `./ci/defs/job_configs.py` and `./ci/workflows/pull_request.py`, and - `requires=[CLICKHOUSE_EXAMPLES]`, an artifact provided by `Build (arm_release)` (the `--build-examples` variant). So a registry-only edit makes `Parser memory check` affected, and the rescue pass in `_filter_unaffected_jobs` schedules `Build (arm_release)` to produce `CLICKHOUSE_EXAMPLES` — exactly the waste the new test pins against. Each PR was green on its own: #115221's branch predates #104631's merge, and #104631 could not run the not-yet-existing test. The combination on master is what breaks. First observed in #115036 (`CI Tests`, head `1c383b2ae00`): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=1c383b2ae000d256fc2e04e60b4b4b5ddab93b96&name_0=PR&name_1=CI%20Tests ### How to reproduce On master: ``` python3 -m pytest ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py::test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data ``` Fails at `8518542d957` (the #115221 merge commit) and on current master; the test does not exist on its parent. Possible directions (either restores the invariant): drop the registry paths from `Parser memory check`'s `digest_config` (no other job digests the registry; its own script and `utils/parser-memory-profiler/` stay), or teach the rescue pass / the test about registry-digesting consumers of build artifacts.
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: JSON -> text serialization is ~4.4x slower since 26.4 (`getDefaultSerialization` is called per value and now goes through the global serialization pool)
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the situation Every read path that writes a `JSON` column as text became about 4.4x slower in 26.4. Read paths that write the same column in **binary** form did not change. The cause is a per-value call in `SerializationDynamic`: ```cpp // src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationDynamic.cpp:971 (master) nested_serialize(*dynamic_column.getVariantInfo().variant_type->getDefaultSerialization(), variant_column, row_num, ostr); ``` The shared-variant branch of the same function does the same thing at line 964. `SerializationJSON::serializeTextImpl` calls this once **per JSON path, per row**. `IDataType::getDefaultSerialization()` has never been cached, so this call was always hot. Before 26.4 it only allocated a `SerializationVariant`. Since [#96563](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96563) ("Added a serialization object pool") it goes through a process-wide pool: `getDefaultSerialization()` -> `DataTypeVariant::doGetSerialization()` -> `SerializationVariant::create()` -> `ISerialization::pooled()` -> `SerializationObjectPool::getOrCreate()` `getOrCreate` takes a `std::shared_lock` on one global `SharedMutex`, does an `absl::flat_hash_map::find`, and calls `weak_ptr::lock()`. The `shared_ptr` it returns is released immediately after the value is written, which runs the custom deleter and can take the **write** lock to erase the map entry. The pool does not remove the construction cost that it is meant to avoid. `DataTypeVariant::doGetSerialization()` must first build the `serializations` and `variant_names` vectors (one `IDataType::getName()` string per variant, plus a recursive `getDefaultSerialization()` per nested type) to compute the pool key. So the pool adds a hash, a lock, a map lookup and atomic `weak_ptr` traffic **on top of** the work that 26.2 did, on a path that runs about 10^7 times for a 1M-row scan. Because the pool is global and the reference counts are shared, the added cost is contended state. It should get worse as core count goes up. **Why the binary paths are not affected.** They resolve the serialization once per column per block and keep it. `SerializationObject::serializeBinary` uses the `dynamic_serialization` member, and Native's bulk path caches `dynamic_state->variant_serialization`. Only the text path re-acquires the serialization for every value. The asymmetry is also visible in `SerializationDynamic.cpp` itself. The row-level **binary** serializer already avoids the global pool with a thread-local cache: ```cpp // line 762 — binary, not regressed getDataTypesCache().getSerialization(variant_type_name)->serializeBinary(...); ``` `serializeForHashCalculation` does the same at lines 786 and 797. The **text** path at lines 964 and 971 is the one that still goes to the global pool. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? 26.4 and later, including `master`. Measured on official Docker images: | Version | Regressed | | --- | --- | | 26.2.18.8 | no | | 26.3.19.3 | no | | 26.4.5.143 | **yes** | | 26.7.3.19 | **yes** |. ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE json_bench (id UInt64, payload JSON) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO json_bench (id, payload) SELECT number AS id, CAST( ( number, ['info', 'warn', 'error', 'debug'][(number % 4) + 1], map('user', randomPrintableASCII(8), 'session', randomPrintableASCII(12), 'region', randomPrintableASCII(4)), [randomPrintableASCII(5), randomPrintableASCII(6), randomPrintableASCII(4)], CAST( (randomPrintableASCII(6), (toInt64(rand64() % 180000000) - 90000000) / 1000000.0, (toInt64(rand64() % 360000000) - 180000000) / 1000000.0) AS Tuple(country String, lat Float64, lon Float64) ), (number % 2) = 0 ) AS Tuple(user_id UInt64, event String, props Map(String, String), tags Array(String), geo Tuple(country String, lat Float64, lon Float64), active Bool) )::JSON AS payload FROM numbers(1000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE json_bench FINAL; ``` The payload has 10 leaf paths. All of them are dynamic paths, well below the `max_dynamic_paths` default of 1024, so nothing goes to shared data. **Query A — text output (regressed):** ```sql SELECT sum(length(toString(payload))) FROM (SELECT payload FROM json_bench LIMIT 200000); ``` `toString()` is used to keep the measurement free of output-format, socket and compression cost. `FORMAT TSV`, `FORMAT JSONEachRow`, and `FORMAT RowBinary` with `output_format_binary_write_json_as_string = 1` all show the same regression. **Query B — binary output (control, not regressed):** ```sql SELECT * FROM json_bench LIMIT 200000 FORMAT Native; ``` **Results.** `max_threads = 4`, server-side `query_duration_ms` from `system.query_log`, 10 interleaved rounds per version in shuffled order, all four servers holding an identical 1M-row single-part table: | Version | Query A median | Query A range | vs 26.2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 26.2.18.8 | 766 ms | 739–951 | 1.00x | | 26.3.19.3 | 698 ms | 643–925 | 0.91x | | 26.4.5.143 | 3347 ms | 3217–3461 | **4.37x** | | 26.7.3.19 | 3592 ms | 3491–3683 | **4.69x** | The ranges do not overlap, in either direction. 26.7 is also reliably worse than 26.4 (26.7 min 3491 > 26.4 max 3461). Query B (`FORMAT Native`) stays at a 69–80 ms median on all four versions. ### Expected performance The 26.2 and 26.3 result: about 770 ms for Query A, that is ~4.4x faster than 26.4+. ### Additional context **Profile.** `query_profiler_cpu_time_period_ns = 1000000` on `SELECT * FROM json_bench LIMIT 200000 FORMAT TSV`, `max_threads = 4`, symbol sample counts from `system.trace_log`: 26.2.18.8 (386 root samples): ``` 297 SerializationJSON<SimdJSONParser>::serializeTextEscaped 240 SerializationDynamic::serializeTextJSON 154 DataTypeVariant::doGetDefaultSerialization <-- 40% of the query 65 SerializationVariant::SerializationVariant ``` 26.7.3.19 (915 root samples): ``` 840 SerializationJSON<SimdJSONParser>::serializeTextEscaped 737 SerializationDynamic::serializeTextJSON 713 IDataType::getDefaultSerialization <-- 78% of the query 523 DataTypeVariant::doGetSerialization 363 ISerialization::pooled 333 SerializationObjectPool::getOrCreate 275 SerializationVariant::create 163 <pool deleter> __on_zero_shared 102 SerializationObjectPool::getOrCreate::$_0::operator() 100 SerializationVariant::~SerializationVariant ``` 26.4.5.143 shows the same symbols in the same order. Serialization acquisition went from 40% of the query to 78%, while the query itself became 4.4x slower. In absolute terms that call is about 7x more expensive than it was. **Ruled out.** `output_format_parallel_formatting` is not involved: on 26.4 the query is slow with the setting both on (12976 ms) and off (10175 ms). Nothing in the window changes `SerializationJSON::serializeTextImpl`, `SerializationDynamic::serializeTextImpl`, `writeJSONString` or `writeEscapedString`. There is no relevant JSON/object default change in the 26.3 or 26.4 entries of `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp`. Shared data is not involved, since 10 paths stay well below `max_dynamic_paths`. **Possible directions.** Use the existing thread-local `getDataTypesCache().getSerialization(...)` at lines 964 and 971, which is what the binary serializer two functions above already does. Alternatively, hold the resolved serialization in `SerializationJSON` / `SerializationDynamic` for the duration of the block. Either way the pool lookup leaves the per-value loop. **Related work.** This fix pattern is already accepted for other call sites of the same problem: * [#113344](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113344) (open) — "Use cached serializations for `Dynamic` fields". Replaces `getDefaultSerialization()` with `getDataTypesCache().getSerialization(...)` in `SerializationDynamic::serializeBinary(const Field &)` and `deserializeBinary(Field &)` (lines 718 and 730), for the same reason: those calls "enter the globally locked `SerializationObjectPool` for every value". It reports up to 122% improvement. It does **not** touch the text path, so it does not fix this issue. * [#112264](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112264) (closed) — names the same `getDefaultSerialization()` -> `SerializationObjectPool` cost as the expensive part of `ColumnDynamic::serializeValueIntoArena` in the aggregation prefetch path. Together with this report, that is three separate hot call sites paying the global pool per value. It may be worth checking the remaining `getDefaultSerialization()` calls that sit inside row loops rather than fixing them one at a time.
signals.author: alex-clickhouse

signals.title: Recursive CTE over MergeTree with parallel replicas: logical error `UNION query ... is not recursive` or infinite recursion
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe what's wrong When a recursive CTE reads from a `MergeTree` table and parallel replicas are enabled, the query breaks in one of two ways depending on how the CTE is used: 1. If the CTE is referenced from an `IN` subquery, the query fails with a logical error: `UNION query r is not recursive. (LOGICAL_ERROR)`. In debug and sanitizer builds this aborts the server (this is how it surfaced in a Stress test (arm_msan) CI run). 2. If the CTE is the top-level `FROM`, the recursion never converges and fails with `Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (1000) exceeded (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION)` on a 3-row table whose recursion should terminate after 3 iterations. Without parallel replicas the same queries return correct results. The logical error is thrown from `RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator` (`src/Processors/Sources/RecursiveCTESource.cpp:84`) because `collectTableNodesWithTemporaryTableName` finds no table node referencing the CTE's temporary table inside the union node. A recursive CTE with no table read inside it (e.g. `SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3`) works fine under the same settings, so the parallel replicas rewrite of the table read inside the CTE appears to replace or lose the recursive self-reference before `RecursiveCTESource` is built. The non-convergence in the second case points at the same root cause: the reference to the working table resolves incorrectly, so every iteration keeps producing rows. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on a recent master build (26.8.1.1). The involved code paths (`RecursiveCTESource`, parallel replicas planning) are the same in the latest releases. ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE t_pr_cte (n UInt64, p UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY n; INSERT INTO t_pr_cte VALUES (1, 0), (2, 1), (3, 2); -- Manifestation 1: logical error WITH RECURSIVE r AS ( SELECT n FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n = 1 UNION ALL SELECT t.n FROM t_pr_cte AS t INNER JOIN r ON t.p = r.n ) SELECT count() FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n IN (SELECT n FROM r) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'parallel_replicas', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1; -- Manifestation 2: infinite recursion WITH RECURSIVE r AS ( SELECT n FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n = 1 UNION ALL SELECT t.n FROM t_pr_cte AS t INNER JOIN r ON t.p = r.n ) SELECT count() FROM r SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'parallel_replicas', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1; ``` Removing the parallel replicas settings makes both queries return the correct result (`3`). ### Expected behavior Both queries return `3`, as they do without parallel replicas (or parallel replicas is not applied to the recursive CTE if it cannot handle it). ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: UNION query r is not recursive. (LOGICAL_ERROR) 4. src/Common/Exception.h:219:77: DB::Exception::Exception<String>(...) 5. src/Processors/Sources/RecursiveCTESource.cpp:84:19: DB::RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator::RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator(std::shared_ptr<DB::Block const>, std::shared_ptr<DB::IQueryTreeNode>) 6. DB::RecursiveCTESource::RecursiveCTESource(std::shared_ptr<DB::Block const>, std::shared_ptr<DB::IQueryTreeNode>) 7. DB::ReadFromRecursiveCTEStep::initializePipeline(DB::QueryPipelineBuilder&, DB::BuildQueryPipelineSettings const&) 8. src/Processors/QueryPlan/ISourceStep.cpp:20:5: DB::ISourceStep::updatePipeline(...) 9. src/Processors/QueryPlan/QueryPlan.cpp:271:47: DB::QueryPlan::buildQueryPipeline(...) 10. src/Interpreters/InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer.cpp:429:34: DB::InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer::buildQueryPipeline() ``` And for the second manifestation: ``` Code: 306. DB::Exception: Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (1000) exceeded, during evaluation of r. Consider raising max_recursive_cte_evaluation_depth setting: While executing RecursiveCTESource. (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION) ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115619 Related: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115619&sha=452c119a225d1107c28037a0c371d692306cd2de&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29 ### Additional context Found while investigating a Stress test (arm_msan) failure of the pull request above: the stress runner replayed a test query containing a recursive CTE with randomized parallel replicas settings and the server aborted on the logical error. The test was rewritten to avoid the recursive CTE, so the pull request only removed the trigger; the underlying bug is unrelated to its changes.

signals.title: DatabaseMySQL::getTablesIterator throws: one unreachable MySQL DB breaks system.tables
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With a `MySQL` database engine attached to an unreachable server, `SELECT ... FROM system.tables` and `SELECT ... FROM system.columns` fail server-wide with `Code: 279 ALL_CONNECTION_TRIES_FAILED` under default settings. Any query whose identifier fails to resolve also answers 279 instead of `UNKNOWN_TABLE`, because the hint lookup iterates every database.** - **Root cause:** `DatabaseMySQL::getTablesIterator` calls `fetchTablesIntoLocalCache` with no try/catch, unlike its sibling `DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator`, which wraps the same work and states the invariant in a comment: 'Do not allow to throw here, because this might be, for example, a query to system.tables. It must not fail on case of some postgres error.' ([`src/Databases/PostgreSQL/DatabasePostgreSQL.cpp:160-161`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Databases/PostgreSQL/DatabasePostgreSQL.cpp#L160-L161), catch at :171-174). Predates this PR; the PR touches the tolerated-failure handling in both files and leaves the asymmetry in place. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `StorageSystemTables` -> `IDatabase::getLightweightTablesIterator` -> `DatabaseMySQL::getTablesIterator` ([`src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp:184`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp#L184)) -> `fetchTablesIntoLocalCache` (:299) -> `mysqlxx::PoolWithFailover::get` throws `ALL_CONNECTION_TRIES_FAILED` ([`src/Common/mysqlxx/PoolWithFailover.cpp:294-296`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Common/mysqlxx/PoolWithFailover.cpp#L294-L296)). Nothing on that path catches. The typo path is `IdentifierResolver::tryGetTableNameHint` -> `TableNameHints::getAllRegisteredNames` -> `IDatabase::getAllTableNames` -> the same iterator. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp:184`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp#L184) — getTablesIterator calls fetchTablesIntoLocalCache with no catch - [`src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp:299`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp#L299) — fetchTablesIntoLocalCache — borrows from mysql_pool, propagates ALL_CONNECTION_TRIES_FAILED - [`src/Databases/PostgreSQL/DatabasePostgreSQL.cpp:171`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Databases/PostgreSQL/DatabasePostgreSQL.cpp#L171) — sibling that does catch, stating the invariant this violates **Impact:** One unreachable MySQL remote makes `system.tables` and `system.columns` unusable for every user and every tool on the server (BI introspection, client autocompletion, monitoring). It also poisons CI: a stateless test that attaches such a database and aborts before its DROP leaves it attached for the rest of the run. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `d8bf9a01b85be`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Tag justification, matching 04210_show_remote_databases_in_system_tables: -- no-fasttest: depends on libmysql (MySQL database engine), not built in fast test. -- no-parallel: the database created here points at an unreachable host and is visible in -- system.tables, so a concurrent scan without a database filter would connect there too. -- An unreachable MySQL database must not break an unfiltered system.tables / system.columns scan. DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS {CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_1:Identifier}; SET send_logs_level = 'fatal'; ATTACH DATABASE {CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_1:Identifier} ENGINE = MySQL('127.0.0.1:1', 'fake_db', 'user', 'password') SETTINGS connect_timeout = 1, connection_max_tries = 1; SELECT count() > 0 FROM system.tables; SELECT count() > 0 FROM system.columns; DROP DATABASE {CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_1:Identifier}; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` 1 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 279. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:19020. DB::Exception: Connections to mysql failed: fake_db@127.0.0.1:1 as user user, ERROR 2002 : mysqlxx::ConnectionFailed: Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (115) ((nullptr):0). (ALL_CONNECTION_TRIES_FAILED) (query: SELECT count() > 0 FROM system.tables;) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Wrap the `fetchTablesIntoLocalCache` call in `DatabaseMySQL::getTablesIterator` in the same tolerate-and-log pattern the PostgreSQL sibling uses, reusing the classifier this PR already adds: `try { fetchTablesIntoLocalCache(local_context); } catch (...) { tryLogCurrentException(__PRETTY_FUNCTION__, "", mysqlToleratedConnectionFailureLogLevel()); }`, then serve whatever `local_tables_cache` holds. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The PR's own tests/queries/0_stateless/04506_remote_database_unreachable_no_error_log.sh attaches an unreachable MySQL database and drops it only on the happy path (no `trap`). If the 120-iteration wait loop or the runner timeout aborts the script, the database survives and every later unfiltered `system.tables`/`system.columns` scan in that CI run throws 279. Worth adding `trap 'clickhouse-client -q "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ..."' EXIT` regardless of whether the source bug is fixed. - `DatabaseMySQL::empty` (src/Databases/MySQL/DatabaseMySQL.cpp:167) has the same shape and is reachable from `DatabaseCatalog`; not separately reproduced. Found during automated review of [PR #109472](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109472). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr109472_001` </details> cc @tiandiwonder @kssenii (from #109472)

signals.title: `to_utc_timestamp` and `from_utc_timestamp` are ~2.7x slower for `DateTime64` after the overflow fix
signals.text: The performance test `utc_timestamp_transform` shows that `to_utc_timestamp` and `from_utc_timestamp` on a `DateTime64` argument became ~2.7 times slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. The `DateTime` variants of the same queries did not regress, which points directly at the `DateTime64` overflow fix. Queries (from `tests/performance/utc_timestamp_transform.xml`, `test2` is `CREATE TABLE test2(d DateTime64) ENGINE Memory` with 10M rows): ```sql select count(1) from test2 where to_utc_timestamp(d, 'Etc/GMT+1') > '1990-01-01 12:00:00' SETTINGS max_threads=1 select count(1) from test2 where from_utc_timestamp(d, 'Etc/GMT+1') > '1990-01-01 12:00:00' SETTINGS max_threads=1 ``` Measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `to_utc_timestamp(DateTime64)` | 0.067 s | 0.182 s | **+172%** | | `from_utc_timestamp(DateTime64)` | 0.067 s | 0.182 s | **+172%** | The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit 3566f9010eaeca8ad8bdabf7dbd8cd536cdb2cdf on 2026-07-30, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. The overflow check is needed for correctness, but a 2.7x slowdown suggests it is done per row in a way that defeats vectorization or adds a per-row branch/exception path; it should be possible to keep saturating/checked behavior much cheaper (e.g. hoisting the timezone offset computation or checking bounds on the whole column). Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109738 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=3566f9010eae This is one of the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @groeneai
signals.author: alexey-milovidov

signals.title: `dictGet` with direct dictionaries is up to 2x slower after column-native IN/set constant handling
signals.text: The performance test `direct_dictionary` shows that `dictGet` with direct dictionaries became substantially slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base — 16 query variants regressed at once, up to 2x for simple-key lookups. Representative queries (from `tests/performance/direct_dictionary.xml`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | simple key, `value_int`, 75k lookups | 0.220 s | 0.435 s | **+98%** | | simple key, tuple of 4 attributes, 75k lookups | 0.225 s | 0.440 s | **+96%** | | simple key, `value_decimal`, 50k lookups | 0.158 s | 0.296 s | **+88%** | | simple key, `value_string_nullable`, 50k lookups | 0.160 s | 0.297 s | **+86%** | | complex key, `value_string`, 50k lookups | 0.476 s | 0.631 s | **+33%** | | complex key, `value_int`, 75k lookups | 0.692 s | 0.910 s | **+32%** | ```sql WITH rand64() % toUInt64(75000) as key SELECT dictGet('default.simple_key_direct_dictionary', 'value_int', key) FROM system.numbers LIMIT 75000 FORMAT Null; ``` The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit ce2fb4e26e8156e469449866f7d64b0e7de768ba on 2026-08-12, flagged on both AMD and ARM (16 query variants). A direct dictionary executes a source query per `dictGet` block and builds a set/filter from the requested keys, so it is plausible that the new column-native IN/set constant handling made that per-lookup path more expensive. Notably, on that commit the per-commit comparison showed exactly 10 slower queries per shard, one under the `SLOWER_QUERIES_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 10` gate (which is `> 10`), so the check stayed green and the regression landed silently. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113051 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=ce2fb4e26e81 This is the largest contributor to the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @yakov-olkhovskiy

signals.title: `GROUP BY` without aggregate functions is 23-30% slower on short string keys after the `HashSet` change
signals.text: The performance test `if_transform_strings_to_enum` shows that `GROUP BY` without aggregate functions over short string keys became 23-30% slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. Queries (from `tests/performance/if_transform_strings_to_enum.xml`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `SELECT transform(number, [2, 4, 6], ['google', 'yandex', 'yahoo'], 'other') as x FROM numbers(100000000) GROUP BY x FORMAT Null` | 0.670 s | 0.874 s | **+30%** | | `SELECT length(URL) > 1000 ? 'LONG' : 'SHORT' as x FROM hits_100m_single GROUP BY x FORMAT Null` | 0.096 s | 0.119 s | **+23%** | Both queries aggregate without aggregate functions over a low-cardinality string key, which is exactly the path switched to `HashSet`. The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit dddf61ccff5828bb6937cfe680874a04be35932f on 2026-08-19, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. signals.title: Short queries with many scalar subqueries are ~20% slower after AutoPR JOIN support
signals.text: The performance test `scalar` shows that a short (~0.1 s) analytical query with 8 scalar subqueries became ~20% slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. Query #0 from `tests/performance/scalar.xml` (8 scalar subqueries over `cdp_tags` feeding `multiIf(bitmapContains(...))` over `cdp_orders` with `PREWHERE`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `scalar #0` | 0.094 s | 0.113 s | **+20%** | The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit 1a969f3a2d697e0a4b86cb04d9fa69eef5271e7d on 2026-08-05, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. The suspected PR does not change execution of this query (it has no JOIN), so the cost is most likely added planning overhead — e.g. `considerEnablingParallelReplicas` / output-bytes estimation now running extra analysis for each of the scalar subqueries. At ~100 ms total runtime, per-query planning cost is the dominant term, so this likely affects all short queries with many scalar subqueries, not just this benchmark. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106073 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=1a969f3a2d69 This is one of the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @nickitat

signals.title: `DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE` refused on the introspection port that lists DESCRIBE as allowed
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **On an introspection port, `DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE 'x'` fails with `QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED` and a message that itself names DESCRIBE as an accepted kind. The same statement works on a regular port.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Parsers/ASTDescribeCacheQuery.h:9`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Parsers/ASTDescribeCacheQuery.h#L9) - the class has no `getQueryKind` override, so `DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE` reports `QueryKind::None` instead of `QueryKind::Describe`. The PR added `Kind` to the four `ASTQueryWithOutputImpl` instantiations it needed but did not sweep the remaining kind-less read-only statements that the new allow-list now gates. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `executeQueryImpl` -> `checkQueryIsAllowedOnIntrospectionPort` ([`src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:2186`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp#L2186)) -> `isAllowedOnIntrospectionPort` ([`src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:1224`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp#L1224)) switches on `ast.getQueryKind()`. `ASTDescribeCacheQuery` derives from `ASTQueryWithOutput` and never overrides `getQueryKind`, so it falls through to `IAST::getQueryKind`'s `QueryKind::None` ([`src/Parsers/IAST.h:516`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Parsers/IAST.h#L516)) and lands in the `default: return false` arm. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Parsers/ASTDescribeCacheQuery.h:9`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Parsers/ASTDescribeCacheQuery.h#L9) — ASTDescribeCacheQuery has no getQueryKind override -> QueryKind::None - [`src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:1224`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp#L1224) — isAllowedOnIntrospectionPort switches on getQueryKind; None hits the default arm - [`src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp:2186`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d8bf9a01b85be/src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp#L2186) — checkQueryIsAllowedOnIntrospectionPort throws QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED listing DESCRIBE as allowed **Impact:** An operator diagnosing a server stuck in startup or shutdown - exactly the window this port exists for, and the window in which filesystem-cache load is a plausible cause - cannot inspect cache state. The error message actively misleads by listing DESCRIBE as permitted. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `d8bf9a01b85be`). ### How to reproduce ```python cd tests/integration && CLICKHOUSE_TESTS_SERVER_BIN_PATH=<build>/programs/clickhouse CLICKHOUSE_TESTS_CLIENT_BIN_PATH=<build>/programs/clickhouse CLICKHOUSE_TESTS_BASE_CONFIG_DIR=<repo>/programs/server python3 -m pytest test_introspection_port/test.py -v -s --timeout=500 (after appending the two assertions above to test_introspection_port) ``` ### Expected behavior ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Received from 172.18.0.2:9010. DB::Exception: There is no cache by name: nonexistent. ... (BAD_ARGUMENTS) (query: DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE 'nonexistent') -- i.e. the same error the regular port 9000 returns ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 392. DB::Exception: Received from 172.18.0.2:9010. DB::Exception: Only diagnostic queries are allowed on the introspection port: SELECT, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN, EXISTS, KILL QUERY, SYSTEM, SET and USE. ... (QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED) (query: DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE 'nonexistent') ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Add `QueryKind getQueryKind() const override { return QueryKind::Describe; }` to `ASTDescribeCacheQuery` (src/Parsers/ASTDescribeCacheQuery.h). This also fixes `system.query_log.query_kind` for the statement. Alternatively, if the exclusion is intended, qualify both the docs table and the `QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED` message. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `ASTExecuteAsQuery` is the only other `ASTQueryWithOutput` subclass without a `getQueryKind` override; it is correctly refused (EXECUTE AS impersonates in the session), so no second finding. Audit performed with `for f in $(grep -rln "public ASTQueryWithOutput\b" src/Parsers/); do grep -q getQueryKind $f || echo $f; done` - exactly two hits. Found during automated review of [PR #110838](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110838). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr110838_001` </details> cc @mstetsyuk @alexey-milovidov @evillique (from #110838)

signals.title: `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER` with literal shard/replica names makes two servers the same `Replicated` replica: LOGICAL_ERROR and crash loop (debug), permanently wedged database (release)
signals.text: 🕵️ ### Describe the bug A `Replicated` database created with `ON CLUSTER` and *literal* shard/replica names — instead of the `{shard}`/`{replica}` macros — registers every host in the cluster as the **same** replica. One of the servers then hits ``` Logical error: 'Ephemeral node /clickhouse/databases/<db>/replicas/s1|d1/active still exists after 45s, probably it's owned by someone else. ...' ``` and aborts (debug/sanitizer builds), re-aborting ~45 s after every restart. On release builds it does not abort, but the database becomes permanently unusable on **both** servers. The same misconfiguration is correctly rejected when the two `CREATE DATABASE` statements are run separately on each server: ``` Code: 253. DB::Exception: Replica d1 of shard s1 of replicated database at /clickhouse/databases/db already exists. Replica host ID: 'host:30301:<uuid>', current host ID: 'host:30302:<uuid>'. (REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS) ``` `ON CLUSTER` defeats that guard. A distributed `CREATE DATABASE` assigns **one database UUID to every host**, so on the second host `DatabaseReplicated::initDatabaseReplica` finds a `replica_path` whose stored `host_id` differs from its own but whose embedded UUID matches, takes the "same UUID, the interserver address must have changed" branch, overwrites `host_id` with its own and continues: ```cpp if (uuid_in_keeper != db_uuid) throw Exception(ErrorCodes::REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS, ...); // After restarting, InterserverIOAddress might change ... // If the UUID in the keeper is the same as the current server UUID, we will update the host_id in keeper current_zookeeper->set(replica_path, host_id, -1); ``` That branch is right for its intended case (the same server coming back under a new FQDN/port, when no other server is live), but here the other host is alive and holding `/replicas/s1|d1/active`. Both `DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker`s then fight over that ephemeral node, and the loser waits `3 * session_timeout_ms` in `zkutil::ZooKeeper::deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches` before raising `LOGICAL_ERROR`. Found by the `La Casa Del Dolor` CI job (amd_debug) on #94148: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=e43941717e2178c119882d2b41b874d625613dd3&name_0=PR The fuzzer's statement was ```sql CREATE DATABASE d0 ON CLUSTER 'allnodes' ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/d0', 's1', 'd1'); ``` ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes. Reproduced on master `26.8.1.1` (debug+UBSan, `0c8a8f100913887455521757dba3e4ec0e0fbc67`) and on the `26.8.1.1833` official release build. ### How to reproduce Two servers sharing one Keeper, both listed in a cluster. `session_timeout_ms` is lowered only to shorten the wait from 90 s to 15 s; the bug does not depend on it. `node1` (also runs Keeper), `config.xml`: ```xml <clickhouse> <tcp_port>30301</tcp_port> <http_port>30341</http_port> <interserver_http_port>30351</interserver_http_port> <path>/tmp/chA/data/</path> <zookeeper> <node><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>9181</port></node> <session_timeout_ms>5000</session_timeout_ms> </zookeeper> <distributed_ddl><path>/clickhouse/task_queue/ddl</path></distributed_ddl> <remote_servers> <two><shard> <replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>30301</port></replica> <replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>30302</port></replica> </shard></two> </remote_servers> <keeper_server> <tcp_port>9181</tcp_port> <server_id>1</server_id> <log_storage_path>/tmp/chA/data/coordination/log</log_storage_path> <snapshot_storage_path>/tmp/chA/data/coordination/snapshots</snapshot_storage_path> <raft_configuration><server><id>1</id><hostname>127.0.0.1</hostname><port>9234</port></server></raft_configuration> </keeper_server> </clickhouse> ``` `node2`: the same file with `tcp_port` 30302, `http_port` 30342, `interserver_http_port` 30352, `path` `/tmp/chB/data/` and no `<keeper_server>` section. Then, on either node, a single query: ```sql CREATE DATABASE dtest ON CLUSTER 'two' ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/dtest', 's1', 'd1'); ``` It reports success on both hosts: ``` 127.0.0.1 30301 0 1 1 127.0.0.1 30302 0 0 0 ``` 15 s later (`3 * session_timeout_ms`) one of the two servers aborts. Both servers end up with the same database UUID, and the single replica znode is owned by whichever server took it over last: ``` :) SELECT name, value FROM system.zookeeper WHERE path='/clickhouse/databases/dtest/replicas'; s1|d1 host:30302:4d9f5111-fa11-4ec2-b3c8-d3fbeb5091c7 -- same UUID as node1's `dtest` ``` **Debug/sanitizer builds** — the losing server aborts with signal 6. Because the metadata is already on disk, it comes up on restart, serves queries for 15 s and aborts again: a permanent crash loop. **Release builds** (verified on `26.8.1.1833`) — no abort, but: - the losing DDL worker retries forever, logging every ~20 s: `<Error> DDLWorker(dtest): Error on initialization of dtest: Code: 49. DB::Exception: Ephemeral node ... still exists after 15s` - `CREATE TABLE dtest.x (c0 Int) ENGINE = Null` **hangs indefinitely on both nodes**, including with `distributed_ddl_task_timeout=3`; the database accepts no DDL at all, on either server - the two servers keep taking `host_id` from each other, so the replica's registered address flips between them - `system.clusters` for the database shows a single host, so `ON CLUSTER` routing for that database is broken too `SELECT` and `SHOW TABLES` still work, and the rest of the server is unaffected — the damage is confined to that database, but it is not recoverable without manual Keeper/metadata surgery. ### Expected behavior `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER` with a replica name already held by a *different, live* server should fail with `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS`, exactly like the non-distributed path already does, and in no case should a user-reachable misconfiguration produce a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. ### Suggested fix **Not by rejecting `ON CLUSTER`.** Every use of it with a `Replicated` database in this repo pairs it with macros — `ON CLUSTER 'cluster' ENGINE=Replicated('/clickhouse/path/','{shard}','{replica}')` in `test_backup_restore_on_cluster`, and the same shape in `test_external_cluster`, `test_refreshable_mat_view_replicated`, `02859_replicated_db_name_zookeeper.sh` and others — so it is the normal way to provision such a database, and banning it would be a breaking change. It would also close only one of the entrances: the precondition is *two hosts holding the same database UUID*, which `ON CLUSTER` produces, but so does an explicit `CREATE DATABASE x UUID '...' ENGINE = Replicated(...)` run on both hosts, and so does restoring one backup onto two hosts. **The UUID match is being read as "this is me" when it only means "this is the same database".** Making the takeover conditional on the replica not being live fixes that, in `DatabaseReplicated::initDatabaseReplica`, right after the existing `uuid_in_keeper != db_uuid` throw: ```cpp /// The UUID matching only means "same database", not "same server": ON CLUSTER hands every host /// one db_uuid, so two hosts given the same replica name land here. Taking the replica over while /// the other host is alive leaves both DDL workers fighting for `<replica_path>/active`. String active_id; if (current_zookeeper->tryGet(fs::path(replica_path) / "active", active_id)) { if (active_id.ends_with(REPLICA_UNSYNCED_MARKER)) active_id.resize(active_id.size() - strlen(REPLICA_UNSYNCED_MARKER)); if (active_id != toString(ServerUUID::get())) throw Exception( ErrorCodes::REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS, "Replica {} of shard {} of replicated database at {} is active on another server " "(host ID: '{}'). If the database is created with ON CLUSTER, use the {{shard}} and " "{{replica}} macros instead of literal names.", replica_name, shard_name, zookeeper_path, replica_host_id); } ``` Comparing against our own `ServerUUID` is what keeps the case the branch was written for working: the same server restarting finds its own stale ephemeral node and still takes the replica over. **One race remains, and it is why the severity matters too.** With `ON CLUSTER` both hosts run the CREATE simultaneously, so both can see no `active` node yet and pass the check above. The loser should then get an ordinary error rather than a `LOGICAL_ERROR`: ```cpp // ZooKeeper.h / ZooKeeper.cpp - the default keeps today's behaviour for the other callers void deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches(const std::string & path, std::function<bool(const std::string &)> condition, int error_code = ErrorCodes::LOGICAL_ERROR); ``` with `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS` passed from `DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:181`. That leaves the five other callers (`ReplicatedMergeTreeRestartingThread`, `StorageKafka2`, `DDLWorker` ×2) untouched — though the same argument arguably applies to them, since "another server holds my `is_active` node" is a misconfiguration rather than a broken internal invariant anywhere it occurs. Optionally, as a usability layer rather than part of the fix: reject `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER c ENGINE = Replicated(path, shard, replica)` on the initiator when neither name contains a macro and `c` has more than one host. That catches this shape before anything is written to Keeper, with a message saying what to write instead. Together that is roughly 20 lines, plus a test — two servers are needed, so `tests/integration/test_replicated_database/`, whose fixtures already provide the topology. ### Error message and/or stacktrace From the CI job (amd_debug, 26.8.1.1): ``` <Fatal> : Logical error: 'Ephemeral node /clickhouse/databases/d0/replicas/s1|d1/active still exists after 45s, probably it's owned by someone else. Either session_timeout_ms in client's config is different from server's config or it's a bug. Node data: '4463091c-64a0-4f2a-bc0b-e2eafcb97be1''. Stack trace: src/Common/Exception.cpp:66:5: DB::abortOnFailedAssertion(...) src/Common/Exception.cpp:115:13: DB::Exception::handleErrorCode(...) src/Common/Exception.cpp:171:19: DB::Exception::Exception(DB::Exception::MessageMasked&&, int, bool) src/Common/ZooKeeper/ZooKeeper.cpp:1462:19: zkutil::ZooKeeper::deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches(String const&, std::function<bool (String const&)>) src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:181:16: DB::DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker::initializeReplication() src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:121:13: DB::DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker::initializeMainThread() src/Interpreters/DDLWorker.cpp:1305:22: DB::DDLWorker::runMainThread() ``` Preceded by: ``` <Warning> ZooKeeper: Ephemeral node ('/clickhouse/databases/dtest/replicas/s1|d1/active') already exists but it isn't owned by us. Will wait until it disappears ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Four closed issues carry the same error string, none of them with this cause — listed so triage does not close this as a duplicate of one of them: - #68570 — same LOGICAL_ERROR in `DatabaseReplicated`, from a stress run. Closed 2025-02-21 by #76554, which changed only `tests/queries/0_stateless/02447_drop_database_replica.sh`: there a fault-injected `serverUUID()` failure wrote an **empty** node value. No server-side change. - #70126 — the same, `Node data: ''` again, closed 2024-09-30 without a server-side change. - #86434 — contention on `/clickhouse/task_queue/replicas/localhost:9000/active`, i.e. the distributed-DDL queue rather than a `Replicated` database replica, caused by every host being configured as `localhost`. Related to #81395. - #86586 — the same message during a Kubernetes rolling upgrade, closed as a duplicate of #86434. Here the node value is a well-formed `ServerUUID` belonging to a **live peer**, the path is a `Replicated` database's own replica, and no fault injection is involved: one `CREATE DATABASE` reproduces it deterministically. The distinguishing mechanism is that `ON CLUSTER` gives both hosts one database UUID, which is what makes the existing `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS` check pass them through.

signals.title: minmax/set skip index on mortonEncode(x,y): any query on x or y throws Code 10
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table with `INDEX i mortonEncode(x, y) TYPE minmax` (or `TYPE set(N)`, or `hilbertEncode`) accepts `CREATE` and `INSERT`, but every `SELECT` whose `WHERE` mentions `x` or `y` fails with `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column x in block. There are only columns: mortonEncode(x, y). (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. Queries on the curve expression itself (`WHERE mortonEncode(x,y) > 100`) still work, as does the same query with `use_skip_indexes = 0` or `analyze_index_with_space_filling_curves = 0`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp:3108`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp#L3108) assumes every space-filling-curve argument name is present in the key expression's sample block. That holds for the primary-key and partition-key expressions (which keep their input columns) but not for a skip-index expression, whose sample block contains only the index expression results. `getAllSpaceFillingCurves` registers the curve without checking that its arguments are resolvable in that sample block. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeIndexMinMax::createIndexCondition` -> `buildCondition` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexMinMax.cpp:201`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexMinMax.cpp#L201)) builds `KeyCondition{filter_dag, context, index.column_names, index.expression}`. The constructor calls `getAllSpaceFillingCurves`, where the curve node IS the index column, so the `key_columns.find` guard added by this PR succeeds and the curve is registered with `arguments = {x, y}`. Later, `extractAtomFromTree` -> `isKeyPossiblyWrappedByMonotonicFunctions` -> `isKeyPossiblyWrappedByMonotonicFunctionsImpl` matches the atom column `x` against `curve.arguments` and calls `sample_block.getByName("x")` at [`src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp:3108`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp#L3108). For a skip index, `sample_block = info.key_expr->getSampleBlock()` (KeyCondition.cpp:3075) is the index sample block, which holds only `mortonEncode(x, y)` - the source columns are projected out. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp:3108`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp#L3108) — curve-argument branch of isKeyPossiblyWrappedByMonotonicFunctionsImpl - unguarded sample_block.getByName(name) - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp:1414`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp#L1414) — getAllSpaceFillingCurves registers the curve without checking that its argument names exist in info.key_expr->getSampleBlock() - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexMinMax.cpp:201`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexMinMax.cpp#L201) — buildCondition passes index.column_names + index.expression, whose sample block omits the source columns - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/57516b9fe4de3/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp#L374) — same construction for TYPE set(N) - same failure **Impact:** A table whose DDL ClickHouse accepted becomes effectively unreadable: any predicate on a column that is an argument of the indexed curve aborts the query during query-plan optimization. Same user-visible shape as the bug this PR fixes (create + insert succeed, reads fail), reached through the skip-index construction site the PR description names as one of the three it covers. Workarounds are `SETTINGS analyze_index_with_space_filling_curves = 0` or `use_skip_indexes = 0` per query, or dropping the index. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `57516b9fe4de3`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/ab664c4c-8f38-4973-8780-589551b21d47) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: a minmax/set skip index over a space-filling curve must not break queries on the curve's arguments. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_curve_minmax_idx; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_curve_set_idx; CREATE TABLE t_curve_minmax_idx (x UInt32, y UInt32, INDEX i mortonEncode(x, y) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t_curve_minmax_idx SELECT number % 100, number % 37 FROM numbers(1000); SELECT count() FROM t_curve_minmax_idx WHERE x = 5; SELECT count() FROM t_curve_minmax_idx WHERE x >= 10 AND x <= 20 AND y >= 5 AND y <= 15; CREATE TABLE t_curve_set_idx (x UInt32, y UInt32, INDEX i hilbertEncode(x, y) TYPE set(100) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t_curve_set_idx SELECT number % 100, number % 37 FROM numbers(1000); SELECT count() FROM t_curve_set_idx WHERE y = 5; DROP TABLE t_curve_minmax_idx; DROP TABLE t_curve_set_idx; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 10 33 27 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` [1 / 1] 05028_space_filling_curve_skip_index_arg: [ FAIL ] 0.09 sec. Reason: return code: 10 Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column x in block. There are only columns: mortonEncode(x, y). (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (version 26.8.1.1841 (official build)) (query 5, line 9) (in query: SELECT count() FROM t_curve_minmax_idx WHERE x = 5;), Stack trace: 4. DB::Block::getPositionByName(String const ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `getAllSpaceFillingCurves`, alongside the new `key_columns.find` guard, also require that every curve argument is resolvable in the key expression's sample block before registering the curve - e.g. treat `!info.key_expr->getSampleBlock().has(child->result_name)` the same way a non-`INPUT` child is treated (clear `curve.arguments` and break). That keeps primary-key and partition-key pruning untouched (their sample blocks contain the source columns) and turns the skip-index case into a plain no-op instead of an exception. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/ManifestFilesPruning.cpp:137` constructs `KeyCondition(inverted_dag, context, {name_and_type->name}, expression)` with a single column name and an arbitrary expression; if that expression can ever contain a curve whose arguments are projected out, it hits the same line. I could not construct an Iceberg table with a space-filling-curve min/max expression in this environment, so it is untested. Found during automated review of [PR #114233](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114233). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114233_001` </details> cc @groeneai @al13n321 (from #114233)

signals.title: Early short-circuit guard calls getResultType on IN's subquery arg: UNSUPPORTED_METHOD
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With `enable_function_early_short_circuit = 1`, a valid query whose decided `and`/`or` has an `IN`/`NOT IN`/`GLOBAL IN` argument over a bare `SELECT count()` subquery fails with `Code: 1 ... Method getResultType is supported only for correlated query node. (UNSUPPORTED_METHOD)`. The same query returns a result with the setting off.** - **Root cause:** resolveFunction.cpp:287 assumes every argument of a resolved `FunctionNode` has a result type. Set-producing arguments (`QueryNode`/`UnionNode` under `in`-family functions) do not. The unguarded call sits outside the fallback try/catch, so instead of declining the optimization the analyzer aborts the whole query. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `QueryAnalyzer::resolveFunction` (resolveFunction.cpp:1186-1188) computes `post_resolution_is_safe` OUTSIDE the try/catch at :1166-1184 -> `hasFunctionNotSuitableForEarlyShortCircuit` walks the resolved clone -> for the resolved `in` node it builds `DataTypesWithConstInfo` at :287 by calling `argument->getResultType()` on every argument -> `in`'s second argument is still a `QueryNode` -> `QueryNode::getResultType` throws `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD` (QueryNode.cpp:172). Confirmed by server stack trace frames 4-8. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:287`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/342d96b5c63d3/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L287) — hasFunctionNotSuitableForEarlyShortCircuit: getResultType on every argument of a resolved function - [`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:1186`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/342d96b5c63d3/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L1186) — post_resolution_is_safe computed outside the try/catch that is meant to make speculative analysis fall back - [`src/Analyzer/QueryNode.cpp:172`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/342d96b5c63d3/src/Analyzer/QueryNode.cpp#L172) — QueryNode::getResultType throws UNSUPPORTED_METHOD for a non-correlated query node **Impact:** Users who enable `enable_function_early_short_circuit` get a hard failure with an internal-sounding error on legitimate SQL. There is no workaround other than turning the setting back off or rewriting the query. Because the setting is a plain analyzer toggle, enabling it globally (or via a profile) breaks any query of the shape `<decided constant> OR/AND (expr IN (SELECT count() FROM <local table>))`. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `342d96b5c63d3`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/25b6a847-621d-4c4c-8042-1957686d7a41) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: a decided AND/OR whose other branch is an IN subquery must still resolve. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_05028; CREATE TABLE t_05028 (x UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x; INSERT INTO t_05028 VALUES (1); SET enable_function_early_short_circuit = 1; SELECT 1 OR (1 IN (SELECT count() FROM t_05028)); SELECT 0 AND (1 IN (SELECT count() FROM t_05028)); SELECT 1 OR (1 NOT IN (SELECT count() FROM t_05028)); DROP TABLE t_05028; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 0 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 1. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:19010. DB::Exception: Method getResultType is supported only for correlated query node. (UNSUPPORTED_METHOD) (query: SELECT 1 OR (1 IN (SELECT count() FROM t_05028));) Having 1 errors! 0 tests passed. ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Skip arguments without a result type when building `DataTypesWithConstInfo` (bail out with `return true` for any argument whose node type is `QUERY`/`UNION`), and move the `post_resolution_is_safe` computation inside the existing try/catch so any unexpected throw degrades to a fallback instead of failing the query. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `getResultType`-on-every-argument pattern would also fire for any future resolved function that keeps a non-expression node as an argument; only the `in` family is reachable today (UNION arguments are rejected earlier by `hasScopeDependentNodesForEarlyShortCircuit`). Found during automated review of [PR #83505](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/83505). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr83505_001` </details> cc @fhw12345 @novikd @alexey-milovidov (from #83505)

signals.title: Support UPDATE of sorting/partition key columns via a server-side insert-then-delete
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Use case Today `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE` and lightweight `UPDATE` both refuse any column that participates in the sorting key, the primary key, the partition key, or the `sign`/`version` columns: ``` DB::Exception: Cannot UPDATE key column `x`. (CANNOT_UPDATE_COLUMN) ``` The common real-world need is not "update the key at scale", it is a one-off correction or backfill of a value that happens to be part of `ORDER BY` — a mis-ingested `tenant_id`, a device id that was recorded wrong for a range of rows, a category that has to be re-mapped after a schema decision changed. These are rare, bounded, and not latency-sensitive. The only options right now are to rebuild the affected data by hand (`INSERT INTO ... SELECT` into a new table, or `INSERT` the corrected rows and then `DELETE` the originals, keeping the two consistent yourself), or to drop and reload a partition. Both are error-prone precisely because the user has to get the atomicity right, which is the part the server is in a much better position to handle. I want to be upfront that this cannot be made cheap. It is a full rewrite of the affected rows and it temporarily stores them twice. The value here is that the operation becomes *possible and safe*, not that it becomes fast. ### Describe the solution you'd like Rather than trying to make mutations able to update key columns in place, implement `UPDATE` on key columns as a **server-side insert-then-delete**: 1. Read the rows matching the `WHERE` clause. 2. Apply the assignments. 3. Write the modified rows back through the ordinary insert path. 4. Retire the original rows with a lightweight delete. The appeal is that ClickHouse already has both halves, and they already solve the two hard problems by construction: * `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPart` sorts each block by the sorting key (`stableGetPermutation`), so the resulting parts are correctly ordered no matter how the key values changed. * `MergeTreeDataWriter::splitBlockIntoParts` routes rows to the partition their new key values actually belong to, so a changed partition key lands in the right place instead of staying in the wrong part. * `_row_exists` retires the originals without rewriting the source parts. So the primary index, the part min/max key bounds, partition pruning and merge inputs all stay correct without any new machinery for maintaining sort order. The engineering that remains is real but bounded and well-understood: * **Atomicity** — a reader must not observe both the old and the new copy of a row, nor neither. This is the core of the work. * **Replication ordering** — the insert and the delete have to reach replicas as one logical step. * **`ReplacingMergeTree` / deduplication** — the new rows must not be collapsed against, or deduplicated away by, the originals. * Behaviour when the `UPDATE` touches both key and non-key columns (the whole row is rewritten either way, so this is mostly a question of which path is chosen). Two consequences worth stating in advance, because they are user-visible: * `_part_offset` and `_block_number` change for the affected rows. Anything that depends on them (including patch parts for the same rows) has to account for that. * Cost is proportional to the rows matched by `WHERE`, not to the columns assigned — this is a row rewrite, not a column rewrite. A reasonable shape would be to keep the current error by default and put this behind an explicit setting, so nobody pays for it accidentally. ### Describe alternatives you've considered **Re-sorting the part inside the mutation.** `MutateTask` contains no sorting at all today — it streams a part's rows through in stored order and writes them back, and it never recomputes the partition id. Adding a sort there would handle the sorting key, but: * it would not help the partition key at all, since the row has to physically move to a different part in a different partition, while a mutation is 1 source part → 1 result part with the same partition id; * it would break the "mutations preserve row order" invariant that patch parts rely on — v2 patches address rows by `(_block_number, _block_offset)` and are sorted by the storage sorting-key prefix (see `getEffectivePatchSortingKeySize`) precisely so that `RangesInPatchParts` can locate rows by key range. If a key value changes, a patch's key no longer matches its target. **Just lifting the check.** This is not viable: nothing anywhere validates that a part is sorted (`checkDataPart` does not), so violating the invariant is silent wrong results rather than an error. #78655 is a live example of the same failure mode arriving through a different door — a rollup `TTL ... GROUP BY ... SET` legitimately changes a partition-key column, and afterwards partition pruning filters out the rows that were rolled up, so `SELECT ... WHERE <partition expr>` silently returns nothing. Related: #99647 refuses materializing columns used in sort key expressions for the same underlying reason. **Leaving it to the user.** This is the status quo. It works, but the atomicity is exactly the part that is easy to get wrong and that the server could do properly. ### Additional context Where the restriction lives, as of 26.8: * `validateUpdateColumns` in `src/Interpreters/MutationsInterpreter.cpp` raises `CANNOT_UPDATE_COLUMN`. * The forbidden set comes from `getKeyColumns` in the same file, and is broader than the documentation sentence "It isn't possible to update columns that are part of the primary or sorting key" suggests — it is partition key columns ∪ sorting key columns ∪ `sign` ∪ `version`. * Lightweight `UPDATE` is subject to the same rule, because `MergeTreeData::updateLightweightImpl` builds a `MutationsInterpreter` too. The `sign`/`version` case is worth separating from the other two. Those columns decide what a `Collapsing`/`Replacing`/`VersionedCollapsing` merge collapses, so changing them changes row identity rather than row content. It may well be right to keep rejecting those even if sorting-key and partition-key updates become possible. I am happy to prototype this if the direction seems acceptable — including the narrower first step of proving out what the insert-then-delete path breaks in the existing test suite before any of the atomicity work.

signals.title: _sample_factor pinned to 1 only in the materialized arm; on-the-fly arm still samples
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A pending mutation whose expression names `_sample_factor` is evaluated with the *reading query's* sample factor when `apply_mutations_on_fly = 1`, but with the constant 1 once materialized. `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE _sample_factor > 1` - a no-op after materialization - makes `SELECT count() FROM t SAMPLE 0.5` return 0 while the mutation is pending and 100 after it lands.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSequentialSource.cpp:339`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/68d548f854a5b/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSequentialSource.cpp#L339) fixes only the materialized arm. The on-the-fly arm reuses the SELECT's `shared_virtual_fields`, so the mutation predicate sees the query's `SAMPLE` factor instead of the constant the PR chose. The PR's stated justification - 'no `SAMPLE` clause reaches this path' - holds for the sequential source but not for the on-the-fly evaluation of the same mutation. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** Two independent evaluations of the same mutation expression: the materialized arm goes `MutationsInterpreter.cpp:2416` -> `createMergeTreeSequentialSource` -> `MergeTreeSequentialSource.cpp:339`, which now pins 1.0. The on-the-fly arm goes `MergeTreeData.cpp:12663` (`need_data_mutations = apply_mutations_on_fly`) -> `ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4747`, which publishes `result.sampling.used_sample_factor`, copied into every read task at `MergeTreeReadPoolBase.cpp:280` and looked up at `IMergeTreeReader.cpp:154`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSequentialSource.cpp:339`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/68d548f854a5b/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSequentialSource.cpp#L339) — materialized arm pins _sample_factor to 1.0 - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4747`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/68d548f854a5b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp#L4747) — on-the-fly arm publishes the reading query's used_sample_factor - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeReadPoolBase.cpp:280`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/68d548f854a5b/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeReadPoolBase.cpp#L280) — shared_virtual_fields copied into every read task, reaching the on-the-fly mutation steps **Impact:** With `apply_mutations_on_fly = 1`, a sampled read of a table with a pending `_sample_factor` mutation returns data that disagrees with the same read after the mutation materializes - and, on a replicated table, with a replica that has already materialized it. In the DELETE shape above every row disappears from the sampled query. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `68d548f854a5b`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test that a pending mutation referencing _sample_factor does not change what a sampled query sees. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_otf_sf; CREATE TABLE t_otf_sf (c0 UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY c0 SAMPLE BY c0; INSERT INTO t_otf_sf SELECT number FROM numbers(100); SYSTEM STOP MERGES t_otf_sf; SET mutations_sync = 0; -- _sample_factor is 1 in a mutation, so this deletes nothing. ALTER TABLE t_otf_sf DELETE WHERE _sample_factor > 1; SELECT 'pending plain', count() FROM t_otf_sf SETTINGS apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; SELECT 'pending sampled', count() FROM t_otf_sf SAMPLE 0.5 SETTINGS apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; SYSTEM START MERGES t_otf_sf; SET mutations_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_otf_sf DELETE WHERE 0; SELECT 'materialized plain', count() FROM t_otf_sf; SELECT 'materialized sampled', count() FROM t_otf_sf SAMPLE 0.5; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_otf_sf; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` pending plain 100 pending sampled 100 materialized plain 100 materialized sampled 100 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` pending plain 100 pending sampled 0 materialized plain 100 materialized sampled 100 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Pin `_sample_factor` to 1.0 for the mutation steps in the on-the-fly path as well (the `need_data_mutations` branch reached from `MergeTreeData.cpp:12663`), so both arms agree; alternatively reject `_sample_factor` in mutation expressions at analysis time, which is what the guard this PR removed did. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `_table` and `_database` remain unseeded in the sequential source, so a mutation naming them still fails per part forever - pre-existing, and the PR's test pins the current behaviour. Found during automated review of [PR #109813](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109813). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109813_001` </details> cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov (from #109813)

signals.title: Stress tests fail to restart the server after `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata`: the test's deliberately malformed `KeeperMap` metadata in ZooKeeper is fatal at startup
signals.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115642 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115198 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 ### Describe what's wrong Stress test jobs fail with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` when the run kills the server while `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata` (added in #115642, merged 2026-08-21) is inside its corruption window. The test deliberately rewrites the `metadata` znode of the still-attached table `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata` to the malformed spelling `primary key: key;\n` in order to assert that a new `CREATE` on the same path is rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and only later repairs the znode and drops the tables. If the server is killed inside that window, the post-stress restart fails: ``` DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table test_7.05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata' failed: Code: 27. DB::Exception: Invalid KeeperMap metadata format version or columns definition in ZK: primary key: key; ``` Observed in #115036, `Stress test (arm_release)`, 2026-08-21 23:24 UTC: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=1b9be4e90ec59d43356e230f4442cbeb005cec87&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 This is the same kill-unsafe test pattern as #115198 (`04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`): a `no-stress` tag is not supported by design ("stress tests must be able to run every test"), so a test must never hold on-disk or in-ZooKeeper state that a concurrently killed-and-restarted server cannot load. There is also the same server-side asymmetry: the running server tolerates the malformed znode for the already-attached table, but the startup load path hard-fails the whole table instead of quarantining it. ### How to reproduce * Run `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata`, kill the server after the `INSERT INTO system.zookeeper ... 'primary key: key;\n'` step (before the final repair/`DROP`), and start the server again — loading the table fails with error 27 while the same state was tolerated before the kill. * In CI: any stress job that kills the server inside that window. No fiddle link: requires killing and restarting the server around ZooKeeper state, which fiddle cannot do.
