signals.title: Perf test measures nothing: 5 of 6 queries plan identically with the pass on/off
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml` is the PR's only performance evidence, but five of its six queries produce byte-identical query plans with `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions` set to 1 and 0 at default settings — including the query its own comment labels "the shape from issue #82378".** - **Root cause:** The performance test declares no `<settings>` and therefore runs with `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1`, which eliminates the function nodes the new pass keys on. The PR's stateless test pins the setting to 0 for exactly this reason; the performance test does not. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** Perf tests run with server defaults plus only the XML's `<settings>` block ([`tests/performance/scripts/perf.py:442-449`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/tests/performance/scripts/perf.py#L442-L449), :712-713); this XML has none. `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` (default 1) rewrites `length(s)` to `s.size`, `notEmpty(s)` to `s.size != 0` and `length(arr)` to `arr.size0` in the analyzer, so no `length`/`empty`/`notEmpty` FUNCTION node survives for `collectVolumeReducingFunctionsReplacingTheirArgument` (pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:218-238) to find. Independently, `SELECT length(arr) ... ORDER BY key` can never be pushed at all: `isSupportedArgumentType` (pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:42-43) accepts only `String`/`FixedString`. **Affected locations:** - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:24 — flagship #82378 query — plan identical with the setting on and off - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:20 — `length(arr)` — Array is excluded by design, can never be pushed - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:3 — header comment claims push below `Limit`, but `canPushBelowStep` accepts only Sorting and Filter - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:42`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp#L42) — isSupportedArgumentType restricts to String/FixedString - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:146`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp#L146) — canPushBelowStep accepts SortingStep and FilterStep only **Impact:** The PR is labelled `pr-performance` and its only performance evidence cannot move. If a later change silently disables `tryPushDownVolumeReducingFunction`, five of the six queries stay green because their plans never depended on it. The one query that does differ (`lengthUTF8(s) ... ORDER BY key LIMIT 10`) exercises the `tryExecuteFunctionsAfterSorting` pinning change, not the new pass. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `a77a83b02c0de`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/2425d123-6bd7-42f4-841f-8e081def2641) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Repro: the perf test's queries plan identically with the optimization on and off. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vrf; CREATE TABLE vrf (key UInt64, s String, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO vrf SELECT number, randomPrintableASCII(100), range(number % 32) FROM numbers(1000); -- 1 = plans identical (perf query measures nothing), 0 = plans differ. SELECT ( SELECT groupArray(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN header = 1, actions = 1, description = 1, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 1) ) = ( SELECT groupArray(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN header = 1, actions = 1, description = 1, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 0) ); -- Positive control: with the subcolumn rewrite off, the pass fires. SELECT countIf(explain LIKE '%[volume-reducing functions]%') > 0 FROM (EXPLAIN description = 1, actions = 0, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 1, optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 0); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vrf; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` PLAN DIFFERS for all six perf-test queries at the settings the perf runner uses, i.e. every measured query exercises the pass it is named after. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key PLAN DIFFERS :: SELECT lengthUTF8(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key LIMIT 10 IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(arr) FROM vrf ORDER BY key IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s) FROM vrf WHERE key % 3 = 0 ORDER BY key IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s), empty(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key -- p ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Add `<settings><optimize_functions_to_subcolumns>0</optimize_functions_to_subcolumns></settings>` to the XML (see tests/performance/map_subcolumns_prewhere.xml:55 for the inline-settings idiom), or switch the wide column to `FixedString`, which the subcolumn rewrite leaves alone. Drop or re-target `SELECT length(arr) ...` — `Array` is excluded by `isSupportedArgumentType`. Fix the header comment at line 3 (`Limit` is not a push-below target) and the `String / Array` wording at line 4. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same reachability caveat applies to the PR description's claim about `SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s)`: at default settings that shape reads only `s.size` and is unaffected by this PR. Found during automated review of [PR #106199](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106199). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr106199_001` </details> cc @fastio @novikd @alexey-milovidov (from #106199)

signals.title: MATERIALIZE PROJECTION is a no-op after MODIFY PROJECTION, contrary to PR docs
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **After `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY PROJECTION p ... WITH SETTINGS (index_granularity = 128)`, the documented rebuild path `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION p` completes successfully (mutation `is_done = 1`, part version bumped) but the projection part keeps the OLD granularity - 11 marks instead of 79. A merge (`OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`) on the same data produces 79.** - **Root cause:** `MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1350` treats presence of the projection in the part as proof it is up to date. That was correct before this PR (a projection definition could never change), but this PR makes the definition mutable, so 'present' no longer implies 'built with the current settings'. The PR nevertheless states the opposite in three places: `AlterCommands.cpp:1102` ('`MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` forces a rebuild'), `docs/reference/statements/alter/projection.mdx:334` ('To rebuild existing parts with the new settings, run MATERIALIZE PROJECTION'), and the PR description. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ALTER ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` -> `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` ([`src/Interpreters/MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1350`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Interpreters/MutationsInterpreter.cpp#L1350)) adds the projection to `materialized_projections` only when the source part does NOT already have it -> `MutateTask` `getProjectionsToRecalculate` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MutateTask.cpp:1102`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Storages/MergeTree/MutateTask.cpp#L1102)) therefore leaves the projection out of `projections_to_recalc` -> the stale projection is carried over unchanged. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/AlterCommands.cpp:1102`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Storages/AlterCommands.cpp#L1102) — comment added by this PR claiming MATERIALIZE PROJECTION forces a rebuild - [`src/Interpreters/MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1350`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Interpreters/MutationsInterpreter.cpp#L1350) — MATERIALIZE PROJECTION skipped when the part already has the projection - docs/reference/statements/alter/projection.mdx:334 — docs added by this PR pointing users at MATERIALIZE PROJECTION to rebuild existing parts **Impact:** The only rebuild path the PR documents silently does nothing: the ALTER succeeds, a mutation is recorded as done, and the projection parts keep the old settings forever. Users who lower `index_granularity` on a projection of a large table and then run `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` will believe the change was applied. The only working path is `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL` (`OPTIMIZE ... FINAL DEDUPLICATE` is refused on tables with projections), which the docs do not mention. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `a77a83b02c0de`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/312cd816-31d2-466a-9f25-137ecb9c6572) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: MATERIALIZE PROJECTION after MODIFY PROJECTION rebuilds existing parts with the new projection settings. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_modify_projection_materialize; CREATE TABLE t_modify_projection_materialize ( k UInt64, v UInt64, PROJECTION p (SELECT v ORDER BY v) WITH SETTINGS (index_granularity = 1024) ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192, index_granularity_bytes = 10485760; INSERT INTO t_modify_projection_materialize SELECT number, number * 2 FROM numbers(10000); ALTER TABLE t_modify_projection_materialize MODIFY PROJECTION p (SELECT v ORDER BY v) WITH SETTINGS (index_granularity = 128); SELECT '-- MATERIALIZE PROJECTION rebuilds the projection with the new granularity'; ALTER TABLE t_modify_projection_materialize MATERIALIZE PROJECTION p SETTINGS mutations_sync = 1; SELECT name, rows, marks FROM system.projection_parts WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_modify_projection_materialize' AND active ORDER BY parent_name; SELECT '-- control: a merge rebuilds it'; OPTIMIZE TABLE t_modify_projection_materialize FINAL; SELECT name, rows, marks FROM system.projection_parts WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_modify_projection_materialize' AND active ORDER BY parent_name; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_modify_projection_materialize; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` -- MATERIALIZE PROJECTION rebuilds the projection with the new granularity p 10000 79 -- control: a merge rebuilds it p 10000 79 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` -- MATERIALIZE PROJECTION rebuilds the projection with the new granularity p 10000 11 -- control: a merge rebuilds it p 10000 79 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Either (a) make `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` rebuild when the part's projection is stale - e.g. drop the `!source.hasProjection(...)` short-circuit for an explicitly named projection, or compare the part's stored projection metadata against the current definition; or (b) correct `docs/.../projection.mdx:334`, the `AlterCommands.cpp:1102` comment and the PR description to say that only a merge (`OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`) applies the new settings to existing parts. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - If option (a) is taken, note that `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` on a part that already has a valid projection would then always rewrite it - a behavior change for existing users who use the command as a repair tool. Found during automated review of [PR #113343](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113343). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr113343_001` </details> cc @diegomestre2 @Michicosun (from #113343)

signals.title: Certain functions can be pushed up in the query pipeline into WHERE if they reduce data size
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the situation ```sql CREATE TABLE test (s String) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO test SELECT rand() % 100 = 12 ? '' : randomString(100) FROM numbers_mt(100000000); ``` ```sql SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE length(s) > 0; -- 0.027 sec. SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s); -- 0.765 sec. SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE s != ''; -- 0.719 sec. ``` The reason for this difference in performance is the following: SELECT expression needs to calculate `length(s)`. If this expression is not already available after `WHERE`, it will request the source column, `s`, be present in the pipeline after filtering. This will lead to filtering `s` and copying the values that passed the filter. However, the function `length` does not throw exceptions, is easy to calculate, and it reduces the data volume, so it will be beneficial to calculate it early in the pipeline if its source column is not needed later in the pipeline. Essentially, we can "push up" the calculation of `length(s)` before filtering, so that we will not need to filter its argument, `s`, which was needed only for the calculation of this function. I'd expect it for a few functions, `length`, `empty`, `notEmpty`, comparisons with empty strings or arrays, and probably even `substring`. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? . ### How to reproduce . ### Expected performance _No response_ ### Additional context Don't be confused with "optimization for subcolumns" and "lazy reading," which are other optimizations. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #106199 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1857` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: short-circuit in SELECT OR/AND clause
signals.text: ### Describe the situation Hi, ClickHouse developers, please consider such queries: ```sql SELECT TRUE OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1; SELECT FALSE AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1; ``` For the first query, there are two conditions in the `WHERE` clause, connected by `OR`, which means that if any one of the conditions is met, it is `TRUE`. Therefore, when we calculate two conditions, if we calculate one of the conditions to be `TRUE`, we can short-circuit the `OR` expressions, which can avoid unnecessary calculations. For the Second query, similarly, if we calculate one of the conditions to be `FALSE`, we can short-circuit the `AND` expressions. However, ClickHouse does not short-circuit to optimize such queries. Especially, short-circuiting is necessary when the computation of the condition is expensive. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? I ran the following case on the last two versions: 25.4.2 and 25.5.1: ### How to reproduce ```sql SET default_table_engine = 'Log'; CREATE DATABASE test; USE test; CREATE TABLE t0(c0 Int64); INSERT INTO t0 SELECT * FROM generate_series(1, 1000000000);-- 1 billion rows SELECT TRUE OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1 AS bool; ┌─bool─┐ 1. │ true │ └──────┘ 1 row in set. Elapsed: 2.896 sec. Processed 1.00 billion rows, 8.00 GB (345.30 million rows/s., 2.76 GB/s.) Peak memory usage: 63.68 MiB. SELECT FALSE AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1 AS bool; ┌─bool──┐ 1. │ false │ └───────┘ 1 row in set. Elapsed: 2.918 sec. Processed 1.00 billion rows, 8.00 GB (342.70 million rows/s., 2.74 GB/s.) Peak memory usage: 63.87 MiB. ```` Moreover, If there is a subquery in the `EXPLAIN` statement, the `EXPLAIN` statement will performs actual execution. ```sql EXPLAIN SELECT TRUE OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1 AS bool; ┌─explain─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 1. │ Expression ((Project names + (Projection + Change column names to column identifiers))) │ 2. │ ReadFromStorage (SystemOne) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 2 rows in set. Elapsed: 2.855 sec. Processed 1.00 billion rows, 8.00 GB (350.30 million rows/s., 2.80 GB/s.) Peak memory usage: 63.83 MiB. EXPLAIN SELECT FALSE AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t0)>1 AS bool; ┌─explain─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 1. │ Expression ((Project names + (Projection + Change column names to column identifiers))) │ 2. │ ReadFromStorage (SystemOne) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 2 rows in set. Elapsed: 3.059 sec. Processed 1.00 billion rows, 8.00 GB (326.87 million rows/s., 2.61 GB/s.) Peak memory usage: 63.78 MiB. ``` <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #83505 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1856` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: SQL interface for creating clusters
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse Inc. ### Use case In some deployment modes, it is not possible to change a configuration file to fill in the `<remote_servers>` section, yet it is still desirable to be able to define a cluster for use with a Distributed table. ### Describe the solution you'd like Create a new entity called `CLUSTER`, which is in fact a collection of named collections. Each named collection would represent a shard. Overall it would look like ``` CREATE NAMED COLLECTION shard1 AS user = 'Nikita', password = 'p@s$w0rd', replicas = 'hostname1:9000|hostname2:9000|hostname3:9000', weight = 42, internal_replication=false; CREATE NAMED COLLECTION shard2 AS user = 'default', password = 'qwerty123', replicas = 'hostname4:9000|hostname5:9000|hostname6:9000', weight = 1, internal_replication=false; CREATE CLUSTER remote_cluster (shard1, shard2); ``` After that it will be available for use in the distributed table. Funnily it seems possble to support a command like `CREATE CLUSTER cluster ON CLUSTER another_cluster`

signals.title: Release pull request for branch 26.3
signals.text: This PullRequest is a part of ClickHouse release cycle. It is used by CI system only. signals.title: Add assertions in IColumn::mutate to verify deep unique ownership of sub-columns
signals.text: Investigation for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/99920 This is a draft PR with diagnostic assertions to help find a COW violation bug where columns stored in `HashJoin` have their `allocatedBytes()` change because internal sub-columns are modified by someone who treats immutable columns as mutable. ## What was found The bug manifests as `data->allocated_size != debug_allocated_size` exception in debug builds. Investigation narrowed it down to: 1. **Removing the single-chunk optimization** in `Squashing.cpp:70-72` fixes the bug — this optimization passes chunks through without `IColumn::mutate`, so columns remain shared with Memory engine blocks 2. The **modification happens between** `addBlockToJoin` calls — during pipeline processing of the next chunk 3. The mutation is a **reallocation** (reserve/grow), not a data write — `protect()` (mprotect) doesn't catch it 4. The assertions in this PR (`IColumn::mutate` deep ownership check) **do NOT fire** — meaning the mutation happens outside the `IColumn::mutate` path entirely. Someone treats an immutable column as mutable without going through `mutate`. ## Reproducer The test `04049_fix_hashjoin_shared_column_allocated_size` reproduces the exception in debug builds. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100185&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100185](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100185+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Disable read-in-order when primary key selectivity is poor
signals.text: When the WHERE clause cannot use the primary key effectively (e.g., `LIKE '%...'`), the `optimize_read_in_order` optimization kills parallelism: each part is read by a single stream instead of many. This can make `ORDER BY` queries 4x slower than the same query without `ORDER BY`. Example on a 2.5B row table with `ORDER BY path` and `WHERE path LIKE '%stderr.log'`: - Without ORDER BY: ~9.5s - With ORDER BY (read-in-order): ~40s - With `optimize_read_in_order = 0`: ~9.6s The fix adds a runtime check in `ReadFromMergeTree::spreadMarkRanges`: if the primary key index selected more than a configurable fraction of all granules and there is no LIMIT, we fall back to parallel reading with per-stream `PartialSortingTransform` + `MergeSortingTransform`, so the output is still sorted as the `SortingStep` above expects. New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` controls the threshold. The default is 1.0, which preserves the previous behavior (never disable read-in-order based on primary key selectivity): the heuristic is opt-in until the default threshold is tuned against the performance report. Set it below 1.0 (e.g. 0.5) to enable the guard. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` that can disable the read-in-order optimization when the primary key selectivity is poor (more than the given fraction of granules selected), falling back to parallel reading with sorting. This avoids severe parallelism loss for queries like `SELECT ... WHERE path LIKE '%...' ORDER BY path`. The default 1.0 preserves the previous behavior; set a lower value (e.g. 0.5) to enable the heuristic. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` (Float, default 1.0): maximum ratio of selected to total primary key granules for `optimize_read_in_order` to stay enabled. When the ratio exceeds this value, read-in-order is disabled in favor of parallel reading with per-stream sorting. The default 1.0 preserves the old behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add small-parts batching settings to SimpleMergeSelector
signals.text: Add three new MergeTree settings that let users reduce the number of merge operations under rapid small-part insertion. When all parts in a candidate merge range are small, fresh, and fewer than a configurable minimum count, the merge is rejected — forcing the system to accumulate more parts before merging. Settings: - `merge_selector_small_parts_threshold` (default 10 MB) — size ceiling for "small" parts - `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count` (default 0 = disabled) — minimum part count required - `merge_selector_small_parts_max_age` (default 600 s) — age safety valve Disabled by default. Simulation test with 200 × 1 MB parts at 1 insert/s shows merge count drops from 42 to 26 (−38%) with negligible WA change. ### Rationale Merging a small number of small parts is wasteful: the I/O cost is high relative to the modest read-performance improvement. Waiting for more small parts to accumulate produces wider merges that achieve the same part-count reduction at lower total write amplification. Cassandra STCS applies the same idea: it requires at least `min_threshold` (default 4) similar-sized SSTables before triggering compaction, and groups SSTables below `min_sstable_size` (default 50 MB) together. The gate is *monotone on the candidate set*: it only rejects candidate ranges, it never introduces a new one. So every range the selector emits with the gate enabled is a range it could also emit with the gate disabled — the gate cannot invent a merge shape, in particular it cannot steer the selector toward merging large dissimilar-sized parts. There is exactly one deliberate exception. The default-on fullness heuristic (`merge_selector_enable_heuristic_to_lower_max_parts_to_merge_at_once`) can lower the effective `max_parts_to_merge_at_once` below `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count`, which would make the minimum unattainable and silently degrade the gate into "block all fresh small merges until `merge_selector_small_parts_max_age`". To avoid that, enumeration is extended through the first all-small, all-fresh candidate of exactly `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count` parts. That extension is deliberately narrow: stale or large ranges keep the lowered cap, an explicitly configured `max_parts_to_merge_at_once` below the minimum keeps it (that is a contradictory configuration, and it is documented as such), and ranges that already reached `min_age_to_force_merge` keep it too — `allow` accepts those before the small-parts gate is evaluated, so the gate is not what blocks them and there is nothing to compensate for. `merge_selector_window_size` is a hard width limit in the same way: it is a global anti-snowball protection and is *not* widened for the gate, so configuring it below `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count` is likewise contradictory. This is documented in the setting description. That is deliberately a statement about the candidate *set*, and it is the only claim this PR relies on. Two things it explicitly does **not** claim: - It is not a "defer only" guarantee within a single selection round. `Estimator` keeps one global best candidate per partition, so rejecting the top-scoring small batch can hand that round to a different, already-eligible range rather than produce no merge. For example, in a fresh partition shaped `[1, 1, 1, 1000, 5, 5, 5, 5, 1000, ...]` MiB with `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count = 4`, the three 1 MiB parts are the best candidate without the gate, and with the gate the four 5 MiB parts are merged instead. The rejected batch is still merged later (or immediately once `min_age_to_force_merge` or the age safety valve fires). - It does not claim the base-ratio predicate (`sum_size / max_size >= lowered_base`) holds for every emitted range. The pre-existing right-tail trimming heuristic can already shorten a range after it passes `allow`, independently of these settings; this PR does not change that behavior. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count`, `merge_selector_small_parts_threshold`, and `merge_selector_small_parts_max_age` MergeTree settings to reduce the number of merge operations under rapid small-part insertion by requiring a minimum batch size before merging small fresh parts. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Three new MergeTree settings are added. When `merge_selector_small_parts_min_count` is set to a non-zero value (e.g. 8), the merge selector will not merge small parts (below `merge_selector_small_parts_threshold` bytes) that are younger than `merge_selector_small_parts_max_age` seconds unless at least that many parts are available. This reduces merge churn under rapid small-part insertion workloads. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100436&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100436](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100436+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree on shared storage
signals.text: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage (currently `S3`; `Azure` is implemented but not yet enabled, pending test coverage), enabling active/standby failover without external coordination (no Keeper). Uses conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) on object storage to maintain a lease file with JSON content `{"version":1,"leader_id":"...","timestamp":...}`. The leader renews its lease periodically; followers monitor and claim leadership when the lease expires. New MergeTree settings: - `leader_election` (Bool, default false) — enable leader election - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — lease renewal interval - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — lease expiry threshold; must be at least 3x the heartbeat interval When not the leader, inserts, merges, and DDL are blocked; background data processing is skipped. Mutations are unsupported on the currently enabled `S3` `plain_rewritable` metadata layout, including on the leader. Participating nodes should keep their clocks synchronized (NTP) to within `leader_election_session_timeout`; the conditional-write protocol always prevents split-brain, but excessive clock skew can cause leadership churn. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91613 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `leader_election` setting for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage, enabling active/standby failover using conditional writes without external coordination. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Three new MergeTree-level settings are added: - `leader_election` (Bool) — When enabled on a non-replicated MergeTree table stored on an `S3` object storage disk (`Azure` is implemented but rejected at table creation until it has test coverage), multiple ClickHouse instances sharing the same data path will elect a single leader. Only the leader performs writes and merges. Followers act as read-only replicas and automatically claim leadership when the current leader's lease expires. Mutations are unsupported on the currently enabled `S3` `plain_rewritable` metadata layout, including on the leader. - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — How often the leader renews its lease and followers check for an expired lease. - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — How long a lease remains valid without renewal. Must be at least 3x `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`. Example, using the same UUID and shared `S3` storage policy on each node: ```sql CREATE TABLE shared_table UUID '12345678-abcd-abcd-abcd-123456789abc' (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS storage_policy = 's3', leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; -- On every follower, attach the same table definition with the same UUID. ATTACH TABLE shared_table UUID '12345678-abcd-abcd-abcd-123456789abc' (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS storage_policy = 's3', leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; ``` <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > High risk because it introduces new leader-election coordination and modifies core `MergeTree` write/DDL/drop and catalog cleanup paths; bugs could cause write unavailability or accidental deletion/incorrect visibility on shared storage. > > **Overview** > Adds a **Beta** `leader_election` mode for non-replicated `MergeTree` tables on shared S3/Azure, using a conditional-write lease file to ensure only one instance performs inserts/merges/mutations while followers remain read-only and can take over on failure. > > Introduces new MergeTree settings (`leader_election`, `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`, `leader_election_session_timeout`) with validation, new `MergeTreeLeaderElection*` metrics/events, and follower part-refresh + leader takeover sync to load new parts and advance block counters before enabling writes. > > Hardens destructive operations for shared-storage tables: blocks most `ALTER`/partition-mutation operations and `RENAME` under leader election, gates background processing on leadership, and updates drop/cleanup logic (`dropSkipsDataDirectoryCleanup`, `DatabaseCatalog`/`StorageTableProxy` fail-closed behavior) to avoid recursive deletion or hangs when tables are shared or cannot be materialized. Adds documentation and integration/stateless tests covering failover, metrics, validation, and rejection cases. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 78c1252915ba512bebf94a147932158e1bacecf0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101039&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101039](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101039+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix cardinality underestimation when join column NDVs are unknown
signals.text: Restore the join-step row count estimation (originally #97114, reverted in #99957 because of regressions reported) and add a trust-propagation mechanism that prevents fabricated estimates from leaking into decisions where they cause regressions. **Trust-propagated cardinality** - `DPJoinEntry` / `RelationStats` carry a `rows_estimate_trusted` flag. It is `true` only when every NDV along the DP path came from real column statistics. - The NDV-unknown fallback in `computeSelectivity` (`1 / max(rows)` for both direct and transitive predicates) still gives the DP a usable estimate, but marks the entry untrusted. - `JoinStepLogical` exposes two accessors: - `getResultRowsEstimation` — raw DP estimate; used by `EXPLAIN` for visibility. - `getTrustedResultRowsEstimation` — returns `nullopt` when untrusted, so outer-scope `estimateReadRowsCount` does not feed a fabricated number upstream (equivalent to master's behavior for join steps). **Guards against fabricated estimates** - Build-side swap (`swap_on_sizes`) is gated by `sides_trustworthy` so a fabricated smaller side cannot flip `HashJoin` onto a huge relation. - When `HashTablesStatistics` returns a `source_rows` below the current estimate, trust is demoted (used in the swap gate) but `estimated_rows` is **not** clamped. Clamping made the DP read different leaf sizes on cold vs warm runs, which flipped greedy ordering and caused degradation in some cases; keeping source upper bounds keeps the plan shape stable across runs. **Regression tests** - `04103_join_build_side_no_stats` — without stats the 100-row dim still builds, fact probes, outer `ResultRows: unknown`. - `04104_join_trust_boundary_propagation` — nested `JoinStepLogical` exposes its result estimate only when trusted. - `04105_plan_stability_hash_table_stats_cache` — cold and warm EXPLAINs of the same query are identical both with and without stats. - `04106_join_plan_stats_toggle` — same 3-table star-join run twice with `SETTINGS use_statistics = 0` and `= 1`; contrasts the left-deep fallback plan against the right-deep pre-joined-dimensions plan. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Restore join-step row count estimation with trust propagation: when column NDVs are available, join cardinality and column stats flow through the DP and to the outer optimizer, enabling better build-side and multi-join ordering decisions; when NDVs are unavailable, an untrusted fallback keeps the DP working but does not drive structural decisions or propagate to upstream joins. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. At a minimum, the following information should be added (but add more as needed). - Motivation: Why is this function, table engine, etc. useful to ClickHouse users? - Parameters: If the feature being added takes arguments, options or is influenced by settings, please list them below with a brief explanation. - Example use: A query or command. --> <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Changes core join-order optimization cardinality/selectivity estimation and build-side swapping logic, which can alter query plans and performance across many workloads despite added safeguards and tests. > > **Overview** > Restores and extends join cardinality estimation in the join-order optimizer, adding end-to-end **trust propagation** so only estimates derived from real table/column statistics influence upstream optimizers and structural decisions. > > When join key NDVs are missing, selectivity now falls back to a row-count-based heuristic but marks the result *untrusted*; untrusted estimates are hidden via `JoinStepLogical::getTrustedResultRowsEstimation()` and are prevented from driving hash-join build-side swapping, while still being usable internally for DP cost comparisons. > > Also adjusts handling of hash-table statistics cache hints to demote trust (instead of clamping row counts) to keep join plans stable between cold and warm runs, and adds several stateless tests covering trust boundaries, build-side choice without stats, and plan stability/statistics toggling. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 255b598d8cc841a84129519a67b7c04ec8aa916c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(promql): Parse Prometheus Query API POST bodies as urlencoded form
signals.text: The Prometheus Query API (`QueryAPIImpl`) read parameters only from `HTMLForm(settings, request)`, which parses the URL query string. For POST requests with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, the PromQL `query` and range parameters live in the body, so they were empty and clients such as `prometheus/client_golang` saw failed or empty evaluations. `QueryAPIImpl` now uses `HTMLForm(settings, request, *request.getStream())` for POST and PUT so the body is merged with any query string (same behavior as `HTMLForm::load`). `RemoteWriteImpl` and `RemoteReadImpl` keep the default path so the raw body stream is not consumed before protobuf handling. Added `tests/integration/test_prometheus_protocols/test_query_api_post_body.py` comparing GET and POST for instant and range queries. Using the [prometheus/compliance](https://github.com/prometheus/compliance) PromQL harness, the reported pass count rose from **4 / 539 (~0.7%)** to **205 / 539 (~38%)** in one full run—about **+37 percentage points** and **~51×** more passing queries versus that baseline, consistent with POST clients no longer sending an empty `query` from the server’s perspective. Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/93191. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix Prometheus Query API ignoring POST form bodies <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.4.1.813` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Add groupBloomFilter aggregate function and bloomFilterContains scalar function
signals.text: Adds the `groupBloomFilter` aggregate function and the `bloomFilterContains` scalar function for memory-efficient probabilistic set-membership testing. This can be used to detect new values, perform approximate deduplication checks, and compare large datasets without materializing exact sets. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11700 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add the `groupBloomFilter` aggregate function for building mergeable Bloom filter states and the `bloomFilterContains` scalar function for testing whether values are probably present. Bloom filter sizing can be configured using an expected element count and false-positive rate or directly using the filter size and number of hashes, with an optional seed. The states support the `-State` and `-MergeState` combinators and can be stored in `AggregatingMergeTree`. Numeric probes, including `Decimal`, are converted to the filter's value type using accurate casts. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101841&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/101841](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F101841+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Lower PromQL predict_linear and honour stale markers in selectors
signals.text: Adds native lowering for PromQL regression and extrapolated range functions over ClickHouse `TimeSeries` data. The implementation lowers `predict_linear` through the ClickHouse time-series linear-regression aggregates, and additionally tightens PromQL selector parsing, `@`-modifier handling, and Prometheus stale-marker filtering for the range functions. Note: `increase` and `deriv` lowering landed on `master` independently - `increase` as `timeSeriesIncreaseToGrid` (which handles counter resets in the aggregate itself) and `deriv` together with a fix that scales the regression slope by the timestamp tick resolution inside `timeSeriesDerivToGrid`. When updating this branch both were resolved in favor of the `master` implementation: the local `rate`-scaled-by-range post-processing for `increase` and the per-second rescaling of `deriv` were dropped. Because `timeSeriesDerivToGrid` now returns a per-second slope, the dynamic (non-constant) `predict_linear` offset no longer converts the slope to timestamp ticks either. Split out from the integration draft #104271; shared base #104484. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added native PromQL-to-SQL lowering for `predict_linear` over ClickHouse `TimeSeries` data, and made instant selectors honour Prometheus stale markers. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104495&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/104495](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F104495+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Transform JOIN hash table payload to row major
signals.text: Resolves [#97883](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97883) Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where fixed and contiguous columns under a certain size are transformed into one row-major block of data. Before the change: ``` col1 Int32 col2 String col3 UInt8 col4 Float64 ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┘ row N → col1[N], col2[N], col3[N], col4[N] ``` After the change: ``` ROW STORE (col1 + col3 + col4, contiguous per row) col2 String (columnar) ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ ← row N (record) │ .... │ ← col2[N] ├──────────┼──────────┼────────────┤ ├──────────┤ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ │ .... │ └──────────┴──────────┴────────────┘ └──────────┘ ``` ### Rational: The row-major format allows the output construction to be a tight loop over each column, basically one pointer load and data copy: ``` for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) { const char * row_store_ptr = row_store_ptrs[i]; col->insertData(row_store_ptr + value_offset, value_size); } ``` In comparison the columnar version has to do more work: load columns[j], row_numbers[j], replicated_columns access, insertFrom ... For the following query `SELECT * FROM rs_probe_200m l JOIN rs_right_10m r ON (l.k % toUInt64(10000000 / 0.9)) = r.k FORMAT Null` from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql` the perf counters for `LazyOutput::buildOutput` in `AddedColumns` look as follows: ``` ┌─variant────────────────────────────┬─query_id─────────────────────────────┬─runtime_ms─┬───────instr─┬──────cycles─┬──────cmiss─┬──brmiss─┬───ipc─┬─cmiss_per_kinstr─┬─brmiss_per_kinstr─┐ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 9d2d6886-2ad7-430f-af2c-6c7cd32f3808 │ 1621 │ 11393048228 │ 31974507197 │ 1470246364 │ 5892574 │ 0.356 │ 129.05 │ 0.517 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 56b33013-8bec-4d7a-a415-2a06beb14bf6 │ 1633 │ 11547943445 │ 31874206968 │ 1484117664 │ 6265932 │ 0.362 │ 128.52 │ 0.543 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 65583fa7-9ce0-4426-95eb-977251d38f75 │ 1708 │ 11338601601 │ 31825721703 │ 1468670383 │ 5921051 │ 0.356 │ 129.53 │ 0.522 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 5ff1b154-3c3f-40c6-bae9-f6cf0feafe81 │ 2548 │ 15453833738 │ 58322156979 │ 2636461094 │ 9533242 │ 0.265 │ 170.6 │ 0.617 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 6e92c1d4-8432-4a79-a6cc-85e38232116d │ 2580 │ 15400954730 │ 58683032344 │ 2623136775 │ 9455570 │ 0.262 │ 170.32 │ 0.614 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 133f384f-c09a-4e12-9e69-85b61272a360 │ 2686 │ 15419169622 │ 59548322941 │ 2647601264 │ 9746405 │ 0.259 │ 171.71 │ 0.632 │ │ row-major-enabled-single-threaded │ 20039e91-b5dc-4b4a-8e22-f4451f6067be │ 30610 │ 9046504977 │ 16964398066 │ 995568814 │ 3235355 │ 0.533 │ 110.05 │ 0.358 │ │ row-major-disabled-single-threaded │ a3f9a822-dae6-45c1-9a4e-63e87a3592e8 │ 56821 │ 15279361788 │ 27940919919 │ 1167368997 │ 4694553 │ 0.547 │ 76.4 │ 0.307 │ └────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┴────────────┴─────────┴───────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Changes: - A `RowDataStore` that takes a set of columns and lays them in row major format. It exposes access to individual rows and the layout of each row (offset and size of fields in a row). - New `IColumn` interfaces that handle building the output columns from the row store, used manly by `AddedColumns.cpp`. - Two new settings to control the row-major transformation: - enable_hash_join_row_store. - min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store: Minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable transforming hash join payload to row-major. Used in the planner to decide when to enable the optimization. - A runtime feedback loop that tracks the number of hash table matches from a join and feeds it to the next execution of the join instead of relying on the estimated join output: - The match count is only published when the probe phase fully completes. - Only joins that went through the join reorder optimizer get a cache key. - Plans serialized to distributed workers don't collect or use the feedback. ### Limitations: 1. Only supports fixed and contiguous types and nullable version of them. Supporting non fixed rows would make the row-major layout non-uniform between rows and output column construction loop would not be as tight anymore. Also transforming unbounded unfixed types to row major could be very heavy. 2. ColumnReplicated might get materialized. The decision is made based on the column state the join sees in the first block. If it's ColumnReplicated the column is excluded from the row store, if it's not the column is included and it's replicated in a future block it get's materialized. 3. If spilling occurs, the row stored data is split back into columns for now. In a follow up we can make the row store a column and spill it as is. ### Build overhead: | Type | Rows | Columns | avg per worker thread (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | Int64 | 2M | 8 | 28.2 | | Int64 | 1M | 16 | 31.9 | | FixedString(16) | 1M | 8 | 24.6 | | FixedString(16) | 2M | 4 | 21.5 | ### Benchmarks: #### from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql`: | # | Right table | Match | Join | Before (s) | After (s) | Speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.265 | 0.237 | 1.12× | | 1 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.182 | 0.178 | 1.02× | | 2 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.108 | 0.525 | 2.11× | | 3 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.532 | 0.335 | 1.59× | | 4 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.350 | 0.249 | 1.41× | | 5 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.216 | 0.183 | 1.18× | | 6 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.607 | 0.553 | 2.91× | | 7 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.698 | 0.357 | 1.95× | | 8 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | FULL | 1.652 | 0.916 | 1.80× | | 9 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | FULL | 1.424 | 0.861 | 1.65× | | 10 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 2.239 | 1.554 | 1.44× | | 11 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.825 | 0.641 | 1.29× | | 12 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 3.771 | 1.820 | 2.07× | | 13 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 1.372 | 0.771 | 1.78× | | 14 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.596 | 1.249 | 1.28× | | 15 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.759 | 0.628 | 1.21× | | 16 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 6.158 | 1.979 | 3.11× | | 17 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 2.563 | 1.111 | 2.31× | ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where qualifying columns are transformed into one row-major block of data in order to speed up join output reconstruction. Controlled by two new settings: `enable_hash_join_row_store` (default true) and `min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store` (default 2, the minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable the transformation). --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104884&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/104884](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F104884+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signals.title: Declarative function signatures, continuation of #3775
signals.text: This is an experimental continuation of [#3775 (2018)](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/3775) by @alexey-milovidov, which proposed a declarative way to describe function signatures so that argument validation and return-type inference can be driven by a small DSL instead of hand-written `getReturnTypeImpl` logic per function. ### What's in this branch A `getSignatureString()` method on `IFunction` and `IFunctionOverloadResolver`. When a function exposes a non-empty signature, the base `getReturnTypeImpl(ColumnsWithTypeAndName)` parses and applies it via a small grammar of type **matchers** (`UInt`, `Number`, `Array(T)`, `MaybeNullable(T)`, `Function((args), R)`, `T : Any` capture, …) and type **functions** (`leastSupertype`, `nativeNumber`, `aggregateFunctionReturnType(AggregateFunction(name, …))`, `subcolumnTypeOf`, `typeFromString`, `DateTime64(scale, tz)`, …). The DSL supports variadic positions (`…`), ellipsis grouping for repeated argument units (`T1, V1, …` repeats the pair), `OR` between alternatives, optional positions `[T]`, const-value capture (`const name String`), lambdas, etc. The grammar / parser / type matchers / type functions live under `src/DataTypes/FunctionSignature.h`, `FunctionSignature.cpp`, `TypeMatchers.cpp`, `TypeFunctions.cpp`. ### Coverage ~191 commits on top of master, each is a small per-family round titled `Function signatures: round N — …`. Current state on this branch: ``` SELECT count(*) AS total, countIf(signature != '') AS with_sig, round(countIf(signature != '') * 100.0 / count(*), 1) AS pct FROM system.functions WHERE NOT is_aggregate AND alias_to = '' AND origin = 'System'; 1416 1395 98.5 ``` (With \`allow_experimental_nlp_functions = 1\`; the few remaining unset ones are setting / config-gated functions like \`aiClassify\`, \`region*\`, \`synonyms\`, whose \`create\` throws unless the relevant config block / setting is present, so \`system.functions.tryGet\` returns null even though the signature is in source. With the right config + setting they all surface — verified in tmp/ test config.) Roughly: - **Authoritative** (DSL drives type-check and return type, the legacy `getReturnTypeImpl` is either gone or bypassed): higher-order array functions (`arrayMap`, `arrayFilter`, `arrayFirst*`, …), `toIntervalX`, comparison, `multiSearch*` / `multiMatch*`, vector L-norms / distances / dot product, `UUIDv7ToDateTime`, `arrayReduce` / `arrayReduceInRanges`, `reverse`, `mapKeys` / `mapValues`, `getSubcolumn`, the `least` / `greatest` resolver, paired-variadic `timeSeriesTagsToGroup` / `timeSeriesStoreTags`, … - **Documentation-only** (signature surfaced via `system.functions` but the legacy `getReturnTypeImpl` still runs because the result type uses promotion / widening / setting-dependent dispatch the current DSL can't express): arithmetic (`plus`, `minus`, `multiply`, `divide`, modulo / intDiv family), array widening (`arraySum` / `arrayCumSum*` / `arrayDifference`), `mapContains*Like`, `dateTrunc`, `toStartOfWeek`, `parseDateTime*`, `transform`, `range`, `toX` conversions, etc. There is a `signature_documentation` opt-in alongside `signature` in the binary-arithmetic, unary-arithmetic, FunctionArrayMapped, and FunctionMapToArrayAdapter families specifically so a function can advertise a signature without the DSL accidentally hijacking the legacy widening logic. ### Status Draft / experimental. - This is an experiment — I'm not asking for it to be merged. There's significant disruption (191 commits touching every function family), and the gain is mostly documentation: today only ~30% of the converted functions are actually DSL-authoritative; the rest are decorative. The arithmetic promotion matrix and the per-Op widening rules in particular would need a richer type-function vocabulary (or new matchers) before they can be expressed declaratively. - The branch has been kept rebased on master throughout and builds cleanly. I've run the stateless test suite on each round. The pre-existing-on-master test failures I hit are listed in commit messages of the rounds where I encountered them (none introduced by this work). - The original PR has been open since 2018 — this branch is intended as a concrete data point on \"what fraction of ClickHouse functions can be reasonably described by a declarative signature, and what would the DSL need to grow to cover the rest.\" That's the question I'd love feedback on. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104948&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/104948](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F104948+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add server setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread`
signals.text: Each thread accumulates up to `max_untracked_memory` (4 MiB by default) of allocations before reporting them to the server-wide `MemoryTracker`. With many threads, this unreported memory can sum to a large amount, causing the server's tracked memory usage to under-count actual consumption and leading to OOM. This PR introduces a server-level setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread` (default 4 MiB) and speculatively charges this amount to the server-wide `MemoryTracker` for each worker thread of a `PipelineExecutor`, including query, merge, and mutation pipelines. The global tracked memory becomes a tighter upper bound on actual consumption when `max_untracked_memory` for those workers does not exceed this setting; operators that permit a larger per-query value must raise the server setting accordingly. The reservation is charged on the server-wide (total) tracker only — deliberately not through the query's tracker chain. Query-level accounting feeds heuristics that compare memory deltas against byte thresholds (conversion of aggregation hash tables to two-level via `group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes`, spill-to-disk decisions), and phantom reservations of `num_threads * 4 MiB` trip those thresholds immediately: an earlier revision of this PR that charged the query tracker showed consistent slowdowns of GROUP BY queries in performance tests for exactly this reason. The reservation itself does not alter query-level or user-level accounting (`max_memory_usage`, `memory_usage` in `system.processes`); however, every pipeline worker flushes its pending real allocation reports before releasing its outermost reservation, so those counters and memory-based heuristics can become visible sooner while a worker yields, downscales, or completes. The speculative reservation uses the throwing path of the memory tracker, so when it would exceed the server memory limit the corresponding job is treated as failed with `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — the same behavior as if the job itself had exceeded the limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new server setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread` (default 4 MiB) which speculatively reserves this amount on the server-wide `MemoryTracker` for each worker thread of a `PipelineExecutor`, including query, merge, and mutation pipelines. When it is at least the workers' `max_untracked_memory`, it makes server-wide tracked memory a tighter upper bound on actual consumption and reduces the risk of OOM with many concurrent pipeline workers. The reservation does not alter query-level or user-level accounting, but workers flush pending real allocation reports before releasing their outermost reservation, so those counters can become visible sooner while a worker yields, downscales, or completes. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - signals.title: Optimize min/max aggregates using column statistics
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds an optimization that answers filterless `min()` and `max()` aggregation queries from per-part column statistics without reading column data, avoiding full scans. ## How it works When a query like `SELECT min(x), max(x) FROM t` runs on a `MergeTree` table with column statistics configured (via `auto_statistics_types = 'basic'`), the optimizer checks whether the aggregate results can be obtained from the per-part `StatisticsBasic` metadata. If all conditions are met, the query plan replaces the `ReadFromMergeTree` step with a `ReadFromPreparedSource` that produces the answer directly from statistics without reading column data. The optimization applies when: - All aggregates are `min()` or `max()` - The table has `auto_statistics_types = 'basic'` and statistics have been materialized for the relevant columns - The table has no active mutations, patch parts, or lightweight deletes that would make stored statistics stale - For GROUP BY queries, the GROUP BY keys must map to partition key columns - If a filter is present, it must be computable from partition-level expressions and virtual columns If any check fails the query silently falls back to a normal `ReadFromMergeTree` read. ## SQL Examples ```sql -- Create a table with column statistics CREATE TABLE t ( key UInt64, value Int32 ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY key SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = 'basic'; -- Insert data (statistics are materialized on insert) SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, toInt32(rand() % 1000) FROM numbers(10000000); -- This query is answered from per-part statistics — no column data is read SELECT min(value), max(value) FROM t; -- GROUP BY partition key is also supported CREATE TABLE t2 ( p UInt8, v UInt32 ) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY p ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = 'basic'; INSERT INTO t2 SELECT number % 10, number FROM numbers(10000000); SELECT p, min(v), max(v) FROM t2 GROUP BY p ORDER BY p; ``` The optimization can be disabled via `SET use_statistics_for_min_max_aggregation = 0`. ## Related PRs Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/93037 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize `min()` and `max()` aggregate functions by utilizing per-part column statistics (`basic`) metadata when available, avoiding full data scans for queries. Controlled by the new setting `use_statistics_for_min_max_aggregation`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105197&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/105197](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F105197+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add INSERT ... RETURNING (non-atomic, user-supplied SELECT)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `INSERT ... RETURNING (SELECT ...)` to run a user-supplied SELECT after INSERT and return its result in one round-trip. Closes #21697. **Backward-incompatible change:** `RETURNING` is now a reserved keyword and can no longer be used as an unquoted implicit column alias (e.g. `SELECT 1 returning`). Use `AS returning` or a quoted identifier instead. --- Closes #21697 ## Summary Draft implementation of `INSERT ... RETURNING` for ClickHouse. The INSERT runs first using the existing pipeline; if it succeeds, a parenthesized `RETURNING (SELECT ...)` subquery runs in the same session and its result set is returned to the client in one round-trip. This is intentionally **not** Postgres-style atomic `RETURNING`. The user supplies the trailing SELECT and owns the `WHERE` clause used to identify inserted rows. ## Syntax For `INSERT VALUES` and `INSERT FORMAT`, `RETURNING` appears **before** the data clause (parser constraint: bytes after `VALUES`/`FORMAT` are raw input): ```sql INSERT INTO t (id, name) RETURNING (SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 123) VALUES (123, 'foo'); INSERT INTO t RETURNING (SELECT count() FROM t WHERE batch_id = 'X') FORMAT JSONEachRow {"batch_id":"X", ...} ``` For `INSERT SELECT`, `RETURNING` appears **after** the source query: ```sql INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM src RETURNING (SELECT count() FROM t WHERE batch_id = 'X'); ``` The parenthesized subquery is required (distinct from Postgres column-list `RETURNING id, name`). ## Semantics - INSERT runs first with its existing pipeline untouched. - If INSERT throws, the RETURNING SELECT does not run. - If INSERT succeeds, a select interpreter is built for the trailing subquery using the same Context; its pipeline is returned as the statement result. - The trailing SELECT inherits session, user, and settings. It can reference any table and use the full SELECT grammar. - Client receives **one result set** (the RETURNING SELECT's), not an INSERT ack plus a result set. ## Limitations (documented, not bugs) - **Not atomic.** Concurrent writers can land rows between INSERT completion and SELECT execution. - **No automatic "the rows I just inserted."** User provides the SELECT and owns its `WHERE`. - **Replication lag is visible** on Replicated tables unless consistency settings are used. - **Incompatible with `async_insert=1`.** Returns `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. - **No special MV interaction.** MVs fire on INSERT; RETURNING SELECT is a normal SELECT. - If INSERT succeeds but RETURNING SELECT fails, inserted data is **not rolled back**. ## Backward-incompatible change `RETURNING` is added to the parser's reserved-keyword list (same list as `FROM`, `WHERE`, `SETTINGS`, etc.) to prevent it from being consumed as an implicit table alias in `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM tablename RETURNING (...)`. As a side-effect, `RETURNING` can no longer be used as an unquoted implicit alias anywhere in ClickHouse SQL: ```sql -- Before: worked (returning was a plain identifier) SELECT 1 returning SELECT * FROM t returning -- After: must use AS or quoting SELECT 1 AS returning SELECT * FROM t AS returning ``` ## Implementation - **Parser** (`ParserInsertQuery.cpp`): parse `RETURNING` + parenthesized SELECT; placement rules above. - **AST** (`ASTInsertQuery.h`): `returning_select` field; clone/format updated. - **Interpreter** (`InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp`): reject `async_insert`; wrap completed INSERT pipeline with RETURNING via `DelayedSource`. - **Pipeline** (`buildInsertReturningPipeline.cpp`): run INSERT to completion, then build SELECT pipeline; native push inserts swap to RETURNING SELECT after data is received. - **executeQuery** / **TCPHandler** / **LocalConnection** / **ClientBase**: inlined-data wrap, native-protocol push path, query-log accounting, process-list propagation. - **Docs**: section added to `insert-into.md` ## Tests added - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04266_insert_returning_21697.sql` — core `INSERT ... RETURNING` semantics, delayed planning/failure behavior, query-cache rejection paths, transactional rollback checks (`implicit_transaction=1` + explicit transaction), and parser keyword regression coverage (`SELECT 1 returning` rejected; explicit/quoted alias accepted). - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04267_insert_returning_native_format.sh` — native TCP `INSERT FORMAT` + external data + `RETURNING`, including `input(...)` + `FORMAT` placement/round-trip stability. - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04410_insert_returning_trailing_settings.sql` — source-side trailing `SETTINGS` scoping/precedence, nested source settings handling, source-side query-cache settings rejection (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), and a plain `INSERT ... SELECT` regression proving nested source subquery settings stay local (non-`RETURNING`). ## Alternatives considered - **`AND SELECT` / `THEN SELECT` keywords** — parser ambiguity or poor discoverability for Postgres migrants. - **Atomic Postgres-style RETURNING** — much larger surface (formats, MVs, distributed, async); deferred as a possible follow-up. - **Multi-statement `;`** — out of scope. ## Open questions for maintainers 1. Is the non-atomic, user-supplied-SELECT model the right v1 framing? 2. Confirm canonical placement rules (before data for VALUES/FORMAT, after source for INSERT SELECT). 3. Restrict trailing SELECT to read-only queries only? (Current implementation: yes, via SELECT parser.) 4. Confirm single-result-set protocol behavior across HTTP/native/JDBC. ## Test plan - [x] Stateless test `04266_insert_returning_21697` - [x] `INSERT VALUES` + `RETURNING` with row filter - [x] `INSERT SELECT` + `RETURNING` with aggregate - [x] `RETURNING` against a table other than INSERT target - [x] INSERT failure prevents `RETURNING` subquery from running - [x] `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` when `async_insert=1` - [x] Native TCP `INSERT FORMAT` + `RETURNING` (`04267_insert_returning_native_format`) - [x] `input(...)` source with `FORMAT` before `RETURNING` (parser/formatter round-trip + execution) - [x] Source-side `SETTINGS` precedence and nested-source scoping (`04410_insert_returning_trailing_settings`) - [x] Plain `INSERT ... SELECT` keeps nested source subquery `SETTINGS` local (no non-`RETURNING` leakage) - [x] Source-side query-cache settings rejection in `INSERT ... RETURNING` source `SETTINGS` - [x] `02310_profile_events_insert` local `clickhouse-local` profile-events check is non-fatal in CI (`InsertedRows` is not emitted consistently there) - [x] Transactional rollback when delayed `RETURNING` planning fails (`implicit_transaction=1` and explicit transaction) - [x] `RETURNING` keyword parser regression (`SELECT 1 returning` rejected; `SELECT 1 AS returning` and quoted alias accepted) - [x] `04266` rollback subtests stabilized by avoiding fixed database-name collisions in flaky/parallel runs (use `t_insert_returning_tx` in the current test DB) - [ ] Replicated-table non-atomic behavior (integration test, future)

signals.title: Push down volume-reducing functions in query plan
signals.text: Adds a query plan optimization that pushes volume-reducing functions (`length`, `lengthUTF8`, `empty`, `notEmpty`) below the `Sorting` and `Filter` steps, so those steps carry the fixed-size result instead of the original `String` / `FixedString` argument. The rewrite is done with `ActionsDAG::split`: the function nodes form the first part, which becomes a new step below the child, and the second part becomes the parent step's `ActionsDAG` and reads the results as inputs. It only fires when the wide argument column really stops flowing through the child step — the column is removed from the child's output, and unless the child reads it itself it is not even produced below the child. `tryExecuteFunctionsAfterSorting` and `trySplitFilter` keep the pushed functions where they are, so the optimizations do not move the same nodes in opposite directions. For the shape from the issue below, `SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s)`, the filter still needs `s` to evaluate its condition, but `length(s)` is now computed before the filter, so the wide column is not copied for the surviving rows. Enabled by default; can be turned off with `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 0`. An earlier attempt at the same optimization was https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86139 by @talmawash, credited as a co-author. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/82378 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86139 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a query plan optimization that pushes volume-reducing functions (`length`, `lengthUTF8`, `empty`, `notEmpty`) below the `Sorting` and `Filter` steps, replacing the wide `String` / `FixedString` argument with the fixed-size result, so it is neither buffered by a sort nor copied by a filter. Controlled by the new setting `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions`, enabled by default. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106199&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/106199](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F106199+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1857` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix Azure endpoint settings being dropped on SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106356 --> `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG` reloaded the per-endpoint Azure settings from the prefix `configuration.disks.`, but startup uses `storage_configuration.disks`. The wrong prefix does not exist, so the settings map was cleared and not reloaded, and a disk's `use_native_copy` was lost until the next restart. This reloads from the same `storage_configuration.disks` prefix used at startup. A regression test asserts native copy still works after `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`. Includes the per-xdist-worker config-path fix from #106356, which the new test depends on. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG` discarding per-endpoint Azure Blob Storage settings (such as `use_native_copy`), which caused a disk's configured settings to be ignored for `BACKUP`/`RESTORE` until the server was restarted. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.6.1.405` - Backported to: `26.5.3.42`, `26.4.5.49`, `26.3.14.40` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix signed integer overflow in condition_variable::wait_for with huge timeouts
signals.text: A wait-timeout setting that reaches `std::condition_variable::wait_for` unchecked overflows the chrono conversion inside it. libc++ evaluates `wait_for(d)` as `steady_clock::now() + d` in nanoseconds, multiplying a millisecond duration by 1000000: a timeout above ~9.2e12 ms overflows Int64, and one above the Int64 millisecond range even turns into a negative duration, so the wait returns at once and the caller busy-loops instead of waiting. UBSan aborts the server; a release build silently wraps. The setting that reaches it in practice is `interactive_delay`, a plain unbounded `UInt64` of microseconds: the server waits `interactive_delay / 1000` milliseconds for the next result chunk in `ConcurrentBoundedQueue::popImpl`, through the lazy output format, on both the `TCPHandler` and the `clickhouse-local` path. Found by serverfuzz on master, and again in the stress test of an unrelated pull request — https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112177&sha=e601607e228ad5d736ad491220ebf4b62d531d51&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177): ``` /ClickHouse/contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__chrono/duration.h:93:79: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 18584892780430 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type '_Ct' (aka 'long long') ... #6 ConcurrentBoundedQueue<DB::Chunk>::popImpl<true>(...) src/Common/ConcurrentBoundedQueue.h:73 #8 DB::LazyOutputFormat::getChunk(unsigned long) src/Processors/Formats/LazyOutputFormat.cpp:25 #11 DB::TCPHandler::processOrdinaryQuery(DB::QueryState&) src/Server/TCPHandler.cpp:1540 SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior ``` Reproduces deterministically: ``` clickhouse-local --query "SELECT 1 SETTINGS interactive_delay = 100000000000000000" ``` Fix: clamp the timeout to one year before constructing the chrono duration, via a small shared helper `saturatedMilliseconds`. The same cap is already used for `CancellationChecker` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96450); it is applied here to the remaining `wait_for` sites that take a user-controlled millisecond timeout, and `saturatedSeconds`/`saturatedSecondsFrom` cover the seconds-typed timeouts and the query cache expiry built as `now() + seconds(query_cache_ttl)`. A `Milliseconds`- or `Seconds`-typed setting can no longer carry such a value in the first place: `SettingFieldTimespan` rejects a value that does not fit into Int64 microseconds, so the clamp there is only defence in depth. That check landed on master after this branch was cut and supersedes the saturating conversion this pull request originally added to `SettingsFields`, which is dropped along with its unit tests in favour of master's stricter ones. What is left for the clamp is every setting that is not a timespan — above all `interactive_delay`. Keeper has its own coordination waits with a different bound; they are handled separately in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a wait-timeout setting, such as `interactive_delay`, was set to a huge value: the wait could time out immediately instead of waiting, and the server could abort under the Undefined Behavior Sanitizer. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106961&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/106961](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F106961+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
