signals.title: Reject a table reference in the IN operator of a constraint expression
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107424 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A constraint whose `IN` operator had a bare identifier on the right-hand side, such as `CONSTRAINT c CHECK a IN (b)`, silently rewrote it into a table reference `default.b` and persisted it. The resulting table rejected every `INSERT` with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, and the server refused to start once the referenced column was dropped. Such a constraint is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when it is supplied by `CREATE TABLE`, a full-definition `ATTACH TABLE`, or `ALTER TABLE ... ADD/MODIFY CONSTRAINT`, and when it is copied by `CREATE TABLE ... AS` or `CLONE AS`. Existing tables keep loading. ### Description `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` turns an `IN` right-hand side into a table identifier. Correct in a SELECT, where `x IN t` is shorthand for `x IN (SELECT * FROM t)`, but wrong for a constraint, evaluated against the inserted row. The rewritten AST is persisted. Measured on master, for `CHECK a IN (b)` with `b` a column: `SHOW CREATE` reports a constraint the user never wrote (`IN (default.b)`), and every `INSERT` fails `Code: 47 UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. Dropping that column makes the metadata unloadable, fatal at startup. Found on `Stress test (amd_msan)` in three unrelated PRs, as the fuzzer's operand-swapped mutation of `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`. This adds `checkConstraintExpressionIsValid`, mirroring #107424's key-expression check, applied only to user-supplied DDL. The recursion stops at subquery boundaries, so `IN <table>` inside a subquery keeps working. **Cases found in review.** `CREATE TABLE ... AS src` and `CLONE AS src` parse no declaration; they copy the source constraints, so a legacy source could seed the shape into a new table. Copied constraints go through the same gate. An `ALTER` command that stores nothing (`ADD ... IF NOT EXISTS` on an existing name, `MODIFY ... IF EXISTS` on a missing one) stays accepted as on master, judged against the commands preceding it in the same statement. **What this removes.** Where the identifier names an existing table the constraint did work, but only in the process that parsed the DDL: the load path never applies that visitor, so after a restart `INSERT` fails `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. I reject it rather than keep a form that write-deads a table at the next restart. Tell me if you would rather keep it. Unlike #107424 I do not reject at load time: such metadata exists in the wild. Existing tables keep loading, stay ALTER-able including `DROP CONSTRAINT`, and Replicated databases still recover them. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112992&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112992](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112992+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Disable the sampling query profiler under Memory Sanitizer
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100242 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106591 Every `MemorySanitizer` report produced in CI since 2026-05-28 is truncated to a single line: ``` ==117==WARNING: MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value MemorySanitizer: nested bug in the same thread, aborting. ``` No stack trace, no `SUMMARY`, no origin — so no MSan failure can be located. In the CI database, `msan` checks recorded 1009 reports with a usable stack in 2026-04 and 0 in 2026-07, while `asan`, `tsan` and `ubsan` reports are unaffected and still carry full stacks. The regression window matches #100242 (merged 2026-05-28), which enabled the sampling query profiler for sanitizer builds. Printing an MSan report takes the sanitizer runtime seconds, because it symbolizes every frame through an `llvm-symbolizer` subprocess, and it holds `ScopedErrorReportLock` for the whole time. A profiler signal delivered to that thread meanwhile runs instrumented code in the handler and trips a second MSan check; compiler-rt treats a same-thread re-entry into the report lock as unrecoverable, writes `nested bug in the same thread, aborting.` with `CatastrophicErrorWrite` and calls `internal__exit`, so the report that was already being written to `MSAN_OPTIONS=log_path` stops after its header line. Reproduced with the `arm_msan` binary built from master `3885f7b7bbf1`, running the same query against the same server three times and forcing a sanitizer report with `max_allocation_size_mb=32 allocator_may_return_null=0`: | configuration | result | | --- | --- | | profiler on (default `global_profiler_real_time_period_ns`) | `nested bug in the same thread, aborting.`, 1-line report | | `<trace_log remove="1"/>` (no profiler at all) | full 31-line report with stack | | `trace_log` on, `global_profiler_*_period_ns = 0`, per-query profiler off | full 31-line report with stack | So it is the profiler timer signals, not the trace collector. This turns `QUERY_PROFILER_SUPPORTED` off under MSan, next to the existing TSan-on-macOS exclusion. The trace collector stays enabled: the memory profiler, `trace_profile_events` and `SYSTEM INSTRUMENT` all feed it from ordinary code rather than from a signal handler. Other sanitizers keep the profiler, because their checks fire only on genuinely invalid accesses, which the handler does not perform. `00974_query_profiler` and `01569_query_profiler_big_query_id` assert that samples reach `system.trace_log`, so they get `no-msan` back. The other profiler and `trace_log` tests either already carry `no-msan`, exercise the memory profiler / `trace_profile_events` / `SYSTEM INSTRUMENT` (unaffected), or make no assertion on sample counts. This does not fix the uninitialized read that the `BuzzHouse (amd_msan)` run below hit — that one is unidentifiable as reported. It makes the next occurrence diagnosable. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=3885f7b7bbf1b8791021e1c97ca2e4eea132de04&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113107&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113107](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113107+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add the `logsql` dialect: LogsQL, the query language of VictoriaLogs
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental `logsql` dialect: LogsQL, the log query language of VictoriaLogs, can now be used to query ClickHouse tables with logs. Enable it with `SET allow_experimental_logsql_dialect = 1, logsql_table = '<table>', dialect = 'logsql'` (plus `logsql_database`, `logsql_time_column`, and `logsql_message_column` as needed). LogsQL queries are translated at parse time into ordinary `SELECT` queries, so text filters expect `String`-backed log columns, while the `math` pipe applies raw arithmetic and needs numeric operand columns (`String` field values are not coerced to numbers). Documentation entry for user-facing changes. - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Implementation notes: - Nearly the whole language is supported: the filters (words, phrases, prefixes, `field:value`, `:=`, `~`, comparisons, `range`, `in` with subqueries, `contains_any`/`contains_all` with subqueries, `seq`, `len_range`, `string_range`, `ipv4_range`, `ipv6_range`, `pattern_match*`, `contains_common_case`/`equals_common_case`, `json_array_contains_any`, `i()`, full `_time:` filters with `day_range`/`week_range`, `_stream:{...}` selectors), and the pipes `fields`, `delete`, `copy`, `rename`, `limit`, `offset`, `sort`/`first`/`last` (including `rank` and `partition by`), `stats` (with `by`-buckets, per-function `if`, `switch`, `rate`), `where`, `uniq`, `top`, `math`, `extract`, `extract_regexp`, `format`, `unpack_json`, `unpack_logfmt`, `join`, `union`, `unroll`, `running_stats`, `total_stats`, `len`, `hash`, `coalesce`, `decolorize`, `split`, `unpack_words`, `time_add`, `sample`, `generate_sequence`, `field_values`, `json_array_len`, `json_array_concat`, `replace`, `replace_regexp`, `pack_json`, `pack_logfmt`. On typed (non-`String`) columns, filters that emit string functions fail with a type error instead of applying VictoriaLogs' schemaless per-value matching. The numeric stats functions (`sum`, `avg`, `median`, `quantile`, `stddev`, `rate_sum`) parse the numeric value out of every field value and skip the values that are not numbers, like VictoriaLogs, which computes its stats in `float64`; a numeric column is therefore aggregated with `Float64` precision and not exactly. - The dialect is modeled on the existing `kusto`/`prql`/`promql`/`polyglot` dialects: a parser under `src/Parsers/LogsQL/` builds a ClickHouse `ASTSelectQuery` directly, so all downstream machinery (analyzer, distributed queries, query log) works as usual. Relational pipes map to real SQL constructs: `join` to `LEFT`/`INNER JOIN ... USING`, `union` to `UNION ALL`, `running_stats`/`total_stats` and the `rank`/`partition by` clauses to window functions. - The lexer and the grammar mirror the reference implementation in VictoriaLogs (`lib/logstorage` of `VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs`, Apache 2.0), including Go-style string literals, compound tokens (`foo-bar.com:123/x`), comments with `#`, and the exact filter/pipe syntax. The test queries are reused from the VictoriaLogs parser tests: 675 of its 878 valid parser-test queries run end-to-end against a ClickHouse table, and 605 of its 612 invalid queries are rejected. - The implicit table is configured by the `logsql_database`/`logsql_table` settings (like `promql_database`/`promql_table`). The special fields `_time` and `_msg` are mapped to columns via `logsql_time_column`/`logsql_message_column`, so real tables (e.g. `system.text_log` with `event_time`/`message`) can be queried after setting those. - Word and phrase filters translate to `hasToken`/`match` with token boundaries, so tables with `tokenbf_v1` indexes on the message column benefit from index analysis. - Documented deviations from VictoriaLogs: word boundaries follow ClickHouse tokenization (ASCII alphanumerics; VictoriaLogs also treats `_` and non-ASCII letters as word characters); numeric comparison filters parse `String` field values per row (rows with non-numeric values do not match) and compare typed numeric columns exactly, but the per-row parsing of field values understands plain numeric text only (decimal integers, floats, scientific notation, `inf`/`nan`) - LogsQL-only spellings such as `10KiB`, `1h`, `0x10`, or `1_000` are supported in query literals but are treated as non-numeric when stored in a field value, whereas VictoriaLogs parses them there too; equality with a non-numeric value compares with the native column type instead of VictoriaLogs' string semantics; `count(field)` counts non-NULL values instead of non-empty strings; `pattern_match*` placeholders are approximated with regular expressions (VictoriaLogs uses a greedy matcher with extra boundary rules); `seq()` matches substrings in order without word-boundary checks. - The only constructs that remain `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (with clear errors naming the construct) are the ones with no ClickHouse meaning: VictoriaLogs storage introspection (`block_stats`, `blocks_count`, `query_stats`, `value_type`, `histogram` buckets, `set_stream_fields`, `stream_context`), features that require the dynamic set of fields of a schemaless store (`facets`, `field_names`, wildcard field selectors like `foo*:filter`, stats over all fields like `sum(*)`, `unpack_json` without a `fields` list), `unpack_syslog` (a stateful wall-clock-dependent parser), and `collapse_nums` (its number-boundary rules require lookaround which RE2 lacks). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113207&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113207](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113207+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not push sorting into Merge children across an order-breaking cast
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112931 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong `ORDER BY` and `DISTINCT` results, and a `CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE` error for aggregate functions, when reading a `Merge` table whose declared column type differs from a source table's type in a way that does not preserve sort order, for example `UInt64` over a source holding negative `Int64`. ### Description Related: #112931 `StorageMerge::getQueryProcessingStage` reports whatever stage its children report, so a `Distributed` child makes the shards apply the `ORDER BY` while the initiator only merges the sorted streams. `ReadFromMerge::convertAndFilterSourceStream` then casts each child's output to the declared types, and that cast lands *above* the child's own sort, so an order-breaking conversion reinterprets the values after they were sorted. The promise cannot be withdrawn, since the merging step was chosen from the stage, not from a sort property. It also enables DISTINCT-in-order, which in debug builds throws `Equal values are not contiguous within the range assumed to be sorted`. The fix refuses the delegation where it is issued: `getQueryProcessingStage` returns `FetchColumns` when a child's column type differs from the declared type un-order-preservingly, as it already does for `JOIN`. The flag is applied after the stage arithmetic, since `FetchColumns` is zero and `std::max` would erase the refusal. The type test must be order-preserving *and* injective, because it composes elementwise inside `Array`. Following `ToNumberMonotonicity`, it accepts integer widening that keeps the signedness or targets a signed type, adding `Nullable`, stripping `LowCardinality`, an `Enum` target at least as wide as the source, and `Array` over `Array` with an accepted element pair. Everything else is refused, including a narrower `Enum` target, which truncates and so reverses the order even where `contains` accepts the pair. A false "safe" gives silently wrong results; a false "unsafe" costs one pushdown. `Merge` derives such pairs itself via `getLeastSupertypeOrVariant`. Read-in-order needs no change: its monotonicity analysis already rejects the inserted `_CAST`. `Tuple`, `Map`, `StorageBuffer`, `StorageView`, `StorageMaterializedView` and `buildQueryTreeForShard` need their own fixes. Found by the AST fuzzer, which had retyped a `Merge` column to `IPv4` over `Int64` (2508-36d8, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112931&sha=581f5ddc3b2ce1429d9064179dad535fafea72a4&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29)). Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115455 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113242&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113242](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113242+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Has token with nullable
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106922 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/88119 With a `text` index on a `Nullable` column, direct read from the text index replaced the search predicate with a `UInt8` virtual column filled from the posting lists. A `NULL` row has no tokens, so the predicate was materialized as `0` where it should be `NULL`. The predicate is now rebuilt as `if(str.null, NULL, <virtual column>)`, so the `NULL`s come back while the index still answers the predicate. In exact mode the column itself is no longer read, so the `NULL`s are taken from its `.null` subcolumn. This PR also created the infrastructure to support `hasTokenOrNull` in a followup PR. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for text-search predicates on a `Nullable` column with a text index when the predicate is negated or its value is read, e.g. NOT `hasToken(str, 'x')` returned the rows where `str` is NULL. Direct read from the text index materialized the `NULL` result as 0. ```sql CREATE TABLE tab (id UInt32, str Nullable(String), INDEX idx(str) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha')) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 'hello world'), (2, NULL), (3, 'foo bar'), (4, NULL), (5, 'hello there'); SELECT id FROM tab WHERE NOT hasToken(str, 'hello'); -- 2, 3, 4 with the index, 3 without it <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113332&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113332](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113332+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support updating projection settings without forcing immediate re-materialization - ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY PROJECTION
signals.text: Support ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY PROJECTION <name> (<query>) WITH SETTINGS (...). Projection-level settings (index_granularity, index_granularity_bytes, and the other allow-listed settings) could previously be specified only at projection creation time via WITH SETTINGS but never modified. MODIFY PROJECTION is a metadata-only alter that replaces the stored projection settings in place: - Only the WITH SETTINGS clause may change: the projection query body must be identical to the existing definition otherwise the command is rejected with BAD_ARGUMENTS. - The new settings apply lazily: parts written by future inserts and merges use the new values, existing parts keep the old ones until they are merged or the projection is rebuilt with MATERIALIZE PROJECTION. - IF EXISTS is supported - New access type ALTER MODIFY PROJECTION under the ALTER PROJECTION group. Tests: - 04757_alter_modify_projection_settings (old part keeps old granularity while new part and merged part get the new one via system.projection_parts, plus error cases. - 04758_alter_modify_projection_settings_replicated (metadata alter replicates to a second replica). Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108420 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY PROJECTION to change projection-level settings (e.g. index_granularity) of an existing projection without rebuilding it. The new settings apply lazily via merges. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113343&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113343](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113343+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix division by zero in `ReadFromMergeTree` when `StorageMerge` truncates the number of streams
signals.text: The `AST fuzzer (amd_debug)` raised `Integer divide by zero` on ```sql SELECT id FROM merge(currentDatabase(), '^t$') ORDER BY id DESC SETTINGS max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 1073741824, max_threads = 4 ``` The planner computes `max_streams = max_threads * max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 2^32`, which passes the existing overflow check because it fits in `size_t`. `ReadFromMerge::createPlanForTable` passed `UInt32(streams_num)` to `storage->read`, truncating `2^32` to zero. The child `ReadFromMergeTree` then divides by the requested number of streams in `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreamsWithOrder`. `IStorage::read` takes `size_t num_streams`, so this change removes the narrowing cast and adds a regression test. Additionally, `StorageMerge` multiplied the requested number of streams by `max_streams_multiplier_for_merge_tables` with unchecked `Float64` to `size_t` conversions. Both sites now use a shared checked helper that throws `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND` if the product does not fit in `size_t`. `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreams` and `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreamsWithOrder` also now use a division-based comparison when clamping streams to data, avoiding overflow in `num_streams * min_marks_for_concurrent_read`. Because forwarding the full `size_t` stream count exposes arbitrary child engines to absurd requests, `ReadFromMerge::createChildrenPlans` now checks the aggregate source count of a `Merge` read against a limit of 65536 before building any child plan, and rejects excessive reads with `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND`. Child storages report a conservative bound on the sources they create through the new `IStorage::getMaxReadStreams` capability: `File`, `URL`, `Log`, `TinyLog`, `StripeLog`, `Memory`, `Null` and `View` are covered, proxies forward the capability to the nested storage, and a trivial `LIMIT` reduces the request the same way `GenerateRandom` does. When a child's reported bound is below the request, its output resize (`parallelize_output_from_storages`) is disabled so the constructed pipeline matches the accounting. The previously added streaming-read guard and its test are removed because current `master` now bounds effective `MergeTree` stream counts before that code path. Found by the AST fuzzer on an unrelated PR: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113010&sha=59507af89c33f62942e855b50b3e66704cbcf2e9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113010 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix an arithmetic exception in debug and sanitizer builds when reading from a `Merge` table with a very large `max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`: the number of streams was truncated to 32 bits, so multiples of `2^32` became zero. Also throw `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND` instead of invoking undefined behavior when multiplying stream counts for a `Merge` table exceeds `size_t`, avoid an overflow when limiting `MergeTree` streams to the amount of data, and reject a `Merge` table read whose aggregate source count would exceed 65536. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113382](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113382+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reap the test process groups the abort path orphans
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112911 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112911 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description When a stateless run aborts, the report can come back empty: `files: []`, no server log, no `fatal.log`, no test rows. This [`Stateless tests (amd_debug, parallel)` run](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112911&sha=c41e24cb553693def4ded9a8f8151a651dd80531&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29) aborted at test 7326/12303 and emitted nothing until the 9000 s job timeout. Root cause: the parent force-kills its workers on the abort path. A worker killed there sits inside `kill_process_group`'s own `sleep`, and SIGKILL runs no `finally`, so the test process group survives, holding the inherited stdout, and `clickhouse-test | ts | tee` never sees EOF. Nothing can reap it either: `run_single_test` unlinks its PGID record in the `finally` around `proc.wait`, *before* `process_result_impl` reaches `kill_process_group`. The change keeps the record until the group is gone, checked with one `killpg(pgid, 0)` rather than inferred from the leader's exit status, and names it `<run token>.<worker>.<pgid>`, so a kept record survives that worker's next test and a reap is scoped to one invocation: the records are repo-wide and a live parent must not signal another invocation's tests. The token is seeded through a new `_CLICKHOUSE_TEST_RUN_TOKEN` variable, because a `spawn` worker (selected for `aarch` checks) re-executes the runner and would otherwise mint its own. Reaping runs in the parent, the only process guaranteed alive there, in a `finally` around each runner, so a signal to the parent and a normal finish are covered too. It passes a new `diagnostics=False` (default `True`) to skip what is otherwise paid *per group*, serially: a 60 s sanitizer wait, a 10 s stacktrace wait, an unbounded `ps`. Verified by killing the server mid-test on a local Debug build: five processes of the group survive on `master`, none with this change, exit code unchanged. The new `ci/tests` guards fail on `master` and pass here. This does not explain the server death; it makes the next occurrence arrive with the artifacts to. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113393&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113393](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113393+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep an Iceberg table readable after a column is dropped
signals.text: Keep an Iceberg table readable after a column is dropped <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113324 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION` when reading an Iceberg table whose data file still physically contains a column that was dropped from the schema. The Parquet v3 reader now skips a file column whose field id is within the range the table has assigned, and still rejects an unmapped id below that range. Unrecognized ids in Iceberg's reserved metadata range are ignored, as the spec requires. Closes #113324. ### Description Closes #113324. Since 25.11 the v3 Parquet reader is the default, and reading a real column throws `Code: 743 ... Parquet file has column legacy_col with field_id 3 that is not in datalake metadata`. No setting restores the old behaviour: `input_format_parquet_use_native_reader_v3` is obsolete. Root cause: a data file written before `DROP COLUMN` still holds the dropped column with its original field id. Once the pre-drop snapshot is expired, the entry's schema resolves only from the merged manifest's header, which records the post-drop schema, so the reader gets a field-id map lacking id 3. `useColumnMapperIfNeeded` misses, finds the id outside the reserved range, and throws. Manifest merging (an Iceberg Java default) and snapshot expiry are routine housekeeping. Fix: narrow the refusal condition to what the metadata can actually decide. Iceberg's `last-column-id` is a monotonic high-water mark, so `1 <= field_id <= last-column-id` means "this table could have assigned this id", and such a column is simply not projected (Iceberg [Column Projection](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#column-projection)). An id outside that window could not belong to the table and still throws. Inside the window the bound cannot distinguish a dropped column from one never assigned, so both are skipped; deciding exactly would need the union of retained schemas, which `RemoveSnapshots` may collect. The helper now returns `std::nullopt` for a not-projected leaf, handled at both call sites. Not matching by physical column name: re-adding `legacy_col` gives a different field id, so old rows must read NULL. Name matching would serve the dropped column's values, i.e. silent wrong results. The added test pins this. The bound is attached only to mappers built from table metadata; without `last-column-id` the reader rejects as before. ORC needs no change: it uses `ColumnMapper` only when writing. The wrong schema id resolved under manifest merging is a separate defect, not addressed here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113465&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113465](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113465+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix lost rows and LOGICAL_ERROR for a distributed query with no table column
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104510 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query over a `Distributed` table (or `cluster`/`remote`/`clusterAllReplicas` with an inner `view`) spanning more than one shard that references no column of the table anywhere in the query, such as `SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM distributed_table`. Such a query silently returned no rows, and returned `LOGICAL_ERROR` `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` when the table produced a constant. The fix covers the analyzer; `enable_analyzer = 0` is fixed separately by #113955. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104510 A `Block` carries its row count only inside its columns, so a header with no column cannot express "N rows" across a mergeable-stage boundary. When the query references no column of the table expression, `prepareBuildQueryPlanForTableExpression` reads one synthetic column purely to learn the row count. The window function is deferred to the initiator along with the projection that would have consumed that column, so it is pruned. If the table expression produces a constant, the shard keeps one column while the initiator expects none and `OutputPort::pushData` raises `LOGICAL_ERROR`. If no constant survives, both headers are empty, nothing is sent, and every row is lost with no error: over two shards of 1000 rows the query returned nothing where 2000 rows are correct. The fix records that synthetic column's identifier where it is created, and replaces a mergeable-state header holding nothing but such columns with one materialized `UInt8` column. Both headers then agree by construction, and `ExpressionTransform` sizes the constant from the chunk, so a zero-column chunk still yields N rows. The condition is a property of the whole query, not of the window, so two limits are worth stating. A query referencing a column only where it is consumed before the boundary (`WHERE`, `PREWHERE`, `JOIN ON`) reaches the same empty header by another route and is not fixed here: that needs internal-only provenance through the filter plumbing, and folding it in was measured to turn the abort into a new user-visible error on the constant-projection shape. And not every window function is affected: `sum(1) OVER ()` and `rank() OVER (ORDER BY 1)` keep a non-empty shard header. The test covers both symptoms through `cluster`, `clusterAllReplicas`, `remote` and a stored view over seven constant types, plus `UNION ALL` and `JOIN`, and pins the shapes that must not change. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114611

signals.title: Fix materialized CTE gate missing for a reused CTE over Distributed
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113184 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113184 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `LOGICAL_ERROR` "Reading from materialized CTE '...' before its materialization completed - DelayedPortsProcessor gate is missing in the query plan" when a `MATERIALIZED` CTE reads a `Distributed`, `remote()` or `cluster()` table, is filtered by `IN` over another materialized CTE, and is referenced more than once. Closes #113184. ### Description An `IN`-set pipeline built during index analysis runs standalone under its own `CompletedPipelineExecutor`, so no `DelayedPortsProcessor` from another plan gates its readers. Reading a materialized CTE that nothing in that plan materializes then hits the fail-fast check in `MemorySource::generate`. Root cause: a materialized CTE reading a `Distributed`/`remote()` table plans a shard-local plan, where the deeper CTE resolves *by name* to its temporary `StorageMemory`. `isMaterializedCTE()` is then false and the CTE is not yet plan-backed, so `collectMaterializedCTEs` declines to gate it - the arm #108924 added for a read-by-name of a table the initiator owns. That plan later runs standalone, out of reach of the outer gate. Fix: before an in-place build runs a plan, push a `DelayedMaterializingCTEsStep` covering every CTE the plan's node tree reads while no step in that tree materializes it. It becomes the plan root, so its gate dominates every reader in that tree; a CTE already gated in the same tree, already built, or holding no plan is skipped, so the attachment is idempotent and never takes a CTE another plan claimed. Both in-place entry points are covered (`buildSetInplace`, and `buildOrderedSetInplace` on both its clone and destructive branches). No new setting, no default change, no format change. Planning order is untouched, and `Planner.cpp` is byte-identical to master. Attaching the step earlier, at the point where a set subquery's plan is extracted, was measured and does not work: there the CTE holds no plan yet (`has_plan=0` on this reproducer, against a control that reads `1`), so the step would have nothing to carry. <details> <summary>Validation: fresh server per arm, build id and fixture row count asserted before each arm</summary> | arm | before | after | |---|---|---| | reused CTE + `IN` over a deeper CTE, over `remote()` | logical error | correct result | | same, `Distributed` engine | logical error | correct result | | same, non-primary-key filter column | logical error | correct result | | same, `PREWHERE` | logical error | correct result | | same via the `buildSetInplace` route (ordered build declined) | logical error | correct result | | control: plain `MergeTree` | correct result | unchanged | | control: `force_primary_key` (the 03928 shape) | correct result | unchanged | | oracle: `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` sees the set condition | present | present | | its negative control, `use_index_for_in_with_subqueries = 0` | absent | absent | The oracle and its negative control show the index path is still taken rather than silently declined. `04712` fails on the pre-fix binary through the real test runner and passes after, 50 of 50 randomized runs; across 352 `in_subquery` / `prewhere` / `set_index` / `primary_key` tests the failure set is byte-identical before and after. </details> CI carrier: [`AST fuzzer (amd_debug)` on #114375](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114375&sha=0aba0e7d40b0a1755033a9ef4a6a92440b9adb05&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113489&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113489](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113489+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix logical error for RIGHT JOIN with parallel replicas
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113292 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108645 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the logical error `Can't determine table for parallel replicas` for a `RIGHT JOIN` whose right side has no table eligible for parallel replicas, and made such a `RIGHT JOIN` materialize a left side that is not a `MergeTree` instead of letting every replica read it independently. ### Description Master-only logical error thrown at `findParallelReplicasQuery.cpp:637`: release builds reject the query, debug and sanitizer builds abort, reddening Stress and fuzzer jobs. **Root cause.** For `JoinKind::Right` the side read with replicas is the right one, because `buildQueryTreeForShard` materializes the left table expression into a temporary table. `getSupportingParallelReplicasQueries` descended the left expression instead, so a query was accepted for its left side, the rewrite materialized that same side, and the lookup on the rewritten tree threw. `88b22b8fb66c115` (#108645) flipped the target while renaming `getRightTableExpression`; `26.2` through `26.7` still descend right, so the defect is confined to master. **The fix** descends the right expression again (`RIGHT SEMI`/`ANTI` were affected too), then corrects three places that had the materialized side wrong, each of which let every replica read its own copy of data it must not: - `rewriteJoinToGlobalJoin` decided locality from the right side for every kind; it now requires the materialized side of a `RIGHT JOIN` to be eligible for parallel replicas, not merely `MergeTree`. - That question was asked about the raw storage, so an eligible `View`/`MaterializedView` lost its local join; the wrapper is resolved to the table it reads first. - The global-join collector skipped each global join's right child, so a nested global join in the offloaded subtree never got a temporary table. The last two were reported by `clickhouse-gh[bot]`. No backport is requested: every release branch already decides locality from the right side while descending right, so that half is pre-existing there and no repro was measured on a release binary. **Validation.** New stateless test, untagged and parallel-safe. It fails on unmodified master with the logical error, and reverting any hunk reddens only that hunk's own assertions. At the current head it passes 30/30 sequentially and 12/12 at four-way concurrency, and is identical across the `join_use_nulls` and `compatibility` values Stress randomizes. The 127 `parallel_replicas` tests show no regression. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113515&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113515](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113515+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Push the release changelog and version bump to master directly instead of via PRs
signals.text: Direct pushes to `master` by `robot-clickhouse` are permitted (via a ruleset bypass), so the release job no longer needs a pull request and the `CH Inc sync` / merge-queue round-trip to land its changes — it pushes them straight to `master`. - Patch release: push the generated changelog artifacts (`version_date.tsv`, `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md`, `SECURITY.md`, the Docker `Dockerfile`s) directly, dropping the `auto/<tag>` changelog PR. Idempotent — skips when the changelog is already on `master`. - New release: push the post-release master version bump directly, dropping the `bump_version_<v>` PR and its enqueue. Idempotent by version string; retries on a non-fast-forward. With no release PRs left to land on `master`, the merge-queue machinery is removed (`merge_prs`, `_enqueue_release_pr`, `update_release_info`, the enqueue step), and the AutoReleases open-version-bump-PR guard drops. `--skip-docker` now skips only docker image generation and tagging, not the changelog or version bump. The release-branch Release PR (`release`/`release-lts`) is unchanged. Depends on `robot-clickhouse` being an always-bypass actor on the `master-pull-request` and `master-merge-queue-and-statuses` rulesets (clickhouse-private#66856). ## Validation Direct changelog push to `master` succeeded end-to-end: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32500716302 — real `CreateRelease` run (`ref=v25.8.32.4-lts`), log shows `remote: Bypassed rule violations for refs/heads/master` and `docs/changelogs/v25.8.32.4-lts.md` landing on `master`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113528&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113528](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113528+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Auto-retry infra failures on fork PRs
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113052 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The fork-approval gate consumes `run_attempt` 1, concluding `action_required` with zero jobs, so a fork PR's first attempt that runs anything is attempt 2. `retry_infra_failures.yml` assumed attempt 1 is the real run, leaving infra-killed fork runs invisible to the hourly auto-retry. I hit this via the slowdown #113052 fixed, which killed `Config Workflow` on ~65 PRs. **Attempt and window.** The filter widens to `.attempt <= 2`, accepting attempt 2 only if attempt 1 concluded `action_required`, so a real retry stays excluded. The cutoff compared `createdAt`, which GitHub pins to the gated attempt, while `startedAt` advances to the attempt that ran; that skew reaches p99 45.1h over 8946 runs. **Scan depth.** The listing is `createdAt`-ordered, so a gated run sits deeper than its window implies and no row cap exhausts it. The scan walks `createdAt` in 24 hour timestamp partitions over 31 days, bounding the 30 day approval expiry (observed max 26.6 days). A partition at the API's 1000 row ceiling fails the step instead of dropping rows. **Order.** The walk feeds more candidates than `MAX_RERUNS`, so their order decides who is reached. `sort -u` also sorted by the leading `databaseId`, oldest-created first, only a 0.90 pairwise proxy for `startedAt` order. Entries now lead with `startedAt` so the same dedup orders by deadline: the candidate nearest the 6 hour edge is retried on this tick or never, while a fresher one is still admitted by later ticks. Over 312 hourly clocks every clock exceeded `MAX_RERUNS`, and of the candidates on their final tick this loses 35%, against 56% and 100% for ascending and descending id. Attempt 3 stays excluded and the infra heuristic is unchanged, so this restores visibility rather than reruns. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113564&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113564](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113564+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Bind the parallel replicas shard scope to the cluster that produced it
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/81738 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results and a `LOGICAL_ERROR` when a query reads with parallel replicas inside a distributed sub-query whose `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` numbers its shards differently from the cluster the query is distributed over, for example a `VIEW` carrying its own `SETTINGS cluster_for_parallel_replicas`, or a read through `clusterAllReplicas` of that same cluster. The shard number shipped by the initiator was applied to the other numbering and selected the wrong shard. Parallel replicas are now declined for such a read. ### Description `prepareClusterForParallelReplicas` indexes the `_shard_num` scalar into `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` as if both described the same cluster. They are independent: `_shard_num` is shipped over the wire by a distributed query's initiator, while `cluster_for_parallel_replicas` is a per-query setting any nested `SETTINGS` clause can change, including inside a `view(...)`. - Above the other cluster's shard count, the read throws `LOGICAL_ERROR: Shard number is greater than shard count`, aborting debug and sanitizer builds. - In range, no check fires and the read silently returns **the wrong shard's data**: `10000090` where `90` is correct. `21ef1f1d1c9ba39` removed a `_cluster_for_parallel_replicas` scalar, reasoning that the setting alone identifies the cluster; a view with its own `SETTINGS` falsifies that. This restores the provenance as a second column of the `_shard_num` block, so overwriting the number replaces it atomically. A scope is honoured only when its provenance identifies the same shard *numbering*, not merely the same cluster name: `clusterAllReplicas` derives a renumbered cluster that keeps the name. Otherwise parallel replicas are declined at every admission site, giving the same results as `enable_parallel_replicas = 0`. No assertion is weakened: with admission gated, the `LOGICAL_ERROR` becomes correct rather than misapplied. Absent provenance means "trust the shard number", so mixed-version clusters keep today's behaviour. Each consequence reproduces on unpatched master and passes here. Added a stateless test, an integration test for the wrong-shard read, and gtests for wire cases SQL cannot build. signals.title: Fix `Files metadata is empty` logical error on the object storage queue read path
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/93009 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Logical error: 'Files metadata is empty'` when reading from, altering, or flushing an `S3Queue`/`AzureQueue` table whose metadata handle is gone: concurrently with a `DROP`/`DETACH`, after a failed `startup`, or after a failed `DROP`. Such a table now reports `TABLE_IS_DROPPED` instead. `SYSTEM FLUSH OBJECT STORAGE QUEUE` on such a table no longer crashes the server. ### Description `StorageObjectStorageQueue::getTableMetadata` threw `LOGICAL_ERROR` whenever `files_metadata` was null, and `createFileIterator` calls it first. Plan optimization reaches it via `ReadFromObjectStorageQueue::applyFilters`, so an ordinary `SELECT` aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds (7 occurrences in 90 days, 4 unrelated PRs, 0 on master). Three reachable states leave an addressable table with a null handle: * a concurrent `DROP`/`DETACH`: the storage is shut down before any exclusive lock is taken, and for an Atomic database none is taken at all, while a `SELECT` holds only `lockForShare`; * a failed `startup`: the catalog entry is created first, and never rolled back; * a failed `DROP`: the database does fallible disk work before detaching (the #93009 route). The handle was also a plain `shared_ptr` with no synchronisation, unlike the twelve other members of that class, and `waitForPathToBeProcessed` read it with no null check, which segfaulted. The fix guards it with the existing class mutex and gives every operation one snapshot it owns for its whole duration, so a handle observed non-null cannot become null halfway through. `getTableMetadata` is removed rather than reimplemented on the accessor: it returned a reference into the object the snapshot owns, which a snapshot local to the accessor would leave dangling. Its seven callers each take their own. Where the state is legitimate the code reports `TABLE_IS_DROPPED`, matching `IStorage`; the background streaming path returns instead, a null handle there meaning shutdown. Such a table now reports a clear error; it does **not** become usable again, since recovery is a `DatabaseAtomic`/`InterpreterDropQuery` concern for every engine, out of scope here. All three reproduce on unpatched master with a stack frame-for-frame identical to the CI report, the concurrent-teardown one with no fault injection (8/8). Three integration tests cover them: pristine master reports 1 failure, the fix 18 passes, 30/30 repeats green.

signals.title: CI: bound each docker buildx invocation in the Docker image jobs
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Docker server image` and `Docker keeper image` wedged with no output for about five hours, then died on the praktika 18000s job cap: four times on 2026-08-05 on four unrelated PRs, producing no image and no usable log. No related open issue found. The stall is inside `apt-get update`. apt cannot bound it: `Acquire::http::Timeout` is an **inactivity** timeout, not a wall-clock one. Measured locally, a mirror trickling **a byte per second** runs unbounded past a 700s cap, and `Acquire::Retries=5` does not change that. The failing jobs show that shape. And the retry configured here could never run: both call sites pass `retries` and `retry_errors`, but `Result.from_commands_run` never forwards a `timeout`, so a command that never returns is never retried. All four logs show zero `Retryable error` lines. Both invocations are now wrapped in GNU `timeout`, so an expiry is retried while a real build error still fails fast. The bound starts at 2700s, above the slowest healthy single attempt over 90 days (1819.1s). A fixed bound would not bound the *job*: `main()` loops over os variants and tags, so the invocation count is not fixed, and nine successful builds at 2700s exceed the cap alone. Each invocation instead gets what remains of the cap after a 3600s reserve, divided by the retry count: the scheduled shape's worst case is then 16334s against 18000s. That division is also why the retry count drops from 5 to 2: five attempts fit only up to a 255s bound, seven times below the slowest healthy attempt, where two attempts leave 881s above it. Being one count for all of `Shell.run`'s tokens, it applies to the registry and mirror signatures too. `ci/tests/test_docker_buildx_timeout.py` pins that arithmetic against the job's own cap, and the sentinels arming a real retry by attempt count rather than membership. <details> <summary>Validation (click to expand)</summary> An expiry is recognised on 124, and on the escalated 137 only when `timeout` logged its own KILL diagnostic, so an OOM or an external kill is not mistaken for one: the same discrimination `clickhouse_proc.py` makes with `_TIMEOUT_KILL_DIAG`, with `LC_ALL=C` pinning that translated string. `Acquire::Retries` is deliberately not re-added to the published Dockerfiles, which would revert 7cb40723f9ef632. The `git clone` of `docker-library/official-images` stays unbounded: not the apt layer, never observed wedging. Retry behaviour through the real `Shell.run` at the shipped count of 2: | arm | rc | attempts | verdict | |---|---|---|---| | expiry, child honours SIGTERM | 124 | 2 | retried | | expiry, child ignores SIGTERM (escalated) | 137 | 2 | retried | | succeeds | 0 | 1 | no retry | | real error `exit 7` | 7 | 1 | fails fast | | bare 137 (`kill -9`) | 137 | 1 | no retry | The last two are the discriminating controls. Replacing the KILL diagnostic with a string `timeout` never prints drops the second arm to one attempt, proving the token is read rather than merely present in a list. Quoting is pinned against an unwrapped baseline: the brace group reproduces every argument byte-for-byte, while `bash -c` returns rc=0 and truncates a `--build-arg`. The worst case walks `main()`'s own loop, allowing a wedge in every variant/tag group rather than one per job, since nothing breaks between groups; it is exact by construction, merging combinations that reach the same elapsed. Restoring five retries, or cutting the reserve to 600s, reddens it at 18510s and 18246s. One extra os variant stays green at 17180s, since a shrinking deadline absorbs it, while thirty redden it. A separate arm pins the single tag both scheduled commands request: unreachable `--tag-type release` would build four tags and not fit (23948s). Twenty-four of twenty-six mutations redden a named arm; the other two are controls. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113869&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113869](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113869+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1880` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix out-of-bounds write on a long codec chain
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash and an out-of-bounds write when inserting into a column with a long chain of compression codecs, for example `CODEC(FPC, FPC, ..., FPC)`. `CompressionCodecMultiple` compounded each stage's reserved size in a `UInt32` without checking for overflow, so a long enough chain wrapped the reserved size below its own input and the destination buffer was then sized from the wrapped value while the real payload kept growing. Such a chain is now rejected with `CANNOT_COMPRESS`. A chain of more than 255 codecs, which used to write a part that could not be read back, is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when the codec is created, unless `allow_suspicious_codecs` is set. ### Description `CompressionCodecMultiple::getMaxCompressedDataSize` compounds each stage's reserve in a `UInt32` with no overflow check (`CompressionCodecMultiple.cpp:38`). Every codec reserves at least its own input, so the reserve grows each stage and eventually wraps below its own input. The payload keeps growing too, but more slowly, so from the wrap onward the destination buffer is sized from a small wrapped number while the real data is hundreds of megabytes. `doCompressData`'s unguarded `memcpy(&dest[1 + codecs.size()], ...)` (`:64`) then writes past the end of it. Measured on a plain `MergeTree` table with an ordinary `INSERT` and **no settings**. For `Float32`/FPC the reserve wraps at stage 105 and the payload overtakes it around 135 stages: at 140 ASAN reports a `heap-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 2940232275`, and at 150 the server dies with a SIGSEGV. All of these are now `CANNOT_COMPRESS`; 104 stages still works unchanged. The guard is a per-stage monotonicity check: a stage whose reserve comes back below its own input has wrapped. It is applied at both sites that consume a per-stage reserve. A second check compares the actual post-loop size against the bound, immediately before the `memcpy`; being computed from real output rather than from a bound, it holds wherever inside a codec the arithmetic overflowed. Widening the accumulator does not help: `getCompressedReserveSize` returns `UInt32` and hands back an already-wrapped value. This mirrors the `doDecompressData` hardening in the same file from #60731, making the two directions symmetric. **Behaviour change:** chains of 105-134 stages currently return correct results and are now rejected. Their reserve is already a wrapped, meaningless bound; they avoid overflowing only because the payload has not yet caught up. Not FPC-specific: `DoubleDelta` and `Gorilla` chains wrap the same way, and `Nullable(Float32)` behaves like `Float32`. <details><summary>Validation</summary> Debug build, `clickhouse local` and a real server. The crash arms need the memory limit lifted, since a limit masks the crash as `Code: 241`. | `CODEC(FPC x N)` | before | after | |---|---|---| | 104 | works | works, unchanged | | 105-134 | works, but the reserve has already wrapped | `CANNOT_COMPRESS` | | 140 | ASAN `heap-buffer-overflow`, `WRITE of size 2940232275` | `CANNOT_COMPRESS` | | 150 | SIGSEGV / `span:522` assertion | `CANNOT_COMPRESS` | Chain length is capped at 255 separately: the codec count is stored in one byte, so 256 codecs used to write a part whose count read back as 0 (`Code: 246` on read). 255 codecs round-trips; 256 is now rejected at `CREATE`/`ALTER` with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and on the write path with `CANNOT_COMPRESS` for metadata stored earlier. - Both directions, pristine master `25d677a44eb4be59` vs the fix: FPC x150 / 2 rows is `rc=139` SIGSEGV before and `CANNOT_COMPRESS` after; FPC x104 is byte-identical on both. - ASAN (`master-asan-build`, same base): pre-fix `heap-buffer-overflow`, `WRITE of size 2940232275`, `0 bytes after 2147483648-byte region`. - Mutation arms: removing either guard alone still rejects the chain (the other catches it); removing both reproduces the SIGSEGV. With only the outer bound removed, the inner check reports `Compressed data of size 2940232416 does not fit the reserved buffer of size 1622428514`, the exact write ASAN flags. - New test `04812_codec_chain_reserve_overflow`: 50/50 runs pass with randomized settings and 50/50 with randomization off. - `codec`/`compress` suite (188 tests, identical population on both arms): 20 pre-existing environmental failures on both, identical failure sets, **0 regressions**. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113877&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113877](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113877+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Check the query cancellation while filling `system.parts` and its siblings
signals.text: The tables based on `StorageSystemPartsBase` (`system.parts`, `system.parts_columns`, `system.projection_parts`, `system.projection_parts_columns`) build the whole result eagerly in `initializePipeline`, so a cancelled or timed out query kept building rows over every storage and part until the very end. In a stress test with ThreadFuzzer this took minutes and tripped the hung check: a `SELECT` over `system.parts_columns` (with a filter matching every active part on the server) stayed in the process list for 252 seconds with `is_cancelled = 1` and `max_execution_time = 10`. Check the query status per storage and per part, following the pattern of `system.zookeeper` and `system.remote_data_paths`. The check also covers the storage-discovery prepass in `StoragesInfoStream` (the eager enumeration of all databases and tables), the analogous prepass in `StoragesDroppedInfoStream` (so `system.dropped_tables_parts` is interruptible as well), the skip loop in `StoragesInfoStreamBase::next`, and the per-storage part enumeration itself: the `MergeTreeData` helpers (`getDataPartsVectorForInternalUsage`, `getAllDataPartsVector`, `getProjectionPartsVectorForInternalUsage`, `getAllProjectionPartsVector`) take an optional `need_stop` callback that is checked periodically while the parts snapshot is being built. The two column-oriented tables additionally check the query status inside their column-enumeration loops and their metadata prepass, so a very wide table does not create a long uninterruptible stretch inside a single storage. The return value of `checkTimeLimit` is honored, so with `timeout_overflow_mode = 'break'` the eager build stops at the soft deadline and returns the rows collected so far. The table-lock acquisition in `StoragesInfoStreamBase::tryLockTable` is interruptible as well: instead of a single wait inside `RWLockImpl::getLock` for the whole `lock_acquire_timeout`, the lock is acquired in 100 ms slices with a query-status poll between the attempts (the total timeout and the `DEADLOCK_AVOIDED` semantics are preserved), so a killed or soft-timed-out query does not sit in the lock wait while a concurrent DDL query holds the drop lock. The test `04869_system_parts_lock_wait_cancellation` pins this with a share lock held by a long `SELECT` and a `DROP TABLE` in an `Ordinary` database queued behind it. The test uses the new `slowdown_system_parts_enumeration` failpoint, which only affects the specially named test tables (so concurrently running tests are unaffected). It sleeps 500 ms on every enumerated part, so building the full result for a 20-part table takes at least 10 seconds, and it sleeps 1 second per `COLUMNS_CANCELLATION_CHECK_PERIOD` (128) enumerated columns of a part, so building the full `system.parts_columns` / `system.projection_parts_columns` result over a single part with 1,025 columns (and a projection over all of them) takes at least 8 seconds. The test asserts that queries with a 1 second deadline in the `break` mode finish well under that (the elapsed time is taken from `system.query_log`, because the startup of `clickhouse-client` alone takes seconds in the debug and sanitizer builds), which is only possible by stopping at the per-part and per-column cancellation checkpoints. Timed assertions are needed because a plain row-count assertion cannot distinguish a build with the fix from one without: in the `break` mode the executor drops the eagerly built result after the deadline in both cases. The test also asserts partial row counts under a pre-expired deadline for all five tables, including `system.dropped_tables_parts` over a deterministic dropped-table fixture. The pre-expired-deadline checks also run under the failpoint, so the fewer-rows assertion is deterministic even on a machine fast enough to build the whole result in under a millisecond. For tables with the `_snap` name marker, the failpoint additionally slows down the parts-snapshot walks inside `MergeTreeData` (500 ms per enumerated part) and makes them poll the stop callback on every element, and for tables with the `_meta` name marker it slows down the column-metadata prepass of the column-oriented tables (1 second per 128 enumerated metadata columns), so the timed checks also prove that the snapshot materialization and the prepass are interruptible: all six of these checks fail against a binary with the `need_stop` polls and the prepass checkpoints disabled. Caught by `Stress test (arm_asan_ubsan, s3)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113722&sha=ceedb772f6aa36e221d25ce48f9af71f032a7b08&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113722 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Queries over `system.parts`, `system.parts_columns`, `system.projection_parts`, `system.projection_parts_columns`, and `system.dropped_tables_parts` now react to cancellation and `max_execution_time` while the result is being built. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113909&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113909](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113909+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not merge over a gap containing an outdated part with a higher mutation version
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113864 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Part ... intersects previous part ... It is a bug or a result of manual intervention`) that makes a `MergeTree` table impossible to load: attaching it, and every later attempt to load it, fails with that exception (a server abort in debug and sanitizer builds). A merge could span a block gap holding an outdated part whose mutation version is higher than the merge result's, producing a pair of parts on disk that neither contain nor are disjoint from each other. Closes #113864. ### Description A merge is refused when the block gap it spans holds an outdated part the merge result would not cover. That check compared only the part **level**, while `MergeTreePartInfo::contains` requires both `level >=` and `mutation >=`. An outdated part left by a mutation has level 0, so the check could not see it and the merge produced an intersecting, mutually non-containing pair. Every later part load (`ATTACH TABLE`, or a server restart) then throws; in debug and sanitizer builds that exception aborts the server. Such a gap appears when parts owe different mutation stacks. In the reported case a mutation succeeded on one part (version 59) and threw on its neighbour (left at 45); once killed, the surrounding parts merged into `all_43_62_1_45`, which does not contain the intervening `all_57_57_0_59`. Later no-op merges carried that result to `all_43_62_5_45`, the name in the reported message. `getMaxLevelInBetween` now also accumulates the maximum mutation version over the gap and is renamed `getMaxLevelMutationInBetween`, and `canMergeParts` refuses the merge when that version exceeds `max(left.mutation, right.mutation)`. That is the pairwise maximum rather than the exact result version, which is only known later in `FutureMergedMutatedPart::assign`; since the exact version is a maximum over a superset of any adjacent pair, this can refuse a merge early but never admits one it should refuse. The refusal is non-fatal: the merge is deferred until `old_parts_lifetime` removes the outdated part. The replicated merge predicate has no such hole: it probes the gap with a synthetic part at `MAX_LEVEL`/`MAX_BLOCK_NUMBER`, which dominates on both terms. Validation: on a debug build the new test aborts the server without this change and passes with it; reverting only the added term reddens it while `02521_merge_over_gap` (the existing level-shape test) stays green. A slice of 261 merge/optimize/mutation tests shows no regressions, and the test passes 50/50. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113941&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113941](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113941+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Publish column types and serialization hints atomically in ALTER
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a race in `MergeTree`-family tables where an `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` that changes a column's type runs at the same time as a part being committed. The new column type became visible before the table's serialization statistics were rebuilt for it, so the committing part could be mixed into statistics built for the old type. This picked sparse-vs-full encoding from wrong statistics until the `ALTER` finished, and aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` published the new metadata through the lock-free multiversion store and rebuilt `serialization_hints` afterwards, in a *separate* `lockParts()` scope. In that gap a committing part reaches `updateSerializationHintsForPart` with `part_columns` and `storage_columns` both already NEW, so the "structure may change after alter" guard compares NEW against NEW and lets the part through, while the hint it mutates is still OLD-typed. For `String` -> `Tuple(...)` that hint is a base `SerializationInfo` and the part's info a `SerializationInfoTuple`, `structureEquals` is a `typeid` comparison, and the `chassert` fails. The guard compares part against table, so it cannot notice that the *hint* is stale. `MergeTreeData::setPropertiesAndResetSerializationHints` now publishes and swaps the hints in one `parts_lock` scope, the lock the two sides actually share, since a part commit holds it in `Transaction::commit`. It is prepare-then-commit: the metadata clone happens outside the lock, and inside it the new hints are built *before* anything is published, so a throw leaves both unchanged (previously a throw mid-reset could pair new metadata with a cleared aggregate). Five column-type publishes use it, including the replicated `setTableStructure` rollback, so a failed `alterTable` cannot leave old columns with new-typed hints. Settings-, comment- and statistics-only publishes are untouched, as is the assertion. `parts_lock` is hot, but the hints build already ran under it and the clone is kept out, so the net addition is two moves. The non-replicated rollback restoring `old_metadata` keeps plain `setProperties`, because the rejected new settings are still live there. The new test parks an ALTER inside the window with a failpoint and commits an INSERT concurrently. It aborts with the expected assertion on the old ordering, and passes on the fix while observing the INSERT contend. There is no public CI signal (searched 90 days against non-zero controls): this is a code-proven latent defect, not an observed failure. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114019&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114019](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114019+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report why the stress script failed, not just its exit code
signals.text:
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113857 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stress test (*)` and `Upgrade check (*)` wrap the stress script like this: ```sh ... && echo -e "Test script exit code$OK" \ || echo -e "Test script failed$FAIL script exit code: $?" ``` The script's output is never redirected, so it reaches only the job console; the only thing written into `test_results.tsv`, which `stress_job.py::read_test_results` parses into result rows, is the exit status. In the 30 days to 2026-08-09, all **152** `Test script failed` rows (133 pull requests, 6 on master, 11 flavours) had a byte-identical `info` cell of ` script exit code: 1`. Reading three of those job logs gave two unrelated causes, so the family cannot be triaged from the CI database. This captures the output and puts its tail into the `info` cell of the row the wrapper already emits, outside `/test_output` (uploaded wholesale) so a passing run gains no artifact. The script is redirected there and mirrored to the console with `tail --pid`, not piped: `prepare_for_hung_check` drops databases with a fire-and-forget `Popen(..., shell=True)` inheriting the wrapper's stdout, and a pipe reader waits for those clients long after the script exits. The exit code is `$?` after `wait`. Those clients can also append after the script exits, while the mirror ends with it, so the wrapper waits for the capture to stop growing and then prints the bytes the mirror missed. The wait is a bounded size poll, never a wait on the descriptor, since that is what deadlocked the pipe form, and the offset is the mirror's own byte count rather than the file size, which can already include unmirrored bytes. A writer slower than that bound would leave its bytes in `/tmp`, which is not collected, while master printed them at any delay, so the wrapper looks once more when the job ends, from an `EXIT` trap covering the early exits after the row too. The offset advances, so nothing prints twice, and a failing run keeps the capture as `stress_script.log` with the other artifacts. `escaped_tail` is a single-level sibling of `escaped`, which pre-compensates its terminator for `echo -e`; `escaped` is untouched. The reader decodes `\t`, `\r` and `\n` only, so a byte the `Escaped` rule encodes but it does not keeps a visible backslash, and #113857 makes the codec reversible. This fixes visibility, not the trigger: verify with `length(test_context_raw) > 20`, not by the rows disappearing.
Validation (click to expand) Every arm extracted the real wrapper block from each runner by content anchor and drove it with a stub, asserting through the real `read_test_results`. `ci/tests/test_stress_job.py` is byte-identical to master: the executable harness was removed at the reviewer's request, so this is evidence rather than coverage this branch ships. Row content: master gave a 20-byte `info`, this gives 517 bytes with the exception line, one parsed row either way, and the same for a tab, CR, NUL, quote, backslash, embedded `\n`, a cut mid-UTF-8, 708 KB / 40001 lines, an empty capture and three replayed job logs. Late writers, with a console pipe that ends with the container and survivors killed, as the job log behaves: the piped form times out with an empty `test_results.tsv`; a child printing 2 s or later lost the line from row and console before the drain and keeps it after; at 20 s and 30 s the console and the artifact keep it where the previous head lost both, on both runners and when the epilogue aborts early, matching master's console at every delay. A descriptor never closed bounds the wait at 16 s instead of hanging. Each line appears once, exit codes 0/1/42/143 are unchanged with an empty capture, a non-empty capture and an unwritable artifact directory, where preservation warns, and a passing run adds about 6 s and no artifact. Mutations each reddened the relevant arm: inverting the exit-code comparison, deleting `set +e` or the restoring `set -e`, capturing to `/dev/null`, `echo -e` for `printf`, the counted offset for the file size (console 20/20 to 0/20 at a 1.0 s child), and removing the trap.
