signals.title: Add stateless and fuzzer jobs to the WeeklyCFI workflow
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112152 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115591 The `amd_cfi` build is the only test build with ThinLTO enabled — the same compile profile as official release builds — so besides CFI violations the `WeeklyCFI` workflow also catches ThinLTO-only behavior differences that no other CI job can see (e.g. the `__functional` frame-name suppression surfaced by `test_crash_log` and fixed in #112152). This PR broadens the workflow's coverage from build + integration + stress to: - **Stateless tests** (`amd_cfi, parallel` + `amd_cfi, sequential` lanes, mirroring `amd_debug`). `clickhouse-test` now detects the CFI build from `-fsanitize=cfi` in the `CXX_FLAGS` row of `system.build_options` and exposes a `cfi` build flag, so a test that genuinely cannot hold in this profile can carry a `no-cfi` tag (the same generic `no-<flag>` skip mechanism the sanitizer builds use). No test needs the tag today. CFI is deliberately not treated as a sanitizer: it has near-zero runtime overhead, so tests tagged `no-sanitizers` still run under CFI — consistent with #115591, which stopped the test harnesses from misclassifying the CFI build as a sanitizer build. - **AST fuzzer** (`amd_cfi`): fuzzers assert only on crashes, never on exact query output, so the build profile cannot produce false positives there, and fuzzing reaches virtual-call combinations the curated suites never exercise. Runs against the unmodified CFI binary (no build flag needed). - **BuzzHouse** (`amd_cfi_buzzhouse`): BuzzHouse needs `-DENABLE_BUZZHOUSE=1`, which compiles extra sources into `clickhouse-client`/`dbms` and would change the whole-program ThinLTO graph of the shared CFI binary. To keep the canary binary identical to the release profile, a separate `amd_cfi_buzzhouse` build (identical cmake plus the flag) feeds only this lane. The fuzzer job configs are shared out into `_common_ast_fuzzer_job_config` / `_common_buzz_fuzzer_job_config`; the master and PR workflows are unchanged (their generated YAML did not change). Not added, and why: unit tests (`ENABLE_CFI` is incompatible with `ENABLE_TESTS` — ThinLTO is disabled when building tests), performance comparison (it compares against the non-CFI master-head binary, so results are uninterpretable), upgrade/compatibility checks (version and data compatibility are orthogonal to CFI instrumentation), Keeper Jepsen (requires the standalone `clickhouse-keeper` build, which the CFI build omits). **Validation:** the workflow was temporarily switched to a `pull_request` trigger (same approach as #100419) and all `amd_cfi` jobs passed ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=baf56e50335c45adf2afb691d0a1ef72f49c8bc6&name_0=WeeklyCFI)) — stateless parallel + sequential, integration 4/4, stress, AST fuzzer, and BuzzHouse. The schedule-only trigger (Mondays 03:00 UTC) is restored for merge. **Findings from the validation runs, all filed:** - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115121 — probabilistic server crash (SIGSEGV) in gRPC response compression (`zlib_compress` / `deflateEnd`), still open. - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115122 — empty `symbols`/`lines` in `system.trace_log` under `amd_cfi`; root cause was the test harness misclassifying the CFI build as a sanitizer build and installing `trace_log_no_symbolize.xml`; fixed by #115591 (merged, and master is merged into this branch), so the two `03150_trace_log_*` tests are expected to pass in the weekly stateless lanes. - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115198 — stress runs cannot restart the server if killed inside `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`'s deliberate-corruption window (not CFI-specific; also hit three other PRs). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115036](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115036+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not pop hints on a line displayed programmatically
signals.text: When a query is displayed at once rather than typed — recalled from the history with Up/Down/Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N, found by the incremental (Ctrl-T) or fuzzy (Ctrl-R) history search, pasted, brought back from the external editor, or preloaded — the as-you-type hints no longer appear at its end. With hints visible, the next Up/Down press would navigate the hints instead of the history, so navigating the history quickly was impossible. The hints are shown again as soon as the line is edited. The suppression is armed before the navigation action because replxx repaints (and regenerates the hints) inside `history_move` itself, and the displayed text is additionally pinned afterwards because replxx may throttle that repaint and replay it after the key handler returns (its "rapid refresh" of e.g. a held-down Up key). Verified with a new pty regression test (`04909_client_hints_history_navigation`, 6 cases), including duplicate-history and unchanged-editor same-text redisplays; the existing `04402_clickhouse_client_autocomplete_inline_hints` (11 cases) and the hint-related expect tests still pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The command line client no longer shows the as-you-type hints on a query recalled from the history (or otherwise displayed at once, e.g. pasted), so pressing Up/Down continues to navigate the history instead of the hint list. The hints appear again as soon as the line is edited. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115065&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115065](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115065+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix gRPC and Arrow Flight listeners for wildcard listen hosts
signals.text: `gRPC` treats `::` and `0.0.0.0` as one family-agnostic wildcard: for either of them it binds a dual-stack `::` socket, and falls back to `0.0.0.0` only on a host without IPv6 (see `add_wildcard_addrs_to_server` in `contrib/grpc`). Listing both wildcard addresses in `listen_host` therefore made ClickHouse create two listeners that bind the very same socket address, and the second one either - failed with `EADDRINUSE`, because the Arrow Flight transport disables `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the exception terminated the whole server: ``` <Error> grpc: Failed to add port to server: No address added out of total 1 resolved for '0.0.0.0:9110' (Failed to add any wildcard listeners: Error in bind for address '[::]:9110': Address already in use Error in bind for address '0.0.0.0:9110': Address already in use) <Error> Application: Code: 1002. DB::Exception: Failed init Arrow Flight Server: Unknown error: Server did not start properly. ``` - or silently shared the port with the first one, because plain gRPC keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so each of the two independent servers ended up serving a random half of the connections, and a listener configured for `0.0.0.0` accepted IPv6 connections as well: ``` <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: [::]:9100 <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: 0.0.0.0:9100 LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=55)) LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=56)) ``` Only one gRPC and one Arrow Flight listener is created for a group of wildcard `listen_host` values now, which is what the transport does internally anyway. Also, `listen_try` is honored for the protocols that bind their listening socket when they are started rather than when they are created. `EADDRINUSE` from gRPC or Arrow Flight was reported from the plain `server.start()` loop, outside of the `createServer` handler that implements `listen_try`, so it was fatal even with `listen_try` (and with `listen_reuse_port`) enabled - which contradicts the documented behavior of listening to at least one of the addresses without quitting. Not addressed here: plain gRPC still keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so a gRPC port that is already taken by a different process is silently shared instead of reported. Making that consistent with `listen_reuse_port` for both gRPC and Arrow Flight is a possible follow-up. For the record, gRPC and Arrow Flight are not available as composable protocols (the `protocols` section): the composable stack is a Poco `TCPServer` with a chain of `TCPServerConnectionFactory` layers that receive an already accepted socket, while gRPC and Arrow Flight own the listening socket, the HTTP/2 framing, TLS and their own event loop, so they can neither be a layer nor sit under `tls` / `proxy1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the server failing to start when `listen_host` contains both `::` and `0.0.0.0` and `arrowflight_port` is configured, and fix two gRPC listeners silently sharing one port in the same configuration. `listen_try` now also covers the gRPC and Arrow Flight protocols, which bind their listening socket when they are started. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reload a persisted `url` table with the storage its creation selected
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix compiled `if`/`multiIf` on a negative `Time` value
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `if` and `multiIf` returning a large positive value instead of a negative one when a `Time` branch is combined with `Time64`, `DateTime` or `DateTime64` and the expression is JIT-compiled. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115381 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168 (found there in review; a separate mechanism) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103390 A negative `Time` value read through a JIT-compiled `if`/`multiIf` comes back as a huge positive number: ```sql SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-01:00:00'), toTime64('00:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(1); -- executions 1-3: -01:00:00.000 -- execution 4+: 999:59:59.000 ``` No `SETTINGS` clause is needed to hit this: `compile_expressions` defaults to `1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression` to `3`, so the 4th execution of the expression in a session silently changes the answer. `enable_time_time64_type` also defaults to `1`. The wrong value is ticks `4294963696` = `2^32 - 3600`, i.e. the negative `Int32` tick count zero-extended to 64 bits. Root cause: `typeIsSigned` in `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp` did not list the `Time` family, so the widening cast emitted by `FunctionIfBase::compileImpl` asked whether `Time` is signed, got `false`, and LLVM emitted `zext` where `sext` was required. `Time` is `DataTypeNumberBase<Int32>` and is the only member of the date/time family that widens on this path, which is why the defect is specific to it. `Time64` is included in the same predicate for correctness of the contract: `isDecimal()` matches only `TypeIndex::Decimal32..256` and so does not cover `TypeIndex::Time64` - the same reason `isDateTime64()` is listed separately. No wrong-result carrier reaches the `Time64` half today, so it is not given a test that could not fail. Validation: five wrong-result carriers plus a `Nullable(Time)` case are covered by the new test. The reference values were taken from the non-compiled path on an unpatched binary, so the oracle is independent of this change. With the predicate token removed the test fails on 7 of 13 lines; non-negative `Time`, large-negative `Time`, and `DateTime64` controls are unchanged. 50/50 runs under settings randomization pass. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1864` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Enable the consecutive-keys cache for fixed-size aggregation keys
signals.text: The `keys128` and `keys256` aggregation methods had `consecutive_keys_optimization = false`, so aggregating data whose keys arrive in long runs of equal values (e.g. anything grouped by a fixed-size key that is a prefix of the table sort order) paid a full hash-and-probe per row. Enabling the existing `LastElementCache` for these methods (including the two-level variants) skips the hash table entirely within a run, at the cost of one wide key compare per row; the aggregator's adaptive hit-rate machinery already disables the cache on random keys, verified by a random-key `keys256` microbenchmark showing no regression (3.88 s baseline vs 3.82/3.88 s). On clustered keys (runs of ~200k equal `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` values, 400M rows) this saves ~10% of aggregation CPU. Session: ad94609b-7b39-4f96-af16-7947efc50974 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Aggregation by fixed-size keys of 17-32 bytes (the `keys128`/`keys256` methods, e.g. `GROUP BY` a `UUID` or a `Tuple(UInt64, UInt64)`) now uses the consecutive-keys cache, making aggregation of sorted or clustered data up to 10% faster; the cache disables itself adaptively on random keys. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115155&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115155](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115155+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not fan out the single-row output of an aggregation without keys
signals.text: After `AggregatingStep`, the pipeline was unconditionally resized to `max_threads` output streams. For an aggregation with `GROUP BY` keys that is what enables downstream parallelism, but an aggregation without keys produces at most one row: fanning that single row out to `max_threads` streams cannot create any parallelism — the only chunk still goes to one stream — while every downstream step instantiates `max_threads` processors that are created, scheduled and profiled for nothing. `AggregatingStep::transformPipeline` now keeps a single output stream when `params.keys` is empty (the same way it already does when results must be produced in order of bucket number). For example, `EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT count() FROM t` loses the `Resize 1 → <max_threads>` node and the `× <max_threads>` fan-out of every subsequent transform (see the update of `00172_early_constant_folding`). This was found while profiling tiny instant PromQL stat queries of the shape `sum(a) / sum(b)` over `TimeSeries` tables, where the emitted SQL contains several keyless aggregations and the fan-out multiplied the pipeline size; the effect is generic and this change is independent of the PromQL transpiler. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115171 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): An aggregation without `GROUP BY` keys no longer fans its single-row output out to `max_threads` streams, so queries whose plan continues after such an aggregation get a much smaller pipeline (fewer processors to create, schedule and profile) without losing any parallelism.

signals.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115614 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies nothing is scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it populates the cache inside its own job budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits, and still looks finished because `Finish Workflow` reports success. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days. #115614 has since raised the job cap to 1800s. This adds the other half, so an overrun is a failing step naming the cause instead of a job-level SIGTERM that leaves no result: - Population is bounded, covering every subprocess it starts and not only the clone: the S3 probes and the upload are AWS client subprocesses with retried socket deadlines of minutes, measured at 182s for one call and 557s for the upload. - The bound is the smaller of the configured 1200s and what the job actually has left, since an import-time check relates two configured numbers and holds however long the preamble ran. The job authenticates unconditionally first and `GHAuth.auth` has no deadline (311s to mint a token, still running at 420s for `gh auth login`); a preamble that left nothing now fails naming the elapsed time. Bounding `GHAuth.auth` is separate, as `runner.py`, `changelog_nightly.py` and `revert_ci_regressions.py` share it. - A reserve is held back for the checks after the upload. Each step may spend its whole deadline, so the confirmatory `head-object` on a refused conditional write could get one second, turning an ordinary concurrent-writer collision into a dropped matrix. - The clone is retried, since a population failure now fails the step, as the rest of the repo already assumes. The attempts share the budget; one deadline each would bound no total. Population failure fails the step rather than reporting `OK`, since dependants clone unauthenticated and cannot reach a private submodule. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115176&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115176](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115176+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: CI: report why the LLVM coverage diff report was not generated
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 (touched the same files; closed unmerged, and it was never a fix for this) ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ci/jobs/scripts/generate_diff_coverage_report.sh` produces no report directory in four cases: no coverable C/C++ files changed, no coverage data for the changed files, current coverage empty for them, and a hard failure under `set -euo pipefail`. `llvm_coverage_job.py` inferred all four from one bit, `_diff_report_dir.exists()`, and reported three of them as "No C/C++ source files changed" at three sites. Two are green runs where C/C++ files did change, so the job states the opposite of what happened. On a tool failure it also set the `Print Uncovered Code` sub-result to `OK` for analysis that never ran. Observed on PR #115101, which changed `src/Functions/array/arrayAUC.cpp`: the `gh api` compare call returned `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, and the job made both false claims. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115101&sha=c00b1800c1fcae2cb2138af592a9b3e79b4c8275&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage The script now names its outcome in `ci/tmp/diff_outcome.txt` before every `exit 0`, and the job reports the outcome it is told plus the script's exit status. It also drops a false claim that "LBC analysis will run separately" when current coverage is empty, and echoes each `gh api` compare endpoint, since `gh` reports a failure as a bare `HTTP 404` naming no resource. A script failure still stays RED, and no currently-green outcome becomes red. One behavioural change beyond the labels: `print_uncovered_code.py` now runs only when this run produced a coverage slice holding records, so no other outcome can report an earlier run's numbers, or call changed files "nothing coverable" when only their current coverage was empty. This does not fix the 404 itself, which was environmental: it stopped with the GitHub incident of 2026-08-17 13:40Z to 21:15Z and has not recurred. `ci/tests/test_llvm_coverage_gate.py` grows from 12 to 71 cases: one per outcome, a harness running the real script under stubbed tools, and cases executing the job's own call site and each dispatch it selects. 50 fail on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115225&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115225](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115225+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1849` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: CI: do not authenticate an unused robot token in the Codex code review
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113059 The `Code Review` job died on `gh auth login` for 10 pull requests in the 24 h to 2026-08-17, losing the automated review for those heads. A fork PR cannot re-run it, so recovery needs a fresh push. ``` ERROR: Codex review failed after 3 attempts: CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'auth', 'login', '--with-token']' returned non-zero exit status 1. ``` - report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113059&sha=83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50&name_0=PR&name_1=Code%20Review - log: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/113059/83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50/code_review/job.log `_run_codex_once` authenticated a robot token before every attempt, under `check=True`, but the Codex backend never uses it: `enable_gh_auth=True` has the runner authenticate the app up front, and the prompt runs every agent `gh` call with `GH_CONFIG_DIR` unset. Across the 25 job logs that reached the agent, 246 of 246 executed `gh` calls unset it and none used the scoped robot directory, so that login could only fail the job. In those same logs `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` answered `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` on 27 of 27 attempts, the oldest on 2026-08-03, and `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-1-copilot` never did. Two robots over three attempts rotate as `[X, Y, X]`, so the healthy one gets a single attempt when the shuffle puts the dead one first, and one transient GraphQL 503 there fails the job. This removes that login and its temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR` from the Codex attempt, so it runs on the app identity it already used and retries serve agent failures. `_run_copilot_once` keeps its login, which the Copilot CLI does use. New `ci/tests/test_copilot_review_codex_auth.py`: 5 tests fail on the current code with the error above and pass here; the 2 pinning unchanged behaviour were verified by mutating the code they pin. No secret, process or sleep involved. signals.title: Remove `WasmEdge` in favor of `wasmtime`
signals.text: Removes the `WasmEdge` WebAssembly runtime, leaving `wasmtime` as the only engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime` has been the default and recommended engine, and `WasmEdge` was only reachable by explicitly setting `webassembly_udf_engine` to `wasmedge`. Keeping a second implementation of `IWasmEngine` alive costs a vendored C++ submodule (plus `spdlog`, which nothing else in the tree used), a second engine backend to maintain, and CI lanes configured to switch the server over to it. What is removed: - The `contrib/wasmedge` submodule and `contrib/wasmedge-cmake`, along with `contrib/spdlog`, which existed only to build `WasmEdge`. - `src/Interpreters/WebAssembly/WasmEdgeRuntime.{h,cpp}`, the `USE_WASMEDGE` build option and its `system.build_options` row. - `IWasmEngine::requiresFuelSpecialization`, which existed only to distinguish `WasmEdge` (no fuel specialization) from `wasmtime`. The per-fuel-mode module cache is now unconditional. - The `--wasm-engine` option of `tests/config/install.sh` and the `WasmEdge` CI job option, so the affected stateless lanes are renamed: - `amd_msan, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → `amd_msan, {parallel,sequential}` - `amd_llvm_coverage, old analyzer, s3 storage, DBReplicated, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → the same name without `WasmEdge` `webassembly_udf_engine` is kept as the engine selector; `wasmtime` is now its only accepted value, and any other value is rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` as before. Because `WasmModuleManager` is constructed eagerly during startup (`Server::main` → `Context::setUserScriptsPath` → `Context::initWasmModuleManager`), a server whose config still says `wasmedge` will refuse to start with `Unknown WebAssembly engine 'wasmedge', available engines: 'wasmtime'` rather than fail lazily on first use. Silently aliasing `wasmedge` to `wasmtime` was rejected on purpose: it would be a fallback that hides a stale config. Verified locally on an `aarch64` build: `system.build_options` reports `USE_WASMTIME = 1` with no `USE_WASMEDGE` row; all 23 stateless WebAssembly UDF tests pass (including `04259_wasm_udf_enable_fuel`, which exercises both fuel modes and therefore the module cache path simplified here); and a server configured with `wasmedge` fails startup with the message above. No test coverage is lost. `wasmtime` is disabled under MemorySanitizer (false positives from JIT-generated code), which is why the MSan lanes ran with `WasmEdge` — but every stateless test that executes a WebAssembly module is tagged `no-msan`, so those lanes exercised no WebAssembly UDF code; the option only rewrote the server config. The two `*_ast_json_*` tests that mention `LANGUAGE WASM` only round-trip the query through `parseQueryToJSON` and never instantiate a module. On the coverage lane, those tests now run against `wasmtime` instead of `WasmEdge`. On binaries where `wasmtime` cannot be built, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, `riscv64`, and any `ENABLE_RUST=0` build such as the fast test one, WebAssembly UDF support is now disabled entirely, and it fails close rather than half-working: `Context::initWasmModuleManager` does not construct a `WasmModuleManager` at all, so `system.webassembly_modules` is not attached, persisted `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE WASM` definitions are not loaded at startup, and any attempt to create or use a WebAssembly UDF is rejected with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`. The server itself starts normally, both with a clean config that enables `allow_experimental_webassembly_udf` and with persisted WebAssembly UDF definitions; a warning is written to the log. `05024_wasm_udf_without_wasmtime` asserts this invariant on every lane: `system.webassembly_modules` exists exactly when `USE_WASMTIME` is set and the setting is enabled, and `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE WASM` fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` otherwise. The `wasmedge` mentions left in `docs/reference/settings/server-settings/settings/other.mdx` and in the localized `docs/<locale>/` trees are generated output and are refreshed by the docs autogeneration workflow. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the `WasmEdge` engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime`, which has always been the default, is now the only supported value of the `webassembly_udf_engine` server setting. A server configured with `<webassembly_udf_engine>wasmedge</webassembly_udf_engine>` will not start; remove that setting or set it to `wasmtime`. On binaries where `wasmtime` is unavailable, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDFs are not available at all: the server still starts, but `system.webassembly_modules` is absent and any attempt to create or use a WebAssembly UDF fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115316&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115316](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115316+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix timezoneOffset losing the whole-day component of the UTC offset
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `timezoneOffset` (alias `timeZoneOffset`) returning an offset wrong by exactly one day for time zones whose UTC offset differs from their 1970-01-01 offset by a whole day, such as `Pacific/Kiritimati` and `Pacific/Apia` after they crossed the international date line, and for most zones before 1970. This also fixes `parseDateTime`, `parseDateTimeOrNull`, `parseDateTime64`, `parseDateTimeInJodaSyntax`, `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, `toUTCTimestamp` and `fromUTCTimestamp`, which consume that offset. Closes #115281. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281#issuecomment-5327580058. `timezoneOffset` did not read the offset, it reconstructed it as `(lut[index].date - lut[epoch].date) % 86400` plus `offset_at_start_of_epoch`. That difference is `days * 86400 - (offset_now - offset_epoch)`, so the modulo keeps only the sub-day part of the change since the epoch and discards any whole-day part; the date-line zones stayed pinned at their pre-jump offset, correct before the jump and wrong after. Separately, `%` takes the sign of the dividend, so on a pre-epoch day the remainder is negative, the `res > 43200` wrap never fired, and the result came out near `+86400` instead of a small negative offset. The fix computes the offset directly as `day_number * 86400 - lut[index].date`: local midnight is that many seconds of local time from the epoch, and `date` is the UTC instant of the same midnight. Exact for either sign, no modulo, no wrap branches. The same-day `amount_of_offset_change` correction is unchanged. All 12 in-tree call sites checked. Seven were wrong and are repaired by this one change: the function itself, the `parseDateTime` family (including a zone named in the format string), `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, and `toUTCTimestamp` / `fromUTCTimestamp`. The other five reduce the offset modulo a day (`CAST ... AS Time` / `Time64`, `localtime`), so an exact one-day error already cancelled; the test pins those as controls. Over all 597 rows of `system.time_zones` at 14 instants from 1900 to 2300, against Python `zoneinfo` as an independent oracle: 500 wrong samples across 307 zones before, 18 after, all 18 being `tzdata` differences between the bundled 2025a and the system 2026a. All 488 changed samples differ by exactly one day, so nothing sub-day moved. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Both directions through `tests/clickhouse-test`: on the base master debug snapshot (build id `09e3d57a4bbe30cd`) `01252_weird_time_zone` fails with a 39-line reference diff; with the fix (build id `485b33ed0bf6e99c`) it passes, including 50 of 50 randomized runs. `unit_tests_dbms --gtest_filter='*DateLUT*:*DateTime*:*Date*'` passes 7906 tests, so no calendar component moved. The `timezone` stateless suite passes 42 of 42. Six failures in the wider `datetime` and `extract` suites are pre-existing gaps in my local environment (no `remote()` cluster config, no parquet/iceberg fixtures, no `test.hits`) and reproduce identically on the base binary. New arms: the seven reported zones after their jump; the same zones before it and `Pacific/Chatham` (+13:45) as controls that must not move; the pre-1970 class; agreement between `parseDateTime*` and `toDateTime`; the other offset consumers; the modulo-a-day consumers as regression controls; DST transition days; agreement between the in-range and out-of-range paths; and a sweep over `system.time_zones` with no zone list hardcoded, comparing the reported offset to rendering the instant as local text and reading it back as UTC. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115332&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115332](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115332+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1888` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, event_date, event_time, key`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1893` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not let SET <name> = DEFAULT bypass the settings constraints
signals.text: `SET <name> = DEFAULT` resets a setting rather than assigning to it, so it does not produce a `SettingChange` and never reached `SettingsConstraints`. Any constraint could therefore be escaped by resetting the setting instead of assigning to it: ```sql CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE p SETTINGS max_query_size = 1000 MAX 1000; SET max_query_size = 2000; -- SETTING_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, as expected SET max_query_size = DEFAULT; -- silently restored the default of 262144 ``` A `CONST` constraint was just as escapable, and so was readonly mode, which is enforced by the same check: ```sql SET readonly = 2; SET readonly = 0; -- READONLY, as expected SET readonly = DEFAULT; -- silently left readonly mode ``` This describes the reset as the change it effectively is — to the value declared in the source code, which is what `Context::resetSettingsToDefaultValue` restores — and runs the usual check on it before anything is applied, so that a violation leaves the whole statement without effect. The in-query `SETTINGS <name> = DEFAULT` form goes through the same interpreter and is covered too. A reset that does not change the value is still allowed, because the check drops changes whose new value equals the current one. Resetting a setting that was never touched therefore keeps working under a `CONST` constraint and in readonly mode — which is what CI profiles that pin a setting to its declared default rely on (`max_parser_backtracks` in `limit-recursion-settings.xml`, for example). Settings without a declared default are unaffected: a custom setting is dropped rather than reset and cannot carry a constraint, and an unknown name stays silently ignored. The client only mirrors the reset into its own settings when the server accepted the statement, so its view does not drift. One consequence worth calling out: a profile that caps `max_threads` below the machine's core count now rejects `SET max_threads = DEFAULT`, because the declared default resolves to `auto(<cores>)`. That is the intended reading of the constraint, but it means the CI profiles that cap `max_threads` at 128 would reject that reset on a machine with more than 128 cores. Verified locally against a build of this change: the four rejection paths above are rejected, the rejected statement leaves the value alone, and the no-op reset, custom-setting reset and unknown-setting reset all keep working. `04202_set_default_preserves_max_threads_auto` and `04078_settings_constraints_compatibility_const` still pass, and a sweep of every stateless test that uses `= DEFAULT` plus every test whose name mentions constraints/readonly/settings profiles produced no constraint or readonly error attributable to this change. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115328 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a bypass of settings constraints: `SET <name> = DEFAULT` reset a setting without checking the constraints from the user's profile, so a `MIN`/`MAX`/`CONST` constraint could be escaped by resetting the setting instead of assigning to it, and a session could leave readonly mode with `SET readonly = DEFAULT`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115334&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115334](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115334+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signals.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The recovery is applied both by the background streaming task and by an in-flight direct `SELECT`, whose source retains its consumer until the query finishes. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. signals.title: Use the text index when a tokenizer argument matches the index tokenizer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `text` index is now used for `hasAnyTokens`, `hasAllTokens` and `hasPhrase` called with an explicit tokenizer argument, when that argument denotes the same tokenizer as the index and the index has no `preprocessor` or `postprocessor`. Previously the three-argument form always fell back to a full scan. Closes #115275. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108808 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107186 `MergeTreeIndexConditionText::traverseAtomNode` rejected any function node that was not binary before it looked at the function name, so a three-argument `hasAnyTokens` / `hasAllTokens` / `hasPhrase` never reached `isSupportedFunction` (which already lists all three). The predicate became an unknown atom: no granule pruning and no direct read. This mattered because the three-argument form is the documented workaround for #108808, so users of a non-`splitByNonAlpha` tokenizer had no option that was both correct and indexed. The gate now admits three arguments for those three functions when the argument's tokenizer canonicalizes to the index tokenizer. Equality compares `ITokenizer::getDescription()`, which is the form the direct-read pass already synthesizes for the two-argument case, so registered aliases and spelling variants compare equal while parameters still discriminate (`ngrams(3)` is not `ngrams(4)`). Everything else keeps full-scanning, by design and per @ rschu1ze's ruling on the issue: a different tokenizer, a non-constant or invalid argument, and an index carrying a `preprocessor` or `postprocessor` option (there the index stores tokens of a transformed value that the argument's bare tokenizer never produces, so the two cannot answer the same predicate). No error is raised on a mismatch. `hasPhrase` is included at @CurtizJ's request (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275#issuecomment-5328448695). The direct-read pass is kept argument-count-preserving: it now assigns the tokenizer argument in place when one is already present rather than appending, because that pass can legitimately run over the same node twice and would otherwise build a four-argument call. `02346_text_index_function_hasPhrase{,_positions}` asserted the old full-scan behavior for this exact case. Those sections are retitled and regenerated, and a mismatching-tokenizer sibling case is added at the same site so the full-scan boundary keeps a pinned oracle. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115348&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115348](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115348+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a notebook mode to the Web UI
signals.text: Adds a notebook mode to the Web SQL UI (`/play`): a tab can become an ordered sequence of cells, each either a query with its own result or a block of Markdown text — the shape of document Jupyter, Observable, Hex and Deepnote use, and for the same purpose: keeping a chain of queries, and the reasoning between them, on one page. ## How it works A tab starts as a single query cell and looks exactly as it always has — no headers, no cell chrome, no notebook. Once a query has produced a result, a large muted `[+]` appears under it and expands into the two kinds of cell that can be added, query or text. Adding the second cell is what turns notebook mode on, and it is per tab: one tab can be a notebook while another stays a plain single-query editor, and each tab remembers its own notebook across reloads. From two cells on, each cell gets a header with its position and kind (`1. Query`, `2. Text`) and the editing actions: run, edit, insert a cell before, move up/down, delete. There is still exactly one query editor on the page — the full one, with its highlighting backdrop, autocompletion and query-parameter inputs. In notebook mode it is docked into whichever query cell is active, and shown only while it has the focus; as soon as focus leaves, that cell collapses to its query on a single line, syntax highlighted, whitespace runs reduced to one space, fading out on the right. The Run / progress / copy / download row docks under the query being edited, between it and its result, and appears and disappears with the editor. Results are more compact: a smaller font with the cell padding scaled to match, and a table of at most a quarter of the viewport that is its own scroll container on both axes, so its (thin) scrollbars sit at its own edges and a long or wide result neither pushes the notebook down the page nor widens it. Results and Markdown editors can be resized by dragging their bottom edge, as the query editor already could. A text cell shows its Markdown source with the markers highlighted while it is being edited, and the rendered result once editing finishes. Raw HTML is escaped and link targets are restricted to `http`, `https`, `mailto` and relative URLs. ## Implementation The query text, parameters and result snapshot moved from the tab to a cell. `tab.query` / `tab.result` / `tab.resultEl` and the rest are now accessors onto the cell the editor is docked in, so the editor, history, URL and persistence code is unchanged and always means "the cell in front of the user". A run captures its own cell, so moving on to another cell mid-run does not redirect the response. The Logs/Metrics view and the resource meters follow the cell whose result they describe. The whole notebook is persisted in IndexedDB alongside the rest of the workspace, and history entries record the cell they belong to so Back/Forward cannot push one cell's query into another. A tab holding a single cell renders exactly as before — verified by screenshot diff against `master`: 51 pixels differ, all on one row, all by 1 in a single channel. ## Testing Driven in headless Chrome against a local server: cell creation and deletion, moving and inserting cells, collapsing and expanding, per-tab independence, tab duplicate/close with a docked editor, query parameters inside a cell, per-cell errors, reload restore from IndexedDB, "Run all" inside a cell, the Logs and Metrics views per cell, column and result resizing, the theme switch and download menu inside the docked Run row, Markdown rendering and backdrop alignment, and light and dark themes. Two pre-existing issues were fixed along the way: the download drop-down positioned itself without accounting for `#main`'s scroll offset, and the `#run` submit button needed `form="controls"` once it could be moved out of the form's subtree. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a notebook mode to the Web UI (`/play`). After a query is run, a `[+]` button under the result adds further cells, each either a query with its own result or a block of Markdown text, turning the tab into a notebook in the style of Jupyter or Observable. Cells can be run, reordered, inserted and deleted individually; the query editor collapses to a single line when it is not focused, results are bounded and scroll inside themselves, and the whole notebook is restored on reload. Notebook mode is per tab, so a tab that has only one cell looks and behaves exactly as before. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115378&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115378](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115378+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a `bucketed` schema for `system.metric_log`: a single Map column with Enum keys and 128 buckets
signals.text: Adds a new `schema_type` option `bucketed` for `system.metric_log` (the default `wide` and the `transposed` schemas are unchanged): ```xml <metric_log> <schema_type>bucketed</schema_type> </metric_log> ``` With this schema, all profile events and current metrics are stored in a single `metrics` column of type `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)`, where the `Enum16` value is the global metric index and zero values are not stored (a lookup of a missing key in a `Map` returns `0`). The default table definition uses the bucketed `Map` serialization with a constant number of 128 buckets: ``` SETTINGS map_serialization_version = 'with_buckets', map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts = 'basic', max_buckets_in_map = 128, map_buckets_strategy = 'constant', map_buckets_min_avg_size = 0 ``` Parts created by inserts keep the basic serialization to avoid creating many small files on every flush; merged parts are always split into 128 buckets. Every metric is also exposed through an `ALIAS` column, e.g. `ProfileEvent_Query UInt64 ALIAS metrics['ProfileEvent_Query']`, so all queries, dashboards, and tests written for the `wide` schema continue to work. Reading a single metric goes through the `Map` key subcolumn (`metrics.key_ProfileEvent_Query`), which reads only the bucket containing the key: in a local test it reads ~100 times less data than reading the whole map (616 vs 60716 bytes on the same rows). Supporting changes: - `arrayElement` on a `Map` with `Enum` keys now accepts the string name of the enum value (`m['name']`): the index is cast to the key type, so an unknown name throws the `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM` exception, while a name that is in the `Enum` but absent from the map returns the default value. This previously threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. - The rewrite of `m['key']` to a key subcolumn in `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` now supports `Enum`-keyed maps indexed by the name of the enum value, so both the aliases and ad-hoc queries prune buckets. - System logs can declare additional default engine settings via `getDefaultEngineSettings`, merged with the `settings` from the server configuration when no custom `engine` is specified. - An unknown `metric_log.schema_type` value is now rejected with an error instead of silently disabling the table. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `bucketed` schema type for `system.metric_log`, which stores all metrics in a single `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)` column using the bucketed `Map` serialization with 128 buckets, plus a per-metric `ALIAS` column for compatibility: the table consists of a few columns instead of thousands, zero values are not stored, and reading a single metric reads only one of the 128 buckets. In addition, a `Map` with `Enum` keys can now be indexed by the string name of the enum value, e.g. `map['name']`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115380&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115380](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115380+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Query cache on disk, backed by the filesystem cache
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361 The query cache can now additionally store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache (an entry of the `filesystem_caches` section of the server configuration), selected per query with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`. Compared to the in-memory query cache, this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Design, following the RFC in the issue: - The entries are ordinary filesystem cache entries, indistinguishable from other data in the same filesystem cache: they are not held from deletion, they are evicted by the same rules, and there are no specific limits on their total size or number other than the limits of the filesystem cache itself. The keys are hashed with a salt so that they cannot intersect with other keys in the filesystem cache. - No extra in-memory state is kept: all metadata needed to validate an entry (TTL, user id, roles, the shared flag) is serialized into the entry itself, followed by the result payload in `Native` format, compressed with the codec from the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_codec` (default `ZSTD(3)`; reading is independent of the setting because the compressed frames are self-describing). - The on-disk cache works independently of the in-memory cache and can separately be enabled for reads and/or writes with the new settings `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk` and `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk` (both `true` by default, activated by setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`). If both caches are enabled for reads, the lookup is attempted first from memory and only on a miss from disk. If both caches are enabled for writes, the result is written to both. A result served from memory is not written to disk. - A stale (expired TTL), partially evicted, corrupt, or inaccessible (another user's non-shared) entry is treated as a cache miss; stale entries are overwritten on the next write. - Introspection of the on-disk entries in `system.query_cache` is out of scope, per the issue. New profile events: `QueryCacheOnDiskHits`, `QueryCacheOnDiskMisses`, `QueryCacheOnDiskReadBytes`, `QueryCacheOnDiskWrittenBytes`. Tests: `05019_query_cache_on_disk_local` proves persistence across process restarts (separate `clickhouse-local` invocations sharing one filesystem cache directory, including a cached non-deterministic result, TTL expiry, and disabled reads); `05020_query_cache_on_disk` covers the server path with user isolation, sharing via `query_cache_share_between_users`, and error cases (unknown cache name, invalid codec). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The query cache can now store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache: this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Select the filesystem cache with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`; see also the new settings `query_cache_on_disk_codec`, `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk`, and `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk`. Closes [#115361](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115382&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115382](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115382+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
