signals.title: Fix optimize_functions_to_subcolumns rewriting onto the wrong subcolumn
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115632 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115394 `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrites a function to a subcolumn of its argument (`length(arr)` to `arr.size0`, `isNull(n)` to `n.null`, `mapKeys(m)` to `m.keys`, ...) and hardcodes the type that subcolumn has. It only checked that a subcolumn with that name exists, which is wrong in two independent ways, both giving wrong results. A `Tuple` element or a `JSON` path can claim the name with the same type, and declaration order decides which one a read returns: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (c Tuple(`a.size` UInt64, `a` String)) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO t VALUES ((99, 'abc')); SELECT length(c.a) FROM t SETTINGS optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 0; -- 3 correct SELECT length(c.a) FROM t SETTINGS optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1; -- 99 wrong ``` The same shape affects `empty`, `notEmpty`, `isNull`, `isNotNull`, `count`, `mapKeys`, `mapValues`, `mapContains` and `m['key']`. An enclosing `Nullable` wraps the subcolumn without changing which substream it is - `c.a` is a bare `Array` while `c.a.size0` is `Nullable(UInt64)`, because `Array` cannot be inside `Nullable`. Only `length` lacked the guard the other rewrites already had: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (c Nullable(JSON(`a` Array(Int64)))) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t VALUES ('{"a":[1,2]}'), (NULL); SELECT length(c.a) FROM t SETTINGS optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 0; -- 2, 0 correct SELECT length(c.a) FROM t SETTINGS optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1; -- 2, \N wrong ``` To tell these apart, subcolumn resolution now reports the substreams path identifying the resolved subcolumn, not just its data (`getSubcolumnData` becomes `getSubcolumnInfo`). Subcolumns resolved from the data get a synthesized path too, so all of them are identifiable the same way. The optimizer asks the serialization owning the substream whether the resolved subcolumn is the one the rewrite means, and additionally requires the exact type; neither check catches the other's case. Subsumes `subcolumnIsNullableInStorage` and `nestedTypeHasNullSubcolumn`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results from `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns`. A `Tuple` element or a `JSON` path named like an automatic subcolumn claimed it, so for example `length(c.a)` on ``Tuple(`a.size` UInt64, `a` String)`` returned the element instead of the length; `empty`, `notEmpty`, `isNull`, `isNotNull`, `count`, `mapKeys`, `mapValues`, `mapContains` and `m['key']` were affected the same way. Separately, `length` on an `Array` or `Map` inside a `Nullable` (for example ``Nullable(JSON(`a` Array(Int64)))``) returned NULL instead of 0 for a NULL row. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115777&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115777](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115777+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Drop registry files from the `Parser memory check` digest
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115766 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115221 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104631 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py::test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data` fails on current master, so the `CI Tests` job is red for every pull request that touches `ci/`. The test (added in #115221) asserts that a registry-only edit schedules no build; `Parser memory check` (added to the PR workflow in #104631) digests `ci/defs/defs.py`, `ci/defs/job_configs.py` and `ci/workflows/pull_request.py` while requiring `CLICKHOUSE_EXAMPLES`, so a registry-only edit marks it affected and the rescue pass in `_filter_unaffected_jobs` schedules `Build (arm_release)` just to produce the artifact. Each PR was green on its own — #115221's branch predates #104631's merge, and #104631 could not run the not-yet-existing test — the combination on master is what breaks. Fix: drop the registry paths from the job's `digest_config`, keeping its own script and `utils/parser-memory-profiler/`. No other job digests the registry, so this also restores the convention. `python3 -m pytest ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py` passes with the change (37/37; the failing test plus the rest of the module). First observed in #115036: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=1c383b2ae000d256fc2e04e60b4b4b5ddab93b96&name_0=PR&name_1=CI%20Tests ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115783&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115783](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115783+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Per-shard OpenTelemetry spans for distributed SELECT queries
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114813 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115619 Every remote shard read of a distributed `SELECT` is now covered by a span that identifies the query fragment. Until now the trace of a distributed query showed the remote side (`TCPHandler`, remote `query` span) but nothing on the initiator identified *which shard of which cluster* a subtree belonged to, or where the query was actually sent. On the asynchronous connection paths the span covering the read context fiber becomes the per-shard fragment span renamed to `RemoteQueryExecutor::execute`. The synchronous sending path gets an equivalent `RemoteQueryExecutor::sendQuery` span. * `clickhouse.cluster`, `clickhouse.shard_num` — filled on the classic distributed path (`ReadFromRemote`) * `clickhouse.processed_stage` — the stage requested from the shard * `clickhouse.query_id`, `clickhouse.initial_query_id` * `clickhouse.target_host` — the established connection addresses, added once known Implementation: * `AsyncTaskExecutor` accepts initial span attributes and provides a thread-safe `addSpanAttribute` for attributes that become known only during task execution. * Attributes are only built when the query is traced; when tracing is off the cost is an empty vector per executor. * New test `05025_opentelemetry_remote_query_executor_shard_spans` checks both shards' spans and all attributes over `test_cluster_two_shards` for all combinations of `async_socket_for_remote`/`async_query_sending_for_remote`, and pins the attribute flush on cancellation (`KILL QUERY` while the fiber is suspended). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/uidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Distributed `SELECT` queries now produce a per-shard OpenTelemetry span (`RemoteQueryExecutor::execute`, or `RemoteQueryExecutor::sendQuery` on the synchronous path) with attributes identifying the fragment: `clickhouse.cluster`, `clickhouse.shard_num`, `clickhouse.processed_stage`, `clickhouse.query_id`, `clickhouse.initial_query_. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115784&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115784](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115784+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not run the server-side AST fuzzer on a collaborative worker context
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113729 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Duplicate announcement received for replica number N`) when the server-side AST fuzzer is enabled with `ast_fuzzer_runs`. The fuzzer re-ran a query on a node acting as a parallel replicas participant or a cluster function worker, so the fuzzed query announced itself to the initiator's reading coordinator a second time under the same replica number. ### Description `executeASTFuzzerQueries` runs as a query-finish callback and re-executes mutated copies of the query that just finished. When that query was a collaborative worker for another node, its context carries a borrowed replica identity and a live coordination channel back to the initiator: `merge_tree_all_ranges_callback` plus `number_of_current_replica` for a parallel replicas participant, `next_task_callback` for a cluster function worker. `Context::createCopy` copies both and `resetInputCallbacks` does not clear them, so a fuzzed query announces again under the same replica number and the coordinator rejects the second arrival with a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. `e8194c7dc437eb0` already pins `allow_experimental_parallel_reading_from_replicas = 0` on the fuzz context for this reason. That pin is a setting value written before the fuzzed query's own settings are applied, so the fuzzed query re-enables it, and not through one bounded route: its own `SETTINGS` clause, the alias `enable_parallel_replicas`, a `SETTINGS profile = ...` that never names the setting, or the inner `SELECT`'s clause applied later on a derived context. This change keeps the pin and decides one level up instead, from a field already on the context, so nothing has to propagate. The initiating client query is still fuzzed, so query shapes stay covered, and behaviour changes only when `ast_fuzzer_runs > 0`, which is off by default. The new counter `ASTFuzzerSkippedCollaborativeWorker` makes the skip observable; the test asserts it rises for a worker and stays put for an ordinary query whose own fuzz runs still execute. Also noticed, not the cause here and not addressed: `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:731` skips its plain-MergeTree guard for a `StorageMaterializedView` destination, which reports neither predicate. Reported by CI: [Stress test (arm_tsan) on 858261cb](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115681&sha=858261cb4bb9e68db7eeed82dba277592650339f&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), and on four other unrelated pull requests across three sanitizer builds in eleven days. The linked issue reports the same message through the local-plan callback, not the wire packet path: related, different defect. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115786&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115786](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115786+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support the plan-based parallel replicas in automatic parallel replicas
signals.text: Automatic parallel replicas builds a plan with parallel replicas, finds the node that would sit at the top of the plan executed on the replicas, and instruments the corresponding node of the single-node plan to collect runtime dataflow statistics. `findTopNodeOfReplicasPlan` located that node by matching the branch that reads from the other replicas against `ReadFromParallelRemoteReplicasStep`. With `parallel_replicas_plan_based` that branch is a `ReadFromParallelReplicas` step, which ships a serialized plan fragment instead of a query. The rest of the plan is shaped exactly the same - a `Union` of the local branch and the branch reading from the other replicas - but the top node was never found, so no statistics were collected and automatic parallel replicas never enabled parallel replicas for any query. This recognizes both steps. Verified against a local server with `parallel_replicas_plan_based=1`: 10 of the 12 `*_autopr_*` stateless tests that fail with the plan-based implementation as the default now pass. The remaining two are left for a follow-up and keep the previous behaviour of skipping the optimization: - `04341_autopr_mode1_apply_join` - with join runtime filters the plan-based local branch carries an extra pass-through `Expression`, so the node hashes of the two plans differ and no match is found. - `03634_autopr_input_bytes_estimation_compact` - for a plain read the plan fragment is the reading step itself, which cannot estimate the number of bytes sent to the initiator. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112351 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Automatic parallel replicas can now collect runtime statistics and enable parallel replicas for supported queries when `parallel_replicas_plan_based` is enabled.

signals.title: Choose IEJoin key conditions by estimated selectivity
signals.text: When the `JOIN ON` expression contains more inequality conditions between the joined tables than the two the IEJoin algorithm uses as its key conditions, pick the two with the smallest estimated joint selectivity instead of the first two in syntax order. The conditions not chosen as keys are evaluated per pair of rows passing both key conditions (a filter over the join result for `ALL INNER JOIN`, a residual condition inside the operator for the other kinds), so the least selective key pair minimizes that work: on an adversarial three-condition query (50k×50k rows, marginal selectivities 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.0005) the planner-chosen order now runs in ~0.015 s instead of ~5.5 s, matching a manually reordered `ON` clause. Selectivity is estimated from the column min/max statistics (the `basic` type, collected by default) under a uniformity assumption. To make the estimates reachable at planning time: `ColumnStats` now carries `min_value`/`max_value`/`null_fraction` (resolving the TODO in `ConditionSelectivityEstimator.h`), `remapColumnStats` keeps them only across value-preserving hops, and `estimateReadRowsCount` is declared in `joinOrder.h` and called on the join inputs. Conditions reading the same column on one side (the band shape `lo < x AND x < hi`) are correlated, so such pairs are scored with the sharp Frechet bound `P(A) + P(B) - 1` instead of the independence product, which also preserves the band-join fast path. When any estimate is unavailable (no statistics, `use_statistics = 0`, expression keys, non-MergeTree inputs), the previous syntax order is kept. Pairwise scoring is capped at 64 candidates; beyond that the two smallest marginal selectivities are chosen in linear time. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The IEJoin algorithm now chooses which two `JOIN ON` inequality conditions to use as its key conditions by their estimated selectivity from the column min/max statistics, instead of taking the first two in syntax order. The remaining conditions are evaluated per candidate pair, so picking the most selective pair can speed up such joins by orders of magnitude. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115790&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115790](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115790+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114999 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Mask the `aws_external_id` setting of the `DataLakeCatalog` database engine in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` and `system.databases.engine_full`. It was previously printed in plaintext, unlike the other AWS credential settings. Closes: #114999 ### Description `aws_external_id` was missing from `DataLake::SETTINGS_TO_HIDE`, so any user able to run `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` or read `system.databases` saw it verbatim at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Every other credential setting of the engine was already masked. Root cause: `ASTSetQuery::formatImpl` consults that map to decide whether to print a masking rule instead of the value; the key was absent, so the fallthrough printed the secret. This adds the missing entry. Both surfaces share one seam (`StorageSystemDatabases` builds `engine_full` with the same formatter `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` uses), and the map also backs `ASTSetQuery::hasSecretParts`, so log masking is covered too. The stored metadata and replicated-DDL propagation format with secrets shown, so the database still authenticates after a restart. The codebase already classifies the value as a secret: `external_id` is a member of `s3_secret_keys` in `src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.h`, whose comment calls it the shared secret of the assume-role triple while `role_arn` and `role_session_name` are non-secret identifiers that stay visible. So the identical value was masked in the inline `s3()` form and leaked only here. `aws_role_arn` and `aws_role_session_name` are therefore left visible, and the new test pins them visible so a future over-masking change fails. Validation: new stateless test `05030_datalake_catalog_hide_aws_external_id.sh` asserts `[HIDDEN]` at the default and the true value still retrievable with `clickhouse-format --show_secrets`, so the fix redacts rather than destroys. It fails on master and passes here; 50 randomized runs of it and of the neighbouring `04401` pass. Both real surfaces were checked directly in both directions. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115791&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115791](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115791+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: TopN dynamic filtering for reading Parquet files
signals.text: Extends the `ORDER BY <column> LIMIT n` dynamic-filtering optimization (`use_top_k_dynamic_filtering`, previously `MergeTree`-only) to Parquet reads through the `file` table function and the `File` engine. `tryOptimizeTopK` now also matches sources that opt in via `SourceStepWithFilterBase::supportsTopKDynamicFilter` and hands them a `FormatTopKFilterInfo` (the sort column plus the shared `TopKThresholdTracker` the sorting transforms publish into) through `FormatFilterInfo`. The native Parquet reader uses it twice: - as the first PREWHERE step, an internal `__topKFilter(sort_column)` drops rows that cannot enter the top-K heap; because it runs first, the columns of the later filter steps and of the output are then read only for the surviving rows, with whole pages skipped where possible; - right before a row group's column data would be read (the latest point with a threshold at hand), the row group is skipped entirely when the sort column's min/max statistics prove that none of its rows can improve the heap. The statistics are used only when they prove the chunk has no nulls, since they describe non-null values only and null rows may themselves belong to the top-K. Both uses only ever remove rows the sort + limit above would discard, so they compose with any `WHERE` / `PREWHERE` in any order, and a stale (not yet tightened) threshold is always safe. The existing gates apply unchanged: `query_plan_max_limit_for_top_k_optimization`, the `Dynamic`/`Variant` exclusion, and the variable-length opt-in (`use_top_k_dynamic_filtering_for_variable_length_types`). Measured on the ClickBench `t3a.small` emulation (2 pinned cores, 2 GiB cgroup, file in page cache): | query | before | after | |---|---|---| | Q23 `SELECT * FROM hits WHERE URL LIKE '%google%' ORDER BY EventTime LIMIT 10` | 36.4 s | 7.4 s | | Q24 `SELECT SearchPhrase FROM hits WHERE SearchPhrase <> '' ORDER BY EventTime LIMIT 10` | 3.2 s | 2.4 s | | Q26 `... ORDER BY EventTime, SearchPhrase LIMIT 10` | 2.7 s | 1.7 s | On a file sorted by the sort column (1M rows, 100 row groups, 2 threads), `ORDER BY k LIMIT 5` reads 43608 rows instead of 1000000 — with more reading threads the reduction is smaller because more row groups pass the pre-read checkpoint before the first threshold is published. Object storage reads (`s3`, Iceberg) can adopt the same channel as a follow-up: their `FormatFilterInfo` is rebuilt per file for schema evolution and lazy materialization, which needs separate plumbing. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114262 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Queries with `ORDER BY <column> LIMIT n` over Parquet files (the `file` table function and the `File` engine) now use TopN dynamic filtering (setting `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering`): rows that cannot enter the top-K are filtered inside the reader before the remaining columns are read, and whole row groups are skipped when their min/max statistics prove they cannot contribute. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115798&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115798](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115798+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not strand processors queued for removal in `ExecutingGraph`
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115625 Processor removal in `ExecutingGraph` recently became deferred: `updatePipeline` only records `update.to_remove` into a pending group, and `updateNode` retires that group once every processor in it reports `Finished`. Two paths leave a recorded group behind, so its processors stay in the pipeline until the whole query is destroyed: - `updatePipeline` records the group and then returns `Cancelled`, which makes `updateNode` return before it reaches the code that retires groups; - the retiring code handles a single group per prepared node, so a backlog can outlive the last `updateNode` call. This change retires every group that is ready instead of just one, and also retires them on the way out when `updatePipeline` does not return `Done`. This is what `Processors.UpdatePipelineMultipleCoordinatorsMultithreaded` caught on master — it cancels the executor while 16 coordinators are cycling, so one of them gets its removal stranded and an extra source is still alive at the end of the test: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b16561cc816cf56cadd0c35ed9ad48964ad7758d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%29 ``` src/Processors/tests/gtest_update_pipeline.cpp:504 Expected: (alive) <= (1u), actual: 2 vs 1 ``` The existing test only reproduces this rarely, so a deterministic one is added: `Processors.UpdatePipelineRemovalIsNotStrandedByCancellation` cancels the pipeline from inside `prepare`, so the `updatePipeline` that retires the source is exactly the one that observes the cancellation. It fails before this change and passes after it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115800&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115800](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115800+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a maintained ReadPlan to the experimental ReaderExecutor
signals.text: Introduces a maintained `ReadPlan` to the experimental `ReaderExecutor` (gated by `use_reader_executor`, default off). Instead of re-resolving the cache chain on every read window, the executor resolves the residency of a look-ahead span once, holds the pinned hit-readers and miss-writers across serves, and answers per offset which tier serves it - coalescing consecutive misses (across cells and tiers) into one source read, capped at the window, that populates every populating tier. The plan grows on the right (`extend`) and retires the consumed prefix on the left (`retireBefore`) as the cursor advances. Serve semantics are unchanged (the existing executor tests pass); only the resolve is now held across windows instead of repeated per window. This is also the structure the later prefetch slice drives: it fills the same held writers ahead of the cursor without changing this interface. Details: - **Look-ahead** is configurable via the experimental `reader_executor_plan_look_ahead` setting (default 16 MiB); `resolve` is a cheap probe, so looking ahead costs no I/O. The plan is refilled in batches: it grows only once less than half the look-ahead remains ahead of the cursor, then resolves back to the full length. - **Concurrent downloads** are handled in one pass over the tiers (fastest-first): a segment another query committed since `resolve` is served from cache; a segment a concurrent downloader currently leads is waited on once (`CacheWriter::waitAndRead`) and served from cache if it lands; otherwise this reader takes the download role and the source fetch populates the tier. Only after the pass, if nothing served the head, is the coalesced miss run read from source. A single iteration - no waiting/reclaim loop. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `ReaderExecutor` now resolves cache residency once into a maintained read plan (configurable via `reader_executor_plan_look_ahead`) instead of re-resolving on every read window.

signals.title: Parquet: fuse dictionary-index decoding with the dictionary gather
signals.text: Dictionary-encoded Parquet data pages were decoded in two passes: expand the RLE/bit-packed indexes into a temporary `UInt32` column, then gather the dictionary values at those indexes into the output column (`Dictionary::index`). In `hits.parquet`, ~74% of all values sit in RLE runs of a repeated index (average run length 91 — the stats are quoted in a comment in the decoder), so most of that work was expanding runs into explicit indexes only to gather the very same dictionary value again and again — plus a full write + read pass over the temporary indexes column for everything else. This fuses the two passes (`PageDecoder::decodeAndIndex`, overridden by `BitPackedRLEDecoder`): - an RLE run becomes a single dictionary lookup and a bulk fill of the value; - bit-packed runs are unpacked into a small stack buffer — with the bounds check hoisted out of the inner loop to once per batch, so the loop body is branch-free — and gathered from there; - `Mode::Column` dictionaries keep the old path (`IColumn::index` needs the indexes as a column anyway), as does anything else through the base-class fallback in the reader. On ClickBench Q3 (`SELECT SUM(AdvEngineID), COUNT(*), AVG(ResolutionWidth) FROM hits`) over `hits.parquet` on 2 cores this is 21% faster (0.46 s → 0.36 s, best of 3, interleaved A/B of otherwise identical builds); in the profile, the dictionary gather that took 27% of the query's CPU disappears, closing about half of the gap to DuckDB on this query (0.25 s). Results are bit-identical on checksums over seven dictionary-encoded `hits` columns (including strings) and on nullable dictionary-encoded columns; the Parquet dictionary-filter, prewhere, filter-pushdown and preserve-order stateless tests all pass. The existing `clickbench_parquet_short.xml` performance test covers these query shapes. Profiling context, for the record: after this change the remaining CPU of such queries is snappy decompression, the (now leaner) bit-unpacking, and the aggregation itself. Possible future refinements: SIMD bit-unpacking and batching the per-run `insertRawUninitialized` bookkeeping. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reading dictionary-encoded Parquet data got faster: the dictionary indexes are now decoded and resolved to values in one fused pass, turning runs of a repeated value into bulk fills instead of per-row gathers (~20% faster scans of dictionary-encoded numeric columns). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115819&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115819](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115819+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Gate the release_base perf comparison on the delta to the previous master run
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115803 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115804 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115805 The `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, N/6)` checks compare each master commit against the build at the latest release branch point, so every performance change since that point accumulates in the report. With the absolute slower-count gate (more than `SLOWER_QUERIES_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 10` per shard), the check inevitably drifts into permanent red: shard `3/6` failed on all 198 master commits of the past week (28 accumulated slower queries), was red for the entire previous release cycle as well, and only went green for two weeks after the 26.7 branch cut reset the baseline. A permanently red check points at no specific commit and trains everyone to ignore it — meanwhile real regressions (see the linked issues) land silently because the per-commit `master_head` mode rarely exceeds 10 slower queries for a single PR. This PR changes the `release_base` gate to fail only on a large delta to the previous master commit: the job fetches the previous valid master run's result from S3 (walking `master_track_commits_sha`, skipping runs that produced no report or ended with errors) and fails when the slower count grew by more than `SLOWER_QUERIES_DELTA_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 5`. Red now blames the commit that introduced the regression and recovers on the next commit by itself. If no previous run can be found, the gate falls back to the old absolute threshold. The reported message is extended with the delta, e.g. `5 too long, 24 faster, 28 slower; delta vs prev master run (5ad58af3): +2`. The `master_head` mode keeps the absolute gate. The threshold is based on 10 days of master runs: run-to-run count-delta noise is p90 ≤ 3 per shard (max 3–7 outside of regression landings), while real regression landings showed +8..+16. Replayed over 58 real master runs of the always-red shard `3/6`: 57 turn green and the only `FAIL` lands exactly on the commit that introduced the `direct_dictionary` regression (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115803). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115821&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115821](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115821+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL: speed up duplicate series zero scan
signals.text: ### TL;DR Use `memoryIsZero` to return early for all-zero PromQL condition vectors. Keep the existing scalar fallback for other values. The local 10M-row microbenchmark is up to 26.8x faster. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up duplicate-series checks for all-zero PromQL condition vectors. ### Summary PromQL duplicate-series detection calls `timeSeriesThrowDuplicateSeriesIf` with a condition column. The function used to scan the whole column value by value even when every value was zero. This change uses `memoryIsZero` as an all-zero check. If the bytes are all zero, the function returns immediately. Otherwise, it keeps the existing scalar scan. This preserves the behavior for non-zero values and special floating-point values such as `-0.0`. ### Benchmark Local arm64 macOS. 10M preallocated values. Median of 7 runs. The old path is the existing scalar scan. | Input | Old path | New path | Speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | UInt8, all zero | 7.393 ms | 0.275 ms | 26.8x | | Float64, all zero | 3.442 ms | 2.246 ms | 1.53x | | Float64, `-0.0` | 3.676 ms | 3.440 ms | 1.07x | The `-0.0` case does not take the early return because its sign bit is set. It still uses the scalar fallback and returns the same result. ### Tests - Add all-zero vector coverage to `03779_time_series_tags_functions`. - Add `-0.0` fallback coverage. - Add non-zero vector error coverage. - Add a performance fixture for 1M and 10M rows. - Compile the changed C++ translation unit. - Run `git diff --check`.

signals.title: Warn on low sccache hit rate in build job
signals.text: The CI build job runs `sccache --show-stats` after every build, but the hit rate was only printed to the raw job log — a degraded or stale compiler cache that silently turned a build nearly cold was invisible in the CI report. This adds a non-blocking workflow warning when the post-build sccache hit rate is below 40%, so a low-hit cache is surfaced for investigation without blocking merge, as requested in the issue. The rate is parsed from `sccache --show-stats --stats-format json`. Builds with no cached compilations (cold cache) and cache-warmup builds, whose hit rate is expected to be near zero, are skipped, and any parsing failure is non-fatal so the check can never fail an already-green build. signals.title: Install the test configs for real in the CFI classification guard
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115591 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113107 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ci/tests/test_cfi_not_a_sanitizer_build.py` did not run `tests/config/install.sh`: it `eval`ed a fragment cut out with `sed -n '/^function is_sanitizer_build()/,/^fi$/p'`. That range ends at the first bare `^fi$` after the anchor, which on master closes `if is_sanitizer_build; then ln -sf ... trace_log_no_symbolize.xml ...`, so the wiring was captured only by luck of layout. Inserting any bare `fi` between the function and that `if` truncates the range, so the fragment loses the `ln -sf` and all five `test_installer_disables_symbolization_under_a_sanitizer` parameters fail on a correct tree. #113107 does exactly that. The four `test_installer_keeps_symbolization_without_a_sanitizer` parameters share the helper and go *vacuously* green there, since "nothing installed" is their expected answer. The guard now runs the real installer with a stub `clickhouse` earlier on `PATH`, into the test's `tmp_path`, and asserts the resulting symlink. No `sed`, no `eval`, so rearranging that region cannot affect it. Same nine parameters, one function, 21 lines replaced. `tests/config/install.sh` is not modified: the shell predicate is correct and is the subject under test. The link must resolve to the installer's own copy, not merely exist: `ln -sf` succeeds against an absent source, and a dangling link leaves the server reading nothing. Validated with the #113107 installer (5 failed before, 22 passed after) and with a bare `fi` injected before the consuming `if` (22 passed). Six mutations of a scratch `install.sh` confirm the oracle still discriminates: the bare `-fsanitize=` revert reds only `amd_cfi`; deleting the wiring, ignoring the build flags either way, pointing the symlink elsewhere, and leaving it dangling each red the expected arms. 20 runs, 20 identical passes. `pytest ci/tests/` failure ids are unchanged. One limit: `assert run.returncode == 0` catches less than it looks, since the installer's probes sit in command substitutions, so a stub refusing every call still exits 0. Such a break surfaces through the symlink assertion instead. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115825&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115825](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115825+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)** ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Reject PromQL vector matching modifiers when one operand is a scalar.** ### Summary PromQL rejects `on(...)` and `ignoring(...)` when one binary operator operand is a scalar. ClickHouse currently accepts queries such as: `up + on(job) 1` and evaluates them like `up + 1`, silently dropping the requested matching labels. This change rejects non-empty vector matching labels when either operand is a scalar. Empty `on()` and `ignoring()` clauses remain valid. ### Why it matters PromQL-compatible clients expect invalid vector matching expressions to fail instead of returning a plausible result with different semantics. ### Tests - Add regression coverage for scalar math and comparison expressions with vector matching labels. - Keep coverage for valid scalar expressions and empty matching clauses. - Syntax-check the changed C++ translation unit with the existing compile command. - Run `git diff --check`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115828&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115828](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115828+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Web UI: bring back the color highlight of high read speeds
signals.text: The progress line of the Web UI wraps the outstanding numbers of the read stats - huge row and byte counts and high read speeds - in `<b>`, and a CSS rule used to paint them in a color, so an extreme speed stood out: ``` Read 240.00 G rows, 5.12 TB (1.71 T/sec, 36.57 TB/sec) ``` The rule was lost when the progress line was reworked to paint its text through a `background-clip: text` gradient mask keyed to the `--progress` custom property. Since then the numbers were only bold - the computed color of `#stats b` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`. Restore the highlight, painting it in the top tier of the rate palette that the metrics table already uses, so that an extreme speed reads the same way in both places. Two deliberate deviations from the original rule: - the mask makes the text of the whole line transparent and `-webkit-text-fill-color` is inherited, so the highlight has to set that property as well - a rule setting only `color` is silently ignored; - the color is no longer the progress color: the read stats now sit over the bar, and the bar is painted in the progress color, so the old highlight would have blended into it at high progress. Checked in a headless browser in both themes, while the query runs (at 60% and at 99% of the bar) and after it finishes. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Web UI: bring back the color highlight of high read speeds and huge row and byte counts in the progress line. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115830&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115830](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115830+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Speed up to_utc_timestamp and from_utc_timestamp on DateTime64
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up `toUTCTimestamp`/`to_utc_timestamp` and `fromUTCTimestamp`/`from_utc_timestamp` on `DateTime64` arguments, restoring the throughput they had before the overflow fix in #109738. Results are unchanged. Closes #115802. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 My #109738 fixed a signed-overflow and a wrong-offset-at-a-boundary bug on the `DateTime64` path of these functions, but it did the arithmetic and the clamp in `Int128`, once per row. `Int128` here is `wide::integer<128, signed>`, a software big-integer, so `operator*` sign-normalizes through branches before a native multiply and reassembles a two-`UInt64` struct. Each row gained that call plus two 128-bit compares and selects where it previously had one `imul` and one `add`. The `DateTime` branch was untouched and did not regress. The wide arithmetic is redundant. The floored split guarantees `seconds * scale_multiplier + micros == value` exactly, so shifting the seconds by the offset and reassembling equals shifting the underlying value by `offset * scale_multiplier`; the `Int128` multiply only re-derived its own input. This PR shifts the underlying value directly with a saturating `Int64` add/sub (`common::addOverflow`/`subOverflow`: one `add`/`sub` plus a flag test). `offset * scale_multiplier` cannot overflow `Int64`: scanning `timeZoneOffset` over all 597 shipped time zones (4.18M samples, including out-of-LUT extremes) gives `max|offset| = 130800`, and `scale_multiplier <= 10^9`, so the product stays 70000x below the `Int64` limit. Both semantics from #109738 are kept: the split still floors, and the result is still saturated. Measured on the queries from `tests/performance/utc_timestamp_transform.xml` (10M rows, `max_threads=1`, optimized build, arms differing by exactly this hunk): `0.102s -> 0.062s`, against `0.061s` before #109738. The `DateTime` queries are the control and stay at `0.033s` throughout. That is x86_64, so the ratio is smaller than the ARM 2.7x in the issue, but the fix returns to the pre-#109738 cost rather than narrowing the gap. Results are bit-identical to master over 12.9M `(value, scale, timezone, direction)` cases plus 112K cases built on the 1,056 real offset-transition seconds. `03891_utc_timestamp_datetime64_overflow` passes byte-identical, and still reddens if the saturation is dropped, its direction flipped, or the floor correction removed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115838&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115838](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115838+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113242 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #115455 Related: #113242 Related: #114677 `Stress test (*)` jobs abort with `Logical error: 'Equal values are not contiguous within the range assumed to be sorted'` at `DistinctSortedStreamTransform.cpp:184`: 87 times across 78 unrelated pull requests since `04870` was merged on 2026-08-17, against 5 in the 20 days before, and it is still firing today. The engine defect is old and is not what I change here. The stress profile sets `ast_fuzzer_runs = 5` and `ast_fuzzer_any_query = true` (`tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib`), so the server-side AST fuzzer re-runs mutated copies of every statement of every stateless test, `CREATE` included. In `04870` it retypes the fixture's `Merge` parent and substitutes the clone into a `SELECT`, and a `Merge` parent whose column type differs from its child's is the precondition for the assertion. My test is the amplifier, and this PR removes only that. The defect itself is #113242, still open. The change is one statement, `SET ast_fuzzer_runs = 0;`, pinning the setting to its own declared default. It weakens nothing: all seven arms still run and still assert, and the `.reference` file is unchanged. Nine stateless tests already pin it, several for this same reason. It is file-level rather than per-query because the chain needs both a fuzzed `CREATE`, to mint the clone, and a fuzzed `SELECT`, to substitute it in. `-- Tags: no-stress` is not an option, `clickhouse-test` rejects it. Validation, one debug binary differing only in the test file: with the fuzzer armed the unpinned test fails 6 of 30 runs and the pinned test passes 30 of 30. I also reproduced the abort on a hand-built mistyped fixture, with a stack matching CI. 50 randomized runs, and 50 with the fuzzer armed, pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115839&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115839](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115839+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Sort release branches by version, not lexically
signals.text: `_release_branches()` sorts the open `release`-labeled PR head branches as plain strings, so once a minor version reaches two digits the ordering is wrong — e.g. `25.10` sorts before `25.9`. It's benign in `auto_release_job.py`'s current per-branch loop (every branch is processed regardless of order), but any newest-first consumer would pick the wrong branch. Sort by a numeric `(major, minor, …)` key via a small `_branch_version_key` helper. Flagged by the review bot on #113528 (its `_select_patch_dry_run_ref` relies on newest-first order); fixing the ordering at the source here. signals.title: Docs: clarify that use_skip_indexes_if_final stale-result risk requires exact mode to be disabled
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Documentation (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... The `use_skip_indexes_if_final` description states the stale-result risk as if it were an unconditional consequence of enabling the setting, and mentions `use_skip_indexes_if_final_exact_mode` only in a trailing clause whose `(default is enabled)` is easy to read as referring back to `use_skip_indexes_if_final` itself. Both settings default to `true` (`src/Core/Settings.cpp`, and `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` records the `0 -> 1` flip for both in 25.6). With the shipped defaults there is no stale-result risk: `use_skip_indexes_if_final_exact_mode` runs the `PrimaryKeyExpand` step (`findPKRangesForFinalAfterSkipIndex`, `src/Processors/QueryPlan/PartsSplitter.cpp`), which adds back granules in the other parts that overlap the primary key ranges the skip index selected. The "risk of missing recent updates" applies only when that setting is turned off, which is exactly what the existing sibling description says ("This setting should be disabled only if approximate results based on looking up the skip index are okay for an application"). Reworded so the conditionality and the default are explicit. Documentation only, no behavior change. Before: > Skip indexes may exclude rows (granules) containing the latest data, which could lead to incorrect results from a query with the FINAL modifier. When this setting is enabled, skipping indexes are applied even with the FINAL modifier, potentially improving performance but with the risk of missing recent updates. This setting should be enabled in sync with the setting use_skip_indexes_if_final_exact_mode (default is enabled). After: > Skip indexes may exclude rows (granules) containing the latest data, which could lead to incorrect results from a query with the FINAL modifier. When this setting is enabled, skipping indexes are applied even with the FINAL modifier, potentially improving performance. Correct results still depend on setting use_skip_indexes_if_final_exact_mode, which is enabled by default and scans the additional parts that overlap the ranges returned by the skip index. The risk of missing recent updates applies only if that setting is disabled. The rendered page (https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/use-skip-indexes) is inside `AUTOGENERATED` markers, so per `docs/reference/AGENTS.md` only the `DECLARE` doc string is edited here; the nightly docs autogeneration job regenerates the `.mdx`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115846&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115846](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115846+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not buffer the serialized step when computing the hash-table-stats cache key
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113736 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113333 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reduced memory usage and query-plan optimization time for keyed aggregations over large constant-folded literals. The aggregation hash-table-statistics cache key is now hashed as it is serialized instead of being accumulated in memory first, so a plan carrying a large literal no longer holds a copy of it during optimization. For an 80 MB literal, peak memory drops by about 250 MB and optimization time by about 2.5x. The computed key is unchanged. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113736 `calculateHashFromStep` buffered a step's whole serialized form, then hashed it in a second pass. That stream is hash input only, and `serializeConstant` writes a constant-folded literal out in full, so a large literal was copied just to be hashed and dropped. This hashes the stream as it is produced, through a small `WriteBuffer` feeding a `SipHash` over a 32 KiB window. **The key value is bit-identical to before**, since `SipHash::update` carries state across calls including any sub-word remainder. That matters because a collision is harmless for only one of the three consumers: `considerEnablingParallelReplicas` uses these hashes as a node matcher across two plan builds, transplanting cached dataflow statistics on a match. Truncating the key would make different constants compare equal there. Measured with `clickhouse local` on a `GROUP BY` over an 80 MB `repeat()` literal, 3 runs: | 80 MB literal | `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` | peak RSS | |---|---|---| | before | 176 / 179 / 175 ms | 668 / 671 / 668 MB | | after | 68 / 70 / 73 ms | 407 / 419 / 419 MB | | setting off (floor) | 43 / 39 / 40 ms | 407 / 413 / 407 MB | Peak memory now sits at the floor. Same at 800 MB: 3460 to 1817 MB, floor 1817 MB. The O(N) term remains: `serializeBinary` still walks every byte, and each aggregation node serializes its own subtree. Removing it means giving up exact key identity, which given the matcher above is the code owner's call. A gtest asserts the streamed key equals the previously buffered key across window-boundary alignments, and fails under two deliberate perturbations of the sink. 12 real cache keys spanning constants, Array, Tuple, Nullable, LowCardinality and Decimal are unchanged. Reported by @ egor-click. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115847&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115847](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115847+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Push down string filters from PREWHERE into the scan
signals.text: Implements pushing down of string filtering into the scan phase. When a query has a substring search condition on a `String` (or `Nullable(String)`) column in `PREWHERE` (`LIKE`, `position`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, or equality with a non-empty string), and this condition does not match an empty string, the filter is pushed down into the column deserialization: every value is checked against the filter, and if it does not match, the value is read as an empty string, without copying its data into the column. This makes reading faster and lowers memory usage when the condition is selective. The result of the query does not change, because the condition is a conjunct of `PREWHERE`, which is guaranteed to filter out the rows with non-matching values, and because such conditions never match an empty string, so even a kept `PREWHERE` column is bit-identical. The optimization works for reading from `MergeTree` and from `Parquet`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added setting `apply_string_filters_during_scan` (disabled by default): substring search conditions on `String` columns (`LIKE`, `position`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`) from `PREWHERE` are pushed down into the column scan, and non-matching values are read as empty strings without copying their data. Works for reading from `MergeTree` and from the `Parquet` format. ### Implementation details - `StringValueFilter` (`src/Common/`) holds the extracted conditions (substring / prefix / suffix / equality, all with non-empty needles, so that an empty string never matches) and checks values with a bounds-safe substring searcher. A single filter object is shared by all readers of a column within one query and disables itself adaptively when the observed fraction of matching values makes the check unprofitable (more than half of the values match). - `extractStringValueFilters` (`src/Interpreters/`) walks the top-level `AND` chain of the `PREWHERE` actions and extracts filters from `like` (with fixed substrings parsed out of the pattern, honoring escaping), `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `equals` with a non-empty string, bare `position`, and comparisons of `position` with a constant that reject the zero result (e.g. `position(s, 'x') > 0`, `position(s, 'x') = 5`, but not `position(s, 'x') = 0`). - `MergeTree`: the filters are attached to `MergeTreeReaderSettings` in `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline`, only when `prewhere_info->need_filter` is set (rows are guaranteed to be physically filtered). The readers apply a filter to a column only when it is a full `String`/`Nullable(String)` column with the plain serialization (not sparse), is not requested together with another column reading from the same storage column (e.g. the `.size` subcolumn, which could share deserialized data through caches), and is not overwritten by an on-fly mutation (`PREWHERE` is then evaluated on mutated values). Renamed columns are handled by keying the filter by the name in the part. Both string serialization versions are supported (`single_stream` and `with_size_stream`), for wide and compact parts. - `Parquet` (native reader): the filters are attached to the prewhere-step string leaves and applied in the plain and delta-length page decoders per value; for dictionary-encoded pages the filter is checked only once per dictionary entry, and the per-row gather materializes empty strings for non-matching entries. - New profile events: `StringValueFilterValuesChecked`, `StringValueFilterValuesReplaced`, `StringValueFilterBytesSkipped`. - The setting is added to the settings randomization in `clickhouse-test`. ### Testing - New stateless tests cover wide/compact parts, both string serialization versions, `Nullable(String)`, escaped `LIKE` patterns, conditions that must not be pushed down (`position(s, 'x') = 0`, `NOT`, `OR`, patterns matching an empty string), `AND` chains, multiple columns, and both Parquet page encodings; every query is checked with the setting enabled and disabled, plus profile events assert that the optimization actually fires. - All existing stateless tests matching `prewhere` were run locally with the setting forced on: the results are identical to the run with the setting disabled. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115848&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115848](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115848+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> ### ClickBench results Measured on the `hits` table (100M rows, 96-core aarch64, hot cache, interleaved A/B runs, query condition cache disabled to measure the scan itself). The affected queries are those with substring conditions (`URL LIKE '%google%'`, `Title LIKE '%Google%'`), written with explicit `PREWHERE`; the remaining 39 queries do not extract any filter and are unaffected. MergeTree (min of 5 runs): | Query | off, s | on, s | speedup | memory | |---|---|---|---|---| | Q20 `count() PREWHERE URL LIKE '%google%'` | 0.102 | 0.086 | 1.19× | −51% | | Q21 | 0.118 | 0.095 | 1.24× | −46% | | Q22 (`Title LIKE '%Google%'`) | 0.208 | 0.185 | 1.12× | −21% | | Q23 (`SELECT *`) | 0.134 | 0.116 | 1.16× | −59% | The filter replaces ~99.98M of 100M values and skips copying 8.4-8.8 GiB per query. The initial per-value implementation was 10-15% *slower* than the baseline on MergeTree (a substring search per short value loses to the baseline's bulk copy plus one bulk scan in `like`); the bulk-scan implementation (one scan per buffer of concatenated values) turned it into the win above. Parquet (`file('hits.parquet')`, same queries, quieter round): Q20 1.57×, Q21 1.18×, Q22 1.12×, Q23 ~1× (dominated by reading the other 100 columns). When the setting is enabled, the `WHERE` to `PREWHERE` optimization also moves suitable substring search conditions even when they use all queried columns (normally that is pointless, but with the string filter the scan itself becomes cheaper). This makes the official `WHERE`-form of Q20 use `PREWHERE` and the string filter as written: 1.25× faster (min of 5 runs, 0.119 s → 0.095 s) and −59% memory. Plain equality with a string constant is deliberately excluded from this relaxation: it is too common, and it would change the plans of too many queries where the primary key index does the job anyway. In Q23 the top-k dynamic filter occupies `PREWHERE` and the `LIKE` stays in `WHERE`, which is unaffected.

signals.title: HTTP: support PUT uploads to table paths
signals.text: Implements the first step from [#38775](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/38775): allow an HTTP `PUT` request to upload data to an existing table when the URL path contains the database, table, and input format. Related: - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/38775 - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/46925 ## What's in the box - `PUT /database/table.CSV` inserts the request body into `database.table` as CSV. - `PUT /database/table.JSONEachRow` works the same way for JSONEachRow. - Reuses the existing HTTP path parser and input format registry. - Keeps the existing GET table-as-file behavior unchanged. - Keeps PUT requests with an explicit `query` parameter read-only. - Enables the PUT mutation exception only for the built-in catch-all path handler. - Configured dynamic handlers keep their existing readonly behavior. - Requires an existing table and a request body. - Rejects missing or unknown formats, compression suffixes, and paths without a format suffix. The larger ticket also mentions schema inference/table creation and POST multipart uploads. Those are intentionally left for follow-up work. ## Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ## Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add path-based PUT uploads to existing tables in the HTTP interface. ## Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) in `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/http.mdx`. ## Tests - Added `05029_http_put_table_upload` for path uploads and validation errors. - Added keep-alive regressions for failed PUT and DELETE requests with request bodies. - Extended `test_dynamic_handler_put_delete_still_readonly` to cover the default query parameter on configured dynamic handlers. - `git diff --check` - `bash -n tests/queries/0_stateless/05029_http_put_table_upload.sh` - `python3 -m py_compile tests/integration/test_http_handlers_config/test.py` <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115849&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115849](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115849+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep nullability when casting to a LowCardinality target
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103485 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `cast_keep_nullable` not preserving nullability when the target type is `LowCardinality`. Casting a NULL-capable value to `LowCardinality(T)` threw `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` instead of producing `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`. Closes #103485. ### Description With `cast_keep_nullable = 1`, casting a NULL-capable source to a `LowCardinality(U)` target threw `Code: 349 CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN`: ```sql SET cast_keep_nullable = 1; SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::LowCardinality(String); -- threw 349 SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String); -- threw 349 ``` `CastOverloadResolver::getReturnTypeImpl` decided whether to preserve nullability with `type->canBeInsideNullable()`. `DataTypeLowCardinality` does not override that predicate, so it inherits the default `false`, the wrap was skipped, and the target could not hold the NULL. The predicate is correct - `Nullable(LowCardinality(T))` really is an invalid type - but it asks the wrong question: a `LowCardinality` target represents NULL as `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`. The fix uses the existing `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe`, which pushes `Nullable` inside the wrapper and otherwise behaves exactly like the old guard. I deliberately did not add a `canBeInsideNullable()` override to `DataTypeLowCardinality`: that would make the predicate false for its other callers, and #115464 relies on its current meaning. This completes the half left by `3a71053` in #95747, which fixed the same guard's source arm. An `Array` target still throws 349, correctly: there is no nullable `Array` form to move the NULL into, and `04035_cast_keep_nullable_dynamic` pins that. Out of scope: the `accurateCastOrNull` family still rejects `LowCardinality` targets with `Code: 43`; lifting that needs its own design. One observable change under `cast_keep_nullable = 1`: a non-NULL cast to an LC target now yields `LowCardinality(Nullable(U))` rather than `LowCardinality(U)`. No setting default changes, so `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` needs no entry, matching the #95747 precedent. The new stateless test covers both source shapes, `String`, `FixedString` and numeric dictionary types, NULL and non-NULL values, `Dynamic` and `Variant` sources, and four negative controls. It fails on master and passes here. Reported by the ClickGap retrospective scan of #95747; fix requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103485#issuecomment-5369160612. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115851&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115851](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115851+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a release-pipeline dry-run PR check
signals.text: Add a digest-gated PR job that rehearses the release pipeline in `--dry-run` so a change to the release code is caught before it can break a real release. `Release Dry Run (new)` runs `release_job.py --ref master --release-type new --dry-run --skip-repo --skip-docker`. It's gated (via `digest_config`) to the release files, so it only runs when they change. It runs on the small PR pool (not `amd-release-maker`, which the PR workflow's `pr-` label prefix can't resolve) and authenticates `gh` with a minted PR token (`enable_gh_auth`) — a dry run pushes nothing, so no robot PAT is needed. `Release Dry Run (patch)` uses `--ref auto`, which picks the newest unreleased release-branch commit (a pass when none exists); release branches are sorted version-aware (`25.10` after `25.9`). Both checks exercise the generic prepare/setup path — the changelog-push-to-`master` and the R2/package/docker steps are real-only (gated by `not dry_run` / `not skip_repo`), so a dry run never reaches them; those are validated by real release runs. Supporting changes in `release_job.py`: skip the SSM robot token on a dry run; make `master` a local branch when the checkout is detached (the PR case); don't apply the skip-repo/skip-docker recovery-misuse guard on a dry run; and the `--ref auto` candidate scan. Split out of #113528 to keep that PR focused on the direct-push conversion. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

signals.title: Reject a subcolumn as a UNIQUE KEY element
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114470 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114470 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE TABLE` accepting a subcolumn as a `UNIQUE KEY` element, of either a user column (for example `` UNIQUE KEY (`c.null`) ``) or a virtual one (`` UNIQUE KEY (`_partition_value.1`) ``), which produced a table that could never be inserted into, failing every `INSERT` with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. Such a definition is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. Closes #114470. ### Description A backticked subcolumn name parses as a single identifier, so the existing `UNIQUE KEY` DDL guard accepted it. It asks `ColumnsDescription::has`, which searches only the top-level column index, while subcolumns live in a separate one; and its fallback failed, since `getKeyFromAST` does resolve a subcolumn name. The table could then be read and dropped but never written to. The same mistake exists one level over, in the virtuals index: its lookup is exact-name, so `` `_partition_value.1` `` misses there too, while the subcolumn index only holds subcolumns of user columns. That form is reachable from any table with a `PARTITION BY`. The fix adds two predicates beside the existing virtual-column and ALIAS/EPHEMERAL checks, each asking the index that actually holds the thing. Both derive from the type's own serialization rather than a list of names, so they cover every family: I measured 13 reachable user-column ones against the report's five, and 5 virtual ones, all on `_partition_value`, the only virtual with a composite type. Both are gated on fresh definitions (`CREATE`, and full-definition `ATTACH`, which is CREATE-like user input). `UNIQUE KEY` shipped in 26.5 and this guard reached no released branch, so such tables already exist; ungated they would fail to attach and become impossible to drop. Verified with two binaries per predicate: a table from a pre-fix binary still attaches and drops under the fixed one, and with the gate removed it fails to load. The leading `has(name)` term is load-bearing and has coverage: a stored column may be named after another column's (or a virtual's) subcolumn, and a flattened `Nested` member is itself a stored column named `n.x`. All stay accepted, with an `INSERT`. For a `JSON` parent, `` `c.a` `` was already rejected and is now rejected earlier. No setting is added and no default changed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115854&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115854](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115854+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL rate/increase/delta/idelta/irate over native histograms
signals.text: ## Summary Fifth slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115736. Adds the rate family — `rate`, `increase`, `delta`, `idelta`, `irate` — over stored native histograms, reset-aware and faithful to upstream `extrapolatedRate` + `histogramRate`: - **Arithmetic kernel** (`TimeSeriesHistogramKernel.h`): a decoded in-memory float histogram porting upstream `FloatHistogram` field-for-field — `sub`/`add` (with schema reconciliation and NHCB custom-bucket-bound reconciliation), `copyToSchema`, `mul`/`div`, `compact`, and the full `detectReset` (counter-reset hint short-circuits, count/schema/zero-threshold/zero-count rules, per-bucket comparison). The exponential-bound table moves here as a shared header-inline constant. - **Aggregates** `timeSeriesHistogram{Rate,Increase,Delta,InstantRate,InstantDelta}ToGrid`: per grid window, collect the histogram samples, reduce the last to the minimum schema, subtract the first, re-add the previous sample on each detected reset, and extrapolate to the window boundaries (`durationToStart`/`durationToEnd` clamping, counter zero-point clamp); `rate` additionally divides by the range seconds. `irate`/`idelta` use the two newest samples without extrapolation. - **Converter**: the five functions over the histogram arm produce the result histogram into `histogram_values`. A window mixing float and histogram samples drops the element on both arms, matching upstream's `MixedFloatsHistograms` rule. Over a subquery, each arm is resampled from the inner grid masked by `sample_kinds`. - **Upstream-parity details**: `delta` keeps `min(first, last)` schema and does not drop over a custom-bucket middle sample (the scan is counter-only upstream); the instant path drops a mixed exponential/custom newest pair rather than throwing. Also fixes two unrelated pre-existing bugs: PromQL regex matchers were anchored `^<pattern>$` without grouping (so `^n|g$` meant `(^n)|(g$)`), now anchored `^(...)$`; and a self-cycle in `fromSelector`'s table-expression AST. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL `rate`, `increase`, `delta`, `idelta`, and `irate` over stored Prometheus native histograms, with upstream-compatible counter-reset handling and range extrapolation. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115685 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115734 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115735 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115736 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115860&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115860](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115860+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix flaky test 00818_inner_join_bug_3567
signals.text: `PrettyCompact` starts a new table for every chunk it receives, and glues consecutive chunks together only while they keep arriving within `output_format_pretty_squash_consecutive_ms` (50 ms by default). The `ALL LEFT JOIN` in `00818_inner_join_bug_3567` emits its single non-joined row in a chunk of its own, so whenever the next chunk is more than 50 ms behind — which happens on a loaded runner, most often under TSan — the result is printed as two tables: ``` ┌─a─┬──────────b─┬─c─┬──────────d─┬─c─┐ 1. │ a │ 2018-01-01 │ │ 1970-01-01 │ │ + └───┴────────────┴───┴────────────┴───┘ + ┌─a─┬──────────b─┬─c─┬──────────d─┬─c─┐ 2. │ b │ 2018-01-01 │ B │ 2018-01-01 │ B │ 3. │ c │ 2018-01-01 │ C │ 2018-01-01 │ C │ └───┴────────────┴───┴────────────┴───┘ ``` All 27 recorded failures of this test in the last 180 days have exactly this signature. The test only uses a `Pretty` format to show the column names of the join result, so it switches to `PrettyCompactMonoBlock`, which squashes everything into a single table regardless of chunking and timing. The reference file is unchanged. Verified with the randomized settings of the failed run and `output_format_pretty_squash_consecutive_ms = 0` (the worst case): 15/15 runs of the old test differ from the reference, 15/15 runs of the new one match it.
