signals.title: Build the IN-subquery set once when a correlated subquery body is materialized
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` logical error when a correlated subquery whose body contains `IN (subquery)` runs with `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0`, which `make_distributed_plan = 1` also sets. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 With `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0` the decorrelated subquery body is duplicated by cloning it, and the clone included the `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` holding the body's `IN` set. A `FutureSetFromSubquery` hands out its source plan only once (`build` moves `source` out), and `makePlansForSets` treats an absent plan as nothing to build, so the second copy became a childless `CreatingSets`: its `in()` then read a set nothing had built. Reproducer: ```sql SET allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1, correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0; SELECT (SELECT x) FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(['a','b']) AS x GROUP BY 1, 1 IN (SELECT 7)); ``` The set is now taken out of the fragment before it is cloned, and one builder is attached above the plan root, so it dominates every copy. Readiness is structural rather than dependent on which join arm runs first, which matters because the abort reproduces with `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind` set to either `left` or `right`. This follows `extractSetsForDistributedPlan`, which solves the same problem for distributed plans. This also fixes a second, latent defect. `buildOrderedSetInplace` clones the source plan as a non-destructive snapshot and relies on a plan holding a `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` being non-clonable, so a stopped speculative build cannot consume a nested set's source. Since `f886da073cea2bf` added `DelayedCreatingSetsStep::clone()` that clone silently succeeded and shared the inner subqueries. Full-plan cloning now rejects a step that still holds sets, restoring the documented fallback; the step clone Cascades needs is unchanged. Validation: the reproducer aborts before and returns `a`/`b` after; the new test aborts the server on a pristine-master binary and passes on the fixed one; `EXPLAIN PLAN` shows exactly one builder and no leftover placeholder for both join kinds; 50/50 randomized runs pass; the correlated, common-subplan and distributed-plan suites show the same failures before and after. Found by the AST fuzzer on #109377: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109377&sha=424d8efed247654e71f2bad3aa996e203fc08feb&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115868&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115868](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115868+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: K-way merge optimizations: batch lookahead, sorted array of cursors, batch queue for special merges
signals.text: Three k-way merge optimizations motivated by the analysis in https://maksimkita.com/blog/k-way-merge.html, plus a follow-up refinement: 1. **O(1) whole-cursor batch detection** (`SortingQueueImpl::updateBatchSize`). When the batch exceeds the linear detection limit, one comparison against the last row of the front cursor takes the entire remainder as a single batch. Merging cursors with non-intersecting key ranges (e.g. parts sorted by the primary key that do not overlap) now costs O(1) comparisons per batch instead of a linear detection followed by a binary search over the remainder. 2. **Sorted array of cursors** as an alternative queue container. Reinserting the advanced front cursor costs exactly `ceil(log2(K))` comparisons (a binary search) plus a shift of plain pointers, versus up to `2 * log2(K)` comparisons for the heap. It is selected only for cursors with expensive comparators: the generic multi-column `SortCursor` and `SortCursorWithCollation`. Above 256 cursors it falls back to the heap behavior (a sorted array is a valid heap layout, so the switch is free). Measured on 64-way in-order merges of parts with fully overlapping ranges: 7-8% faster for two- and four-column sorting keys, no change for the specialized single-column cursors (which stay on the heap: e.g. strings measured 18% slower with the array, since their comparisons usually resolve within the first bytes). 3. **Batch sorting queue for the special merge algorithms** (`Replacing`/`Summing`/`Aggregating`/`Collapsing`/`VersionedCollapsing`/`Graphite`). They advanced the queue one row at a time, restructuring the heap on every row; now the queue is restructured once per batch. `ReplacingSortedAlgorithm` additionally fast-forwards to the last row of a run of equal keys within a batch when processing a row has no effects besides replacing the selected row (no version and no `is_deleted` columns, no row sources, no vertical FINAL) — the run end is found with `getEqualRangeEndAssumeSorted` instead of per-row comparisons. Measured: `SELECT ... FINAL` over 8 parts of `ReplacingMergeTree` with runs of ~10 duplicates per key inside each part is 26-33% faster; FINAL over non-intersecting parts is unchanged; `SummingMergeTree` FINAL is 6% faster on clustered duplicates and ~5% slower in the worst case of fully interleaved hash-distributed keys (a known trade-off; a follow-up that uses the run information to skip per-row key comparisons in the remaining algorithms can win both shapes). 4. **Galloping detection of the batch end**: after the linear detection caps out, the end of the batch is bracketed with exponentially growing steps, so the search costs O(log(batch size)) comparisons on rows near the current position instead of O(log(rows left)) comparisons on far rows that miss caches. Verification: a 25-case differential harness (multi-column/string/nullable/collation/LowCardinality `ORDER BY` checksums incl. row order, external sort, >256-cursor merges, FINAL for all six engines, vertical merges, `enable_vertical_final`, `is_deleted`, insert-time merging with a permutation) produces identical results against master at every commit; ~300 targeted stateless tests and the merge/sort unit tests pass. A new performance test `kway_merge_expensive_comparator` covers the array-container cases and guards the heap cases. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up k-way merges: merging sorted streams with multi-column or collated sorting keys uses a sorted array of cursors instead of a heap (7-8% faster), merges of non-intersecting parts detect the whole cursor as one batch in O(1) comparisons, and the merges of `ReplacingMergeTree`, `SummingMergeTree`, `AggregatingMergeTree`, `CollapsingMergeTree`, `VersionedCollapsingMergeTree` and `GraphiteMergeTree` process rows in batches (`SELECT ... FINAL` from `ReplacingMergeTree` with many duplicates is up to 30% faster). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115869&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115869](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115869+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix lost rows when a plan-based parallel replicas fragment has no output columns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113469 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results with `parallel_replicas_plan_based = 1` when the plan fragment sent to the replicas has no output columns, for example `SELECT count() FROM (SELECT 1 FROM t LIMIT 500)`. Such a query returned `0`, or an empty result set, instead of the correct value. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113469 (same defect class, disjoint path). No open issue. With `parallel_replicas_plan_based = 1`, a query whose distributed fragment ends up with no output columns loses every row it reads, silently and with no error: ```sql SELECT count() FROM (SELECT 1 FROM t LIMIT 500); -- returns 0, must be 500 ``` Root cause. `query_plan_remove_unused_columns` prunes the fragment's last column when the outer aggregate needs only a row count and a `LIMIT` keeps that aggregate out of the fragment. `ReadFromParallelReplicasStep` adopts the empty header, and a result travelling back from a replica is a `Block`, whose row count is the size of its first column: with no columns it is unrepresentable. The block is then dropped by `!block.empty()` on both sides (`TCPHandler.cpp`, `RemoteQueryExecutor.cpp`), and the Native format refuses it outright. Local execution is unaffected: a `Chunk` stores its row count independently of its columns. Only fragment shipping reaches this. Classic parallel replicas and `serialize_query_plan = 1` over `remote()` force the shard header to the initiator's mergeable-stage header (`addConvertingActions`), keeping a column; both measured correct. The fix keeps one materialized constant column in the fragment when its own columns were all pruned away, restoring the "at least one output column" precondition the protocol, `Block` and both guards already assume. It is inserted where the fragment is built, so the remote plan and the local half of the local+remote union get identical headers, and the converting projection `replaceNodeWithPlan` already inserts keeps the placeholder out of the result. `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`, the default, is affected too: its local half normally covers all the marks so the answer happens to be right, but under the `slowdown_parallel_replicas_local_plan_read` failpoint it also returns `0`. Validation: 7 defect shapes go from wrong to correct, 13 controls unchanged, `read_bytes` unchanged, and `04546_pr_plan_based_remote_only` reddens on master and passes here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115871&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115871](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115871+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix DeltaLake trivial count and total_rows over tables with deletion vectors
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114933 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114933 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `SELECT count()` and `system.tables.total_rows` returning too many rows for a Delta Lake table whose deletes are stored as deletion vectors: the count came from the `numRecords` file statistics, which still include the removed rows. Closes #114933. ### Description `SELECT count()` over a Delta table with `delta.enableDeletionVectors = true` counted the deleted rows: the trivial-count optimization answers from the `numRecords` statistics in `_delta_log` and never consulted the file's deletion vector. Any query that scans returned the correct answer, so `count()` disagreed with every other answer the same table gave. `system.tables.total_rows` over a `DeltaLake` engine table over-counted identically, through the same `IStorage::totalRows` seam. `TableSnapshot` accumulates `total_rows` at two places, and both summed `stats->num_records` while holding the file's `dv_info` handle and ignoring it. delta-kernel documents that statistic as stale under a deletion vector in the same doc comment that names `DvInfo::has_vector` as the flag to consult (`kernel/src/scan/state.rs`). Both sites now drop `total_rows` when a file carries a deletion vector, so `count()` becomes an ordinary scan, which already applies the vector correctly, and `total_rows` reports NULL rather than a wrong number. That is what `IcebergMetadata::totalRows` already does under delete files. `total_bytes` is unchanged: a deletion vector does not change data-file size. Subtracting the vector's `cardinality` would be exact, but that field is not reachable without reading the deletion-vector file, the very read this shortcut avoids. The `delta_lake_snapshot_version` disagreement the issue also reports has the same cause and is fixed too, since `getTotalRows` is version-agnostic. On the test fixture, whose vector removes 2 rows, pinning the version that carries the vector returned 4 before and returns 2 now, matching Spark's `VERSION AS OF`. A version pinned before the delete keeps the optimization. Extends `test_deletion_vector`, whose existing assertions use `ORDER BY all`, which makes the planner see the `count()` aggregate twice and decline the optimization, so they never reached this path. New arms cover a bare `count()`, both accumulation sites, `total_rows`, a pinned read of the version carrying the vector, and two controls that the optimization is still applied where no vector is present. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115872&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115872](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115872+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: DataLakeCatalog: cache resolved table storages
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Cache resolved DataLakeCatalog table storages for a configurable staleness window, avoiding repeated catalog resolution and storage construction on every query. ### Summary `DatabaseDataLake::tryGetTableImpl` currently resolves table metadata and reconstructs `StorageObjectStorage` for each query. This adds catalog latency and repeats data-lake initialization work. This PR adds a bounded per-database SLRU of resolved `StoragePtr`s: - `catalog_cache_staleness_ms` controls TTL (`0` disables it) - `catalog_cache_max_entries` bounds entries - keys include local/parallel-replica execution mode - long-lived storages use a global-context copy - storages are fully initialized before concurrent publication - `SYSTEM CLEAR DATALAKE CATALOG CACHE` and cache metrics/events are included - ALTER DATABASE invalidates cached entries The eager initialization for cacheable storages fixes a reproducible first-use race where concurrent queries replaced the same lazy `DataLakeConfiguration::current_metadata` unique_ptr and destroyed another query's live `IcebergMetadata`. ### Validation - Full ClickHouse build against current `master` - TSAN integration test: 64 synchronized first-use reads, cache clear/reseed repeated three times - Local integration result: `1 passed` - Live stress validation: 64 and 128 concurrent readers, 0 query errors and 0 server restarts Controlled warm DataLakeCatalog benchmark (same Iceberg snapshot, one 12-core reader): - before: 50 RPS / 157 ms p50 at 8 clients - after: 1673 RPS / 4.55 ms p50 at 8 clients
signals.author: adonm

signals.title: Iceberg: reuse parsed state and derived storage metadata
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Reuse parsed Iceberg snapshot state and derived storage metadata while the exact table state is unchanged. ### Summary Warm Iceberg reads repeatedly performed two kinds of immutable work: 1. parsed the same metadata JSON and re-registered schemas; 2. rebuilt `StorageInMemoryMetadata`, including `ColumnsDescription` and the analyzed sorting key. This PR adds two lock-free, single-entry caches published with atomic shared pointers: - parsed state keyed by metadata version/path; - derived storage metadata keyed by the complete `TableStateSnapshot` (metadata path/version, schema ID, and snapshot ID). The existing interface still returns a deep copy of `StorageInMemoryMetadata`; the cache avoids JSON parsing, schema traversal, sort-expression parsing, and repeated key analysis. Time-travel reads bypass both singleton caches and never publish into the current-state entry, preventing historical queries from evicting or poisoning ordinary reads. Concurrent misses may duplicate work but publish only complete immutable values. ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - TSAN integration matrix: snapshot reads passed 6/6 across S3, Azure, and local storage (Iceberg v1/v2) - Snapshot-read integration coverage asserts derived-cache hits and an ordinary read immediately after a historical read - Live exact-hit benchmark: - 1271 -> 1375 RPS (+8.2%) - CPU/query 4.565 -> 4.163 ms (-8.8%) - `IcebergMetadataUpdateMicroseconds` 0.341 -> 0.010 ms/query - one derived-metadata cache hit/query, zero warm misses
signals.author: adonm

signals.title: Iceberg: cache immutable object metadata
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Cache object metadata for immutable Iceberg data and delete files to avoid repeated object-storage HEAD requests. ### Summary Iceberg data/delete files are immutable and are replaced under new paths. The object-storage reader nevertheless fetched size/ETag/mtime for each selected file on every query. This PR adds a bounded per-process SLRU for `ObjectMetadata` when reading `IcebergDataObjectInfo`: - cache identity includes connection/namespace information and the resolved path - tag-bearing metadata has a distinct key - real ETags are retained for downstream cache validation - hit/miss/eviction events and size/count metrics are exposed ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - New stateless IcebergLocal regression - Live validation: first read `1 miss / 0 hits`; second read `0 misses / 1 hit` - On a delayed object endpoint this removed the fixed per-query HEAD wait
signals.author: adonm

signals.title: Iceberg: cache partition candidates per manifest
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Cache complete partition candidate row indexes for Iceberg manifests and reuse them across point predicates in the same partition. ### Summary The existing manifest path walks every row for each query, even when partition pruning keeps only a few entries. This PR builds an immutable candidate-row vector on the first complete manifest scan and publishes it only after all rows finish successfully. Cache identity includes table root, manifest path, table snapshot, partition-condition serialization, schema IDs, and inherited sequence number. Different point literals in the same partition reuse candidates and still run per-query min/max pruning. New snapshots cannot reuse old candidates. Cancelled, partial, or exceptional scans never publish partial vectors. `SYSTEM CLEAR ICEBERG MANIFEST PRUNE CACHE`, events, and metrics are included. ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - Stateless regression covers different literals, explicit clear, and new-snapshot invalidation - Live validation: warm measurement had one candidate-cache hit per query; a new snapshot missed and returned its newly added row, then hit on the next query
signals.author: adonm

signals.title: Parquet: share cached footer metadata between readers
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Share immutable cached Parquet footer metadata between V3 readers instead of deep-copying it per query. ### Summary `ParquetMetadataCache` stores a parsed `FileMetaData`, but `getOrSetMetadata` returned it by value. Files with hundreds of row groups and wide schemas therefore deep-copied the entire footer for every reader. This PR returns an aliasing shared_ptr that retains the cache cell. V3 readers keep the immutable footer alive even if the cache entry is evicted. Noncached readers still own a local metadata value. ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - New `ParquetMetadataCache` unit test verifies pointer reuse, one loader invocation, and lifetime after eviction - Unit test result: 1/1 passed - Controlled Iceberg point lookup: CPU/query 5.90 ms -> 3.97 ms; 1204 -> 1643 RPS
signals.author: adonm

signals.title: Parquet: binary-search and cache ordered row-group fences
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Binary-search ordered, non-overlapping Parquet row-group ranges for conjunctive point predicates and cache the validated fence index. ### Summary Parquet V3 currently builds and checks a full hyperrectangle for every row group. For point lookups in physically ordered files, only one row group can match, but hundreds of generic checks are still performed. This PR: - extracts only top-level conjunctive single-column finite points from `KeyCondition` - decodes actual footer statistics for that primitive - proves all nonempty row-group ranges are strictly ordered and non-overlapping - binary-searches zero or one candidate - runs the original full condition on the candidate for residual correctness - falls back unchanged for OR predicates, overlap, disorder, nullable infinity, missing/malformed stats, or unsupported mappings - caches proven and failed fence indexes in a bounded 64 MiB per-process LRU keyed by strong file ETag, physical column, and decoded/output type ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - Stateless regression covers sorted hit, absent point, late disorder, and OR fallback - Expected predicate checks: sorted=1, absent=0, disorder=509, OR=509 - Live Iceberg validation: 509 full checks/query -> 1, one row group read, exact results preserved - Combined with indexed pages: CPU/query 7.04 ms -> 5.90 ms before footer sharing

signals.title: Add experimental unity_v2 catalog
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105038 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100669 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry: Added a new experimental `unity_v2` catalog type to the DataLakeCatalog database engine. It serves both Delta Lake and Iceberg tables from a single Unity Catalog, detecting the format of each table and routing Iceberg tables through the Unity Catalog Iceberg REST endpoint. It supports Databricks authentication with an OAuth service principal, a personal access token, or a pre-obtained OAuth token, and vended credentials for managed and external tables, including UniForm. Enable it with the setting `allow_experimental_database_unity_v2_catalog`. ### Summary Create "unity_v2" catalog. It supports both Delta and Iceberg tables, in contrast to the current "unity" catalog, which only supports Delta. The V2 catalog is behind an experimental feature flag. After a release or two, we can switch it to be the main "unity" catalog. Credit to @melvynator for the prototype in #100669. ### Tests Added integration tests. Also, ran manual tests. I first created the following tables in Databricks. ``` CREATE TABLE delta_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA; INSERT INTO delta_managed VALUES (1, 1.0); CREATE TABLE delta_external (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA LOCATION 's3://<test-bucket>/tables/delta_external'; INSERT INTO delta_external VALUES (2, 2.0); CREATE TABLE iceberg_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING ICEBERG; INSERT INTO iceberg_managed VALUES (3, 3.0); CREATE TABLE uniform_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableIcebergCompatV2' = 'true', 'delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats' = 'iceberg'); INSERT INTO uniform_managed VALUES (4, 4.0); CREATE TABLE uniform_external (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA LOCATION 's3://<test-bucket>/tables/uniform_external' TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableIcebergCompatV2' = 'true', 'delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats' = 'iceberg'); INSERT INTO uniform_external VALUES (5, 5.0); ``` Then created the following databases: ``` CREATE DATABASE unity_oauth_token ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://dbc-xxxxx.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.1/unity-catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'unity_v2', warehouse = 'external-loc-catalog', catalog_credential = 'eyJ...'; CREATE DATABASE unity_static ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://dbc-xxxxx.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.1/unity-catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'unity_v2', warehouse = 'external-loc-catalog', catalog_credential = '{client_id}:{client_secret}'; CREATE DATABASE unity_pat_token ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://dbc-xxxxx.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.1/unity-catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'unity_v2', warehouse = 'external-loc-catalog', catalog_credential = 'dapi....'; ``` For each database, I ran the following queries and verified expected results: ``` show tables from db; select * from db.`test_schema.delta_managed`; select * from db.`test_schema.delta_external`; select * from db.`test_schema.iceberg_managed`; select * from db.`test_schema.uniform_managed`; select * from db.`test_schema.uniform_external`; show create table db.`test_schema.delta_managed`; show create table db.`test_schema.delta_external`; show create table db.`test_schema.iceberg_managed`; show create table db.`test_schema.uniform_managed`; show create table db.`test_schema.uniform_external`; ``` <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115879&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115879](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115879+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL arithmetic operators and sum/avg aggregation over native histograms
signals.text: ## Summary Sixth slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115860. Adds PromQL arithmetic operators and `sum`/`avg` aggregation over stored native histograms, mirroring the histogram arms of `vectorElemBinop` and of the `parser.SUM`/`parser.AVG` branches of `aggregation` in Prometheus promql/engine.go: - **Scalar functions** `timeSeriesHistogram{Add,Sub,MulByScalar,DivByScalar}` over the native-histogram arithmetic kernel: histogram OP histogram is only `+` (`add`) and `-` (`sub`, result marked as a gauge); histogram OP float is only `*` (`mul`) and `/` (`div`); every result is `compact(0)`-ed; schema-incompatible pairs (exponential vs custom buckets) produce NULL (upstream drops the sample). - **Aggregates** `timeSeriesHistogram{Sum,Avg}OverGroup`: compensated Kahan-Neumaier accumulation per group for `sum` (new `kahanAdd` in the kernel); the direct mean with the incremental-mean fallback on overflow for `avg`; an empty or schema-incompatible group produces NULL (upstream drops the group element). - **Converter**: arithmetic binary operators over a combined float+histogram grid (`StoreMethod::HISTOGRAM_GRID`) resolve each operand per step by `sample_kinds` and produce the float and histogram arms independently (disallowed kind combinations drop the sample, matching upstream); `sum`/`avg` aggregate the kind-masked arms separately via the `-ForEach` combinator and drop steps whose group mixes float and histogram samples. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL arithmetic operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) and `sum`/`avg` aggregation over stored Prometheus native histograms, with upstream-compatible schema-compatibility and mixed-sample dropping rules. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115685 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115734 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115735 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115736 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115860 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115880&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115880](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115880+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reject an explicit STATISTICS clause on a column that is not physically stored
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115769 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Declaring `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column is now rejected when the table is created or altered, instead of being accepted and making every subsequent `INSERT` fail with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. Closes #114791. ### Description Related: #115769, whose review asked for this shape. Declaring `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` column was accepted, but the table could not be written to at all: such a column is absent from every written block, so with `materialize_statistics_on_insert` (default 1) every `INSERT` failed `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. Statistics on a non-physical column were already refused elsewhere: `addImplicitStatistics` skips `Alias`/`Ephemeral`, and `ADD STATISTICS` checks `columns.hasPhysical`. Only the two inline column-declaration spellings had no such check. This adds it where the resulting metadata is known: `registerStorageMergeTree` for `CREATE`, `MergeTreeData::checkAlterIsPossible` for `ALTER`, using one pair read from the column's own metadata: `!columns.hasPhysical(name) && column.statistics.hasExplicitStatistics()`. The `ALTER` check is a delta check, refusing only a state the statement produced, and both exempt `Replicated`-database DDL replay so a rolling upgrade cannot wedge a secondary's queue. Existing such tables still load, read and detach/attach. ```sql CREATE TABLE tab (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(tdigest)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); -- before: accepted; INSERT then failed Code: 10 (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) -- after: Code: 708. Cannot add statistics to column 'b': it is not physically stored. (ILLEGAL_STATISTICS) ``` Three disclosed behaviour changes. `MODIFY COLUMN b <type> ALIAS <expr>` on a column that already had explicit statistics is refused although it has no `STATISTICS` token, and `CREATE TABLE dst AS src` / `CLONE AS` off such a table is refused; `DROP STATISTICS b` first is the remedy for both. **Known gap, not fixed here:** `SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA` on a grandfathered table is also refused and leaves it detached, because that path reparses stored metadata and sets `attach` without `attach_short_syntax`, so the definition is misclassified as fresh input (`InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1489-1492`). That belongs in the caller, not in this predicate; say the word and I will send it here or separately. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Ten rejection arms (both `CREATE` spellings, deprecated `MergeTree(...)` syntax, full-definition `ATTACH`, `ALTER ADD`/`MODIFY` including no-type `MODIFY COLUMN b STATISTICS(...)` and chained `ADD COLUMN b ALIAS a+1, MODIFY COLUMN b STATISTICS(...)`) were each measured against a build without this change and one with it: accepted before, `ILLEGAL_STATISTICS` after. Six negative controls are byte-identical on both builds: the two `IF NOT EXISTS` no-ops, `MATERIALIZED`/`DEFAULT` with statistics, alias converted to `MATERIALIZED` with statistics, implicit statistics on an alias, and a physical column with only implicit statistics converted to an alias. For a table created before the check: loads, reads, `DROP STATISTICS`, an unrelated `ADD COLUMN`, `DETACH`/`ATTACH` with statistics intact and a pure `RENAME COLUMN` all succeed; changing the statistics on the offending column is refused. Control: the same procedure with `CODEC(ZSTD(1))` instead fails to load on the same binary, which is what this check avoids. Replication: on `ReplicatedMergeTree` the `ALTER` is refused on the initiator with an empty `system.replication_queue` and both replicas usable. On a `Replicated` database both checks fire for a client statement, while an `ALTER` or a full-definition `ATTACH` committed by an older initiator is still applied on replay with no retrying queue entry. A further replica created with no column list (columns from ZooKeeper) still succeeds, while the same `CREATE` with an explicit offending column list is refused. `02864_statistics_ddl` passes 50/50 with randomized settings and 50/50 without, and fails on a build without this change, so the expected-error annotations are not pinning current behaviour. `01318_alter_add_column_exists`, `04542_create_if_not_exists_as_select_skips_create_only_validation` and `03224_invalid_alter` pass. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115882&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115882](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115882+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix CAST of an Array(Map) constant sent to a remote server
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115647 A `Map` is physically an `Array(Tuple(key, value))`, and that is also how a `Map` constant is written down when the analyzer serializes a query for a remote server: `ConstantNode::toASTImpl` renders the field as an array of tuples and wraps it into `_CAST(..., 'Array(Map(K, V))')`. On the receiving side `CAST` compared the nesting depth of `Array(Array(Tuple(K, V)))` (two) with `Array(Map(K, V))` (one) and rejected the cast before ever reaching the element wrapper, which converts `Array(Tuple(K, V))` to `Map(K, V)` without trouble. So any query whose constant folds to an `Array(Map(...))` failed once it was shipped to a shard or to a parallel replica: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (m Map(String, String)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY m; INSERT INTO t SELECT map('k', toString(number)) FROM numbers(4); SELECT count() FROM remote('127.0.0.{1,2}', currentDatabase(), t) WHERE has([map('k', '3')], m); ``` ``` Code: 53. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.2:9000. DB::Exception: CAST AS Array can only be performed between same-dimensional array types: In scope SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM default.t AS __table1 WHERE has(_CAST([[('k', '3')]], 'Array(Map(String, String))'), __table1.m). (TYPE_MISMATCH) ``` `CAST` now counts a `Map` as the array of tuples it stands for when comparing nesting depth, so both spellings sit at the same depth. A genuine depth mismatch, such as `Array(String)` to `Array(Array(String))`, is still rejected. This is what makes `04510_not_has_function_explain` fail in the `ParallelReplicas` job on `master`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=31e78bbbb66e018db116f4956eb25cbbc27960e6&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20ParallelReplicas%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29 - that test got a `has([map('k', NULL)], m)` query in #115647, and the query hits this cast whenever the filter is actually shipped to a replica. The bug itself is much older and reproduces on any version with a plain `Distributed` query. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `TYPE_MISMATCH` ("CAST AS Array can only be performed between same-dimensional array types") for a query with a constant of type `Array(Map(...))`, such as `has([map('k', 'v')], m)`, executed over a `Distributed` table or with parallel replicas. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115883&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115883](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115883+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Require forward progress when counting rows in Avro, MsgPack and ProtobufList
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115437 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115437 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SELECT count()` never terminating, or returning an invented row count, on a corrupted `Avro`, `MsgPack` or `ProtobufList` file. The `optimize_count_from_files` fast path counted rows without requiring the read position to advance, so a two byte `ProtobufList` file produced billions of rows and never returned. Such input is now rejected with the same error the ordinary read path gives. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim, who [offered to review](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115437#issuecomment-5341268327); [I took it](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115437#issuecomment-5369600816). `IRowInputFormat::read()` re-enters `countRows()` until it returns 0, so a `countRows()` that reports a row without consuming input never terminates. Three formats could, at two layers: - **ProtobufList** discarded `readFieldNumber`'s result, which is false *without consuming* once the envelope message ends, while `reader->eof()` only reports the underlying buffer. Now honoured, throwing the read path's own `PROTOBUF_BAD_CAST` at the same guard. - **MsgPack** treated `parse_helper::execute`'s `parse_return` **enum** as a bool, so `PARSE_PARSE_ERROR (-1)` left the loop as if it had succeeded, offset unadvanced. Each status is now handled; the read path is unaffected (details below). `countRows` also discarded `readObject`'s result, counting a partial row as complete when the object count is not a multiple of the column count; it now raises the read path's own "Not enough values to complete the row". - **Avro** takes its row count from the block header, so counting without decoding the payload cannot tell a count that is present from one merely claimed. `supportsCountRows()` is therefore false and the dead `countRows()` removed, so count queries take the read path, which already rejects these inputs. Cost on 3M rows / 32MB: 0.109s to 0.136s. Beyond the report: a header declaring 10^9 rows returned `1000005000` rows from a 10KB file **as a successful answer** rather than a hang, so nothing alerted the user. Out of scope: a zero width Avro schema (only a NULL column) with a **negative** count hangs the ordinary read path too. No ClickHouse side change reaches it -- `hasMore()`/`decr()` live in `contrib/avro`, driven by `readRow` and the Iceberg manifest deserializer as well. That needs a `ClickHouse/avro` change first, where I have no write access; the patch is ready and I will follow up. <details><summary>Sibling coverage, refuted alternatives and validation</summary> MsgPack read path: `parse_error` throws before `execute()` can return `-1`, and no `MsgPackVisitor` method returns `false`, so neither error status is reachable with that visitor. Verified by measurement. Two simpler designs are refuted by measurement. A bound on the declared count by input size fails because valid Avro holds 1000 rows in 139 bytes (all NULL column) and 200000 in 797 bytes (deflate). A central guard in `IRowInputFormat::read()` fails because `Npy` and `RawBLOB` legitimately return rows consuming zero bytes. Both cases are test arms, so neither can be reintroduced silently. Also out of scope: a zero width schema declaring 10^9 rows still reports them, but the read path now agrees, so the file is self consistent rather than misreported. All 15 remaining `countRows()` implementations were swept empirically, 17 formats x 6 adversarial inputs: only the three reported formats hung, and none does now. The same sweep prints a hang on unpatched master, so it can see what it reports absent. `CapnProto`, `MySQLDump` and `RowInputFormatWithNamesAndTypes` look similar when read but consume or throw on every input tested. `Npy` and `RawBLOB` legitimately return rows consuming zero bytes and must not be guarded. Read path identity: 17 order independent oracles (`count()` plus `sum(cityHash64(...))`, sorted rows, `DESCRIBE`) at `max_block_size` 1 / 7 / 13 / 1000 / 65505, all identical before and after; 13 of 13 deliberate mutations detected, so the comparison is not blind. New test `04946_count_from_files_forward_progress.sh` asserts the error code on a bounded run, never elapsed time. Run against unpatched master it differs from its reference on 5 lines, and they are exactly the five `optimize_count_from_files = 1` arms; it passed 50 of 50 randomized runs. The `avro msgpack protobuf` suites give an identical per test verdict list before and after. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115884&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115884](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115884+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Make per-key duplicate-key bookkeeping cheaper when parsing JSON objects
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113731 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improved the performance of parsing JSON objects into a `JSON` column. The per-key duplicate-key bookkeeping now keeps its two type sets as bit masks in a single map entry instead of two maps of nested sets. The gain grows with the number of keys per object, and applies whether or not the object contains a repeated key. ### Description Related: #113731 Since `ObjectJSONNode::traverseAndInsert` was split into two passes, duplicate-key bookkeeping costs two `getJSONElementType()` calls, two `unordered_map` nodes and two nested `unordered_set` allocations per traversed key, where the single-pass version paid one of each. The cost scales with key count, not byte size. The split carries backport labels, so release branches inherit it. `JSONElementType` has two enumerators, so a set of them is two bits. Both per-key sets now live in one map entry as bit masks: the types the first pass accepted, and those the second already emitted. That removes the nested-set allocations and the separate `visited_keys` map, and the second pass goes from up to four hash lookups per key to one. Measured on x86_64 release builds with `UserTimeMicroseconds`, paired interleaved, 7 runs per side, across the patch releases bracketing the split (v26.6.2.160, v26.6.3.62). The regression: **1.4772** at 1000 keys per object against **1.0398** at 10 keys per object at equal byte volume, so it tracks key count rather than a general slowdown, and **1.3277** on `json_type_parsing` query 3. Against master: **0.6604** on query 3, **0.5589** at 1000 keys, **0.5676** with the duplicated key last. Pre-scanning each object to skip the bookkeeping entirely was rejected: faster still without a repeated key, but it charges the scan to objects that have one, measuring 1.13 to 1.14 there. Duplicated literal-and-object keys are accepted by default, so that is not a rare shape. Behaviour is unchanged, so no new test is added. A differential matrix of 60 duplicated-key cases (both orderings, three-way duplicates, typed paths, shared data, escaped dots, both settings crossed) is byte-identical to master in results and error text, while diverging from a pre-split binary. Breaking either mask changes 5, 9 or 11 of the existing duplicated-key tests' queries. Root cause analysis by egor-click, who proposed the pre-scan variant. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115888&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115888](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115888+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report a not-implemented ORC compression codec instead of aborting
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115412 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an abort on debug and sanitizer builds when reading an ORC file whose compression codec the bundled ORC reader does not implement. Such a file is now reported with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of the bare `STD_EXCEPTION` (code 1001) naming a C++ type that a release build used to give. ### Description Truncating an in-repo ORC file kills the process with no output at all: ```bash head -c 289 tests/queries/0_stateless/data_orc/orc_nested_union_type.orc > t289.orc clickhouse local --query "SELECT * FROM file('t289.orc', ORC) FORMAT Null" # Aborted (core dumped), stdout and stderr both empty ``` The truncation leaves byte 6 in the postscript's compression field. liborc does not implement codec 6, so it throws `orc::NotImplementedYet`, a `std::logic_error`. `getFileReader` had no handler, so it reached `getCurrentExceptionMessage`, which on a debug or sanitizer build deliberately treats an in-flight `std::logic_error` as an internal-invariant violation and aborts. That logs to the root logger, unattached in `clickhouse local`, so the process dies while composing its own message. A release build does not abort. Measured on 26.7.6.6, it reports `Code: 1001. DB::Exception: orc::NotImplementedYet: Unknown compression codec 6. (STD_EXCEPTION)`. The fix translates that one exception type at the `orc::createReader` boundary, through a shared `createORCReader` used by both production call sites (`NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp` and `Storages/Hive/HiveFile.cpp`, equally unguarded). The assertion in the formatter is left alone: it guards real internal bugs, and the ORC reader raises `std::logic_error` from ClickHouse-supplied inputs elsewhere, which must keep aborting. Hence a catch typed on `orc::NotImplementedYet` alone. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` rather than `INCORRECT_DATA` because the file may be valid: codec 6 is `BROTLI`, which the ORC spec declares but the C++ reader does not implement. A file with no compression field at all is still reported corrupt, by `ParseError`. Only the ORC half of the issue. Avro is not fixed: I could not obtain a reproducer, and would rather not add a handler I cannot test. Could you share the fixture? Validation: the abort reproduces on five entry paths, all five fixed. Neighbouring truncations, the nine `data_orc` fixtures and a stride-1 sweep are identical before and after. The Hive site is compile-verified only, since exercising it needs HDFS. New test `05036_orc_unimplemented_codec_no_abort`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115889&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115889](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115889+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not reject a distributed plan whose sort column passes through a step unchanged
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737 Requested by @ PedroTadim in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737#issuecomment-5368109515. Reported by @ XuJia0210. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `Unknown identifier` raised during query plan optimization under `make_distributed_plan = 1` when a window query's sort column passes through an `Expression` step that does not mention it. Closes #115737. ### Description Under `make_distributed_plan = 1` and `distributed_plan_optimize_exchanges = 1`, a valid query was rejected while `optimizeExchanges` moved a sorted `GatherExchange` above an `Expression` step: ``` Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown identifier: '__table3.a'. (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) ``` Root cause. `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` builds a step's output header from the evaluated DAG outputs plus every input-header column that matched no DAG input, copied through unchanged. Such a pass-through column is in the header while having no node in `dag.outputs`. The move-up check tested `expression_header->has(...)` first, which passes, and the short-circuit `||` then called `isSortColumnPreserved`, whose `findInOutputs` scans only `outputs` and throws instead of answering. The change uses the existing `tryFindInOutputs` and answers "preserved" when the DAG does not mention the column. That is the correct answer, not the convenient one: `ExpressionActions` forwards an unconsumed input column's `ColumnPtr` verbatim, and both step types are `ISimpleTransform`s that cannot reorder rows, so a merge keyed by such a column stays valid. `Optimizations/Cascades/DagNameTranslation` already answers the same question the same way for the same machinery, via its `TranslatedName::Passthrough` case. Reaching the branch needs a column-keyed inner window to build the sorted gather and an outer window keyed by a constant to put an all-pass-through step above it; the new test builds exactly that. It asserts the move-up positionally: "no longer throws" would also pass for the fail-closed answer, and a `GatherExchange` is present whether or not it moved. Only the `Expression` carrier is reachable today, so the test covers that one. For a focused `Filter` the analyzer's `__tableN` renaming makes the preceding `expression_header->has(...)` test fail, so the `||` short-circuits before the lookup, and a `Filter` arm would pass on unpatched master. Validation: 43 `distributed_plan` and 119 `window` tests give identical results on the patched and unpatched binary apart from the new test; 50 randomized runs of the new test pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115890&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115890](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115890+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added a new filesystem cache setting `use_real_disk_size` (disabled by default). When enabled, cache reservations are accounted in filesystem allocation units (block size) instead of raw reserved bytes, so the `FilesystemCacheSize` metric, the eviction-size metrics, and `current_size` in `system.filesystem_cache_settings` use block-aligned reservation accounting. The accounting is a block-aligned approximation of the reservation footprint on disk, not the exact allocated size; an in-flight read can include reserve-ahead bytes that have not yet been written. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written Documented the `use_real_disk_size` filesystem cache setting in `docs/concepts/features/configuration/server-config/storing-data.mdx`. It accounts cache reservations in filesystem allocation units (block size), so `FilesystemCacheSize`, the eviction-size metrics, and `current_size` in `system.filesystem_cache_settings` use block-aligned reservation accounting (a block-aligned approximation of the reservation footprint on disk). The per-segment `size` in `system.filesystem_cache` is not affected by this setting and stays the segment's logical range size; for a partially downloaded segment, use `downloaded_size` for the bytes actually written. <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. signals.title: Add early short-circuit evaluation for OR/AND in the analyzer to prevent unnecessary scalar subquery execution
signals.text: <!--- Disable AI PR formatting assistant: true --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): You can now enable early short-circuit folding for builtin `and` and `or` during analysis with the `enable_function_early_short_circuit` setting. This can skip executing dead single-row `count()` scalar subqueries while preserving normal type inference and semantic validation. Resolves #83017 ### Details When `enable_function_early_short_circuit` is enabled (and `short_circuit_function_evaluation` is not disabled), the analyzer detects decisive constants in builtin `and` / `or` expressions. The optimization is deliberately conservative. It is attempted only for expressions without outer-scope Identifier/Column dependencies and only for scalar subqueries of the statically single-row forms `SELECT count()` or `SELECT count(*)` without GROUP BY/window/HAVING/QUALIFY/LIMIT BY. All other scalar forms use normal analysis and execution. A dedicated temporary `QueryAnalyzer` resolves a clone in type-only mode using an isolated, cache-disabled scope. It never mutates the live resolver state. Scalar values are represented by non-constant type placeholders, and expressions containing aggregate/`arrayJoin` semantic carriers outside scalar-subquery boundaries are not replaced. Resolves #83017 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=83505&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/83505](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F83505+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1856` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Add pointwise and global min/max functions to `NumericIndexedVector`
signals.text: <!---AI changelog entry and formatting assistance: false--> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added pointwise min/max operations and global min/max value functions for NumericIndexedVector. Also improved and refactored the internal implementation of `pointwiseLess` for better correctness, performance, and code reuse across signed and unsigned numeric types. Resolves #88274 ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes #### Motivation: These additions extend the NumericIndexedVector family with commonly used numerical comparison and reduction capabilities, enabling more expressive analytical queries and feature computation over vectorized numeric aggregates. This work also addresses user requests for richer NumericIndexedVector operators — see [issue #88274](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/88274). #### New functions: - numericIndexedVectorPointwiseMax(v1, v2) — pointwise maximum between two numeric indexed vectors. - numericIndexedVectorPointwiseMin(v1, v2) — pointwise minimum between two numeric indexed vectors. - `numericIndexedVectorPointwise*`— functions now accept a Bitmap as the second argument. - numericIndexedVectorGetMaxValue(v) — returns the maximum value stored in a single numeric indexed vector. - numericIndexedVectorGetMinValue(v) — returns the minimum value stored in a single numeric indexed vector. All functions are compatible with both signed and unsigned numeric types, as well as floating-point vectors. #### Other changes: - Reimplemented and refactored pointwiseLess that correctly handles signed two's-complement representations. - Unified common bitmap selection logic to enhance code reuse and reduce redundant Roaring bitmap operations. - Introduced shared helpers for efficient bit-slice accumulation and extrema computation. #### Example usage: ``` SQL WITH numericIndexedVectorBuild(mapFromArrays([1, 2, 3], [10.0, -2.5, 5.5])) AS vec1, numericIndexedVectorBuild(mapFromArrays([1, 2, 3], [3.0, -8.0, 7.2])) AS vec2 SELECT numericIndexedVectorToMap(numericIndexedVectorPointwiseMax(vec1, vec2)) AS max_result, numericIndexedVectorToMap(numericIndexedVectorPointwiseMin(vec1, vec2)) AS min_result, numericIndexedVectorGetMaxValue(vec1) AS global_max, numericIndexedVectorGetMinValue(vec1) AS global_min;\G ``` #### Result: ``` SQL Row 1: ────── max_result: {1:10,2:-2.5,3:7.199999988079071} min_result: {1:3,2:-8,3:5.5} global_max: 10 global_min: -2.5 ``` <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=88840&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/88840](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F88840+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Optimization of `GROUP BY` in the presence of `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize `GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT` and `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` queries by maintaining a bounded heap during aggregation to prune groups that cannot appear in the result, significantly reducing memory usage and execution time for high-cardinality grouping. Controlled by the `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization` setting. Based on the initial implementation by [Dmitriy Terenichev](https://github.com/Dmitry909) ([#78553](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78553)). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/72610 Query shapes that benefit from this optimization: - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N` -- single key, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key LIMIT N` -- single key, no ORDER BY - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2, k3 ASC LIMIT N` -- 3+ keys, full match - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, ORDER BY is a prefix of GROUP BY - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 1 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 2 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 LIMIT N` -- composite keys, no ORDER BY - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL ORDER BY URL ASC LIMIT N` -- String keys - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL LIMIT N` -- String keys, no ORDER BY Not supported (optimization is skipped): - `ORDER BY agg()` (ORDER BY aggregate function, not a GROUP BY key) (handled by [another PR](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98607)) - `WITH TOTALS`, `HAVING`, `GROUPING SETS`, `CUBE`, `ROLLUP` - `LIMIT WITH TIES` - ~~Non-final aggregation (distributed partial aggregation)~~ - `max_rows_to_group_by` is set - `rows_before_limit_at_least` mode (exact count) - a COLLATE on any of the matched GROUP BY keys (a COLLATE on a later ORDER BY column past the full key prefix cannot affect which groups qualify and does not disable the optimization) - ORDER BY columns that are not a leading prefix of GROUP BY keys <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96630&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96630](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96630+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix JSON/XML format statistics race condition with parallel replicas
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `rows_read` and `rows_before_limit_at_least` reported as 0 or stale in JSON/XML format output when a query with `LIMIT` reads from remote connections (parallel replicas or the `remote` table function). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) No documentation changes needed — this is a bug fix with no user-facing API changes. --- ## Summary - When parallel replicas are used with `LIMIT`, `rows_read` in JSON/XML output is reported as 0 - Root cause: race condition where `finalizeImpl` writes statistics BEFORE `PipelineExecutor::finalizeExecution` collects remaining progress from connection draining - Fix: two-phase output format finalization — statistics are written AFTER all progress has been collected - The same drain also delivers late `ProfileInfo` packets that update the `rows_before_limit_at_least` / `rows_before_aggregation` counters, so the deferral covers the whole trailer, and the native-protocol `ProfileInfo` sent to the client is refreshed from the post-drain counters ## Approach Split the output format's finalization so statistics are written AFTER `finalizeExecution` collects all remaining progress: - **Phase 1** (during pipeline, in `finalizeImpl`): Write everything EXCEPT the trailer after the `rows` field (`rows_before_limit_at_least`, `rows_before_aggregation`, the `"statistics"` section) and closing delimiter - **Phase 2** (after `finalizeExecution`): Re-read the rows-before-* counters, write the trailer and close the document via a finalize callback ### Key changes: - `IOutputFormat`: Added `hasDeferredStatistics`, `writeDeferredStatisticsAndFinalize`, `completeDeferredStatistics` mechanism; `snapshotRowsBeforeCounters` re-reads the shared counters before the deferred trailer is written - `PipelineExecutor`: Added `setFinalizeCallback` called at end of `finalizeExecution` after progress collection - `CompletedPipelineExecutor`: Sets the finalize callback to invoke `completeDeferredStatistics` - `JSONRowOutputFormat`, `XMLRowOutputFormat`, `JSONColumnsWithMetadataBlockOutputFormat`: Override deferred statistics methods; the whole trailer (`rows_before_limit_at_least`, `rows_before_aggregation`, `statistics`) is deferred to phase 2 (`JSONUtils::writeRowsBeforeAndStatistics` factors out the shared writer) - `ParallelFormattingOutputFormat`: Propagates deferred statistics through the parallel formatting pipeline - `LazyOutputFormat` / `PullingOutputFormat`: `getProfileInfo` re-snapshots the rows-before-* counters, so the `ProfileInfo` packet sent to native-protocol clients (TCP `clickhouse-client`, gRPC, `LocalConnection`) carries the post-drain values — by the time it is sent, the executor thread has been joined and the counters are final - New failpoint `tcp_handler_sleep_before_secondary_query_trailing_packets` delays a secondary query's trailing `Totals` / `Extremes` / `ProfileInfo` / `Progress` / `EndOfStream`, making the race deterministic for tests Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85785 ## Test plan - [x] Build succeeds (Release) - [x] Test `00365_statistics_in_formats` passes - [x] JSON format tests pass (`00159_parallel_formatting_json_and_friends_1/2`, `00378_json_quote_64bit_integers`, `00685_output_format_json_escape_forward_slashes`, `01447_json_strings`, `01449_json_compact_strings`, `01486_json_array_output`, `02554_format_json_columns_for_empty`) - [x] XML format tests pass (`00307_format_xml`, `02122_parallel_formatting_XML`) - [x] `03918_statistics_in_formats_parallel_replicas` — forward guard: parallel-replicas `rows_read` matches the single-node value - [x] New deterministic reproducer `04603_rows_before_limit_parallel_replicas_late_packets` — fails without the fix (failpoint forces the trailing packets into the drain window); checks `rows_read` under parallel replicas and `rows_read` + `rows_before_limit_at_least` through the `remote` table function, over HTTP (server-side formatting) and native TCP (client-side formatting), across `JSON`, `JSONColumnsWithMetadata`, and `XML` - [ ] CI: Run with parallel replicas to verify `rows_read` is no longer 0 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches query pipeline execution, cancellation, and output formatting/finalization paths; while scoped to statistics/progress reporting, it changes timing and thread-synchronization and could affect query completion/cancellation behavior under parallel replicas. > > **Overview** > Fixes a race where JSON/XML output could report `rows_read=0` with parallel replicas + `LIMIT` by ensuring final `Progress` packets (drained after cancellation/early completion) are incorporated before statistics are emitted. > > This introduces **two-phase output finalization**: `IOutputFormat` can defer writing statistics/closing delimiters (`hasDeferredStatistics`/`writeDeferredStatisticsAndFinalize`), and `PipelineExecutor` now supports a `setFinalizeCallback` invoked at the end of `finalizeExecution()` after collecting remaining progress; `CompletedPipelineExecutor` wires this to `IOutputFormat::completeDeferredStatistics()`. > > Cancellation/draining logic is tightened to preserve trailing progress and avoid blocking hard cancels: `PipelineExecutor` triggers a `PartialResult` cancel on normal completion, `ISource::cancel` skips `onCancel` for `PartialResult` but allows later escalation, `RemoteSource` adds explicit cancel-reason upgrades and aborts drain via `RemoteQueryExecutor::abortDrain`, and `RemoteQueryExecutor::finish()` drains until all replica connections complete while swallowing expected cancel exceptions. Adds a stateless regression test `03918_statistics_in_formats_parallel_replicas` to assert `rows_read > 0` across JSON/XML formats over TCP/HTTP. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5818266286a7645dcf1b57212bf9b3214cfd2ec8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96978&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96978](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96978+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Validate IN tuple/subquery column count mismatch in analyzer
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/74442 The analyzer (`resolveFunction`) now validates that the number of elements on the left side of `IN` matches the number of columns in the right-side subquery. Previously, constant folding could optimize away the `IN` expression and silently hide the mismatch: for example, `(1, 1) IN (SELECT 1)` wrapped in a subquery with a constant-false outer `WHERE` succeeded silently. Now it correctly throws `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` during analysis. A single `Tuple` column on the right side is still accepted, since `FunctionIn` compares the whole left-side value against it; `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` wrappers are unwrapped before the check. Covered by the new test `03380_in_tuple_subquery_column_count`, including the original reproducer from the issue. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Detect column count mismatch between a tuple and a subquery in the `IN` clause during analysis, preventing constant folding from silently hiding the error. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=97540&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/97540](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F97540+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Skip writing all-default columns during MergeTree INSERT
signals.text: ## Summary During MergeTree INSERT, columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (e.g., all zeros for `UInt64`, all empty strings for `String`, all `NULL`s for `Nullable`) are detected and excluded from the part's column list before constructing `MergedBlockOutputStream`. This avoids writing unnecessary `.bin` files (Wide parts) or data streams (Compact parts), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads where most columns in each INSERT are left at their type's default. The optimization is opt-in via the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (off by default). It additionally requires `serialization_info_version` to be set to `with_missing_columns` (the format version that records frozen defaults for missing columns), so that a cluster pinned to a lower version for compatibility never writes parts that older servers cannot read. The block itself is passed intact to the writer, so skip indices, projections, primary index, and min-max index are all computed from the full data. Reading a part that lacks a column fills it with type-defaults automatically — the same mechanism used by `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on existing parts. To keep reads stable, a structured `missing_columns` array is recorded in the part's `serialization.json` (a new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` serialization-info version). Each entry carries the column name and a `type_default` marker. On read, `fillMissingColumns` consults this marker and fills a missing column with its type-default even if the column later gains a new `DEFAULT` expression, so that a subsequent `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the values that were actually inserted. The marker is propagated through merges, mutations, and on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN`, so the inserted type-defaults survive part-lifecycle operations. The `MissingColumnInfo` struct also reserves a `DefaultKind::Expression` variant for future use (issue #92475: `ALTER MODIFY DEFAULT` freezes old expression into parts). This PR only writes `type_default` markers; reading an `expression` marker throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` to fail closed until Phase 2 implements expression evaluation. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/4968, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92475 **On-disk format (`serialization.json`):** ```json { "missing_columns": [ { "name": "b", "default": "type_default" } ], "version": 2 } ``` **Changes:** - Add MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (default `false`). - Add `IColumn::hasOnlyTypeDefaults` with optimized overrides for `ColumnVector`/`ColumnDecimal` (`memoryIsZero`), `ColumnString`/`ColumnArray` (zero offsets), `ColumnNullable` (all-`1` null map), `ColumnSparse` (no stored non-default values), and `ColumnTuple` (delegates to sub-columns). - Filter all-default columns in `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` (`skipEmptyColumnsOnInsert`). Columns with a `DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED`/`ALIAS` expression are never skipped. A column is skipped only when `IDataType::getDefault()` coincides with the column's zero representation (`isDefaultAt(0)` on a column filled via `getDefault()`), which correctly excludes types like `Date32` (type-default 1900-01-01 ≠ memory-zero) and `Enum` (first declared value ≠ 0). Patch parts are excluded, and at least one physical column is always kept. - Gate the optimization on `serialization_info_version >= with_missing_columns`. The populating step is authoritative about the part format version, so `SerializationInfoByName::getVersion` never silently upgrades a part past the configured value (which would make older servers reject it during a rolling upgrade). - Record the missing columns in `serialization.json` via `SerializationInfoByName` (new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` version). Only `type_default` markers are written; `expression` markers are rejected on read until Phase 2. The list is written in sorted order so that identical parts produce identical checksums on different replicas. - Propagate the missing-columns marker through the part lifecycle: through merges (`MergeTask`, for columns that end up absent from the merged part), through mutations (`MutateTask::getColumnsForNewDataPart`, including renames of missing columns), through compact-part renames (`splitAndModifyMutationCommands`), and through on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN` on read (`IMergeTreeReader::fillMissingColumns` translates the requested name back through `alter_conversions`). - Add a stateless test with 46 cases covering: basic skip; all-default keeps one column; merges (horizontal and vertical); mutation; `Nullable`; key columns; `DEFAULT` expression not skipped; `Array`; `Tuple`; `ColumnSparse` source; compact parts; `LowCardinality`; stable values across `ALTER ... DEFAULT`; a non-zero-default `Enum`; marker across mutation/merge/rename after `ALTER DEFAULT`; version gate; DETACH/ATTACH TABLE; DETACH/ATTACH PARTITION; BACKUP/RESTORE; FREEZE; CHECK TABLE; MATERIALIZE COLUMN; CLEAR COLUMN; lightweight DELETE; chained mutations; INSERT SELECT; REPLACE PARTITION; ATTACH PARTITION FROM; ALTER ADD/DROP COLUMN; projections; FixedString; Map; mixed parts merge; Date/DateTime; pre-ADD-COLUMN + skip merge; type-changing mutation; compact-part rename+mutation; Date32 regression. - Add an integration test (`test_skip_empty_columns`) with 6 cases: replicated consistency; merge marker propagation across replicas; mixed-version version gate; backward-compat fallback for old parts; restart durability; REPLACE PARTITION across replicated tables. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): MergeTree INSERT can now skip writing columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (zeros, empty strings, `NULL`s), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads. Enabled by the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` together with `serialization_info_version = 'with_missing_columns'`. Missing columns carry frozen defaults in `serialization.json`, so a later `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the inserted values. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is not required (bug fix, no new user-facing feature) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=98472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/98472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F98472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
