signals.title: Add `GradualResizeProcessor` to limit effective parallelism for GROUP BY on small data volumes
signals.text: When ClickHouse processes GROUP BY, it often overestimates the number of threads needed. With `max_threads = 64` but only a few thousand rows, all 64 `AggregatingTransform` instances get data, produce 64 partial hash tables, and the merge phase has to combine all of them — most nearly empty. This wastes time on merging overhead, which is especially noticeable for heavy aggregate states such as `uniq`, `uniqExact`, `groupArray`, etc. The new `GradualResizeProcessor` starts by pushing data to a single output port (or one port per split group when `min_outstreams_per_resize_after_split` applies), and activates all aggregation streams at once as soon as the configured row or byte threshold is crossed. For small datasets, only one aggregating thread receives data (or one per split group); for large datasets, all threads are used as before. New settings: - `min_rows_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` (default: `0`) - `min_bytes_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` (default: `0`) Both settings default to `0`, so the optimization is opt-in. Set either setting to a non-zero threshold to replace the pre-aggregation `StrictResize` with `GradualResize` for keyed `GROUP BY` queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add opt-in settings `min_rows_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` and `min_bytes_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` that can improve `GROUP BY` performance on small data volumes. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=99495&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/99495](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F99495+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix DPsub join reordering silently dropping single-table ON-clause filters
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111898 The `dpsub` join-order algorithm silently dropped single-table filter and constant predicates that live in a `JOIN ... ON` clause (e.g. `t1.value = 'x'`), returning extra rows. `greedy` uses a different placement path and was unaffected. The predicates are placed in `collectJoinEdgesMask`. Two placement conditions there each silently dropped such a predicate: - `two_relations` required the whole join step to be exactly two relations, so the predicate was dropped whenever its relation was introduced against an already-multi-relation subplan (e.g. `t1` at the top of `t1 JOIN (t2 JOIN t3)`). - `fromLeft() || fromRight() || fromNone()` dropped the predicate for any single-table filter on a relation whose id is >= 2, because `fromLeft`/`fromRight` test relation ids 0 and 1 specifically (they describe the two inputs of a binary join step, not "references a single relation"). The predicate is now attached at the join that introduces its relation (the split whose one side is exactly that relation), and pure constants at the earliest two-relation join. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `dpsub` join-order optimization (`query_plan_optimize_join_order_algorithm = 'dpsub'`) silently dropping single-table filter conditions from a `JOIN ... ON` clause, which could return extra rows. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114629&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114629](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114629+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Implement PromQL functions max_over_time() and min_over_time()
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented functions `max_over_time()` and `min_over_time()`. ### Description Implements `max_over_time(v range-vector)` and `min_over_time(v range-vector)`, previously reported as not implemented. Unlike `sum`/`count`, max/min are not invertible monoids, but they are commutative and associative (merge = `max(a, b)`/`min(a, b)`), so the new header (`AggregateFunctionTimeseriesExtremumOverTime.h`, templated on a bool `is_max_`) reuses `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesSlidingSum`'s existing non-invertible sliding-window fallback (the same two-stacks/recompute machinery already shipped and tested via `deriv`/`predict_linear`) — no new windowing logic was needed. `Bucket == Summary` directly, following `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesToGridSparse`'s (`last_over_time`'s) simplest-case shape, since max/min don't depend on sample order. The comparison is NaN-aware (`candidate > current || isnan(current)`), matching Prometheus's own "a NaN currently held as the running extremum is unconditionally overwritten by the next sample" semantics. Registered `timeSeriesMaxToGrid`/`timeSeriesMinToGrid` in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesHelpers.cpp` and added the two `impl_map` entries in `applyFunctionOverRange.cpp` with `drop_metric_name = true`, matching `rate`/`increase`/`delta`'s convention. **Verified against Prometheus 3.5.0.** **Testing**: new SQL-level test (`04628_max_min_over_time_timeseries_functions.sql`) including an `AggregatingMergeTree` serialize/deserialize/merge round-trip, plus cases in `tests/integration/test_prometheus_protocols/test_evaluation.py` covering both functions over a series with decreases (so results differ meaningfully from `last_over_time`), including a more complex nested query. This flips 13 queries of the PromQL compliance suite from unsupported to passed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112354&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112354](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112354+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix header column order after the no-rescoring vector search rewrite
signal.text: <!--- A technical description of your changes with a motivation --> The second-pass vector search optimization (`vector_search_with_rescoring = 0`) removed the distance function from the `ExpressionStep` outputs and re-appended the rewritten `_distance` alias at the end, changing the header column order. Steps created above the `Sorting` before that rewrite runs — the local top-N `Limit` and the exchange steps of a distributed plan — kept the original column order, and `makeDistributedPlan` failed to rebuild the plan fragments with a logical error: `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting`. Non-distributed plans never re-validate step headers after optimization, which is why this only surfaced with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. The fix reinserts the rewritten output node at the original position of the distance column, so the header column order is preserved and all previously created parent steps stay consistent. Found by AST fuzzer on [#42701](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701) ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=42701&sha=019244e0d46b4d9029fc261a549e1c5cd79b1bbb&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)); the same signature also hit the unrelated #98789 on 2026-08-08. The regression test asserts only the row count: the distributed plan currently returns an incorrect top-N for vector search queries regardless of the rescoring mode — a separate, pre-existing bug. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114456 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting` when a vector search query with `vector_search_with_rescoring = 0` was executed with the experimental `make_distributed_plan` setting. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114457&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114457](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114457+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on premature S3 connection close through the filesystem cache
signal.text: ## Description When an S3 connection closes mid-read while the object still reports its full size, the read used to surface as a cache-layer `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Having zero bytes, but range is not finished`) for what is really a transient I/O failure. `ReadBufferFromS3` now heals a premature stream close by reconnecting and resuming from the current offset instead of reporting a truncated EOF. The expected end of the read is taken from `read_until_position` when set and from the known object `file_size` otherwise, so both the filesystem-cache range-reader path and full-object reads (`S3ObjectStorage::readObject`, `BackupWriterS3::readFile`, which read with `read_until_position == 0`) are covered. It falls back to a regular retryable `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA` only when no progress can be made (an empty response for a non-finished range) and reports `S3_OBJECT_CHANGED_DURING_READ` if the object was overwritten during the read. Includes failpoints and stateless tests (`04417`, `04506`, `04507`, `04509`) that reproduce the premature-close, empty-response, changed-object, and full-object recovery paths. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108948 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Having zero bytes, but range is not finished`) that could occur when an S3 connection was closed prematurely while reading (both through the filesystem cache and for full-object reads). ClickHouse now reconnects and resumes the read from the current offset, and reports a regular retryable read error only when no progress can be made or the object changed during the read. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108950&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/108950](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F108950+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Report a not-implemented ORC compression codec instead of aborting
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115412 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an abort on debug and sanitizer builds when reading an ORC file whose compression codec the bundled ORC reader does not implement. Such a file is now reported with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of the bare `STD_EXCEPTION` (code 1001) naming a C++ type that a release build used to give. ### Description Truncating an in-repo ORC file kills the process with no output at all: ```bash head -c 289 tests/queries/0_stateless/data_orc/orc_nested_union_type.orc > t289.orc clickhouse local --query "SELECT * FROM file('t289.orc', ORC) FORMAT Null" # Aborted (core dumped), stdout and stderr both empty ``` The truncation leaves byte 6 in the postscript's compression field. liborc does not implement codec 6, so it throws `orc::NotImplementedYet`, a `std::logic_error`. `getFileReader` had no handler, so it reached `getCurrentExceptionMessage`, which on a debug or sanitizer build deliberately treats an in-flight `std::logic_error` as an internal-invariant violation and aborts. That logs to the root logger, unattached in `clickhouse local`, so the process dies while composing its own message. A release build does not abort. Measured on 26.7.6.6, it reports `Code: 1001. DB::Exception: orc::NotImplementedYet: Unknown compression codec 6. (STD_EXCEPTION)`. The fix translates that one exception type at the `orc::createReader` boundary, through a shared `createORCReader` used by both production call sites (`NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp` and `Storages/Hive/HiveFile.cpp`, equally unguarded). The assertion in the formatter is left alone: it guards real internal bugs, and the ORC reader raises `std::logic_error` from ClickHouse-supplied inputs elsewhere, which must keep aborting. Hence a catch typed on `orc::NotImplementedYet` alone. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` rather than `INCORRECT_DATA` because the file may be valid: codec 6 is `BROTLI`, which the ORC spec declares but the C++ reader does not implement. A file with no compression field at all is still reported corrupt, by `ParseError`. Only the ORC half of the issue. Avro is not fixed: I could not obtain a reproducer, and would rather not add a handler I cannot test. Could you share the fixture? Validation: the abort reproduces on five entry paths, all five fixed. Neighbouring truncations, the nine `data_orc` fixtures and a stride-1 sweep are identical before and after. The Hive site is compile-verified only, since exercising it needs HDFS. New test `05036_orc_unimplemented_codec_no_abort`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115889&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115889](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115889+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix index granularity collapsing to 1 when mutating an adaptive part on a table with index_granularity_bytes = 0
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111626 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes index granularity collapsing to one mark per row (large mark and primary-index bloat) when a row-changing mutation rewrites an adaptive data part that lives on a table with `index_granularity_bytes = 0`. ### Description A part written with byte-based granularity can land on a table where that sizing is disabled (`index_granularity_bytes = 0`), for example via `RESTORE ... AS ... SETTINGS allow_different_table_def = 1`. A row-changing mutation (`ALTER ... DELETE`, TTL, any full-column rewrite) then rewrites it and inherits the source's granularity info, so the writer sizes granules by bytes while the byte budget is zero. `computeIndexGranularity` computed `0 / size_of_row = 0`, which the floor below turned into 1: one mark per row, a thousands-fold mark and primary-index bloat. Data stayed correct, so correct-result tests did not catch it. Fix: when `index_granularity_bytes = 0`, use the fixed row granularity instead of dividing a zero byte budget. The `index_granularity_bytes > 0` and non-adaptive paths are untouched, verified byte-for-byte against a pre-fix build across small and large byte budgets, both part types, and `index_granularity = 1`. The guard sits on the single function every part writer reaches, so it covers every route into that state, not only the reproducer's: also a restored `Compact` part, unblocked by #111626, and a replicated merge, which honours the assigning replica's part format. signal.title: Sort, filter and page a result in the Web UI
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105249 The Web UI can now sort a result by its columns, filter it by their values, and page through it, without editing the query. None of it happens in the browser. Each change re-runs the query with the corresponding query-construction setting added by #105249 — `order`, `filter`, `limit` + `page` — which the server materializes by wrapping the query as a derived table. What is on screen is therefore the sorted, filtered, paged result of the whole query, not a rearrangement of the rows the page happened to hold. And because the settings are applied to the parsed query rather than to its text, they compose with whatever the query already is: a `UNION`, a trailing `FORMAT` clause, or the query's own `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` all keep working, and the text in the editor is never rewritten. ## Sorting Two arrows in every column header. The arrow of the active direction deactivates it, the other replaces it, a plain click makes the column the only sort key, and <kbd>Shift</kbd> appends it after the keys already in effect (or only flips the direction of a key it already is, keeping its position). With more than one key, each active arrow shows its position in the `ORDER BY` as a superscript. ## Filtering A funnel in every header opens an input for a predicate on that column, with an apply button glued to it. The input opens *inside* the header cell, on the very line the filter is shown on once it is set, so a filter is edited where it is read; the header grows a line for it and shrinks back afterwards. What is typed is the part that follows the column name, so anything the server accepts there works — `> 10`, `BETWEEN 1 AND 5`, `IN (1, 2, 3)`, `% 2 = 0`. A column being filtered shows its predicate under its name for as long as it is set, with a cross to remove it, so it is never invisible that the rows on screen are a subset of the result. Selecting a cell also offers the comparisons that fit its value: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` for a number or a date/time; `=`, `!=`, `contains` for a string; `=`, `!=` for an `Enum`; `true` / `false` for a `Bool`; `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` for a NULL. `contains` becomes a `LIKE` pattern with the value's own `%` and `_` escaped, so it matches literally. There is one filter per column wherever it came from, and the header always displays the one in effect. ## Pagination A result cut off at the display limit gets a pager, which lists the ten pages before the current one, the current one and the next one, plus an ellipsis that takes any page number, and ends with an editable `Per page`. The count of pages is not shown because knowing it would mean counting the rows; the next page is offered only while the current one is full, since a short page is the end of the result. The page size is capped at what the result can display at once — a larger page would return rows the table then truncates away and the next page would start beyond them, silently skipping the rows that never fit. ## Where it applies, and what it is bound to Only to the statements those settings shape, i.e. `SELECT` / `UNION` (resolved by the same CTE-aware statement-kind walk that already decides the `Run all` parallelization, so a write hidden behind a leading `WITH` is not mistaken for one). Not to `SHOW` / `DESCRIBE` / `EXISTS` / `EXPLAIN`, where the settings are silently ignored and a control would promise an order the rows do not have; and not to a multi-query run, whose statements are separate queries with separate columns. A shape belongs to the statement it was made on and is dropped by a run of anything else, so a stale sort can never put an `ORDER BY` on a column the new statement lacks. The two launch paths spell the same statement differently (with and without its trailing `;`), which the binding normalizes — otherwise a shape would be dropped by its own re-run. ## Persistence Kept per tab, and mirrored into the URL (`sort_columns`, `filters`, `page`, `page_size`), the history entry and the tab's result snapshot, alongside the existing color modes and pinned columns. Since the shape decides the rows and not only their presentation, an auto-run (`run=1`) link reproduces the result itself; Download re-runs with the same settings so the exported file matches the table. ## Header icons The pushpin and rainbow emoji became inline SVG on the same grid and stroke weight as the new funnel — they rendered visibly larger than the line art beside them, and being colour glyphs they could take no text colour. All four icons now follow one rule: muted while the feature they control is not in effect on the column, and in a colour reserved for controls in effect (magenta in the light theme, yellow in the dark one) once it is, which is also when they stay shown without hovering. Each lays the header's colour behind itself at 90% alpha so a column name running underneath does not muddle it. ## Testing - `tests/integration/test_play_result_shaping` runs the real shape helpers extracted from the served `/play` page in a Node harness, covering the sort-arrow semantics, the `ORDER BY` / `WHERE` construction and its quoting and `LIKE` escaping, the translation of a page into `limit` + `page`, the validation of a shape read back from a URL, and the statement binding. - `gtest_play_query_is_read_only` now also covers the statement-kind gate: the walk is refactored into a shared `statementKeyword`, and `queryIsShapeable` is verified to be strictly narrower than the read-only classification. - The behaviour itself was driven in a real browser (Chromium via Puppeteer) against a local server, in both themes, for each of the cases above. Documentation: `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/web-ui-result-shaping.mdx`. Written with Claude Code. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The built-in Web SQL UI (`/play`) can now sort a result by its columns, filter it by their values, and page through it, without editing the query. Sorting arrows and a filter input appear in every column header, a selected cell offers the comparisons that fit its value, and a pager with an adjustable page size appears under a result that does not fit on one screen. It is all performed by the server, using the `order`, `filter`, `limit` and `page` query-construction settings, so the whole result is shaped rather than the rows that happen to be displayed; the chosen sort, filters and page travel in the page URL, so a shared link reproduces the result. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115540&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115540](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115540+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix AI functions under-reporting provider usage
signal.text: AI functions under-report what the provider was actually called and billed for. With the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1`, a failing `aiEmbed` logs an exception row showing `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`; flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause 1: counters die while unwinding.** `embedTexts` accumulated into a local `EmbeddingResult` returned by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so failed calls are still counted. The providers lost their token counts the same way. **Cause 2: usage read after validation.** `call` and `embed` parsed `usage` only after validating the response body, so a `200` the provider had already billed for reported no tokens once a check rejected it. This is not only a `system.query_log` undercount: `AIQuotaTracker` never saw those tokens either, so `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` could not trip and a query with `ai_function_throw_on_error = 0` kept issuing billed requests past its cap. **Fix.** One rule in three places: the accumulator lives in caller-owned storage and is published from a scope guard, so every exit reports it. `embedTexts`, `IAIProvider::call` and `IAIProvider::embed` fill an out-parameter instead of returning by value, and both providers read `usage` before the checks that can reject the body. **Not covered.** `aiSimilarity` scores rows only once every batch is embedded, so its row counters are zero on a throwing exit — no row was scored, even though the first row's operands were embedded and billed. A test pins that. **Tests.** Nine integration tests. The eight regression tests were each verified to fail with the source reverted and to pass with it restored; the `aiSimilarity` one records a deliberate choice rather than a fix, so it passes either way. Two cover the quota effect rather than the reporting: a text query whose first response is billed-but-rejected stops dispatching once the cap is met, and `AnthropicProvider`, which had no coverage at all. Merged with https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which introduced the throwing paths on the text side. Its guard around the text-path counters is what publishes them, so the per-attempt accounting here completes that path rather than duplicating it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed AI functions under-reporting provider usage in `system.query_log` and in per-query quotas: counters accumulated before a failed request were dropped, and tokens for a response the provider billed for but that failed validation were never counted. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114905&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114905](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114905+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add a maintained ReadPlan to the experimental ReaderExecutor
signal.text: Introduces a maintained `ReadPlan` to the experimental `ReaderExecutor` (gated by `use_reader_executor`, default off). Instead of re-resolving the cache chain on every read window, the executor resolves the residency of a look-ahead span once, holds the pinned hit-readers and miss-writers across serves, and answers per offset which tier serves it - coalescing consecutive misses (across cells and tiers) into one source read, capped at the window, that populates every populating tier. The plan grows on the right (`extend`) and retires the consumed prefix on the left (`retireBefore`) as the cursor advances. Serve semantics are unchanged (the existing executor tests pass); only the resolve is now held across windows instead of repeated per window. This is also the structure the later prefetch slice drives: it fills the same held writers ahead of the cursor without changing this interface. Details: - **Look-ahead** is configurable via the experimental `reader_executor_plan_look_ahead` setting (default 16 MiB); `resolve` is a cheap probe, so looking ahead costs no I/O. The plan is refilled in batches: it grows only once less than half the look-ahead remains ahead of the cursor, then resolves back to the full length. - **Concurrent downloads** are handled in one pass over the tiers (fastest-first): a segment another query committed since `resolve` is served from cache; a segment a concurrent downloader currently leads is waited on once (`CacheWriter::waitAndRead`) and served from cache if it lands; otherwise this reader takes the download role and the source fetch populates the tier. Only after the pass, if nothing served the head, is the coalesced miss run read from source. A single iteration - no waiting/reclaim loop. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `ReaderExecutor` now resolves cache residency once into a maintained read plan (configurable via `reader_executor_plan_look_ahead`) instead of re-resolving on every read window.

signal.title: Do not let SET <name> = DEFAULT bypass the settings constraints
signal.text: `SET <name> = DEFAULT` resets a setting rather than assigning to it, so it does not produce a `SettingChange` and never reached `SettingsConstraints`. Any constraint could therefore be escaped by resetting the setting instead of assigning to it: ```sql CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE p SETTINGS max_query_size = 1000 MAX 1000; SET max_query_size = 2000; -- SETTING_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, as expected SET max_query_size = DEFAULT; -- silently restored the default of 262144 ``` A `CONST` constraint was just as escapable, and so was readonly mode, which is enforced by the same check: ```sql SET readonly = 2; SET readonly = 0; -- READONLY, as expected SET readonly = DEFAULT; -- silently left readonly mode ``` This describes the reset as the change it effectively is — to the value declared in the source code, which is what `Context::resetSettingsToDefaultValue` restores — and runs the usual check on it before anything is applied, so that a violation leaves the whole statement without effect. The in-query `SETTINGS <name> = DEFAULT` form goes through the same interpreter and is covered too. A reset that does not change the value is still allowed, because the check drops changes whose new value equals the current one. Resetting a setting that was never touched therefore keeps working under a `CONST` constraint and in readonly mode — which is what CI profiles that pin a setting to its declared default rely on (`max_parser_backtracks` in `limit-recursion-settings.xml`, for example). Settings without a declared default are unaffected: a custom setting is dropped rather than reset and cannot carry a constraint, and an unknown name stays silently ignored. The client only mirrors the reset into its own settings when the server accepted the statement, so its view does not drift. One consequence worth calling out: a profile that caps `max_threads` below the machine's core count now rejects `SET max_threads = DEFAULT`, because the declared default resolves to `auto(<cores>)`. That is the intended reading of the constraint, but it means the CI profiles that cap `max_threads` at 128 would reject that reset on a machine with more than 128 cores. Verified locally against a build of this change: the four rejection paths above are rejected, the rejected statement leaves the value alone, and the no-op reset, custom-setting reset and unknown-setting reset all keep working. `04202_set_default_preserves_max_threads_auto` and `04078_settings_constraints_compatibility_const` still pass, and a sweep of every stateless test that uses `= DEFAULT` plus every test whose name mentions constraints/readonly/settings profiles produced no constraint or readonly error attributable to this change. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115328 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a bypass of settings constraints: `SET <name> = DEFAULT` reset a setting without checking the constraints from the user's profile, so a `MIN`/`MAX`/`CONST` constraint could be escaped by resetting the setting instead of assigning to it, and a session could leave readonly mode with `SET readonly = DEFAULT`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115334&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115334](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115334+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix lost rows and LOGICAL_ERROR for a distributed query with no table column
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104510 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query over a `Distributed` table (or `cluster`/`remote`/`clusterAllReplicas` with an inner `view`) spanning more than one shard that references no column of the table anywhere in the query, such as `SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM distributed_table`. Such a query silently returned no rows, and returned `LOGICAL_ERROR` `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` when the table produced a constant. The fix covers the analyzer; `enable_analyzer = 0` is fixed separately by #113955. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104510 A `Block` carries its row count only inside its columns, so a header with no column cannot express "N rows" across a mergeable-stage boundary. When the query references no column of the table expression, `prepareBuildQueryPlanForTableExpression` reads one synthetic column purely to learn the row count. The window function is deferred to the initiator along with the projection that would have consumed that column, so it is pruned. If the table expression produces a constant, the shard keeps one column while the initiator expects none and `OutputPort::pushData` raises `LOGICAL_ERROR`. If no constant survives, both headers are empty, nothing is sent, and every row is lost with no error: over two shards of 1000 rows the query returned nothing where 2000 rows are correct. The fix records that synthetic column's identifier where it is created, and replaces a mergeable-state header holding nothing but such columns with one materialized `UInt8` column. Both headers then agree by construction, and `ExpressionTransform` sizes the constant from the chunk, so a zero-column chunk still yields N rows. The condition is a property of the whole query, not of the window, so two limits are worth stating. A query referencing a column only where it is consumed before the boundary (`WHERE`, `PREWHERE`, `JOIN ON`) reaches the same empty header by another route and is not fixed here: that needs internal-only provenance through the filter plumbing, and folding it in was measured to turn the abort into a new user-visible error on the constant-projection shape. And not every window function is affected: `sum(1) OVER ()` and `rank() OVER (ORDER BY 1)` keep a non-empty shard header. The test covers both symptoms through `cluster`, `clusterAllReplicas`, `remote` and a stored view over seven constant types, plus `UNION ALL` and `JOIN`, and pins the shapes that must not change. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114611

signal.title: PromQL arithmetic operators and sum/avg aggregation over native histograms
signal.text: ## Summary Sixth slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115860. Adds PromQL arithmetic operators and `sum`/`avg` aggregation over stored native histograms, mirroring the histogram arms of `vectorElemBinop` and of the `parser.SUM`/`parser.AVG` branches of `aggregation` in Prometheus promql/engine.go: - **Scalar functions** `timeSeriesHistogram{Add,Sub,MulByScalar,DivByScalar}` over the native-histogram arithmetic kernel: histogram OP histogram is only `+` (`add`) and `-` (`sub`, result marked as a gauge); histogram OP float is only `*` (`mul`) and `/` (`div`); every result is `compact(0)`-ed; schema-incompatible pairs (exponential vs custom buckets) produce NULL (upstream drops the sample). - **Aggregates** `timeSeriesHistogram{Sum,Avg}OverGroup`: compensated Kahan-Neumaier accumulation per group for `sum` (new `kahanAdd` in the kernel); the direct mean with the incremental-mean fallback on overflow for `avg`; an empty or schema-incompatible group produces NULL (upstream drops the group element). - **Converter**: arithmetic binary operators over a combined float+histogram grid (`StoreMethod::HISTOGRAM_GRID`) resolve each operand per step by `sample_kinds` and produce the float and histogram arms independently (disallowed kind combinations drop the sample, matching upstream); `sum`/`avg` aggregate the kind-masked arms separately via the `-ForEach` combinator and drop steps whose group mixes float and histogram samples. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL arithmetic operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) and `sum`/`avg` aggregation over stored Prometheus native histograms, with upstream-compatible schema-compatibility and mixed-sample dropping rules. signal.title: Fix flaky test 00818_inner_join_bug_3567
signal.text: `PrettyCompact` starts a new table for every chunk it receives, and glues consecutive chunks together only while they keep arriving within `output_format_pretty_squash_consecutive_ms` (50 ms by default). The `ALL LEFT JOIN` in `00818_inner_join_bug_3567` emits its single non-joined row in a chunk of its own, so whenever the next chunk is more than 50 ms behind — which happens on a loaded runner, most often under TSan — the result is printed as two tables: ``` ┌─a─┬──────────b─┬─c─┬──────────d─┬─c─┐ 1. │ a │ 2018-01-01 │ │ 1970-01-01 │ │ + └───┴────────────┴───┴────────────┴───┘ + ┌─a─┬──────────b─┬─c─┬──────────d─┬─c─┐ 2. │ b │ 2018-01-01 │ B │ 2018-01-01 │ B │ 3. │ c │ 2018-01-01 │ C │ 2018-01-01 │ C │ └───┴────────────┴───┴────────────┴───┘ ``` All 27 recorded failures of this test in the last 180 days have exactly this signature. The test only uses a `Pretty` format to show the column names of the join result, so it switches to `PrettyCompactMonoBlock`, which squashes everything into a single table regardless of chunking and timing. The reference file is unchanged. Verified with the randomized settings of the failed run and `output_format_pretty_squash_consecutive_ms = 0` (the worst case): 15/15 runs of the old test differ from the reference, 15/15 runs of the new one match it. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=55e5ac561cf3d55abf07459ee46425f4f15b5a45&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115865&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115865](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115865+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1894` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: K-way merge optimizations: batch lookahead, sorted array of cursors, batch queue for special merges
signal.text: Three k-way merge optimizations motivated by the analysis in https://maksimkita.com/blog/k-way-merge.html, plus a follow-up refinement: 1. **O(1) whole-cursor batch detection** (`SortingQueueImpl::updateBatchSize`). When the batch exceeds the linear detection limit, one comparison against the last row of the front cursor takes the entire remainder as a single batch. Merging cursors with non-intersecting key ranges (e.g. parts sorted by the primary key that do not overlap) now costs O(1) comparisons per batch instead of a linear detection followed by a binary search over the remainder. 2. **Sorted array of cursors** as an alternative queue container. Reinserting the advanced front cursor costs exactly `ceil(log2(K))` comparisons (a binary search) plus a shift of plain pointers, versus up to `2 * log2(K)` comparisons for the heap. It is selected only for cursors with expensive comparators: the generic multi-column `SortCursor` and `SortCursorWithCollation`. Above 256 cursors it falls back to the heap behavior (a sorted array is a valid heap layout, so the switch is free). Measured on 64-way in-order merges of parts with fully overlapping ranges: 7-8% faster for two- and four-column sorting keys, no change for the specialized single-column cursors (which stay on the heap: e.g. strings measured 18% slower with the array, since their comparisons usually resolve within the first bytes). 3. **Batch sorting queue for the special merge algorithms** (`Replacing`/`Summing`/`Aggregating`/`Collapsing`/`VersionedCollapsing`/`Graphite`). They advanced the queue one row at a time, restructuring the heap on every row; now the queue is restructured once per batch. `ReplacingSortedAlgorithm` additionally fast-forwards to the last row of a run of equal keys within a batch when processing a row has no effects besides replacing the selected row (no version and no `is_deleted` columns, no row sources, no vertical FINAL) — the run end is found with `getEqualRangeEndAssumeSorted` instead of per-row comparisons. Measured: `SELECT ... FINAL` over 8 parts of `ReplacingMergeTree` with runs of ~10 duplicates per key inside each part is 26-33% faster; FINAL over non-intersecting parts is unchanged; `SummingMergeTree` FINAL is 6% faster on clustered duplicates and ~5% slower in the worst case of fully interleaved hash-distributed keys (a known trade-off; a follow-up that uses the run information to skip per-row key comparisons in the remaining algorithms can win both shapes). 4. **Galloping detection of the batch end**: after the linear detection caps out, the end of the batch is bracketed with exponentially growing steps, so the search costs O(log(batch size)) comparisons on rows near the current position instead of O(log(rows left)) comparisons on far rows that miss caches. Verification: a 25-case differential harness (multi-column/string/nullable/collation/LowCardinality `ORDER BY` checksums incl. row order, external sort, >256-cursor merges, FINAL for all six engines, vertical merges, `enable_vertical_final`, `is_deleted`, insert-time merging with a permutation) produces identical results against master at every commit; ~300 targeted stateless tests and the merge/sort unit tests pass. A new performance test `kway_merge_expensive_comparator` covers the array-container cases and guards the heap cases. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up k-way merges: merging sorted streams with multi-column or collated sorting keys uses a sorted array of cursors instead of a heap (7-8% faster), merges of non-intersecting parts detect the whole cursor as one batch in O(1) comparisons, and the merges of `ReplacingMergeTree`, `SummingMergeTree`, `AggregatingMergeTree`, `CollapsingMergeTree`, `VersionedCollapsingMergeTree` and `GraphiteMergeTree` process rows in batches (`SELECT ... FINAL` from `ReplacingMergeTree` with many duplicates is up to 30% faster). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115869&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115869](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115869+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix use-of-uninitialized-value in WITH FILL suffix over a merge
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107074 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-of-uninitialized-value in `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL ... STALENESS` when the fill suffix generates no rows (for example when the staleness window leaves nothing to fill) and the result is read through a merge of sorted streams (such as a two-shard `Distributed` table). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer under MSan on top of #107074. `FillingTransform`, when all input chunks are processed, may run the suffix path. If the fill constraints are satisfied but no fill rows are produced (e.g. `WITH FILL ... STALENESS` with an exhausted staleness window), `generateSuffixIfNeeded` returns `true` while the result columns are freshly `cloneEmpty()`'d and carry no data. Previously the transform still emitted a 0-row chunk built from those empty columns. A downstream `MergingSortedTransform` (as used when reading from a two-shard `Distributed` table) then built a sort cursor over that empty chunk and compared row 0, reading past the end of the empty column. Fix: do not emit the suffix chunk when it has no rows. Minimal reproducer (needs a two-shard merge on the initiator): ```sql CREATE TABLE m (key Int) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO m VALUES (100); CREATE TABLE d2 AS m ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), m); SELECT _shard_num FROM d2 ORDER BY _shard_num ASC WITH FILL TO 46 STALENESS 1; ``` CI finding: `AST fuzzer (amd_msan)`, report https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107074&sha=3ec54c88d4eb535a5d644fc1ab91af31d717f9a5&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29 MSan use-of-uninitialized-value in `ColumnVector<UInt32>::doCompareAt` (`MergingSortedAlgorithm::consume`), origin `FillingTransform::initColumns` (`cloneEmpty`) via the suffix path. Verified on a local `amd_msan` build: reproduces before the fix (server aborts), clean after; the new regression test returns `1\n2`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110183&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110183](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110183+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(LowCardinality(String), Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, event_date, event_time, key`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1893` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Do not run the server-side AST fuzzer on a collaborative worker context
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113729 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Duplicate announcement received for replica number N`) when the server-side AST fuzzer is enabled with `ast_fuzzer_runs`. The fuzzer re-ran a query on a node acting as a parallel replicas participant or a cluster function worker, so the fuzzed query announced itself to the initiator's reading coordinator a second time under the same replica number. ### Description `executeASTFuzzerQueries` runs as a query-finish callback and re-executes mutated copies of the query that just finished. When that query was a collaborative worker for another node, its context carries a borrowed replica identity and a live coordination channel back to the initiator: `merge_tree_all_ranges_callback` plus `number_of_current_replica` for a parallel replicas participant, `next_task_callback` for a cluster function worker. `Context::createCopy` copies both and `resetInputCallbacks` does not clear them, so a fuzzed query announces again under the same replica number and the coordinator rejects the second arrival with a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. `e8194c7dc437eb0` already pins `allow_experimental_parallel_reading_from_replicas = 0` on the fuzz context for this reason. That pin is a setting value written before the fuzzed query's own settings are applied, so the fuzzed query re-enables it, and not through one bounded route: its own `SETTINGS` clause, the alias `enable_parallel_replicas`, a `SETTINGS profile = ...` that never names the setting, or the inner `SELECT`'s clause applied later on a derived context. This change keeps the pin and decides one level up instead, from a field already on the context, so nothing has to propagate. The initiating client query is still fuzzed, so query shapes stay covered, and behaviour changes only when `ast_fuzzer_runs > 0`, which is off by default. The new counter `ASTFuzzerSkippedCollaborativeWorker` makes the skip observable; the test asserts it rises for a worker and stays put for an ordinary query whose own fuzz runs still execute. Also noticed, not the cause here and not addressed: `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:731` skips its plain-MergeTree guard for a `StorageMaterializedView` destination, which reports neither predicate. Reported by CI: [Stress test (arm_tsan) on 858261cb](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115681&sha=858261cb4bb9e68db7eeed82dba277592650339f&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), and on four other unrelated pull requests across three sanitizer builds in eleven days. The linked issue reports the same message through the local-plan callback, not the wire packet path: related, different defect. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115786&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115786](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115786+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix division by zero in `ReadFromMergeTree` when `StorageMerge` truncates the number of streams
signal.text: The `AST fuzzer (amd_debug)` raised `Integer divide by zero` on ```sql SELECT id FROM merge(currentDatabase(), '^t$') ORDER BY id DESC SETTINGS max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 1073741824, max_threads = 4 ``` The planner computes `max_streams = max_threads * max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 2^32`, which passes the existing overflow check because it fits in `size_t`. `ReadFromMerge::createPlanForTable` passed `UInt32(streams_num)` to `storage->read`, truncating `2^32` to zero. The child `ReadFromMergeTree` then divides by the requested number of streams in `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreamsWithOrder`. `IStorage::read` takes `size_t num_streams`, so this change removes the narrowing cast and adds a regression test. Additionally, `StorageMerge` multiplied the requested number of streams by `max_streams_multiplier_for_merge_tables` with unchecked `Float64` to `size_t` conversions. Both sites now use a shared checked helper that throws `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND` if the product does not fit in `size_t`. `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreams` and `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreamsWithOrder` also now use a division-based comparison when clamping streams to data, avoiding overflow in `num_streams * min_marks_for_concurrent_read`. Because forwarding the full `size_t` stream count exposes arbitrary child engines to absurd requests, `ReadFromMerge::createChildrenPlans` now checks the aggregate source count of a `Merge` read against a limit of 65536 before building any child plan, and rejects excessive reads with `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND`. Child storages report a conservative bound on the sources they create through the new `IStorage::getMaxReadStreams` capability: `File`, `URL`, `Log`, `TinyLog`, `StripeLog`, `Memory`, `Null` and `View` are covered, proxies forward the capability to the nested storage, and a trivial `LIMIT` reduces the request the same way `GenerateRandom` does. When a child's reported bound is below the request, its output resize (`parallelize_output_from_storages`) is disabled so the constructed pipeline matches the accounting. The previously added streaming-read guard and its test are removed because current `master` now bounds effective `MergeTree` stream counts before that code path. Found by the AST fuzzer on an unrelated PR: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113010&sha=59507af89c33f62942e855b50b3e66704cbcf2e9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113010 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix an arithmetic exception in debug and sanitizer builds when reading from a `Merge` table with a very large `max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`: the number of streams was truncated to 32 bits, so multiples of `2^32` became zero. Also throw `PARAMETER_OUT_OF_BOUND` instead of invoking undefined behavior when multiplying stream counts for a `Merge` table exceeds `size_t`, avoid an overflow when limiting `MergeTree` streams to the amount of data, and reject a `Merge` table read whose aggregate source count would exceed 65536. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113382](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113382+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add experimental unity_v2 catalog
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105038 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100669 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry: Added a new experimental `unity_v2` catalog type to the DataLakeCatalog database engine. It serves both Delta Lake and Iceberg tables from a single Unity Catalog, detecting the format of each table and routing Iceberg tables through the Unity Catalog Iceberg REST endpoint. It supports Databricks authentication with an OAuth service principal, a personal access token, or a pre-obtained OAuth token, and vended credentials for managed and external tables, including UniForm. Enable it with the setting `allow_experimental_database_unity_v2_catalog`. ### Summary Create "unity_v2" catalog. It supports both Delta and Iceberg tables, in contrast to the current "unity" catalog, which only supports Delta. The V2 catalog is behind an experimental feature flag. After a release or two, we can switch it to be the main "unity" catalog. Credit to @melvynator for the prototype in #100669. ### Tests Added integration tests. Also, ran manual tests. I first created the following tables in Databricks. ``` CREATE TABLE delta_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA; INSERT INTO delta_managed VALUES (1, 1.0); CREATE TABLE delta_external (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA LOCATION 's3://<test-bucket>/tables/delta_external'; INSERT INTO delta_external VALUES (2, 2.0); CREATE TABLE iceberg_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING ICEBERG; INSERT INTO iceberg_managed VALUES (3, 3.0); CREATE TABLE uniform_managed (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableIcebergCompatV2' = 'true', 'delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats' = 'iceberg'); INSERT INTO uniform_managed VALUES (4, 4.0); CREATE TABLE uniform_external (id INT, v DOUBLE) USING DELTA LOCATION 's3://<test-bucket>/tables/uniform_external' TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableIcebergCompatV2' = 'true', 'delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats' = 'iceberg'); INSERT INTO uniform_external VALUES (5, 5.0); ``` Then created the following databases: ``` CREATE DATABASE unity_oauth_token ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://dbc-xxxxx.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.1/unity-catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'unity_v2', warehouse = 'external-loc-catalog', catalog_credential = 'eyJ...'; CREATE DATABASE unity_static ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://dbc-xxxxx.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.1/unity-catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'unity_v2', warehouse = 'external-loc-catalog', catalog_credential = '{client_id}:{client_secret}'; signal.title: Build the IN-subquery set once when a correlated subquery body is materialized
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` logical error when a correlated subquery whose body contains `IN (subquery)` runs with `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0`, which `make_distributed_plan = 1` also sets. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 With `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0` the decorrelated subquery body is duplicated by cloning it, and the clone included the `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` holding the body's `IN` set. A `FutureSetFromSubquery` hands out its source plan only once (`build` moves `source` out), and `makePlansForSets` treats an absent plan as nothing to build, so the second copy became a childless `CreatingSets`: its `in()` then read a set nothing had built. Reproducer: ```sql SET allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1, correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0; SELECT (SELECT x) FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(['a','b']) AS x GROUP BY 1, 1 IN (SELECT 7)); ``` The set is now taken out of the fragment before it is cloned, and one builder is attached above the plan root, so it dominates every copy. Readiness is structural rather than dependent on which join arm runs first, which matters because the abort reproduces with `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind` set to either `left` or `right`. This follows `extractSetsForDistributedPlan`, which solves the same problem for distributed plans. This also fixes a second, latent defect. `buildOrderedSetInplace` clones the source plan as a non-destructive snapshot and relies on a plan holding a `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` being non-clonable, so a stopped speculative build cannot consume a nested set's source. Since `f886da073cea2bf` added `DelayedCreatingSetsStep::clone()` that clone silently succeeded and shared the inner subqueries. Full-plan cloning now rejects a step that still holds sets, restoring the documented fallback; the step clone Cascades needs is unchanged. Validation: the reproducer aborts before and returns `a`/`b` after; the new test aborts the server on a pristine-master binary and passes on the fixed one; `EXPLAIN PLAN` shows exactly one builder and no leftover placeholder for both join kinds; 50/50 randomized runs pass; the correlated, common-subplan and distributed-plan suites show the same failures before and after. Found by the AST fuzzer on #109377: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109377&sha=424d8efed247654e71f2bad3aa996e203fc08feb&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115868&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115868](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115868+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: optimizeExchanges throws Unknown identifier for an ActionsDAG pass-through sort column
signal.text: ## Description `optimizeExchanges` can throw during `QueryPlan::optimize` when it tries to move a sorted Gather across an `ExpressionStep` or `FilterStep` whose maintained sort column is passed through implicitly: ```text Code: 47 Unknown identifier: '__table2.state' ``` One triggering plan shape contains a partitioned window followed by an outer filter: ```sql SELECT * FROM ( SELECT state, season, dense_rank() OVER ( PARTITION BY state, season ORDER BY total_sales DESC ) AS category_rank FROM ... ) WHERE category_rank <= 3 ORDER BY state, season, category_rank ``` The failure occurs during query-plan optimization, before plan splitting or execution, and does not depend on Stateless Workers. ## Root cause `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` builds a step's output header from both explicit DAG outputs and unconsumed input columns copied through unchanged. A pass-through sort column can therefore exist in the output header without having a corresponding node in `dag.outputs`. After confirming that the output header contains the sort column, `isSortColumnPreserved` unconditionally calls: ```cpp dag.findInOutputs(column_name) ``` `findInOutputs` searches only explicit DAG outputs and throws Code 47 when the column is an implicit pass-through. The lookup therefore treats a valid unchanged column as missing. ## Introduction and exposure The unsafe lookup was introduced by #106020. The distributed `PARTITION BY` window placement added by #114111 allows this plan shape to reach the pre-existing defect.

signal.title: Add per-part aggregation cache for incremental GROUP BY
signal.text: Cache intermediate per-part aggregation states in an LRU cache. On repeated GROUP BY queries, reuse cached states for unchanged MergeTree parts and only aggregate new ones. Uses the existing `AggregatingProjectionStep` mechanism to merge cached and fresh results. ### Changelog category Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry Add per-part aggregation cache for incremental GROUP BY over MergeTree tables. Gated behind `allow_experimental_part_aggregation_cache`. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Adds a new caching layer that rewrites `GROUP BY` query plans and stores intermediate aggregation states, which can affect correctness/performance and memory usage if hashing/invalidation/configuration is wrong. Gated behind experimental/settings but touches core query planning and system commands. > > **Overview** > Adds an **experimental per-part aggregation cache** for `GROUP BY` over `MergeTree` tables, caching intermediate (non-final) per-part aggregation states and reusing them across repeated queries to avoid re-aggregating unchanged parts. > > Wires the cache into server/local startup and config reload (`part_aggregation_cache.max_size_in_bytes`), introduces session settings to gate/enable reads+writes, and adds `SYSTEM DROP PART AGGREGATION CACHE` plus a `system.part_aggregation_cache` table for introspection. > > Implements a new query-plan optimization (`optimizeUsePartAggregationCache`) that splits aggregation into cached-part reads (`PartAggregationCacheSource`) + normal aggregation for uncached parts, with a populator that can precompute missing entries. signal.title: Do not reject a distributed plan whose sort column passes through a step unchanged
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737 Requested by @ PedroTadim in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115737#issuecomment-5368109515. Reported by @ XuJia0210. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `Unknown identifier` raised during query plan optimization under `make_distributed_plan = 1` when a window query's sort column passes through an `Expression` step that does not mention it. Closes #115737. ### Description Under `make_distributed_plan = 1` and `distributed_plan_optimize_exchanges = 1`, a valid query was rejected while `optimizeExchanges` moved a sorted `GatherExchange` above an `Expression` step: ``` Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown identifier: '__table3.a'. (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) ``` Root cause. `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` builds a step's output header from the evaluated DAG outputs plus every input-header column that matched no DAG input, copied through unchanged. Such a pass-through column is in the header while having no node in `dag.outputs`. The move-up check tested `expression_header->has(...)` first, which passes, and the short-circuit `||` then called `isSortColumnPreserved`, whose `findInOutputs` scans only `outputs` and throws instead of answering. The change uses the existing `tryFindInOutputs` and answers "preserved" when the DAG does not mention the column. That is the correct answer, not the convenient one: `ExpressionActions` forwards an unconsumed input column's `ColumnPtr` verbatim, and both step types are `ISimpleTransform`s that cannot reorder rows, so a merge keyed by such a column stays valid. `Optimizations/Cascades/DagNameTranslation` already answers the same question the same way for the same machinery, via its `TranslatedName::Passthrough` case. Reaching the branch needs a column-keyed inner window to build the sorted gather and an outer window keyed by a constant to put an all-pass-through step above it; the new test builds exactly that. It asserts the move-up positionally: "no longer throws" would also pass for the fail-closed answer, and a `GatherExchange` is present whether or not it moved. Only the `Expression` carrier is reachable today, so the test covers that one. For a focused `Filter` the analyzer's `__tableN` renaming makes the preceding `expression_header->has(...)` test fail, so the `||` short-circuits before the lookup, and a `Filter` arm would pass on unpatched master. Validation: 43 `distributed_plan` and 119 `window` tests give identical results on the patched and unpatched binary apart from the new test; 50 randomized runs of the new test pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115890&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115890](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115890+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
