signal.title: Fix DeltaLake trivial count and total_rows over tables with deletion vectors
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114933 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114933 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `SELECT count()` and `system.tables.total_rows` returning too many rows for a Delta Lake table whose deletes are stored as deletion vectors: the count came from the `numRecords` file statistics, which still include the removed rows. Closes #114933. ### Description `SELECT count()` over a Delta table with `delta.enableDeletionVectors = true` counted the deleted rows: the trivial-count optimization answers from the `numRecords` statistics in `_delta_log` and never consulted the file's deletion vector. Any query that scans returned the correct answer, so `count()` disagreed with every other answer the same table gave. `system.tables.total_rows` over a `DeltaLake` engine table over-counted identically, through the same `IStorage::totalRows` seam. `TableSnapshot` accumulates `total_rows` at two places, and both summed `stats->num_records` while holding the file's `dv_info` handle and ignoring it. delta-kernel documents that statistic as stale under a deletion vector in the same doc comment that names `DvInfo::has_vector` as the flag to consult (`kernel/src/scan/state.rs`). Both sites now drop `total_rows` when a file carries a deletion vector, so `count()` becomes an ordinary scan, which already applies the vector correctly, and `total_rows` reports NULL rather than a wrong number. That is what `IcebergMetadata::totalRows` already does under delete files. `total_bytes` is unchanged: a deletion vector does not change data-file size. Subtracting the vector's `cardinality` would be exact, but that field is not reachable without reading the deletion-vector file, the very read this shortcut avoids. The `delta_lake_snapshot_version` disagreement the issue also reports has the same cause and is fixed too, since `getTotalRows` is version-agnostic. On the test fixture, whose vector removes 2 rows, pinning the version that carries the vector returned 4 before and returns 2 now, matching Spark's `VERSION AS OF`. A version pinned before the delete keeps the optimization. Extends `test_deletion_vector`, whose existing assertions use `ORDER BY all`, which makes the planner see the `count()` aggregate twice and decline the optimization, so they never reached this path. New arms cover a bare `count()`, both accumulation sites, `total_rows`, a pinned read of the version carrying the vector, and two controls that the optimization is still applied where no vector is present. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115872&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115872](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115872+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Perf test measures nothing: 5 of 6 queries plan identically with the pass on/off
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml` is the PR's only performance evidence, but five of its six queries produce byte-identical query plans with `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions` set to 1 and 0 at default settings — including the query its own comment labels "the shape from issue #82378".** - **Root cause:** The performance test declares no `<settings>` and therefore runs with `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1`, which eliminates the function nodes the new pass keys on. The PR's stateless test pins the setting to 0 for exactly this reason; the performance test does not. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** Perf tests run with server defaults plus only the XML's `<settings>` block ([`tests/performance/scripts/perf.py:442-449`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/tests/performance/scripts/perf.py#L442-L449), :712-713); this XML has none. `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` (default 1) rewrites `length(s)` to `s.size`, `notEmpty(s)` to `s.size != 0` and `length(arr)` to `arr.size0` in the analyzer, so no `length`/`empty`/`notEmpty` FUNCTION node survives for `collectVolumeReducingFunctionsReplacingTheirArgument` (pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:218-238) to find. Independently, `SELECT length(arr) ... ORDER BY key` can never be pushed at all: `isSupportedArgumentType` (pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:42-43) accepts only `String`/`FixedString`. **Affected locations:** - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:24 — flagship #82378 query — plan identical with the setting on and off - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:20 — `length(arr)` — Array is excluded by design, can never be pushed - tests/performance/push_down_volume_reducing_functions.xml:3 — header comment claims push below `Limit`, but `canPushBelowStep` accepts only Sorting and Filter - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:42`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp#L42) — isSupportedArgumentType restricts to String/FixedString - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp:146`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a77a83b02c0de/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/pushDownVolumeReducingFunctions.cpp#L146) — canPushBelowStep accepts SortingStep and FilterStep only **Impact:** The PR is labelled `pr-performance` and its only performance evidence cannot move. If a later change silently disables `tryPushDownVolumeReducingFunction`, five of the six queries stay green because their plans never depended on it. The one query that does differ (`lengthUTF8(s) ... ORDER BY key LIMIT 10`) exercises the `tryExecuteFunctionsAfterSorting` pinning change, not the new pass. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `a77a83b02c0de`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/2425d123-6bd7-42f4-841f-8e081def2641) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Repro: the perf test's queries plan identically with the optimization on and off. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vrf; CREATE TABLE vrf (key UInt64, s String, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO vrf SELECT number, randomPrintableASCII(100), range(number % 32) FROM numbers(1000); -- 1 = plans identical (perf query measures nothing), 0 = plans differ. SELECT ( SELECT groupArray(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN header = 1, actions = 1, description = 1, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 1) ) = ( SELECT groupArray(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN header = 1, actions = 1, description = 1, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 0) ); -- Positive control: with the subcolumn rewrite off, the pass fires. SELECT countIf(explain LIKE '%[volume-reducing functions]%') > 0 FROM (EXPLAIN description = 1, actions = 0, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) SETTINGS query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 1, optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 0); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vrf; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` PLAN DIFFERS for all six perf-test queries at the settings the perf runner uses, i.e. every measured query exercises the pass it is named after. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key PLAN DIFFERS :: SELECT lengthUTF8(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key LIMIT 10 IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(arr) FROM vrf ORDER BY key IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM vrf WHERE notEmpty(s) IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s) FROM vrf WHERE key % 3 = 0 ORDER BY key IDENTICAL PLAN :: SELECT length(s), empty(s) FROM vrf ORDER BY key -- p ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Add `<settings><optimize_functions_to_subcolumns>0</optimize_functions_to_subcolumns></settings>` to the XML (see tests/performance/map_subcolumns_prewhere.xml:55 for the inline-settings idiom), or switch the wide column to `FixedString`, which the subcolumn rewrite leaves alone. Drop or re-target `SELECT length(arr) ...` — `Array` is excluded by `isSupportedArgumentType`. Fix the header comment at line 3 (`Limit` is not a push-below target) and the `String / Array` wording at line 4. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same reachability caveat applies to the PR description's claim about `SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s)`: at default settings that shape reads only `s.size` and is unaffected by this PR. signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103485 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `cast_keep_nullable` not preserving nullability when the target type is `LowCardinality`. Casting a NULL-capable value to `LowCardinality(T)` threw `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` instead of producing `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`. Closes #103485. ### Description With `cast_keep_nullable = 1`, casting a NULL-capable source to a `LowCardinality(U)` target threw `Code: 349 CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN`: ```sql SET cast_keep_nullable = 1; SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::LowCardinality(String); -- threw 349 SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String); -- threw 349 ``` `CastOverloadResolver::getReturnTypeImpl` decided whether to preserve nullability with `type->canBeInsideNullable()`. `DataTypeLowCardinality` does not override that predicate, so it inherits the default `false`, the wrap was skipped, and the target could not hold the NULL. The predicate is correct - `Nullable(LowCardinality(T))` really is an invalid type - but it asks the wrong question: a `LowCardinality` target represents NULL as `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`. The fix uses the existing `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe`, which pushes `Nullable` inside the wrapper and otherwise behaves exactly like the old guard. I deliberately did not add a `canBeInsideNullable()` override to `DataTypeLowCardinality`: that would make the predicate false for its other callers, and #115464 relies on its current meaning. This completes the half left by `3a71053` in #95747, which fixed the same guard's source arm. An `Array` target still throws 349, correctly: there is no nullable `Array` form to move the NULL into, and `04035_cast_keep_nullable_dynamic` pins that. Out of scope: the `accurateCastOrNull` family still rejects `LowCardinality` targets with `Code: 43`; lifting that needs its own design. One observable change under `cast_keep_nullable = 1`: a non-NULL cast to an LC target now yields `LowCardinality(Nullable(U))` rather than `LowCardinality(U)`. No setting default changes, so `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` needs no entry, matching the #95747 precedent. The new stateless test covers both source shapes, `String`, `FixedString` and numeric dictionary types, NULL and non-NULL values, `Dynamic` and `Variant` sources, and four negative controls. It fails on master and passes here. Reported by the ClickGap retrospective scan of #95747; fix requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103485#issuecomment-5369160612. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115851&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115851](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115851+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `SELECT count()` never terminates on corrupted Avro / MsgPack / ProtobufList files — the `optimize_count_from_files` fast path counts rows without requiring forward progress
signal.text: 🕵️ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour `SELECT count()` over a corrupted file can run forever, emitting billions of phantom rows from a tiny input. Reading the same file normally rejects it immediately, so only the count fast path is affected. The smallest reproducer is **two bytes**: ```bash printf '\x00\x00' > bad.pb clickhouse local --query " SELECT count() FROM file('bad.pb', ProtobufList, 'a UInt64, b Int32, c Float64, d String')" # never returns ``` Measured on a server with `max_execution_time = 0`: ``` elapsed 6 s -> 958.50 million rows read, 5.37 MiB elapsed 12 s -> 1.92 billion rows read, 4.36 MiB elapsed 18 s -> 2.89 billion rows read, 362.43 KiB ``` Memory does not grow — it falls — so this is pure unbounded counting, not an allocation problem. **The decisive observation:** it is only the count fast path. For the same file, | query | result | |---|---| | `SELECT count() FROM file(...)` | **never returns** | | `SELECT count() FROM file(...) SETTINGS optimize_count_from_files = 0` | clean error in ~0 s | | `SELECT * FROM file(...) FORMAT Null` | clean error in ~0 s | | `SELECT a FROM file(...) LIMIT 5` | clean error in ~0 s | The real reading path validates the data and rejects it. `countRows()` does not. ### Affected formats Confirmed identical behaviour in three formats — in every case `count()` hangs while `SELECT *` and `optimize_count_from_files = 0` return a clean error in under a second: | format | reproducer | behaviour with default settings | |---|---|---| | ProtobufList | 2 bytes (`00 00`) | 2.89 billion rows in 18 s | | Avro | 57 KB (valid file + 1000 appended bytes) | 4.89 billion rows in 25 s | | MsgPack | 3.8–210 KB, five independent inputs | 66–145 million rows/s | Neighbouring inputs behave correctly, which narrows the ProtobufList case usefully: | input | result | |---|---| | empty file (0 bytes) | returns `0` | | `00` (1 byte) | returns cleanly | | `00 00` (2 bytes) | **never returns** | ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? Reproduced on 26.8.1.1599. Not build-dependent — nothing here relies on debug assertions. ### Expected behavior `countRows()` must not report more rows than the input can contain, and must terminate. A loop that produces a row without consuming any input should stop and raise `INCORRECT_DATA`, matching what the normal read path already does for these same files. ### Root cause The three `countRows()` implementations share one shape: the loop condition never requires the input position to advance. **`ProtobufListInputFormat::countRows`** — the return value of `readFieldNumber` is discarded, and a zero-length nested message consumes nothing, so `eof()` never becomes true: ```cpp size_t num_rows = 0; while (!reader->eof() && num_rows < max_block_size) { int tag = 0; reader->readFieldNumber(tag); // return value ignored reader->startNestedMessage(); reader->endNestedMessage(); // zero-length message consumes no input ++num_rows; } ``` **`AvroRowInputFormat::countRows`** — `hasMore()` is true while the block's `objectCount_` is non-zero, and `decr()` only decrements that counter. A corrupted object count in the block header is therefore a licence to count that many rows: ```cpp while (file_reader_ptr->hasMore() && num_rows < max_block_size) { file_reader_ptr->decr(); file_reader_ptr->decoder().drain(); ++num_rows; } ``` `contrib/avro`'s `DataFileReaderBase::readDataBlock()` decodes `objectCount_` and `byteCount` straight from the file and validates neither, so the count comes directly from the corrupted bytes. **`MsgPackRowInputFormat::countRows`** — `readObject` with a null visitor can consume nothing on malformed input, so `buf->eof()` never becomes true: ```cpp while (!buf->eof() && num_rows < max_block_size) { for (size_t i = 0; i < columns; ++i) readObject(null_parser); ++num_rows; } ``` ### Possible fix Roughly **13 lines in total**, and the bulk of it is one shared change. #### 1. A shared forward-progress guard — 3 lines, fixes all three formats There is a single call site for `countRows()`, in `IRowInputFormat::generate()` (`src/Processors/Formats/IRowInputFormat.cpp`, ~L90-102), and it **already captures the input offset before the call and computes the delta after it** for `approx_bytes_read_for_chunk`. So the check needs no new plumbing: ```cpp size_t chunk_start_offset = getDataOffsetMaybeCompressed(getReadBuffer()); ... num_rows = countRows(params.max_block_size_rows); + if (num_rows > 0 && getDataOffsetMaybeCompressed(getReadBuffer()) == chunk_start_offset) + throw Exception(ErrorCodes::INCORRECT_DATA, + "Counted {} rows while consuming no input; the file is malformed", num_rows); if (num_rows == 0) { readSuffix(); return {}; } ``` This covers every format implementing `countRows()`, not just the three found here. *Caveat worth checking before relying on it alone:* a format that counts a whole block out of an already-filled buffer would trip the guard on a valid file. It looks safe — valid 200 000-row Avro and MsgPack files still count correctly, because the first `countRows()` call fills the buffer and therefore advances the offset, and later calls that return 0 rows never reach the check — but that is a two-format spot check, not a proof across all thirteen. Running the format test suite would settle it. #### 2. Per-format hardening — about 10 lines, and each is unambiguous * **ProtobufList** (~2 lines) — honour `readFieldNumber`'s return value and stop when it is `false`, instead of discarding it. * **MsgPack** (~4 lines) — the same forward-progress check locally, using `buf->count()`; the null-visitor parse can silently consume nothing. * **Avro** (~4 lines + a submodule bump) — bound the block header in `readDataBlock()` (`lang/c++/impl/DataFile.cc`): reject `objectCount_ < 0`, `byteCount < 0`, and `objectCount_ > byteCount`. An object occupies at least one byte, so a block cannot hold more objects than it has bytes; that single comparison kills the Avro case and cannot reject a well-formed file. This one is the only part needing two repositories. `contrib/avro` is a submodule of ClickHouse's own fork, **https://github.com/ClickHouse/avro** (currently pinned at `7b7f6a5bc42e56b6f74de9fc8f52a2a629c53145`, tracking `master`), so it is a PR there followed by a ClickHouse PR bumping the pointer. There is direct precedent for exactly this kind of hardening in that fork — the pinned commit itself is *"Bound Avro string/bytes decode allocation to actual input"*, and ClickHouse carries *"Avro: bound string/bytes decode allocation (bump avro submodule)"* and *"Add hard limit (256) to the max depth in avro internal parser"*. If only one change is taken, take #1: it is the smallest, needs no submodule work, and is the only one that also protects the formats this corpus never reached. ### Workaround `SET optimize_count_from_files = 0` — verified to make all three cases fail cleanly and fast. ### Additional context The `Protobuf` / `ProtobufList` split is informative: the two share the message decoder and differ in the length-delimited list framing and its `countRows()`, which is exactly where the defect is.

signal.title: Has token with nullable
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106922 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/88119 With a `text` index on a `Nullable` column, direct read from the text index replaced the search predicate with a `UInt8` virtual column filled from the posting lists. A `NULL` row has no tokens, so the predicate was materialized as `0` where it should be `NULL`. The predicate is now rebuilt as `if(str.null, NULL, <virtual column>)`, so the `NULL`s come back while the index still answers the predicate. In exact mode the column itself is no longer read, so the `NULL`s are taken from its `.null` subcolumn. This PR also created the infrastructure to support `hasTokenOrNull` in a followup PR. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for text-search predicates on a `Nullable` column with a text index when the predicate is negated or its value is read, e.g. NOT `hasToken(str, 'x')` returned the rows where `str` is NULL. Direct read from the text index materialized the `NULL` result as 0. ```sql CREATE TABLE tab (id UInt32, str Nullable(String), INDEX idx(str) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha')) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 'hello world'), (2, NULL), (3, 'foo bar'), (4, NULL), (5, 'hello there'); SELECT id FROM tab WHERE NOT hasToken(str, 'hello'); -- 2, 3, 4 with the index, 3 without it <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113332&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113332](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113332+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds to compact partitions that no longer receive inserts
signal.text: ## Summary Closes #79697. This adds an opt-in `MergeTree` setting, `min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds`, addressing the issue's use case in the background merge selector itself (similar in spirit to #105454). When set to a non-zero value and every part in a partition is at least that many seconds old — i.e. the partition no longer receives inserts — the `Simple` and `StochasticSimple` merge selectors waive the size-ratio requirement in `allow()` that otherwise refuses "unbalanced" merges of a large part together with small ones. That waiver is the whole of the setting's effect. It introduces no cross-heuristic relations: every other knob keeps its own meaning and its own default, and a workload that needs one of them off must turn it off explicitly through its own setting. - `window_size` still bounds which parts are examined. - `min_parts_to_merge_at_once` still sets the floor on how many parts a merge must cover. - `enable_heuristic_to_remove_small_parts_at_right` still trims a trailing small part from a selected range of three parts or more. Compacting a trailing small part is the point of #79697, and it happens out of the box: that trim only applies to ranges of three parts or more, and `min_parts_to_merge_at_once` defaults to `0`, so the cheapest candidate in an idle partition is the two-part range ending at the small tail. That follows from those settings' own defaults rather than from this one overriding them, so raising `min_parts_to_merge_at_once` deliberately still does what it says. This setting cannot be combined with `min_age_to_force_merge_seconds` + `min_age_to_force_merge_on_partition_only`, and the combination is rejected in `sanityCheck`. That pair routes a stale partition to the whole-partition merge, which is the only merge marked `final` — and a final merge is what enables `ReplacingMergeTree` `CLEANUP`. Since `selectPartsToMerge` returns as soon as a regular merge is found, forcing regular merges by partition age would pre-empt that path and silently stop cleanup from running. The two mechanisms are complementary: use the pair for partitions that fit into a single merge, and this setting for the ones that do not. Each merge still respects `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool`, so a partition larger than that limit converges to a few max-size parts. Unlike `min_age_to_force_merge_seconds` with `min_age_to_force_merge_on_partition_only`, the partition does not have to fit into a single merge, and unlike plain `min_age_to_force_merge_seconds`, actively written partitions are unaffected. The default is `0` (disabled), preserving existing behavior. Merged parts start with age 0, which re-arms the threshold, so compaction of an idle partition proceeds in naturally throttled rounds. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the `min_partition_age_to_force_merge_seconds` `MergeTree` setting: when every part in a partition is at least this old, the `Simple` and `StochasticSimple` merge selectors compact that partition's parts within the `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool` limit. ### Documentation entry: - [x] Documentation is generated from the setting description in `MergeTreeSettings.cpp`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115547&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115547](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115547+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Compare read-in-order virtual row on its covered sort-key prefix
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106740 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106630 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110725 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a wrong result (mis-ordered merge) for read-in-order queries with a virtual row when `distinct-in-order` or `LIMIT BY` widens the read to a longer sort-key prefix than `ORDER BY` set it up for, and when a key column fixed by the filter is skipped by `ORDER BY` (e.g. `WHERE b = 1 ORDER BY a, c` on key `(a, b, c)`). The virtual row announced a wrong merge boundary: in release builds the merge could be silently mis-ordered, in debug builds the boundary assertion fired, and a `Nullable` key column after the skipped one threw the `Virtual row has different type` exception. The virtual row optimization now stays enabled in these cases. ### Description Alternative to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110725: instead of dropping the virtual row conversion when the in-order read prefix changes (and disabling it for skipped key columns), keep the optimization enabled and compare the virtual row only on the sort-key prefix it validly covers. **Root cause.** The read-in-order virtual row announced a wrong merge boundary in two ways: 1. *Widened prefix.* `optimizeReadInOrder` builds the virtual row conversion for the prefix `ORDER BY` needs (e.g. `CounterID`). A later optimization (`optimizeDistinctInOrder`, `optimizeLimitByInOrder`) re-requests the read with a longer prefix (`CounterID, EventDate`), but the `pk_block` width was derived from the conversion's input count, so the extra sort column was default-filled with `0` in `setVirtualRow`. In reverse order `0` understates the real values, so a real row exceeded the announced boundary: `Virtual row boundary violated in MergingSortedAlgorithm ... the virtual row announced UInt64_0 but the source then produced UInt64_1` in debug builds, a silently mis-ordered merge in release builds. 2. *Skipped fixed key.* For key `(a, b, c)` and `WHERE b = 1 ORDER BY a, c`, the fixed key `b` is skipped without an `ORDER BY` counterpart, but the conversion DAG indexed key columns densely, mapping `c` onto key column `b` (visible in `EXPLAIN actions=1`: input `b` aliased to `__table1.c`). The wrong value tripped the boundary check; a wrong type (`Nullable` key) threw the `Virtual row has different type` logical error even in release builds. Moreover, index values of the columns after the skipped key are semantically unusable: the index describes pre-filter data, so the entry `(5, 0, 9)` does not bound the filtered row `(5, 1, 3)` projected to `(a, c)`. **Fix.** - The virtual row conversion outputs only the sort-description prefix it can announce exactly: index values while the key prefix is contiguous, plus constants for fixed columns from `ORDER BY`. A skipped fixed key column ends the index-backed part: the index entry at a mark boundary may hold a filtered-out value for it, so its later components bound nothing in the filtered stream. A column fixed by the filter that stays in `ORDER BY` keeps disabling the virtual row, as before this fix. - The merge compares a virtual row only on the covered prefix and places it first on a covered-prefix tie (equivalent to treating the uncovered columns as minus infinity in the merge order, without materializing any values). The covered prefix is derived from the pk block column names in `MergingSortedAlgorithm` and carried per cursor in `SortCursorImpl::sort_prefix_limit`, honored by the generic `SortCursor::greaterAt`. A truncated virtual row can only occur with a multi-column sort description (its coverage is at least the first column), which always uses the generic cursor, so the single-column specialized queues are unaffected; the JIT comparator is bypassed when a truncated cursor participates. - `ReadFromMergeTree::readInOrder` reads index values for the whole used sorting-key prefix instead of only the conversion inputs. The in-order merges inside the read step sort by the full prefix, and index values are exact bounds for it even after filtering (a filter only removes rows), so these merges always see fully covered virtual rows. - `ReadFromMergeTree::requestReadingInOrder` drops the conversion only when a re-request makes it unsound: a prefix narrower than the one it was built for (the conversion could lose its inputs), or one not fully backed by the primary index. - `setVirtualRowConversions` builds the conversion with `project_inputs` so a raw index column cannot shadow a same-named conversion output when the merge looks sort columns up by name (matters with the old analyzer). This handles all key types uniformly — e.g. a descending `String` column after a skipped key keeps the optimization even though the type has no greatest value to pad with. Verified on release and debug builds (the boundary assertion is compiled only into debug builds): the previously aborting repros now return correct results, and `EXPLAIN` keeps `Virtual row conversions` for the widened and skipped-key reads. The test is based on the one from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110725, extended with checks that the optimization stays enabled, a descending skipped-key case, a `String` case in both directions, and a fixed key kept in `ORDER BY` (still disabled, as before). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111457&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111457](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111457+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix lost rows when a plan-based parallel replicas fragment has no output columns
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113469 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results with `parallel_replicas_plan_based = 1` when the plan fragment sent to the replicas has no output columns, for example `SELECT count() FROM (SELECT 1 FROM t LIMIT 500)`. Such a query returned `0`, or an empty result set, instead of the correct value. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113469 (same defect class, disjoint path). No open issue. With `parallel_replicas_plan_based = 1`, a query whose distributed fragment ends up with no output columns loses every row it reads, silently and with no error: ```sql SELECT count() FROM (SELECT 1 FROM t LIMIT 500); -- returns 0, must be 500 ``` Root cause. `query_plan_remove_unused_columns` prunes the fragment's last column when the outer aggregate needs only a row count and a `LIMIT` keeps that aggregate out of the fragment. `ReadFromParallelReplicasStep` adopts the empty header, and a result travelling back from a replica is a `Block`, whose row count is the size of its first column: with no columns it is unrepresentable. The block is then dropped by `!block.empty()` on both sides (`TCPHandler.cpp`, `RemoteQueryExecutor.cpp`), and the Native format refuses it outright. Local execution is unaffected: a `Chunk` stores its row count independently of its columns. Only fragment shipping reaches this. Classic parallel replicas and `serialize_query_plan = 1` over `remote()` force the shard header to the initiator's mergeable-stage header (`addConvertingActions`), keeping a column; both measured correct. The fix keeps one materialized constant column in the fragment when its own columns were all pruned away, restoring the "at least one output column" precondition the protocol, `Block` and both guards already assume. It is inserted where the fragment is built, so the remote plan and the local half of the local+remote union get identical headers, and the converting projection `replaceNodeWithPlan` already inserts keeps the placeholder out of the result. `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`, the default, is affected too: its local half normally covers all the marks so the answer happens to be right, but under the `slowdown_parallel_replicas_local_plan_read` failpoint it also returns `0`. Validation: 7 defect shapes go from wrong to correct, 13 controls unchanged, `read_bytes` unchanged, and `04546_pr_plan_based_remote_only` reddens on master and passes here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115871&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115871](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115871+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Make test_good_intent_size not depend on Kafka batch timing
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_storage_kafka/test_intent_sizes.py::test_good_intent_size` produces `message_4` and `message_5` and then waits for `Saving intent of 2 ... at offset 3`, i.e. it assumes both records land in one consuming cycle. Nothing guarantees that. `kafka_produce` flushes per message, so the two records reach the broker at different times, while the batch ends on the first of three conditions in `StorageKafka2.cpp:1224-1225`, one of which is a deadline of `kafka_flush_interval_ms` measured from a `Stopwatch` constructed per cycle at `StorageKafka2.cpp:1390`, before any message is seen. A cycle that opens before the records exist burns its window on stalled polls and closes at one row, so the engine logs `intent of 1` at offset 3 and then `intent of 1` at offset 4. `Saving intent of 2` is then never printed at all, so the test burns its full 30 s `wait_for_log_line` budget and fails. The failure reads like a too-tight wait, but no wait budget can help. Nor can a wider window: because the `Stopwatch` starts before the first poll, every finite `kafka_flush_interval_ms` still has a phase in which the produce lands too late, so widening only shrinks that phase. That was already the mitigation in 7dcb1c10eed3eed (500 to 3000 ms, by the test's author, for this same check). This stops the stream across the produce instead, so the next cycle's first poll already sees both records and a 2-row batch is guaranteed: ``` SYSTEM STOP test.kafka -> produce message_4 + message_5 -> SYSTEM START test.kafka ``` `STOP` rather than `PAUSE` because only `STOP` also cancels the in-flight cycle, and an already-open window is the hazard. The aborted cycle commits nothing (its `OffsetGuard` rolls back to committed offsets), so `at offset 3` and the final data assertion are unchanged. No assertion is relaxed. The same STOP/produce/START shape is already used by `test_system_stop.py` against this engine. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Forcing the losing interleaving deterministically (the two records produced one cycle period apart, matching the reported failure): - old test: FAILS, server log shows `Saving intent of 1 ... at offset 3` and `... at offset 4`, `grep -c "Saving intent of 2"` = 0 - old test without forcing: PASSES (control) - patched test, same forcing: PASSES, `Saving intent of 2 ... at offset 3` present - patched test with the awaited line changed to `intent of 3`: FAILS, so the assertion still discriminates 50/50 passes of the patched test (12 serial, 38 under `pytest -n 3`, the configuration the failure was seen in), and `test_intent_sizes.py` plus the whole `test_system_stop.py` suite together: 35/35. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115771&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115771](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115771+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1892` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Reject an explicit STATISTICS clause on a column that is not physically stored
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115769 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Declaring `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column is now rejected when the table is created or altered, instead of being accepted and making every subsequent `INSERT` fail with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. Closes #114791. ### Description Related: #115769, whose review asked for this shape. Declaring `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` column was accepted, but the table could not be written to at all: such a column is absent from every written block, so with `materialize_statistics_on_insert` (default 1) every `INSERT` failed `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. Statistics on a non-physical column were already refused elsewhere: `addImplicitStatistics` skips `Alias`/`Ephemeral`, and `ADD STATISTICS` checks `columns.hasPhysical`. Only the two inline column-declaration spellings had no such check. This adds it where the resulting metadata is known: `registerStorageMergeTree` for `CREATE`, `MergeTreeData::checkAlterIsPossible` for `ALTER`, using one pair read from the column's own metadata: `!columns.hasPhysical(name) && column.statistics.hasExplicitStatistics()`. The `ALTER` check is a delta check, refusing only a state the statement produced, and both exempt `Replicated`-database DDL replay so a rolling upgrade cannot wedge a secondary's queue. Existing such tables still load, read and detach/attach. ```sql CREATE TABLE tab (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(tdigest)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); -- before: accepted; INSERT then failed Code: 10 (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) -- after: Code: 708. Cannot add statistics to column 'b': it is not physically stored. (ILLEGAL_STATISTICS) ``` Three disclosed behaviour changes. `MODIFY COLUMN b <type> ALIAS <expr>` on a column that already had explicit statistics is refused although it has no `STATISTICS` token, and `CREATE TABLE dst AS src` / `CLONE AS` off such a table is refused; `DROP STATISTICS b` first is the remedy for both. **Known gap, not fixed here:** `SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA` on a grandfathered table is also refused and leaves it detached, because that path reparses stored metadata and sets `attach` without `attach_short_syntax`, so the definition is misclassified as fresh input (`InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1489-1492`). That belongs in the caller, not in this predicate; say the word and I will send it here or separately. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Ten rejection arms (both `CREATE` spellings, deprecated `MergeTree(...)` syntax, full-definition `ATTACH`, `ALTER ADD`/`MODIFY` including no-type `MODIFY COLUMN b STATISTICS(...)` and chained `ADD COLUMN b ALIAS a+1, MODIFY COLUMN b STATISTICS(...)`) were each measured against a build without this change and one with it: accepted before, `ILLEGAL_STATISTICS` after. Six negative controls are byte-identical on both builds: the two `IF NOT EXISTS` no-ops, `MATERIALIZED`/`DEFAULT` with statistics, alias converted to `MATERIALIZED` with statistics, implicit statistics on an alias, and a physical column with only implicit statistics converted to an alias. For a table created before the check: loads, reads, `DROP STATISTICS`, an unrelated `ADD COLUMN`, `DETACH`/`ATTACH` with statistics intact and a pure `RENAME COLUMN` all succeed; changing the statistics on the offending column is refused. Control: the same procedure with `CODEC(ZSTD(1))` instead fails to load on the same binary, which is what this check avoids. Replication: on `ReplicatedMergeTree` the `ALTER` is refused on the initiator with an empty `system.replication_queue` and both replicas usable. On a `Replicated` database both checks fire for a client statement, while an `ALTER` or a full-definition `ATTACH` committed by an older initiator is still applied on replay with no retrying queue entry. A further replica created with no column list (columns from ZooKeeper) still succeeds, while the same `CREATE` with an explicit offending column list is refused. `02864_statistics_ddl` passes 50/50 with randomized settings and 50/50 without, and fails on a build without this change, so the expected-error annotations are not pinning current behaviour. `01318_alter_add_column_exists`, `04542_create_if_not_exists_as_select_skips_create_only_validation` and `03224_invalid_alter` pass. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115882&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115882](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115882+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Push down volume-reducing functions in query plan
signal.text: Adds a query plan optimization that pushes volume-reducing functions (`length`, `lengthUTF8`, `empty`, `notEmpty`) below the `Sorting` and `Filter` steps, so those steps carry the fixed-size result instead of the original `String` / `FixedString` argument. The rewrite is done with `ActionsDAG::split`: the function nodes form the first part, which becomes a new step below the child, and the second part becomes the parent step's `ActionsDAG` and reads the results as inputs. It only fires when the wide argument column really stops flowing through the child step — the column is removed from the child's output, and unless the child reads it itself it is not even produced below the child. `tryExecuteFunctionsAfterSorting` and `trySplitFilter` keep the pushed functions where they are, so the optimizations do not move the same nodes in opposite directions. For the shape from the issue below, `SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s)`, the filter still needs `s` to evaluate its condition, but `length(s)` is now computed before the filter, so the wide column is not copied for the surviving rows. Enabled by default; can be turned off with `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions = 0`. An earlier attempt at the same optimization was https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86139 by @talmawash, credited as a co-author. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/82378 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86139 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a query plan optimization that pushes volume-reducing functions (`length`, `lengthUTF8`, `empty`, `notEmpty`) below the `Sorting` and `Filter` steps, replacing the wide `String` / `FixedString` argument with the fixed-size result, so it is neither buffered by a sort nor copied by a filter. Controlled by the new setting `query_plan_push_down_volume_reducing_functions`, enabled by default. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106199&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/106199](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F106199+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1857` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Add stateless and fuzzer jobs to the WeeklyCFI workflow
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112152 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115591 The `amd_cfi` build is the only test build with ThinLTO enabled — the same compile profile as official release builds — so besides CFI violations the `WeeklyCFI` workflow also catches ThinLTO-only behavior differences that no other CI job can see (e.g. the `__functional` frame-name suppression surfaced by `test_crash_log` and fixed in #112152). This PR broadens the workflow's coverage from build + integration + stress to: - **Stateless tests** (`amd_cfi, parallel` + `amd_cfi, sequential` lanes, mirroring `amd_debug`). `clickhouse-test` now detects the CFI build from `-fsanitize=cfi` in the `CXX_FLAGS` row of `system.build_options` and exposes a `cfi` build flag, so a test that genuinely cannot hold in this profile can carry a `no-cfi` tag (the same generic `no-<flag>` skip mechanism the sanitizer builds use). No test needs the tag today. CFI is deliberately not treated as a sanitizer: it has near-zero runtime overhead, so tests tagged `no-sanitizers` still run under CFI — consistent with #115591, which stopped the test harnesses from misclassifying the CFI build as a sanitizer build. - **AST fuzzer** (`amd_cfi`): fuzzers assert only on crashes, never on exact query output, so the build profile cannot produce false positives there, and fuzzing reaches virtual-call combinations the curated suites never exercise. Runs against the unmodified CFI binary (no build flag needed). - **BuzzHouse** (`amd_cfi_buzzhouse`): BuzzHouse needs `-DENABLE_BUZZHOUSE=1`, which compiles extra sources into `clickhouse-client`/`dbms` and would change the whole-program ThinLTO graph of the shared CFI binary. To keep the canary binary identical to the release profile, a separate `amd_cfi_buzzhouse` build (identical cmake plus the flag) feeds only this lane. The fuzzer job configs are shared out into `_common_ast_fuzzer_job_config` / `_common_buzz_fuzzer_job_config`; the master and PR workflows are unchanged (their generated YAML did not change). Not added, and why: unit tests (`ENABLE_CFI` is incompatible with `ENABLE_TESTS` — ThinLTO is disabled when building tests), performance comparison (it compares against the non-CFI master-head binary, so results are uninterpretable), upgrade/compatibility checks (version and data compatibility are orthogonal to CFI instrumentation), Keeper Jepsen (requires the standalone `clickhouse-keeper` build, which the CFI build omits). **Validation:** the workflow was temporarily switched to a `pull_request` trigger (same approach as #100419) and all `amd_cfi` jobs passed ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=baf56e50335c45adf2afb691d0a1ef72f49c8bc6&name_0=WeeklyCFI)) — stateless parallel + sequential, integration 4/4, stress, AST fuzzer, and BuzzHouse. The schedule-only trigger (Mondays 03:00 UTC) is restored for merge. **Findings from the validation runs, all filed:** - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115121 — probabilistic server crash (SIGSEGV) in gRPC response compression (`zlib_compress` / `deflateEnd`), still open. - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115122 — empty `symbols`/`lines` in `system.trace_log` under `amd_cfi`; root cause was the test harness misclassifying the CFI build as a sanitizer build and installing `trace_log_no_symbolize.xml`; fixed by #115591 (merged, and master is merged into this branch), so the two `03150_trace_log_*` tests are expected to pass in the weekly stateless lanes. - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115198 — stress runs cannot restart the server if killed inside `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`'s deliberate-corruption window (not CFI-specific; also hit three other PRs). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115036](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115036+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Cancel in-flight merges and mutations on server shutdown
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115732 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Cancel in-flight merges, mutations and part fetches during graceful server shutdown instead of waiting for the running step to finish. Previously a single slow merge step or a large part download could delay shutdown for its whole duration. ### Description `ContextSharedPart::shutdown` waits for the MergeTree background executors before `DatabaseCatalog::shutdown` (the reordering that fixed the SIGBUS in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85433), but nothing cancels the tasks that are already running: the executors' `wait` only prevents new steps from starting, and the per-storage `merges_blocker` cancellation happens later, in `DatabaseCatalog::shutdown`. So shutdown blocks until the currently running task step completes. This caused the `Possible deadlock on shutdown (see gdb.log)` failure in the stress test (azure, amd_msan) on master: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=a013c79d6ac80373b820381527ea85823ab03834&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_msan%29&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_msan%29 There, a background merge of `t_lwu_key_prefix` (854090 rows in 5 parts plus 3 `MergeOnKey` patch parts, left over from `04509_lwu_sorting_key_common_prefix`) spent ~37 seconds per 8192-row block inside `applyPatchesMergeOnKey` under MSan — quadratic patch application over an all-equal sorting key, tracked separately in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115732. Together with a randomized `merge_max_block_size` of ~24k rows and 5 sources to prime, the first `pull` of the merge pipeline alone needed ~8 minutes, so the executor thread never reached a step boundary, `MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor::wait` blocked the whole time, and the hung check fired: `gdb.log` shows the main thread in `ContextSharedPart::shutdown` → `MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor::wait` and the `MergeMutate` thread inside `processEqualKeyCursors` (`applyPatches.cpp:468`); the server log shows `Shutting down merges executor` at 01:27:53 and no further shutdown progress until gdb attached at 01:33:53, with `MergeWrittenRows` flat the whole time. The fix cancels the in-flight work before waiting for the executors, in three ordered steps so that the cancellation is not racy: 1. `MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor::requestShutdown` flips all four background executors into shutdown mode without joining them: new tasks are rejected by `trySchedule` and pending tasks are not started (worker threads exit at the next step boundary), so the set of running tasks cannot grow anymore. 2. `MergeList::cancelAll` and the new `ReplicatedFetchList::cancelAll` cancel everything that is currently running, and also mark entries inserted later as cancelled, so a task that is inside its first step and has not registered itself in the list yet cannot escape the cancellation. 3. The executors are joined. Merge and mutate tasks check `MergeListElement::is_cancelled` on every block through `MergeProgressCallback` (the same mechanism the OOM canary uses), so a running merge aborts with the `ABORTED` exception within one block instead of running to completion. In-flight fetches are cancelled too, checked in `ReplicatedFetchReadCallback` on every buffer refill: a replicated merge can fall back to `executeFetch` inside the same task step before any `MergeList` entry exists, and a plain `GET_PART` fetch would otherwise block the `fetch_executor` join for the whole download. The results of these merges and fetches would have been discarded after the restart anyway, so finishing them was pure waste. This also restores the pre-https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85433-fix semantics, where per-storage shutdown cancelled merges and fetches before anything waited on the executors. Also adds the `merge_tree_sequential_source_sleep_before_read` failpoint and an integration test (`test_shutdown_cancels_merges`) with two cases: a 16-part merge whose every reading step sleeps for 10 seconds, and a fetch of a ~150 MB part from a sender throttled to 1 MiB/s — in both, the server must stop within 90 seconds. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115733&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115733](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115733+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Iceberg: reuse parsed state and derived storage metadata
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Reuse parsed Iceberg snapshot state and derived storage metadata while the exact table state is unchanged. ### Summary Warm Iceberg reads repeatedly performed two kinds of immutable work: 1. parsed the same metadata JSON and re-registered schemas; 2. rebuilt `StorageInMemoryMetadata`, including `ColumnsDescription` and the analyzed sorting key. This PR adds two lock-free, single-entry caches published with atomic shared pointers: - parsed state keyed by metadata version/path; - derived storage metadata keyed by the complete `TableStateSnapshot` (metadata path/version, schema ID, and snapshot ID). The existing interface still returns a deep copy of `StorageInMemoryMetadata`; the cache avoids JSON parsing, schema traversal, sort-expression parsing, and repeated key analysis. Time-travel reads bypass both singleton caches and never publish into the current-state entry, preventing historical queries from evicting or poisoning ordinary reads. Concurrent misses may duplicate work but publish only complete immutable values. ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - TSAN integration matrix: snapshot reads passed 6/6 across S3, Azure, and local storage (Iceberg v1/v2) - Snapshot-read integration coverage asserts derived-cache hits and an ordinary read immediately after a historical read - Live exact-hit benchmark: - 1271 -> 1375 RPS (+8.2%) - CPU/query 4.565 -> 4.163 ms (-8.8%) - `IcebergMetadataUpdateMicroseconds` 0.341 -> 0.010 ms/query - one derived-metadata cache hit/query, zero warm misses

signal.title: Add `splitByRegexp` tokenizer for text indexes
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103783 The existing text-index tokenizers cannot preserve tokens that contain special characters. For example, `splitByNonAlpha` tokenizes `C++` as just `c`, so a text index over a column of technology names (`C++`, `C#`, `F#`, ...) produces false positives and there is no way to search for the original term: `hasToken` rejects needles with separator characters, and searching for the stripped token matches unrelated rows. Usage: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, description String, INDEX idx description TYPE text(tokenizer = splitByRegexp('[^\p{L}\p{N}#+]+'))) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `splitByRegexp` tokenizer for text indexes and the `tokens` function. It splits the input into tokens using a regular expression as the separator, for example `tokenizer = splitByRegexp('[^\p{L}\p{N}#+]+')`, which allows preserving tokens containing special characters such as `C++` or `C#` that other tokenizers would break apart. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110002&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110002](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110002+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix performance regression in text serialization of JSON and Dynamic columns
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115796 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96563 `SerializationDynamic::serializeTextImpl` got the serialization of the whole `Variant` type for every value, which builds the serializations and names of all the variants and goes through the globally locked `SerializationObjectPool`. `SerializationJSON` calls it once per JSON path per row. Resolve the exact variant by its global discriminator and take its serialization from the thread-local `DataTypesCache`, like the row-level binary serializer already does. `toString` over a 1M-row `JSON` table, 200k rows, `max_threads = 4`: | | master | this PR | 26.2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `JSON`, 10 dynamic paths | 6.4 s | 0.26 s | 1.0 s | | `JSON(max_dynamic_paths=0)` | 8.2 s | 1.79 s | 2.4 s | ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix performance regression introduced in 26.4 when writing `JSON` and `Dynamic` columns in text formats. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115852&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115852](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115852+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in normal projection optimization with correlated subqueries
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103695 (same `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` error family) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` raised when a normal projection was used to read the input of a correlated subquery (decorrelated into a join) and all parts were served from the projection. Depending on the settings it was reported as `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` or as `Block structure mismatch in joined block stream`. It is an exception in release builds and aborts the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, reproduces on current master and is unrelated to the pull requests it was seen on: [amd_msan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100332&sha=766a499fbbfcfb5b1cbd865a4f435f75c7b5ee28&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29) (STID 2270-3452), [amd_tsan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=92472&sha=0d58afae81ce01111323d3f73a59d6d032d199f7&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29) (STID 0993-3a3c), and `Stress test (arm_debug)`. Root cause: `optimizeUseNormalProjections` reads the projection over `required_columns = reading->getAllColumnNames()`. Columns of that set which the rebuilt `query.dag` does not consume survive as pass-throughs, because `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` appends every un-consumed input, and widen the rewritten read's output header. The all-parts-from-projection branch spliced that widened node in without the `blocksHaveEqualStructure` check the Union branch already had, so a downstream step got more columns than its declared header. Change: emit the replaced header's columns by name, dropping the surplus pass-throughs so the projection stays usable, and hoist the equal-structure check to cover both replacement branches. It stays below the narrowing as a fail-closed net for what narrowing cannot repair (a missing column, or a type difference), skipping the projection and keeping the regular read. Since `filterPartsByProjection` mutates the parent analysis result in place, it now runs only after that check passes, so a skipped projection no longer drops parts; `has_parent_parts` moves ahead of it and is computed non-destructively. Validation: the load-bearing regression test is `03324_union_block_structure_mismatch`. Reverting only this change makes its first statement fail with `PROJECTION_NOT_USED`; that statement previously carried `-- { serverError PROJECTION_NOT_USED }`, so the projection is now used where it was refused before. `04410` and `04907` pin the plan shape via `EXPLAIN`: every read served by the projection, none declined, no base-table arm. The `04410` carriers abort on the commit the fuzzer reports came from, but not at the current merge-base, where an earlier pass prevents the widening; they are kept as plan-shape pins, not as the proof. The failing-test set across the projection, prewhere, part_offset and correlated suites is unchanged. <details><summary>Both carriers: error signatures</summary> Carrier 1, virtual columns (`_part_offset` in the projection), output port assert: ``` Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort. Expected 2, found 4 src/Processors/Port.h:425 src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:101 DB::JoiningTransform::prepare() ``` Carrier 2, real columns. The inner decorrelation join's right side carries exactly one column by design, so the leaked columns trip its structure check instead of the output port one: ``` Block structure mismatch in joined block stream: different number of columns: __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 0) __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 2), payload String String(size = 2), id UUID Sparse(size = 2, UUID(size = 1), UInt64(size = 0)) src/Core/Block.cpp:863 DB::assertBlocksHaveEqualStructureAllowReplicated src/Interpreters/ConstantJoin.cpp:230 DB::ConstantJoin::addBlockToJoin src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:373 DB::FillingRightJoinSideTransform::work() ``` `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0` selects the `ConstantJoin` assert; adding `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'` selects the output port one. Runnable reproducers for both are the statements in the new test file. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111401&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111401](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111401+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)
