signal.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - No replay compatibility is provided for `Replicated` databases, again following the `LIVE VIEW` precedent: a lagging replica that upgrades and then replays a retained `CREATE WINDOW VIEW` DDL queue entry stalls on a plain `SYNTAX_ERROR` — the same long-standing behavior as for any queue entry with unknown syntax (for example, one written by a newer server) — and the replica should be recreated. An earlier revision of this PR carried a token-level rewriting layer in `DatabaseReplicatedWorker` that tried to skip such entries and their follow-ups; it was removed as an unmaintainable fallback path (review kept finding shapes of retained `RENAME`/`EXCHANGE`/`ATTACH` history that it silently mishandled), in favor of failing closed. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114747](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114747+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: PromQL: reject vector matching with scalar operands
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)** ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Reject PromQL vector matching modifiers when one operand is a scalar.** ### Summary PromQL rejects `on(...)` and `ignoring(...)` when one binary operator operand is a scalar. ClickHouse currently accepts queries such as: `up + on(job) 1` and evaluates them like `up + 1`, silently dropping the requested matching labels. This change rejects non-empty vector matching labels when either operand is a scalar. Empty `on()` and `ignoring()` clauses remain valid. ### Why it matters PromQL-compatible clients expect invalid vector matching expressions to fail instead of returning a plausible result with different semantics. ### Tests - Add regression coverage for scalar math and comparison expressions with vector matching labels. - Keep coverage for valid scalar expressions and empty matching clauses. - Syntax-check the changed C++ translation unit with the existing compile command. - Run `git diff --check`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115828&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115828](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115828+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Speed up to_utc_timestamp and from_utc_timestamp on DateTime64
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up `toUTCTimestamp`/`to_utc_timestamp` and `fromUTCTimestamp`/`from_utc_timestamp` on `DateTime64` arguments, restoring the throughput they had before the overflow fix in #109738. Results are unchanged. Closes #115802. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 My #109738 fixed a signed-overflow and a wrong-offset-at-a-boundary bug on the `DateTime64` path of these functions, but it did the arithmetic and the clamp in `Int128`, once per row. `Int128` here is `wide::integer<128, signed>`, a software big-integer, so `operator*` sign-normalizes through branches before a native multiply and reassembles a two-`UInt64` struct. Each row gained that call plus two 128-bit compares and selects where it previously had one `imul` and one `add`. The `DateTime` branch was untouched and did not regress. The wide arithmetic is redundant. The floored split guarantees `seconds * scale_multiplier + micros == value` exactly, so shifting the seconds by the offset and reassembling equals shifting the underlying value by `offset * scale_multiplier`; the `Int128` multiply only re-derived its own input. This PR shifts the underlying value directly with a saturating `Int64` add/sub (`common::addOverflow`/`subOverflow`: one `add`/`sub` plus a flag test). `offset * scale_multiplier` cannot overflow `Int64`: scanning `timeZoneOffset` over all 597 shipped time zones (4.18M samples, including out-of-LUT extremes) gives `max|offset| = 130800`, and `scale_multiplier <= 10^9`, so the product stays 70000x below the `Int64` limit. Both semantics from #109738 are kept: the split still floors, and the result is still saturated. Measured on the queries from `tests/performance/utc_timestamp_transform.xml` (10M rows, `max_threads=1`, optimized build, arms differing by exactly this hunk): `0.102s -> 0.062s`, against `0.061s` before #109738. The `DateTime` queries are the control and stay at `0.033s` throughout. That is x86_64, so the ratio is smaller than the ARM 2.7x in the issue, but the fix returns to the pre-#109738 cost rather than narrowing the gap. Results are bit-identical to master over 12.9M `(value, scale, timezone, direction)` cases plus 112K cases built on the 1,056 real offset-transition seconds. `03891_utc_timestamp_datetime64_overflow` passes byte-identical, and still reddens if the saturation is dropped, its direction flipped, or the floor correction removed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115838&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115838](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115838+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Parquet: share cached footer metadata between readers
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry: Share immutable cached Parquet footer metadata between V3 readers instead of deep-copying it per query. ### Summary `ParquetMetadataCache` stores a parsed `FileMetaData`, but `getOrSetMetadata` returned it by value. Files with hundreds of row groups and wide schemas therefore deep-copied the entire footer for every reader. This PR returns an aliasing shared_ptr that retains the cache cell. V3 readers keep the immutable footer alive even if the cache entry is evicted. Noncached readers still own a local metadata value. ### Validation - Independent full ClickHouse build against current `master` - New `ParquetMetadataCache` unit test verifies pointer reuse, one loader invocation, and lifetime after eviction - Unit test result: 1/1 passed - Controlled Iceberg point lookup: CPU/query 5.90 ms -> 3.97 ms; 1204 -> 1643 RPS

signal.title: Use the text index when a tokenizer argument matches the index tokenizer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `text` index is now used for `hasAnyTokens`, `hasAllTokens` and `hasPhrase` called with an explicit tokenizer argument, when that argument denotes the same tokenizer as the index and the index has no `preprocessor` or `postprocessor`. Previously the three-argument form always fell back to a full scan. Closes #115275. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108808 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107186 `MergeTreeIndexConditionText::traverseAtomNode` rejected any function node that was not binary before it looked at the function name, so a three-argument `hasAnyTokens` / `hasAllTokens` / `hasPhrase` never reached `isSupportedFunction` (which already lists all three). The predicate became an unknown atom: no granule pruning and no direct read. This mattered because the three-argument form is the documented workaround for #108808, so users of a non-`splitByNonAlpha` tokenizer had no option that was both correct and indexed. The gate now admits three arguments for those three functions when the argument's tokenizer canonicalizes to the index tokenizer. Equality compares `ITokenizer::getDescription()`, which is the form the direct-read pass already synthesizes for the two-argument case, so registered aliases and spelling variants compare equal while parameters still discriminate (`ngrams(3)` is not `ngrams(4)`). Everything else keeps full-scanning, by design and per @ rschu1ze's ruling on the issue: a different tokenizer, a non-constant or invalid argument, and an index carrying a `preprocessor` or `postprocessor` option (there the index stores tokens of a transformed value that the argument's bare tokenizer never produces, so the two cannot answer the same predicate). No error is raised on a mismatch. `hasPhrase` is included at @CurtizJ's request (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275#issuecomment-5328448695). The direct-read pass is kept argument-count-preserving: it now assigns the tokenizer argument in place when one is already present rather than appending, because that pass can legitimately run over the same node twice and would otherwise build a four-argument call. `02346_text_index_function_hasPhrase{,_positions}` asserted the old full-scan behavior for this exact case. Those sections are retitled and regenerated, and a mismatching-tokenizer sibling case is added at the same site so the full-scan boundary keeps a pinned oracle. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115348&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115348](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115348+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Stress tests fail to restart the server after `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata`: the test's deliberately malformed `KeeperMap` metadata in ZooKeeper is fatal at startup
signal.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115642 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115198 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 ### Describe what's wrong Stress test jobs fail with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` when the run kills the server while `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata` (added in #115642, merged 2026-08-21) is inside its corruption window. The test deliberately rewrites the `metadata` znode of the still-attached table `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata` to the malformed spelling `primary key: key;\n` in order to assert that a new `CREATE` on the same path is rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and only later repairs the znode and drops the tables. If the server is killed inside that window, the post-stress restart fails: ``` DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table test_7.05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata' failed: Code: 27. DB::Exception: Invalid KeeperMap metadata format version or columns definition in ZK: primary key: key; ``` Observed in #115036, `Stress test (arm_release)`, 2026-08-21 23:24 UTC: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=1b9be4e90ec59d43356e230f4442cbeb005cec87&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 This is the same kill-unsafe test pattern as #115198 (`04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`): a `no-stress` tag is not supported by design ("stress tests must be able to run every test"), so a test must never hold on-disk or in-ZooKeeper state that a concurrently killed-and-restarted server cannot load. There is also the same server-side asymmetry: the running server tolerates the malformed znode for the already-attached table, but the startup load path hard-fails the whole table instead of quarantining it. ### How to reproduce * Run `05024_keeper_map_parenthesized_metadata`, kill the server after the `INSERT INTO system.zookeeper ... 'primary key: key;\n'` step (before the final repair/`DROP`), and start the server again — loading the table fails with error 27 while the same state was tolerated before the kill. * In CI: any stress job that kills the server inside that window. No fiddle link: requires killing and restarting the server around ZooKeeper state, which fiddle cannot do.

signal.title: Do not buffer the serialized step when computing the hash-table-stats cache key
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113736 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113333 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reduced memory usage and query-plan optimization time for keyed aggregations over large constant-folded literals. The aggregation hash-table-statistics cache key is now hashed as it is serialized instead of being accumulated in memory first, so a plan carrying a large literal no longer holds a copy of it during optimization. For an 80 MB literal, peak memory drops by about 250 MB and optimization time by about 2.5x. The computed key is unchanged. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113736 `calculateHashFromStep` buffered a step's whole serialized form, then hashed it in a second pass. That stream is hash input only, and `serializeConstant` writes a constant-folded literal out in full, so a large literal was copied just to be hashed and dropped. This hashes the stream as it is produced, through a small `WriteBuffer` feeding a `SipHash` over a 32 KiB window. **The key value is bit-identical to before**, since `SipHash::update` carries state across calls including any sub-word remainder. That matters because a collision is harmless for only one of the three consumers: `considerEnablingParallelReplicas` uses these hashes as a node matcher across two plan builds, transplanting cached dataflow statistics on a match. Truncating the key would make different constants compare equal there. Measured with `clickhouse local` on a `GROUP BY` over an 80 MB `repeat()` literal, 3 runs: | 80 MB literal | `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` | peak RSS | |---|---|---| | before | 176 / 179 / 175 ms | 668 / 671 / 668 MB | | after | 68 / 70 / 73 ms | 407 / 419 / 419 MB | | setting off (floor) | 43 / 39 / 40 ms | 407 / 413 / 407 MB | Peak memory now sits at the floor. Same at 800 MB: 3460 to 1817 MB, floor 1817 MB. The O(N) term remains: `serializeBinary` still walks every byte, and each aggregation node serializes its own subtree. Removing it means giving up exact key identity, which given the matcher above is the code owner's call. A gtest asserts the streamed key equals the previously buffered key across window-boundary alignments, and fails under two deliberate perturbations of the sink. 12 real cache keys spanning constants, Array, Tuple, Nullable, LowCardinality and Decimal are unchanged. Reported by @ egor-click. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115847&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115847](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115847+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Include the peer address in deferred connect errors
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/48205 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Connect errors detected after a non-blocking connect (for example, while fetching a part from another replica) now name the peer: `Connection refused`, `Network is unreachable`, `No route to host`, and `Host is down`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes `Poco::Net::SocketImpl::connect(address, timeout)` reports connect failures in two ways: an immediate failure of `::connect` already included `address.toString()`, but an error discovered after `EINPROGRESS` via `poll()` + `SO_ERROR` — the normal outcome when the peer is a remote host, as in replicated part fetches — reaches the caller through `error(err)`, with no address argument at all. This is why logs showed bare `Connection refused` with no hint of which replica was unreachable. The message now becomes `Connection refused: <ip>:<port>`. The address reported is the endpoint that was actually dialled: the address the resolver picked for this connection (so the resolved IP is shown, which also helps diagnose stale DNS entries, as noted in the issue), or the proxy endpoint when a proxy is in use and not bypassed. An immediate failure already carries the address, so those messages are left untouched rather than repeating it. **Scope.** `Connection refused` is rethrown as a `ConnectionRefusedException` carrying the endpoint. The other deferred `SO_ERROR` failures lose the address on the same path and arrive as plain `NetException`s with Poco's bare text (`Network is unreachable`, `No route to host`, `Host is down`); those are restated as `NetException`s with the endpoint appended. `NetException` subclasses such as `SSLException`, and immediate failures whose text already names the peer, pass through untouched. The integration test uses two instances because the deferred-error path only triggers for non-loopback connects, and covers both an IP literal and a hostname, so the resolved address is asserted rather than the name from the URL. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115718&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115718](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115718+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Transform JOIN hash table payload to row major
signal.text: Resolves [#97883](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97883) Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where fixed and contiguous columns under a certain size are transformed into one row-major block of data. Before the change: ``` col1 Int32 col2 String col3 UInt8 col4 Float64 ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ │ .... │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┘ row N → col1[N], col2[N], col3[N], col4[N] ``` After the change: ``` ROW STORE (col1 + col3 + col4, contiguous per row) col2 String (columnar) ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ ← row N (record) │ .... │ ← col2[N] ├──────────┼──────────┼────────────┤ ├──────────┤ │ col1 │ col3 │ col4 │ │ .... │ └──────────┴──────────┴────────────┘ └──────────┘ ``` ### Rational: The row-major format allows the output construction to be a tight loop over each column, basically one pointer load and data copy: ``` for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) { const char * row_store_ptr = row_store_ptrs[i]; col->insertData(row_store_ptr + value_offset, value_size); } ``` In comparison the columnar version has to do more work: load columns[j], row_numbers[j], replicated_columns access, insertFrom ... For the following query `SELECT * FROM rs_probe_200m l JOIN rs_right_10m r ON (l.k % toUInt64(10000000 / 0.9)) = r.k FORMAT Null` from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql` the perf counters for `LazyOutput::buildOutput` in `AddedColumns` look as follows: ``` ┌─variant────────────────────────────┬─query_id─────────────────────────────┬─runtime_ms─┬───────instr─┬──────cycles─┬──────cmiss─┬──brmiss─┬───ipc─┬─cmiss_per_kinstr─┬─brmiss_per_kinstr─┐ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 9d2d6886-2ad7-430f-af2c-6c7cd32f3808 │ 1621 │ 11393048228 │ 31974507197 │ 1470246364 │ 5892574 │ 0.356 │ 129.05 │ 0.517 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 56b33013-8bec-4d7a-a415-2a06beb14bf6 │ 1633 │ 11547943445 │ 31874206968 │ 1484117664 │ 6265932 │ 0.362 │ 128.52 │ 0.543 │ │ row-major-enabled-multi-threaded │ 65583fa7-9ce0-4426-95eb-977251d38f75 │ 1708 │ 11338601601 │ 31825721703 │ 1468670383 │ 5921051 │ 0.356 │ 129.53 │ 0.522 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 5ff1b154-3c3f-40c6-bae9-f6cf0feafe81 │ 2548 │ 15453833738 │ 58322156979 │ 2636461094 │ 9533242 │ 0.265 │ 170.6 │ 0.617 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 6e92c1d4-8432-4a79-a6cc-85e38232116d │ 2580 │ 15400954730 │ 58683032344 │ 2623136775 │ 9455570 │ 0.262 │ 170.32 │ 0.614 │ │ row-major-disabled-multi-threaded │ 133f384f-c09a-4e12-9e69-85b61272a360 │ 2686 │ 15419169622 │ 59548322941 │ 2647601264 │ 9746405 │ 0.259 │ 171.71 │ 0.632 │ │ row-major-enabled-single-threaded │ 20039e91-b5dc-4b4a-8e22-f4451f6067be │ 30610 │ 9046504977 │ 16964398066 │ 995568814 │ 3235355 │ 0.533 │ 110.05 │ 0.358 │ │ row-major-disabled-single-threaded │ a3f9a822-dae6-45c1-9a4e-63e87a3592e8 │ 56821 │ 15279361788 │ 27940919919 │ 1167368997 │ 4694553 │ 0.547 │ 76.4 │ 0.307 │ └────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┴────────────┴─────────┴───────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Changes: - A `RowDataStore` that takes a set of columns and lays them in row major format. It exposes access to individual rows and the layout of each row (offset and size of fields in a row). - New `IColumn` interfaces that handle building the output columns from the row store, used manly by `AddedColumns.cpp`. - Two new settings to control the row-major transformation: - enable_hash_join_row_store. - min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store: Minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable transforming hash join payload to row-major. Used in the planner to decide when to enable the optimization. - A runtime feedback loop that tracks the number of hash table matches from a join and feeds it to the next execution of the join instead of relying on the estimated join output: - The match count is only published when the probe phase fully completes. - Only joins that went through the join reorder optimizer get a cache key. - Plans serialized to distributed workers don't collect or use the feedback. ### Limitations: 1. Only supports fixed and contiguous types and nullable version of them. Supporting non fixed rows would make the row-major layout non-uniform between rows and output column construction loop would not be as tight anymore. Also transforming unbounded unfixed types to row major could be very heavy. 2. ColumnReplicated might get materialized. The decision is made based on the column state the join sees in the first block. If it's ColumnReplicated the column is excluded from the row store, if it's not the column is included and it's replicated in a future block it get's materialized. 3. If spilling occurs, the row stored data is split back into columns for now. In a follow up we can make the row store a column and spill it as is. ### Build overhead: | Type | Rows | Columns | avg per worker thread (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | Int64 | 2M | 8 | 28.2 | | Int64 | 1M | 16 | 31.9 | | FixedString(16) | 1M | 8 | 24.6 | | FixedString(16) | 2M | 4 | 21.5 | ### Benchmarks: #### from `04054_hash_join_with_row_store.sql`: | # | Right table | Match | Join | Before (s) | After (s) | Speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.265 | 0.237 | 1.12× | | 1 | `rs_right_100k` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.182 | 0.178 | 1.02× | | 2 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.108 | 0.525 | 2.11× | | 3 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.532 | 0.335 | 1.59× | | 4 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 0.350 | 0.249 | 1.41× | | 5 | `rs_right_100k_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.216 | 0.183 | 1.18× | | 6 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.607 | 0.553 | 2.91× | | 7 | `rs_right_10m_nullable` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.698 | 0.357 | 1.95× | | 8 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.9 | FULL | 1.652 | 0.916 | 1.80× | | 9 | `rs_right_10m` | 0.3 | FULL | 1.424 | 0.861 | 1.65× | | 10 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 2.239 | 1.554 | 1.44× | | 11 | `rs_right_1m_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.825 | 0.641 | 1.29× | | 12 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.9 | INNER | 3.771 | 1.820 | 2.07× | | 13 | `rs_right_1m_nullable_x10` | 0.3 | INNER | 1.372 | 0.771 | 1.78× | | 14 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 1.596 | 1.249 | 1.28× | | 15 | `rs_right_mixed_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 0.759 | 0.628 | 1.21× | | 16 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.9 | INNER | 6.158 | 1.979 | 3.11× | | 17 | `rs_right_wide_10m` | 0.3 | INNER | 2.563 | 1.111 | 2.31× | ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Introduce an alternative layout for hash table payload in hash joins, where qualifying columns are transformed into one row-major block of data in order to speed up join output reconstruction. Controlled by two new settings: `enable_hash_join_row_store` (default true) and `min_rows_ratio_for_hash_join_row_store` (default 2, the minimum estimated ratio of join output rows to build-side rows to enable the transformation). --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104884&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/104884](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F104884+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113059 The `Code Review` job died on `gh auth login` for 10 pull requests in the 24 h to 2026-08-17, losing the automated review for those heads. A fork PR cannot re-run it, so recovery needs a fresh push. ``` ERROR: Codex review failed after 3 attempts: CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'auth', 'login', '--with-token']' returned non-zero exit status 1. ``` - report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113059&sha=83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50&name_0=PR&name_1=Code%20Review - log: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/113059/83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50/code_review/job.log `_run_codex_once` authenticated a robot token before every attempt, under `check=True`, but the Codex backend never uses it: `enable_gh_auth=True` has the runner authenticate the app up front, and the prompt runs every agent `gh` call with `GH_CONFIG_DIR` unset. Across the 25 job logs that reached the agent, 246 of 246 executed `gh` calls unset it and none used the scoped robot directory, so that login could only fail the job. In those same logs `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` answered `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` on 27 of 27 attempts, the oldest on 2026-08-03, and `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-1-copilot` never did. Two robots over three attempts rotate as `[X, Y, X]`, so the healthy one gets a single attempt when the shuffle puts the dead one first, and one transient GraphQL 503 there fails the job. This removes that login and its temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR` from the Codex attempt, so it runs on the app identity it already used and retries serve agent failures. `_run_copilot_once` keeps its login, which the Copilot CLI does use. New `ci/tests/test_copilot_review_codex_auth.py`: 5 tests fail on the current code with the error above and pass here; the 2 pinning unchanged behaviour were verified by mutating the code they pin. No secret, process or sleep involved. Out of scope: `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` still needs rotating operationally (`--copilot` would still need it); and 8 further failures that window are a separate defect, `gh api -X PATCH` on `issues/comments/<id>` returning 503 after its retries. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115232&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115232](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115232+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: PromQL histogram_count/histogram_sum over native histograms
signal.text: ## Summary Second slice of Prometheus native-histogram support for the `TimeSeries` engine (PromQL evaluation), building on the storage layer of #115685. Today `histogram_count`/`histogram_sum` over a native-histogram series are not implemented at all; this PR adds the end-to-end path: - **Selector + resample**: a `TimeSeries` selector over a histogram-enabled storage now produces a combined grid carrying the float arm (`values`), the histogram arm (`histogram_values`, one payload tuple per step), and a `sample_kinds` precedence oracle (`timeSeriesLastToGrid` over the sample kind). New aggregate `timeSeriesHistogramLastToGrid` resamples the histogram arm onto the query grid with the usual staleness window. - **Mixed-type instant precedence**: instant evaluation returns the newest sample of *either* type per series, matching Prometheus. The resample keeps the per-slot winner's sample and NULLs the loser's; an exact-timestamp tie resolves to the histogram (upstream rejects duplicate timestamps, so no upstream rule exists). - **Functions**: `histogram_count` and `histogram_sum` over native histograms (scalar `timeSeriesHistogramCount`/`timeSeriesHistogramSum` extracting the payload `count`/`sum`), applied per step to series whose newest sample is a histogram; float-only series are skipped, matching upstream. - **HTTP serving**: instant and range responses gain the Prometheus `histogram`/`histograms` JSON shapes, with bucket boundaries reconstructed from the stored schema (exponential + NHCB custom buckets, zero-threshold clamping) and block writers hardened so an all-stale-skipped block can never emit a leading/double comma. Everything stays behind `allow_experimental_time_series_table`. `histogram_quantile`/`histogram_fraction`, `histogram_avg`/`histogram_stddev`/`histogram_stdvar`, range functions (`rate` etc.), and the `warnings`/`infos` envelope are follow-ups. Depends on #115685 (storage); this PR is based on current master and will shrink to just the engine slice once #115685 merges. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL `histogram_count` and `histogram_sum` over stored Prometheus native histograms, and serves them in the HTTP query API as `histogram`/`histograms` JSON. Instant queries over series mixing float and histogram samples return the newest sample of either type, matching Prometheus. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115685 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115734&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115734](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115734+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Improve canceling queries in nested expression functions in FilterTransform
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103705 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve canceling queries by `KILL QUERY` and Ctrl+C in `clickhouse-client` while a long-running function is evaluated in a filter expression: `FilterTransform` (`WHERE`, including the `FilterSortedStreamByRange` path) and `TotalsHavingTransform` (`HAVING` with `WITH TOTALS`) now forward cancellation into nested expression functions. This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103705 by @rvasin (Roman Vasin), whose commits are preserved here — all credit for the feature goes to them. The original branch is in a fork with maintainer edits disabled, so the merge conflicts with `master` and the remaining review feedback could not be pushed there. On top of the original PR, this PR: - Merges `master` and resolves the conflicts (`FailPoint.cpp` failpoint list, `FilterTransform.cpp` includes). - Addresses the two unresolved review threads (the AI review "Request changes" verdict): - `FilterSortedStreamByRange` holds a private `FilterTransform` and calls its `transform` directly, but the pipeline cancels only the outer processor. Now `FilterSortedStreamByRange::onCancel` forwards the cancellation into the inner transform, so `cancelExecution` reaches functions of range-filter predicates from `PartsSplitter`. - `TotalsHavingTransform` evaluated the `HAVING` expression without a cancellation callback, so a long-running function in `HAVING` remained uninterruptible. signal.title: Remove `WasmEdge` in favor of `wasmtime`
signal.text: Removes the `WasmEdge` WebAssembly runtime, leaving `wasmtime` as the only engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime` has been the default and recommended engine, and `WasmEdge` was only reachable by explicitly setting `webassembly_udf_engine` to `wasmedge`. Keeping a second implementation of `IWasmEngine` alive costs a vendored C++ submodule (plus `spdlog`, which nothing else in the tree used), a second engine backend to maintain, and CI lanes configured to switch the server over to it. What is removed: - The `contrib/wasmedge` submodule and `contrib/wasmedge-cmake`, along with `contrib/spdlog`, which existed only to build `WasmEdge`. - `src/Interpreters/WebAssembly/WasmEdgeRuntime.{h,cpp}`, the `USE_WASMEDGE` build option and its `system.build_options` row. - `IWasmEngine::requiresFuelSpecialization`, which existed only to distinguish `WasmEdge` (no fuel specialization) from `wasmtime`. The per-fuel-mode module cache is now unconditional. - The `--wasm-engine` option of `tests/config/install.sh` and the `WasmEdge` CI job option, so the affected stateless lanes are renamed: - `amd_msan, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → `amd_msan, {parallel,sequential}` - `amd_llvm_coverage, old analyzer, s3 storage, DBReplicated, WasmEdge, {parallel,sequential}` → the same name without `WasmEdge` `webassembly_udf_engine` is kept as the engine selector; `wasmtime` is now its only accepted value, and any other value is rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` as before. Because `WasmModuleManager` is constructed eagerly during startup (`Server::main` → `Context::setUserScriptsPath` → `Context::initWasmModuleManager`), a server whose config still says `wasmedge` will refuse to start with `Unknown WebAssembly engine 'wasmedge', available engines: 'wasmtime'` rather than fail lazily on first use. Silently aliasing `wasmedge` to `wasmtime` was rejected on purpose: it would be a fallback that hides a stale config. Verified locally on an `aarch64` build: `system.build_options` reports `USE_WASMTIME = 1` with no `USE_WASMEDGE` row; all 23 stateless WebAssembly UDF tests pass (including `04259_wasm_udf_enable_fuel`, which exercises both fuel modes and therefore the module cache path simplified here); and a server configured with `wasmedge` fails startup with the message above. No test coverage is lost. `wasmtime` is disabled under MemorySanitizer (false positives from JIT-generated code), which is why the MSan lanes ran with `WasmEdge` — but every stateless test that executes a WebAssembly module is tagged `no-msan`, so those lanes exercised no WebAssembly UDF code; the option only rewrote the server config. The two `*_ast_json_*` tests that mention `LANGUAGE WASM` only round-trip the query through `parseQueryToJSON` and never instantiate a module. On the coverage lane, those tests now run against `wasmtime` instead of `WasmEdge`. On binaries where `wasmtime` cannot be built, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, `riscv64`, and any `ENABLE_RUST=0` build such as the fast test one, WebAssembly UDF support is now disabled entirely, and it fails close rather than half-working: `Context::initWasmModuleManager` does not construct a `WasmModuleManager` at all, so `system.webassembly_modules` is not attached, persisted `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE WASM` definitions are not loaded at startup, and any attempt to create or use a WebAssembly UDF is rejected with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`. The server itself starts normally, both with a clean config that enables `allow_experimental_webassembly_udf` and with persisted WebAssembly UDF definitions; a warning is written to the log. `05024_wasm_udf_without_wasmtime` asserts this invariant on every lane: `system.webassembly_modules` exists exactly when `USE_WASMTIME` is set and the setting is enabled, and `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE WASM` fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` otherwise. The `wasmedge` mentions left in `docs/reference/settings/server-settings/settings/other.mdx` and in the localized `docs/<locale>/` trees are generated output and are refreshed by the docs autogeneration workflow. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Removed the `WasmEdge` engine for WebAssembly UDFs. `wasmtime`, which has always been the default, is now the only supported value of the `webassembly_udf_engine` server setting. A server configured with `<webassembly_udf_engine>wasmedge</webassembly_udf_engine>` will not start; remove that setting or set it to `wasmtime`. On binaries where `wasmtime` is unavailable, including MemorySanitizer, `arm_v80compat`, and `riscv64`, WebAssembly UDFs are not available at all: the server still starts, but `system.webassembly_modules` is absent and any attempt to create or use a WebAssembly UDF fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115316&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115316](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115316+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Decompile JIT-fused functions before serializing a query plan
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115310 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112028 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111893 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a query serialized for distributed execution (`serialize_query_plan = 1`) failing with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` when a lambda body contains `AND` with a comparison constant wider than `UInt8`. Example: `mapExists((k, v) -> k LIKE '%2' AND v < 1000, col)` against a `Distributed` table with `serialize_query_plan = 1` used to throw `Unknown function and(UInt8, less(UInt64, 1000 : UInt16))`. Now it works correctly, and expression compilation stays fully enabled (no performance regression for `compile_expressions`). --- ### Problem `compile_expressions` (JIT) can fuse a sub-expression like `and(less(...))` inside a lambda body into a single `LLVMFunction` node. `LLVMFunction::getName()` (in `Interpreters/ExpressionJIT.cpp`) returns `dag_.dump()` -- a dump of the fused sub-expression, not a real function name. Something like `and(UInt8, less(UInt64, 1000 : UInt16))`. `ActionsDAG::serialize()` writes `node.function_base->getName()` for `FUNCTION` nodes when shipping a query plan for distributed execution. For a normal function that's fine (e.g. `and`), but for a JIT-fused node it writes the dump string instead. The receiving node tries to resolve that string as a function name via `FunctionFactory` and fails with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`. This looks like one of a few independent `serialize_query_plan = 1` round-trip fidelity bugs (see #112028 for a similar issue with `LowCardinality` types, #111893 for a table-resolution issue) -- different root causes, same general area of the feature still having rough edges. ### Fix First pass at this fix just disabled `compile_expressions` whenever `serialize_query_plan = 1`, gating it in `ExpressionActionsSettings`. That's correct but broader than necessary -- it costs JIT-compiled-expression performance for the *whole* query's execution (initiator and every remote shard alike, since `serialize_query_plan` stays true in the settings context throughout), not just for the specific node that needs to cross the wire. This version keeps `compile_expressions` fully enabled everywhere and instead adds `ActionsDAG::decompileFunctions()`, the reverse of the existing `compileFunctions()`: it rebuilds the original, real, resolvable sub-expression from a JIT-fused node's own `CompileDAG`. `CompileDAG::Node` already retains the real `FunctionBasePtr` for each fused sub-function plus their connectivity (`arguments`, index-based), so this is a faithful reconstruction, not a re-derivation. `serialize()` now clones the DAG and calls `decompileFunctions()` on the clone before writing it out, whenever any node is JIT-compiled -- the original (still fused, fast to execute locally) DAG is left untouched for actual execution. ### Testing - Used a live tracer to confirm `ActionsDAG::serialize()` is exercised by the repro (fires 4 times, matching the lambda's nested capture-DAG serialization). - Used a live tracer to confirm `decompileFunctions()` actually fires when JIT fusion is forced to happen (`compile_expressions = 1`, `min_count_to_compile_expression = 0`) during the repro -- and the query still returns correct results with no error. This proves fusion happened and was correctly reversed for the wire, not merely avoided. - Confirmed `serialize_query_plan = 0` still JIT-compiles normally (unaffected either way, since `ExpressionActionsSettings` no longer reads `serialize_query_plan` at all). - Added `tests/queries/0_stateless/04927_serialize_query_plan_lambda_jit.sql` covering the repro, the aggressive-JIT-settings variant (deterministically forces fusion via `min_count_to_compile_expression = 0`), and the `serialize_query_plan = 0` negative control. Please review, happy to make changes if needed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115439&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115439](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115439+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add memory-pressure-adaptive read sizing to the experimental ReaderExecutor
signal.text: Brings the `MemoryPressureMonitor` from the ReaderExecutor redesign to master as a self-contained, experimental slice (gated by the existing experimental `ReaderExecutor`). The monitors form a hierarchy that mirrors the memory-tracker chain — global (server total) ← per-user ← per-query — each classifying its scope's pressure into four levels with a snap-up / sticky-cooldown state machine and escalating against its parent. The executor samples the level once per read window and shrinks its window and block size under pressure, floored at `MIN_READER_EXECUTOR_SIZE` (128 KiB). Thresholds are three shared server-wide settings, validated and applied on startup and on `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG` (a reload takes effect on the next sample). Also raises the default `reader_executor_window_size` to 8 MiB. Prefetch-aware sizing is deferred to the later prefetch/scheduler slice. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `ReaderExecutor` now shrinks its read window and block size under memory pressure, configured via `reader_executor_memory_pressure_{elevated,high,critical}_level_pct`; its default read window is now 8 MiB. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115635&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115635](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115635+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add --dump-schema option to clickhouse-client and clickhouse-local
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/60681 Adds a `--dump-schema[=<db1,db2,...>]` option that dumps `CREATE DATABASE`/`CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE DICTIONARY`/`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`/`CREATE VIEW` statements for one or more databases, or all non-system user databases if no value is given, to stdout, then exits — similar to `pg_dump --schema-only`. Tables are ordered (via `TablesDependencyGraph`, the same class `DatabaseCatalog` uses to load tables at startup and backups use to order their restore; ties within a level broken by `(database, name)` for determinism) using every dependency signal `system.tables` exposes, combined: `loading_dependencies_*` (dictionaries), inverted `dependencies_*` (a materialized view's source — recorded only on the source row, not the view), `target_database`/`target_table` (a materialized view's `TO` target, explicit or implicit), and — since the server tracks none of this for plain views at all (`DROP TABLE` on a view's source succeeds even with the view still referencing it) — a best-effort scan of each view's stored, server-formatted `SELECT` text for other dumped tables' names. A genuine dependency cycle is a clear error rather than being silently reordered. This is entirely a client-side feature: `system.tables.create_table_query` and `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` already give the server-computed DDL text, so no server-side or wire-protocol changes are needed — the new code (`src/Client/SchemaDumper.{h,cpp}`) just issues a couple of queries over the existing connection (same pattern as `Suggest.cpp`) and prints the results in dependency order. `--dump-schema` also accepts a comma-separated database list (`--dump-schema=db1,db2`), and two modifiers: - `--dump-schema-exclude=db1,db2` dumps all user databases except the listed ones (rejected if combined with an explicit database list — the two are mutually exclusive ways of selecting the same thing). - `--dump-schema-dir=<path>` writes one `<database>.sql` file per dumped database into that directory (created if it doesn't exist, e.g. `mkdir clickhouse-lab && clickhouse-client --dump-schema --dump-schema-exclude=... --dump-schema-dir=clickhouse-lab`) instead of writing everything to stdout. Database names are escaped with `escapeForFileName` before being used as filenames; two target databases whose escaped names collide case-insensitively are rejected unconditionally (regardless of the destination filesystem's actual case sensitivity — reliably probing that portably isn't worth it when the point of a dump is to be replayed somewhere else later anyway), rather than one silently overwriting the other's file. Per-database write failures are detected instead of reported as success, and when a table in one dumped database depends on a table in another, the files (and their confirmation lines) are ordered — and a note printed — so replaying them in the printed order works; a database-level circular dependency (distinct from, and not implied by, a table-level cycle) is rejected with a clear error since no file order could satisfy it. A few things worth calling out for review: - Implicit materialized-view storage tables are excluded from the dump (recreated automatically by their owning `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` statement) — but only when confirmed to be a *live* materialized view's own target with the generated-name shape (`.inner_id.*`/`.inner.*`), not merely name-shaped like one, so a real user table literally named `` `.inner.foo` `` stays in the dump. Orphaned mid-refresh leftovers (`.tmp.inner_id.*`/`.tmp.inner.*`) are filtered by name, since they're never any live target. - `--dump-schema` forces non-interactive mode (like `--query`/`--queries-file`) and is rejected if combined with either of them, so its stdout is never mixed with an interactive banner, warnings, or another query's output. For `clickhouse-local`, it's also rejected combined with `--file`/`--structure`. `--dump-schema-exclude`/`--dump-schema-dir` are rejected if `--dump-schema` itself isn't given — all validated in `processConfig()`, before `connect()`, so a plain argument mistake fails fast instead of after a connection attempt (which could otherwise block on an interactive password prompt). - Verified end-to-end via real replays into a fresh `clickhouse-local` instance: a source table with a materialized view (implicit storage), a dictionary, a plain view, a view-on-view chain, and an explicit `TO` target, named so that alphabetical order alone would produce an unreplayable dump without the fix; single/list/exclude/all-databases selection; `--dump-schema-dir` output with a genuine cross-database dependency; the case-insensitive filename collision guard (using a case-sensitive APFS volume to stand in for a Linux source, confirming both that `Foo`/`foo` coexist there and that the guard fires when dumping them); and all the rejection cases (unknown database, combined with `--query`/`--file`/`--structure`, list + exclude together, dir without `--dump-schema`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `--dump-schema[=<db1,db2,...>]` option to `clickhouse-client` and `clickhouse-local` that dumps `CREATE DATABASE`/`CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE DICTIONARY`/`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`/`CREATE VIEW` statements for the given database(s), or all user databases if no value is given, to stdout in dependency order, then exits — similar to `pg_dump --schema-only`. `--dump-schema-exclude=<db1,db2,...>` skips the listed databases when dumping all of them, and `--dump-schema-dir=<path>` writes one `<database>.sql` file per dumped database into that directory instead of stdout. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114098&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114098](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114098+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `max_rows` setting for databases
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109355 Adds a `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases: a ceiling on active MergeTree rows counted toward the database limit. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition-import/move operations. A batch `INSERT` may overshoot, and the next `INSERT` throws `TOO_MANY_ROWS`. Enforcement is a best-effort snapshot check, not a reservation spanning the commit: concurrent operations may each observe free headroom and transiently overshoot the limit together; the next checked operation then fails. On replicated attach paths the limit is charged only for parts that ZooKeeper actually accepts: an `ATTACH` deduplicated by its block id stays a no-op even when the database is over the limit, and a partially duplicated `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` pays only for the accepted remainder. The counted total is exposed through the nullable `system.databases.rows` column. It intentionally excludes engines that do not participate in `max_rows` accounting. The setting can be changed at runtime with `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_rows = N`; its default value, `0`, is unlimited. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add the `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases, limiting active MergeTree rows counted across a database. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition imports as a best-effort snapshot check, is reconfigurable via `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING`, and is exposed through `system.databases.rows`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111166&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111166](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111166+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: PromQL rate/increase/delta/idelta/irate over native histograms
signal.text: ## Summary Fifth slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115736. Adds the rate family — `rate`, `increase`, `delta`, `idelta`, `irate` — over stored native histograms, reset-aware and faithful to upstream `extrapolatedRate` + `histogramRate`: - **Arithmetic kernel** (`TimeSeriesHistogramKernel.h`): a decoded in-memory float histogram porting upstream `FloatHistogram` field-for-field — `sub`/`add` (with schema reconciliation and NHCB custom-bucket-bound reconciliation), `copyToSchema`, `mul`/`div`, `compact`, and the full `detectReset` (counter-reset hint short-circuits, count/schema/zero-threshold/zero-count rules, per-bucket comparison). The exponential-bound table moves here as a shared header-inline constant. - **Aggregates** `timeSeriesHistogram{Rate,Increase,Delta,InstantRate,InstantDelta}ToGrid`: per grid window, collect the histogram samples, reduce the last to the minimum schema, subtract the first, re-add the previous sample on each detected reset, and extrapolate to the window boundaries (`durationToStart`/`durationToEnd` clamping, counter zero-point clamp); `rate` additionally divides by the range seconds. `irate`/`idelta` use the two newest samples without extrapolation. - **Converter**: the five functions over the histogram arm produce the result histogram into `histogram_values`. A window mixing float and histogram samples drops the element on both arms, matching upstream's `MixedFloatsHistograms` rule. Over a subquery, each arm is resampled from the inner grid masked by `sample_kinds`. - **Upstream-parity details**: `delta` keeps `min(first, last)` schema and does not drop over a custom-bucket middle sample (the scan is counter-only upstream); the instant path drops a mixed exponential/custom newest pair rather than throwing. Also fixes two unrelated pre-existing bugs: PromQL regex matchers were anchored `^<pattern>$` without grouping (so `^n|g$` meant `(^n)|(g$)`), now anchored `^(...)$`; and a self-cycle in `fromSelector`'s table-expression AST. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL `rate`, `increase`, `delta`, `idelta`, and `irate` over stored Prometheus native histograms, with upstream-compatible counter-reset handling and range extrapolation. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115685 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115734 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115735 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115736 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115860&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115860](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115860+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: PromQL histogram_quantile/histogram_fraction over native histograms
signal.text: ## Summary Fourth slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115735. Adds native `histogram_quantile` and `histogram_fraction`, faithful to upstream, and fixes two cross-slice defects: - **`histogram_quantile` (native)**: a new native branch of the existing applier (scalar `timeSeriesHistogramQuantile(histogram, phi)`), UNION ALL'd with the untouched classic-bucket branch. Faithful to upstream `HistogramQuantile`: out-of-range/NaN phi and `count = 0` short-circuits, forward/reverse iterator choice by `phi` (and NaN sum), rank walk over non-empty buckets, zero-bucket single-sided natural bounds, custom-bucket `-Inf`/`+Inf` short-circuits, and linear (custom / zero bucket) vs log-scale (exponential, with negative mirroring) interpolation. - **`histogram_fraction` (native)**: new applier (scalar `timeSeriesHistogramFraction(histogram, lower, upper)`), mirroring upstream `HistogramFraction` — the per-bucket rank walk with linear/exponential `FractionBelow` interpolation, `±Inf` bound handling, and `(upperRank - lowerRank) / count`. Classic-bucket `histogram_fraction` does not exist in ClickHouse and is a separate upstream task (issue #114704), so float-only input returns an empty result, consistent with the other native-histogram functions. - **Fix — `last_over_time` over a subquery on a histogram-enabled storage**: the combined grid was passed through unchanged, so an instant query threw and a range query silently returned the inner matrix on the wrong steps — for every series, including pure-float ones. Each grid arm is now resampled onto the aggregation grid via `timeSeriesFromGrid` (the histogram arm through the `-Array` combinator). - **Fix — float-only series in native-histogram functions**: `histogram_count`/`sum`/`avg`/`stddev`/`stdvar` kept float-only groups as all-NULL rows, which were still counted by the duplicate-series check after the `__name__` drop — a colliding float-only series failed the whole query where upstream skips it. They are now filtered with `has(sample_kinds, 1)`, matching the quantile/fraction appliers. Based on current master; the diff shrinks to just this slice as #115685, #115734, and #115735 merge. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL `histogram_quantile` (with native interpolation) and `histogram_fraction` over stored Prometheus native histograms, alongside the classic-bucket `histogram_quantile`. Also fixes `last_over_time` over a subquery on a histogram-enabled storage. signal.title: PromQL histogram_avg/histogram_stddev/histogram_stdvar over native histograms
signal.text: ## Summary Third slice of Prometheus native-histogram support (PromQL evaluation), building on #115734. Adds `histogram_avg`, `histogram_stddev`, and `histogram_stdvar` over native histograms, faithful to upstream: - **Bucket helpers, one source of truth**: the span expansion and exponential-bound reconstruction used by the HTTP JSON writer are moved into `TimeSeriesNativeHistograms` and shared with the new functions. `getHistogramBoundExponential` is made bit-identical to Prometheus by porting upstream's `exponentialBounds` table verbatim (schemas 0-8), including its last-ulp deviations from the exactly-rounded values — so bucket boundaries and everything derived from them match Prometheus bit-for-bit, which the upcoming conformance testing relies on. Overflow handling also matches upstream exactly (MaxFloat64 only for the last regular bucket, +Inf beyond). - **`histogram_avg`** = `sum / count`, no special-casing (0/0 → NaN), matching upstream. - **`histogram_stddev` / `histogram_stdvar`**: variance is estimated from bucket representative values exactly as upstream — arithmetic mean for custom (NHCB) buckets, zero for the zero bucket, geometric mean (mirrored for negatives) for exponential buckets — accumulated with Kahan-Neumaier summation, then `variance / count`; stddev takes the square root. - **Lexer**: the PromQL grammar gains the three function tokens and the checked-in generated lexer is regenerated (only the serialized ATN and token table change). Series whose newest sample at a step is a float are skipped per step; float-only series are excluded from the result, matching upstream. Based on current master; the diff shrinks to just this slice as #115685 and #115734 merge. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `TimeSeries` engine can now evaluate PromQL `histogram_avg`, `histogram_stddev`, and `histogram_stdvar` over stored Prometheus native histograms, with bucket boundaries computed bit-identically to Prometheus. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115685 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115734 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115735&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115735](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115735+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/labels
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/labels`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus-compatible clients** use **`/api/v1/labels`** to discover the label names available in matching series. This is useful for **Grafana dashboards**, variable pickers, and integrations that need to build label selectors without fetching every series first. The endpoint follows the same **logical label model** as the series endpoint. It reads labels stored in the **`tags` Map** and in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/labels` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint returns a **sorted, distinct list of label names**. It includes **`__name__`** when at least one matching series exists and supports both **unfiltered discovery** and filtering by matching series. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** filters the series used to build the label-name list. Repeated selectors are combined as a **union**. - **`start` and `end`** restrict the matching series by their **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the returned label names and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Label discovery:** collect distinct names from the canonical metric name, the **`tags` Map**, and configured dedicated tag columns. - **Selector support:** reuse the Prometheus series-selector and matcher behavior from **`/api/v1/series`**. - **Storage compatibility:** support both normal TimeSeries storage and **`tags_to_columns`** layouts while preserving the logical label set. - **Repeated selectors:** combine repeated **`match[]`** parameters without returning duplicate label names. - **Time ranges:** apply trusted min/max bounds when available and keep ranged requests valid with the **approximate superset** behavior allowed by Prometheus when bounds are unavailable. - **Result limits:** support empty, zero, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values, including the Prometheus truncation warning. - **HTTP handling:** support the dedicated endpoint and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**, with endpoint parameters kept separate from ClickHouse settings. - **Access control:** enforce the configured **`TimeSeries` table authorization boundary** before reading the underlying target tables. - **Query lifecycle:** execute through the **normal query pipeline**, preserve query completion handling, and record the request in **`query_log`**. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Label collection:** distinct names, sorted output, **`__name__`**, Map labels, and dedicated columns. - **Selectors:** metric filters, label filters, repeated **`match[]`** unions, and requests with no matching series. - **Time ranges:** matching and non-matching intervals, including empty optional parameters. - **Limits:** truncation warnings and the **`limit`** parameter behavior. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants** on the configured `TimeSeries` table. - **Observability:** successful requests recorded as **`QueryFinish`** entries. - **Shared behavior:** the related Prometheus query and series API regression coverage. Also ran **Python syntax checks**, **XML parsing**, and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now describes the `/api/v1/labels` handler and its supported parameters. ### Stack This PR is **stacked on #114867** and includes the **`/api/v1/series`** changes. After **#114867** merges, this branch can be rebased onto `master`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114868&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114868](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114868+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
