signal.title: Weigh the adaptive aggregation's thaw by staged bytes and add the freeze-bytes and bucket top-K settings
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111459 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115480 The behavioral half of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115480, split out so it can merge independently of the restructuring: one behavioral improvement to the adaptive aggregation's thaw, two new settings, and a latent initialization bug fix. ### The thaw verdict is weighted by bytes The thaw previously fired on the staged stream's repeat factor alone (> 12). That misses streams that repeat keys only a few times but drag wide payloads with every staged record. The verdict is now *wasted staged bytes per distinct key*: `(repeat factor − 1) × bytes per record > 300` — a key's first record is the price of storing-it-once; every repeat is bytes the baseline would have absorbed as an in-place update. Near-unique streams measure ~0 by construction and cannot fire; heavy-column streams stand down early in proportion to the damage. Only the keys and the variable-width argument columns count toward a record's bytes. Fixed-width arguments are deliberately excluded: the drain applies them with the same batch executor the scan would have used, so their staging costs about what their consumption saves — a five-`UInt64`-argument stream at repeat 10 stays engaged and is a clear adaptive win, while a bare repeat rule (or counting its fixed bytes) would thaw it away. Measured on `hits` (100M) (off → on, 16/64 threads): - `SELECT URL, min(Title) GROUP BY URL` (90-byte string key): 0.83×/0.73× → **0.99×/1.01×** - `SELECT UserID, min(URL) GROUP BY UserID` (heavy argument, +121% peak RSS before): 0.83×/0.59× → **0.97×/1.00×**, peak RSS 14.5 → 6.3 GB (matching the ordinary path) - Full ClickBench `GROUP BY` sweep within noise; winning shapes unchanged. ### New settings - **`adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes`** (default 4 MiB): the byte twin of the key-count freeze threshold — a thread's local table freezes at whichever bound is reached first. Measured as the local table's own allocated bytes (hash-table buffer plus arenas), checked between blocks like the baseline's conversion thresholds; deliberately not the query-wide tracked memory, which would freeze all the locals off each other's growth. At the default it is a guardrail: calibration on the heaviest shapes shows ordinary tables keep freezing by key count (e.g. `WatchID, min(URL)`: 14 of 16 locals unchanged, two freeze earlier by bytes, at 15582 and 8192 keys), and a full ClickBench `GROUP BY` sweep of default vs `0` is noise (geomeans 1.001 / 1.007 at 16 / 64 threads). The plan-serialization side rides version 7, since all the adaptive settings ship in the same release. - **`query_plan_aggregation_bucket_top_k`** (default true): a dedicated toggle for the bucket top-K conversion, which previously could only be disabled together with every plan rewrite via `query_plan_enable_optimizations`. The contract is worded generally (`ORDER BY` over the aggregation's outputs with `LIMIT n`, gated on provable exactness) so the planned generalization beyond the lone `count()` and a single sort column extends the rule, not the setting. The pushed flag is now visible in `EXPLAIN actions = 1` (`Bucket top-K: n ascending|descending`), which also makes the rewrite observable and testable. ### HashTable Statistics Adaptive Aggregator no longer uses previous run hash tables sizes to resize it's small buffer tables. First, buffer tables are very small so any save in runtime is negligible. Second, if buffer table is resized above `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes`, it will freeze after first block instead storing all frequent keys eventually. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The adaptive `GROUP BY` aggregation (`enable_adaptive_aggregator`) now measures whether deferring rare keys pays off and returns to the ordinary algorithm when their keys or aggregate arguments are too wide to copy profitably, so aggregations over heavy string columns (e.g. `min(URL)` per user) run at the ordinary algorithm's speed and memory. Adds `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes` to bound each thread's frozen table in bytes (whichever of it and the key-count threshold is reached first freezes the table), and `query_plan_aggregation_bucket_top_k` to toggle the top-N aggregation optimization. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115755&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115755](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115755+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Skip writing all-default columns during MergeTree INSERT
signal.text: ## Summary During MergeTree INSERT, columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (e.g., all zeros for `UInt64`, all empty strings for `String`, all `NULL`s for `Nullable`) are detected and excluded from the part's column list before constructing `MergedBlockOutputStream`. This avoids writing unnecessary `.bin` files (Wide parts) or data streams (Compact parts), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads where most columns in each INSERT are left at their type's default. The optimization is opt-in via the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (off by default). It additionally requires `serialization_info_version` to be set to `with_missing_columns` (the format version that records frozen defaults for missing columns), so that a cluster pinned to a lower version for compatibility never writes parts that older servers cannot read. The block itself is passed intact to the writer, so skip indices, projections, primary index, and min-max index are all computed from the full data. Reading a part that lacks a column fills it with type-defaults automatically — the same mechanism used by `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on existing parts. To keep reads stable, a structured `missing_columns` array is recorded in the part's `serialization.json` (a new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` serialization-info version). Each entry carries the column name and a `type_default` marker. On read, `fillMissingColumns` consults this marker and fills a missing column with its type-default even if the column later gains a new `DEFAULT` expression, so that a subsequent `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the values that were actually inserted. The marker is propagated through merges, mutations, and on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN`, so the inserted type-defaults survive part-lifecycle operations. The `MissingColumnInfo` struct also reserves a `DefaultKind::Expression` variant for future use (issue #92475: `ALTER MODIFY DEFAULT` freezes old expression into parts). This PR only writes `type_default` markers; reading an `expression` marker throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` to fail closed until Phase 2 implements expression evaluation. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/4968, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92475 **On-disk format (`serialization.json`):** ```json { "missing_columns": [ { "name": "b", "default": "type_default" } ], "version": 2 } ``` **Changes:** - Add MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` (default `false`). - Add `IColumn::hasOnlyTypeDefaults` with optimized overrides for `ColumnVector`/`ColumnDecimal` (`memoryIsZero`), `ColumnString`/`ColumnArray` (zero offsets), `ColumnNullable` (all-`1` null map), `ColumnSparse` (no stored non-default values), and `ColumnTuple` (delegates to sub-columns). - Filter all-default columns in `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` (`skipEmptyColumnsOnInsert`). Columns with a `DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED`/`ALIAS` expression are never skipped. A column is skipped only when `IDataType::getDefault()` coincides with the column's zero representation (`isDefaultAt(0)` on a column filled via `getDefault()`), which correctly excludes types like `Date32` (type-default 1900-01-01 ≠ memory-zero) and `Enum` (first declared value ≠ 0). Patch parts are excluded, and at least one physical column is always kept. - Gate the optimization on `serialization_info_version >= with_missing_columns`. The populating step is authoritative about the part format version, so `SerializationInfoByName::getVersion` never silently upgrades a part past the configured value (which would make older servers reject it during a rolling upgrade). - Record the missing columns in `serialization.json` via `SerializationInfoByName` (new `WITH_MISSING_COLUMNS` version). Only `type_default` markers are written; `expression` markers are rejected on read until Phase 2. The list is written in sorted order so that identical parts produce identical checksums on different replicas. - Propagate the missing-columns marker through the part lifecycle: through merges (`MergeTask`, for columns that end up absent from the merged part), through mutations (`MutateTask::getColumnsForNewDataPart`, including renames of missing columns), through compact-part renames (`splitAndModifyMutationCommands`), and through on-the-fly `ALTER RENAME COLUMN` on read (`IMergeTreeReader::fillMissingColumns` translates the requested name back through `alter_conversions`). - Add a stateless test with 46 cases covering: basic skip; all-default keeps one column; merges (horizontal and vertical); mutation; `Nullable`; key columns; `DEFAULT` expression not skipped; `Array`; `Tuple`; `ColumnSparse` source; compact parts; `LowCardinality`; stable values across `ALTER ... DEFAULT`; a non-zero-default `Enum`; marker across mutation/merge/rename after `ALTER DEFAULT`; version gate; DETACH/ATTACH TABLE; DETACH/ATTACH PARTITION; BACKUP/RESTORE; FREEZE; CHECK TABLE; MATERIALIZE COLUMN; CLEAR COLUMN; lightweight DELETE; chained mutations; INSERT SELECT; REPLACE PARTITION; ATTACH PARTITION FROM; ALTER ADD/DROP COLUMN; projections; FixedString; Map; mixed parts merge; Date/DateTime; pre-ADD-COLUMN + skip merge; type-changing mutation; compact-part rename+mutation; Date32 regression. - Add an integration test (`test_skip_empty_columns`) with 6 cases: replicated consistency; merge marker propagation across replicas; mixed-version version gate; backward-compat fallback for old parts; restart durability; REPLACE PARTITION across replicated tables. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): MergeTree INSERT can now skip writing columns whose values are entirely type-defaults (zeros, empty strings, `NULL`s), saving disk space for sparse-update workloads. Enabled by the MergeTree setting `skip_empty_columns_on_insert` together with `serialization_info_version = 'with_missing_columns'`. Missing columns carry frozen defaults in `serialization.json`, so a later `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN ... DEFAULT` does not retroactively change the inserted values. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is not required (bug fix, no new user-facing feature) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=98472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/98472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F98472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: UNIQUE KEY accepts a subcolumn, making the table permanently un-insertable
signal.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong A `UNIQUE KEY` element that names a **subcolumn** (`` `c.1` ``, `` `c.null` ``, `` `c.keys` ``, ...) is accepted at `CREATE TABLE`, but every `INSERT` into the resulting table then fails with: ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column c1.1 in block. There are only columns: c0, c1, c2, c3, c4. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` The table is otherwise healthy — it persists across restart, `SELECT` works, `DROP` works — it just can never be written to. Since `UNIQUE KEY` cannot be altered, the only remedy is to recreate the table. This is the exact failure mode the DDL guard added in #107986 was written to prevent. Its comment says so verbatim (`registerStorageMergeTree.cpp`): > Reject expression-style elements at parse time: runtime consumers look up keys via > `block.getByName(<column name>)`, so an expression-style UK passes DDL but crashes the first INSERT. Subcolumns slip past that guard through a three-step gap: 1. **Backticks change the parse.** Bare `c.1` parses as `Function tupleElement(c, 1)` and is correctly rejected as expression-style. Backticked `` `c.1` `` is a plain `ASTIdentifier` whose *name* is the string `"c.1"`, so `is_plain_identifier` accepts it. 2. **`reject_non_physical` looks in the wrong index.** It tests `metadata.columns.has(name) && !hasPhysical(name)`, but `ColumnsDescription::has` searches only the top-level column index; subcolumns live in a separate `subcolumns` index reached via `hasSubcolumn`. So `has("c.1")` is `false` and the check short-circuits. 3. **The fallback assumption does not hold.** The guard's comment ends with *"A name that matches no column at all (not physical, not virtual) is left for `getKeyFromAST` (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)."* But a subcolumn name is not "no column at all" to the `TreeRewriter` — it resolves fine, so `unique_key.column_names` becomes `["c.1", ...]` and no error is raised. At `INSERT`, `SSTIndexWriter::write` does `block.getByName("c.1")` against a block that contains only physical columns → `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. Found by BuzzHouse. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on `master` — version `26.8.1.1154`, commit `59f0c881f8088762625627e14a0434d8db966566`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`. Deterministic. ## How to reproduce Run Fiddle: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/fcb27b57-281c-4b90-81ca-65ea02c2790e Five subcolumn families reach the same end state: | UNIQUE KEY element | column type | result | | --- | --- | --- | | `` `c.1` `` | `Tuple(String)` | `Not found column c.1 in block` | | `` `c.x` `` | `Tuple(x String)` | `Not found column c.x in block` | | `` `c.null` `` | `Nullable(String)` | `Not found column c.null in block` | | `` `c.size0` `` | `Array(Int32)` | `Not found column c.size0 in block` | | `` `c.keys` `` | `Map(String, String)` | `Not found column c.keys in block` | The neighbouring cases are all rejected correctly at `CREATE`, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a deliberate allowance: | UNIQUE KEY element | result | | --- | --- | | `c.1` (no backticks) | Code 36 — "Expression-style elements ... are not yet supported" | | `` `nosuch` `` | Code 47 — missing column | | `` `_part` `` | Code 36 — "virtual columns ... are not allowed" | | `` `c.a` `` on a `JSON` column | Code 549 — rejected by the key-expression type check | A `Nested` subcolumn such as `n.x` is unaffected: it is a genuine top-level physical column, so `has()` finds it and the guard behaves. ## Expected behaviour `CREATE TABLE` rejects a subcolumn in `UNIQUE KEY` with a clear `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, in line with the existing rejections for virtual / `ALIAS` / `EPHEMERAL` / expression-style elements — rather than producing a table that accepts no writes. ## Suggested fix One check next to the existing virtual-column check in `reject_non_physical` (`src/Storages/MergeTree/registerStorageMergeTree.cpp`): ```cpp if (!metadata.columns.has(name) && metadata.columns.hasSubcolumn(GetColumnsOptions::All, name)) throw Exception(ErrorCodes::BAD_ARGUMENTS, "UNIQUE KEY column `{}` is a subcolumn; UNIQUE KEY must name whole stored columns", name); ``` The leading `!metadata.columns.has(name)` keeps real `Nested` columns working, and placing the check before `getKeyFromAST` preserves the existing `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` path for names that match nothing at all. `GetColumnsOptions` is not currently referenced in that file, so this may need `#include <Storages/ColumnsDescription.h>`. If subcolumn keys are meant to be supported eventually, the alternative is to resolve the key expression into the block on the write path instead of rejecting it — but the interim guard's own stated contract ("only bare column names are allowed") argues for rejecting now. ## Additional context Related, same feature, both distinct from this: #110854 (`ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` on a UNIQUE KEY table rewrites metadata before validation and poisons startup) and #104963 (inconsistent AST formatting with `UNIQUE KEY`). Umbrella: #103486.

signal.title: Sort release branches by version, not lexically
signal.text: `_release_branches()` sorts the open `release`-labeled PR head branches as plain strings, so once a minor version reaches two digits the ordering is wrong — e.g. `25.10` sorts before `25.9`. It's benign in `auto_release_job.py`'s current per-branch loop (every branch is processed regardless of order), but any newest-first consumer would pick the wrong branch. Sort by a numeric `(major, minor, …)` key via a small `_branch_version_key` helper. Flagged by the review bot on #113528 (its `_select_patch_dry_run_ref` relies on newest-first order); fixing the ordering at the source here. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113528 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115842&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115842](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115842+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not report "Server died" for a signal-killed run with no failure
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106183 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description A functional-test job synthesizes a `Server died` failure whenever the test command dies from a signal, so an externally killed run reads as a crash nobody observed. On PR #108676 / `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)` the report read `Failed: 0, Passed: 10564, Skipped: 171` with `Server died` as the only failure, while the artifacts show the server answering `system flush logs` after the kill and stopping cleanly under `--do-not-kill`. As of 2026-08-21, 74 jobs across 41 PRs plus 3 master jobs carry this leaf alone in the preceding 30 days. Root cause: `ABORTED_RUN_EXIT_CODES` mixes `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE`, where the parent observed a reason to stop, with the kill-by-signal codes, which establish only that the run was killed, never by whom, and labels both `Server died`. So when the exit code is a kill-by-signal one and no failure was parsed, emit a `Test command killed by signal` leaf instead. `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE` stays excluded; a parsed failure is unchanged. The leaf is `ERROR`, the job result stays `FAIL`. `ERROR` on the leaf because `invert_bugfix_validation_status` flips any `FAIL` row to `OK` without reading its name, turning an exit code into a claimed reproduction; its guard is per-row, and `reconcile_bugfix_crash_repro` still downgrades that row on a `BLOCKER` fatal, so a real crash keeps validating (#105789). `FAIL` on the job result because `is_error` disables coverage collection for the whole job. Validated by 8 new unit tests (11 cases, one parameterized over all four exit code encodings), each load-bearing under mutation, taking the suite from 13 to 24 cases with the existing ones unchanged. The three job shapes carrying this signature were also driven against the pre-fix parser: job result, coverage gate and `pipeline_status` all match. Note `check_ci.can_process` skips `ERROR` rows, so a CIDB sweep needs `test_status IN ('FAIL','ERROR')`.

signal.title: Warn on low sccache hit rate in build job
signal.text: The CI build job runs `sccache --show-stats` after every build, but the hit rate was only printed to the raw job log — a degraded or stale compiler cache that silently turned a build nearly cold was invisible in the CI report. This adds a non-blocking workflow warning when the post-build sccache hit rate is below 40%, so a low-hit cache is surfaced for investigation without blocking merge, as requested in the issue. The rate is parsed from `sccache --show-stats --stats-format json`. Builds with no cached compilations (cold cache) and cache-warmup builds, whose hit rate is expected to be near zero, are skipped, and any parsing failure is non-fatal so the check can never fail an already-green build. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/46502 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115823&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115823](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115823+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Re-land: make Ctrl+C terminate the output of a result set in the client promptly
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/22426 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106430 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107845 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107828 ### Description This re-lands #106430 ("Make Ctrl+C terminate the output of a result set in the client promptly"), which was reverted by #107845, and folds in the data-race fix from the (now closed) #107828 so the feature can land safely this time. Why it was reverted: `BuzzHouse (amd_tsan)` reported a ThreadSanitizer data race on master (STID 5296-4b74) on the client's persistent stdout buffer (`std_out`, an `AutoCanceledWriteBuffer<WriteBufferFromFileDescriptor>`). The interruptible-output feature installed a cancellation hook on `std_out` at the start of `processOrdinaryQuery` and cleared it via `SCOPE_EXIT({ std_out->setCancellationHook({}); })` at the end of the same scope. When the result set is written with parallel formatting, `ParallelFormattingOutputFormat` runs a background collector thread that writes through `std_out` and reads its `cancellation_hook` in `WriteBufferFromFileDescriptor::nextImpl`. On the normal end-of-stream path the collector is joined by `output_format->finalize` before the scope guard runs, so the clear is safe; but on paths that leave `processOrdinaryQuery` by an exception without first finalizing the output (a `NetException`, or a `LocalFormatError` rethrown from `receiveResult`), the scope guard cleared the hook while the collector thread was still alive and reading it — a data race on the `std::function`. The fix (from #107828): the hook is cleared in `resetOutput` right after `output_format.reset()`, which destroys the parallel formatter and joins its collector thread, so the mutation is single-threaded with respect to `std_out`'s hook. The hook is also re-pointed for the teardown flushes that follow: on normal completion the interrupt handler is still armed and is honored, so a fresh Ctrl+C keeps interrupting a flush to a slow or stuck stdout; on exception paths the handler is already stopped (its `cancelled` is then unconditionally true), so the genuine cancellation flag is used instead to avoid discarding already-produced output. `resetOutput` runs on every exit path and at the start of the next query, so `std_out` (which outlives a single query) never carries a stale hook into the next query. The pager and `INTO OUTFILE ... AND STDOUT` buffers are per-query and destroyed in `resetOutput` after the collector join, so they were never affected. The change is split into two commits: the first reapplies #106430 verbatim (a revert of the revert #107845); the second folds in the #107828 fix, confined to `src/Client/ClientBase.cpp`. The low-level `WriteBufferFromFileDescriptor` (used server-wide on a hot single-threaded write path) is unchanged by the fix. Revert that motivated this: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107845 TSAN report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=73e97deb9abbc3258e75d297aabfc3fbe7c3ca5e&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Pressing Ctrl+C in `clickhouse-client`/`clickhouse-local` now promptly stops printing a large result set, even when the output is being written to a slow or stuck destination such as a slow terminal. Previously the first Ctrl+C could appear to have no effect. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108078&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/108078](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F108078+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree on shared storage
signal.text: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage (currently `S3`; `Azure` is implemented but not yet enabled, pending test coverage), enabling active/standby failover without external coordination (no Keeper). Uses conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) on object storage to maintain a lease file with JSON content `{"version":1,"leader_id":"...","timestamp":...}`. The leader renews its lease periodically; followers monitor and claim leadership when the lease expires. New MergeTree settings: - `leader_election` (Bool, default false) — enable leader election - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — lease renewal interval - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — lease expiry threshold; must be at least 3x the heartbeat interval When not the leader, inserts, merges, and DDL are blocked; background data processing is skipped. Mutations are unsupported on the currently enabled `S3` `plain_rewritable` metadata layout, including on the leader. Participating nodes should keep their clocks synchronized (NTP) to within `leader_election_session_timeout`; the conditional-write protocol always prevents split-brain, but excessive clock skew can cause leadership churn. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91613 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `leader_election` setting for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage, enabling active/standby failover using conditional writes without external coordination. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Three new MergeTree-level settings are added: - `leader_election` (Bool) — When enabled on a non-replicated MergeTree table stored on an `S3` object storage disk (`Azure` is implemented but rejected at table creation until it has test coverage), multiple ClickHouse instances sharing the same data path will elect a single leader. Only the leader performs writes and merges. Followers act as read-only replicas and automatically claim leadership when the current leader's lease expires. Mutations are unsupported on the currently enabled `S3` `plain_rewritable` metadata layout, including on the leader. - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — How often the leader renews its lease and followers check for an expired lease. - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — How long a lease remains valid without renewal. Must be at least 3x `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`. Example, using the same UUID and shared `S3` storage policy on each node: ```sql CREATE TABLE shared_table UUID '12345678-abcd-abcd-abcd-123456789abc' (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS storage_policy = 's3', leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; -- On every follower, attach the same table definition with the same UUID. ATTACH TABLE shared_table UUID '12345678-abcd-abcd-abcd-123456789abc' (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS storage_policy = 's3', leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; ``` <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > High risk because it introduces new leader-election coordination and modifies core `MergeTree` write/DDL/drop and catalog cleanup paths; bugs could cause write unavailability or accidental deletion/incorrect visibility on shared storage. > > **Overview** > Adds a **Beta** `leader_election` mode for non-replicated `MergeTree` tables on shared S3/Azure, using a conditional-write lease file to ensure only one instance performs inserts/merges/mutations while followers remain read-only and can take over on failure. > > Introduces new MergeTree settings (`leader_election`, `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`, `leader_election_session_timeout`) with validation, new `MergeTreeLeaderElection*` metrics/events, and follower part-refresh + leader takeover sync to load new parts and advance block counters before enabling writes. > > Hardens destructive operations for shared-storage tables: blocks most `ALTER`/partition-mutation operations and `RENAME` under leader election, gates background processing on leadership, and updates drop/cleanup logic (`dropSkipsDataDirectoryCleanup`, `DatabaseCatalog`/`StorageTableProxy` fail-closed behavior) to avoid recursive deletion or hangs when tables are shared or cannot be materialized. Adds documentation and integration/stateless tests covering failover, metrics, validation, and rejection cases. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 78c1252915ba512bebf94a147932158e1bacecf0. signal.title: Fix materialized CTE gate missing for a reused CTE over Distributed
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113184 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113184 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `LOGICAL_ERROR` "Reading from materialized CTE '...' before its materialization completed - DelayedPortsProcessor gate is missing in the query plan" when a `MATERIALIZED` CTE reads a `Distributed`, `remote()` or `cluster()` table, is filtered by `IN` over another materialized CTE, and is referenced more than once. Closes #113184. ### Description An `IN`-set pipeline built during index analysis runs standalone under its own `CompletedPipelineExecutor`, so no `DelayedPortsProcessor` from another plan gates its readers. Reading a materialized CTE that nothing in that plan materializes then hits the fail-fast check in `MemorySource::generate`. Root cause: a materialized CTE reading a `Distributed`/`remote()` table plans a shard-local plan, where the deeper CTE resolves *by name* to its temporary `StorageMemory`. `isMaterializedCTE()` is then false and the CTE is not yet plan-backed, so `collectMaterializedCTEs` declines to gate it - the arm #108924 added for a read-by-name of a table the initiator owns. That plan later runs standalone, out of reach of the outer gate. Fix: before an in-place build runs a plan, push a `DelayedMaterializingCTEsStep` covering every CTE the plan's node tree reads while no step in that tree materializes it. It becomes the plan root, so its gate dominates every reader in that tree; a CTE already gated in the same tree, already built, or holding no plan is skipped, so the attachment is idempotent and never takes a CTE another plan claimed. Both in-place entry points are covered (`buildSetInplace`, and `buildOrderedSetInplace` on both its clone and destructive branches). No new setting, no default change, no format change. Planning order is untouched, and `Planner.cpp` is byte-identical to master. Attaching the step earlier, at the point where a set subquery's plan is extracted, was measured and does not work: there the CTE holds no plan yet (`has_plan=0` on this reproducer, against a control that reads `1`), so the step would have nothing to carry. <details> <summary>Validation: fresh server per arm, build id and fixture row count asserted before each arm</summary> | arm | before | after | |---|---|---| | reused CTE + `IN` over a deeper CTE, over `remote()` | logical error | correct result | | same, `Distributed` engine | logical error | correct result | | same, non-primary-key filter column | logical error | correct result | | same, `PREWHERE` | logical error | correct result | | same via the `buildSetInplace` route (ordered build declined) | logical error | correct result | | control: plain `MergeTree` | correct result | unchanged | | control: `force_primary_key` (the 03928 shape) | correct result | unchanged | | oracle: `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` sees the set condition | present | present | | its negative control, `use_index_for_in_with_subqueries = 0` | absent | absent | The oracle and its negative control show the index path is still taken rather than silently declined. `04712` fails on the pre-fix binary through the real test runner and passes after, 50 of 50 randomized runs; across 352 `in_subquery` / `prewhere` / `set_index` / `primary_key` tests the failure set is byte-identical before and after. </details> CI carrier: [`AST fuzzer (amd_debug)` on #114375](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114375&sha=0aba0e7d40b0a1755033a9ef4a6a92440b9adb05&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113489&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113489](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113489+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fsync snapshot directory in Keeper to survive power loss
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111339 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a rare Keeper data-loss window on local snapshot disks: the snapshot write path now fsyncs the snapshot directory after removing the `tmp_` marker, so a power loss can no longer drop the marker unlink while keeping the snapshot content. Previously such a crash made Keeper treat a good, fully-synced snapshot as incomplete and delete it on restart, losing acknowledged writes even with `force_sync=true`. Snapshot disks backed by object storage are not covered. ### Description `src/Coordination` never fsynced a directory. Each snapshot write path creates an empty `tmp_snapshot_<name>` marker, writes and fsyncs the snapshot content, then unlinks the marker. The unlink is a directory-entry change, which a file-content fsync does not make durable, so a power loss inside the ext4 journal-commit window can persist the content while losing the unlink. On restart the constructor treats a `snapshot_<idx>` with a surviving sibling `tmp_snapshot_<idx>` as incomplete and deletes both; if the covering changelogs were already compacted, Keeper aborts with `CORRUPTED_DATA`. `removeSnapshotMarker` opens the snapshot directory's sync guard before the unlink and fsyncs it on scope exit, at all three snapshot write sites (`writeSnapshotBufferToFile`, `finalizeSnapshotReceiveToDisk`, `writeSnapshotFile`). The fsync is unconditional, matching the already-unconditional content fsync. Scope, one concern per PR. `getDirectorySyncGuard` is implemented on `DiskLocal` and returns null elsewhere, so a `latest_snapshot_storage_disk` on object storage still removes its marker without a durable directory entry. That belongs in `IDisk`, not in Keeper: nothing under `src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/` fsyncs a metadata directory, and every other caller in the tree is the same no-op. Also out of scope: the constructor cleanup unlinks without a directory fsync, but only on superseded or incomplete files, so a lost unlink self-heals on restart; and cross-disk maintenance moves relocate the latest snapshot while `moveFileBetweenDisks` fsyncs neither the copied content nor its directories, tracked separately. `TestStorageSnapshotDirectoryFsync` asserts the snapshot root holds a live sync guard at the instant each marker is unlinked. Four mutations each fail it: no guard, guard released too early, guard on the wrong directory, null guard. dm-flakey on a snapshot filesystem separate from the log filesystem reproduces the original discard. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111397&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111397](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111397+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Publish column types and serialization hints atomically in ALTER
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a race in `MergeTree`-family tables where an `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` that changes a column's type runs at the same time as a part being committed. The new column type became visible before the table's serialization statistics were rebuilt for it, so the committing part could be mixed into statistics built for the old type. This picked sparse-vs-full encoding from wrong statistics until the `ALTER` finished, and aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` published the new metadata through the lock-free multiversion store and rebuilt `serialization_hints` afterwards, in a *separate* `lockParts()` scope. In that gap a committing part reaches `updateSerializationHintsForPart` with `part_columns` and `storage_columns` both already NEW, so the "structure may change after alter" guard compares NEW against NEW and lets the part through, while the hint it mutates is still OLD-typed. For `String` -> `Tuple(...)` that hint is a base `SerializationInfo` and the part's info a `SerializationInfoTuple`, `structureEquals` is a `typeid` comparison, and the `chassert` fails. The guard compares part against table, so it cannot notice that the *hint* is stale. `MergeTreeData::setPropertiesAndResetSerializationHints` now publishes and swaps the hints in one `parts_lock` scope, the lock the two sides actually share, since a part commit holds it in `Transaction::commit`. It is prepare-then-commit: the metadata clone happens outside the lock, and inside it the new hints are built *before* anything is published, so a throw leaves both unchanged (previously a throw mid-reset could pair new metadata with a cleared aggregate). Five column-type publishes use it, including the replicated `setTableStructure` rollback, so a failed `alterTable` cannot leave old columns with new-typed hints. Settings-, comment- and statistics-only publishes are untouched, as is the assertion. `parts_lock` is hot, but the hints build already ran under it and the clone is kept out, so the net addition is two moves. The non-replicated rollback restoring `old_metadata` keeps plain `setProperties`, because the rejected new settings are still live there. The new test parks an ALTER inside the window with a failpoint and commits an INSERT concurrently. It aborts with the expected assertion on the old ordering, and passes on the fix while observing the INSERT contend. There is no public CI signal (searched 90 days against non-zero controls): this is a code-proven latent defect, not an observed failure. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114019&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114019](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114019+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix `bloom_filter` over-pruning for a wide string constant
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106924 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107076 --> Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112206 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `bloom_filter` skip index dropping granules that contain matching rows when a `String` or `FixedString` column is compared for equality against a constant that is wider than the indexed type, so that queries such as `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE s = toFixedString('abc', 5)` no longer silently return too few rows. ### Description `String` and `FixedString` equality compares zero-padded, so a constant of `M` bytes matches an unbounded family of stored values: the value itself and every trailing-`\0` extension of it (`'abc'`, `'abc\0'`, `'abc\0\0'`, ...). The read path built a single hash from the converted constant while the index stores one hash per exact stored value, so at most one member of that family could match and granules holding any other member were pruned away. Because the family is unbounded, no finite set of hashes can represent it, so this declines index analysis for exactly those cases and falls back to a full scan. The rule is about byte length, not the constant's declared type. `convertFieldToType` pads a `String` constant into a `FixedString(N)` target only when it is shorter than `N` and never truncates, so a plain `String` constant wider than the index is also hashed over more bytes than the index stored, while zero-padded comparison still matches at runtime. The index is therefore used only when the indexed type is a `FixedString(N)` with `N` at least the constant's byte length. A `Variant` or `Dynamic` constant is declined for a related reason: it keeps its declared wrapper type while handing out the nested, already-padded value, so its active alternative cannot be recognised here. The guard is asymmetric and keeps pruning wherever the conversion is faithful, which the tests assert in both directions against an `ENGINE = Log` oracle. Two sound cases lose pruning: a constant wider than the index whose extra bytes are not all `\0`, which can never match any row, and a `Variant` or `Dynamic` constant whose active alternative is a plain `String`. Neither changes a result. Keeping the condition identical to the already-merged primary key rule in `KeyCondition` (commit 67f9c2c8a65067) was preferred over refining it. <details> <summary>Validation matrix (index type x constant, before and after)</summary> Each cell compares the indexed table against an `ENGINE = Log` oracle holding the same rows, with `use_skip_indexes = 0` as a third control. `FS(k)` is a `toFixedString(..., k)` constant; `str(k)` is a plain `String` literal of `k` bytes. | index type | `FS(2)` | `FS(3)` | `FS(4)` | `FS(5)` | `str(2)` | `str(4)` | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `String` | WRONG | WRONG | WRONG | WRONG | ok | ok | | `FixedString(2)` | ok | WRONG | WRONG | WRONG | ok | WRONG | | `FixedString(3)` | ok | ok | WRONG | WRONG | ok | WRONG | | `FixedString(4)` | ok | ok | ok | WRONG | ok | ok | The boundary is exactly `N >= M`, with a `String` index behaving as `N = 0`; a `String` constant against a `String` index is always sound because that comparison is byte-exact. After the fix every cell agrees with the oracle. Enumerating the predicate over (index type x constant declared type x byte length) shows the widened condition changes only cells that pair a `FixedString(N)` index with a `String` constant of more than `N` bytes, and no others. The wrapper carriers `LowCardinality(String)`, `Nullable(String)`, `LowCardinality(FixedString(3))` and `Nullable(FixedString(3))` were wrong before and are fixed, as are `LowCardinality(FixedString)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(FixedString))` constants. A `bloom_filter` index on a `Variant` column is rejected at DDL validation, so that type cannot be indexed. Pruning is unchanged for the sound cells, verified through the granule reduction reported by `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`. `IN`, `NOT IN`, `has` on `Array(String)` and the `mapContains` family were measured byte-identical before and after. `notEquals` shares the branch and is covered, but that path never prunes, so nothing observable changes there. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112639&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112639](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112639+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: TTL CLEAR INDEX for MergeTree parts
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107804 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78714 TTL CLEAR INDEX lets a MergeTree table keep secondary indexes for recent parts while dropping the physical index files from old parts. I recommend reviewing commit-by-commit. The motivating case is Observability log storage. For log tables, the raw data is not always the dominant cost. Text indexes can be very large, and most queries only touch recent data. We want to keep the index where it helps and stop paying for it on old parts that are rarely searched. Example syntax: ```sql TTL timestamp + INTERVAL 7 DAY CLEAR INDEX message_text ``` This follows the existing meaning of `ALTER TABLE ... CLEAR INDEX`: remove the per-part index files, but keep the index definition in table metadata. Queries remain correct. Parts without the index just fall back to scanning. ## What this changes The patch adds a new table TTL action, `CLEAR INDEX`, and stores its per-part min/max TTL info in `ttl.txt` as `index_clear_ttl`. When a part is fully past the TTL for a target index, future maintenance may remove that index’s files from the part. If the table later reads that part, the secondary index reader already handles missing index files and simply does not use that index for that part. The patch also adds system table visibility: ```text system.parts.index_clear_ttl_info.{index_name,expression,min,max} ``` ## Merge behavior There are two cases. First, normal merges apply the TTL policy to their output. If a merge output is fully past the `CLEAR INDEX` TTL, the merge should not retain the target index files. This is important for late-arriving data: a tiny old insert should not cause a merge that rebuilds a huge old text index. Second, there is a dedicated TTL maintenance merge type: `MergeType::TTLClearIndex`. This is used for the case where a single old part has expired index files and does not otherwise need a merge. The first implementation is intentionally conservative: it selects one source part and produces one replacement part. Dedicated `TTLClearIndex` selection obeys the normal full-part merge byte and row limits. This keeps cleanup conservative when preserving the part would require copying unchanged files rather than hardlinking them. For eligible full-storage parts, the implementation uses a fast path: hardlink or copy unchanged files, omit the expired index files, rewrite checksums and metadata, and publish the replacement part. Projection directories are copied wholesale because the row set is unchanged. This avoids reading and rewriting the raw data. If the fast path is not safe, the code falls back to the normal rewrite path. The fallback may rewrite the part, but it still must not retain expired index files in the final output. Parts with incomplete TTL metadata are not selected for dedicated cleanup; `MATERIALIZE TTL` or an ordinary merge must first recalculate the current TTL rules. The fast path currently opts out for cases like packed part storage, UUID parts, legacy parts without metadata-version files, metadata version mismatches, patch parts, part-format changes, and projection subdirectories it cannot copy as-is. On remote or zero-copy storage, it copies unchanged files instead of hardlinking them. It handles packed skip-index archives by excluding dirty `skp_idx.packed` files from the hardlink/copy set and rewriting the archive for surviving packed entries. ## Rollout safety `TTLClearIndex` is a new merge type, and merge types are serialized in replicated MergeTree log entries. Older replicas would not understand a new merge type. For that reason, generation is gated by a setting: ```sql enable_ttl_clear_index_merge_type_generation ``` The default is off. The binary can parse and execute `TTLClearIndex`, but a server will not write that merge type to the replicated log unless the setting is enabled. The intended rollout is: 1. deploy code everywhere; 2. once every replica that can read the log understands `TTLClearIndex`, enable generation; 3. later we can consider changing the default. With the gate off, replicas will not schedule dedicated `TTLClearIndex` maintenance work. Regular merges can still apply the clear-index TTL to their outputs, which is safe because missing per-part index files are already supported. ## Interaction with `SYSTEM STOP TTL MERGES` `CLEAR INDEX` is a TTL effect, so it respects the TTL merge blocker. If TTL merges are already stopped before a regular merge starts, the merge continues without applying clear-index TTL effects. If TTL merges are stopped after a merge has already decided to apply clear-index TTL effects, the merge is cancelled, matching existing TTL-delete behavior. ## Validation and edge cases covered The tests cover: - invalid target index names - per-part `index_clear_ttl_info` in `system.parts`, including the target index name - minmax index clearing - text index clearing - the late tiny insert case, where an old cleared part later merges with a small old part - adding `CLEAR INDEX` TTL to a table that already has old indexed data - TTL dependency recalculation after mutating a column used by the TTL expression - replicated execution with embedded Keeper - generation off vs generation on ## Things deliberately left conservative The fast path is narrow on purpose. Physically unsupported parts use the regular fallback, while parts with incomplete TTL metadata wait for recalculation. We can broaden the fast path later once we are comfortable with storage-specific details. The generation gate is also conservative. It is there to make rolling upgrades safe, not to disable all `CLEAR INDEX` TTL behavior. Possible follow-ups: - share more code with the existing `ALTER ... CLEAR INDEX` mutation path - add more schema-evolution tests around dropping or changing target indexes - add more direct instrumentation around which files were hardlinked vs copied in the fast path ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): MergeTree tables now support `TTL ... CLEAR INDEX index_name`, which clears secondary index files from parts once all rows in the part are past the TTL. This can help to manage the lifecycle of large indexes on older data, to conserve disk space. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108069&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/108069](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F108069+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `cast_keep_nullable` fails to preserve nullability when target type is `LowCardinality` because `canBeInsideNullable` returns false for LC types
signal.text: _Found via ClickGap automated review. Please close or comment if this is incorrect or needs adjustment._ _Retrospective finding from a historical scan of [PR #95747](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747) (merged 2026-02-02). Confirmed on current codebase — close with a note if already fixed._ ### Describe what's wrong With `cast_keep_nullable = 1`, casting from any nullable source (both `Nullable(T)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))`) to a `LowCardinality(U)` target throws `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` on NULL values instead of producing `LowCardinality(Nullable(U))` **Root cause:** CastOverloadResolver.cpp:176-177: `type->canBeInsideNullable()` returns false for `LowCardinality` types, preventing `makeNullable` from being called. Should use `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(type)` (DataTypeNullable.cpp:186) which handles LC targets by wrapping the inner dictionary type in Nullable. **Why we believe this is a bug:** CastOverloadResolver.cpp:174-177 → `getReturnTypeImpl` checks `type->canBeInsideNullable()` before calling `makeNullable(type)`. `DataTypeLowCardinality` inherits the default `canBeInsideNullable()` which returns false (IDataType.h:325). So the nullable wrapping is skipped for LC targets, and the return type stays `LowCardinality(U)` without nullability. **Affected locations:** - `src/Functions/CastOverloadResolver.cpp:176` — canBeInsideNullable guard blocks LC target nullability preservation - `src/Functions/CastOverloadResolver.cpp:177` — makeNullable cannot create LowCardinality(Nullable(T)) — only Nullable(LowCardinality(T)) which is invalid **Impact:** Any user with `cast_keep_nullable = 1` casting nullable data to a `LowCardinality` target type gets an exception. This is the same class of bug that PR #95747 intended to fix but only addressed for non-LC targets. ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `596eb6de5409`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test: cast_keep_nullable should preserve nullability when target type is LowCardinality -- Bug: makeNullable + canBeInsideNullable guard fails for LowCardinality targets -- because LowCardinality.canBeInsideNullable() returns false. Should use -- makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullable to get LowCardinality(Nullable(T)) instead. SET cast_keep_nullable = 1; -- Baseline: these work correctly (PR fix for non-LC targets) SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::String AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::String AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Bug: Nullable source to LowCardinality target throws instead of preserving nullability SELECT NULL::Nullable(String)::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Bug: LowCardinality(Nullable) source to LowCardinality target also throws SELECT NULL::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; -- Non-null should work regardless SELECT 'hello'::LowCardinality(Nullable(String))::LowCardinality(String) AS val, toTypeName(val) ORDER BY val; ``` [Try it on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/0120ba7d-ce2f-4594-bfa7-9bb806259746) ### Expected behavior ``` \N Nullable(String) \N Nullable(String) \N LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) \N LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) hello LowCardinality(Nullable(String)) ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` \N Nullable(String) \N Nullable(String) Code: 349. DB::Exception: Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type (CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN) ``` ### Additional context **Open risks:** - The `accurateCastOrNull` path (CastOverloadResolver.cpp:159-168) has a similar issue — it rejects LC targets entirely via validateNestedTypesForAccurateCastOrNull **Suggested fix:** Replace lines 174-177 with: `if (keep_nullable && (arguments.front().type->isNullable() || arguments.front().type->isLowCardinalityNullable() || isDynamic(*arguments.front().type))) return makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(type);` — this uses the existing `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe` (DataTypeNullable.cpp:186) which handles both regular types and LC types correctly. **Analysis details:** Confidence HIGH | Severity P1 | Testability: `STATELESS_SQL` Found during automated review of [PR #95747](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95747). --- _ClickGapAI · Confidence: HIGH · Severity: P1 · Finding: `h_pr95747_001`_

signal.title: Support asynchronous inserts in the Prometheus remote-write protocol
signal.text: The Prometheus remote-write protocol handler now honors the `async_insert` setting (enabled in the user profile or passed as a URL query parameter of the handler): data from multiple concurrent remote-write requests is batched in the asynchronous insert queue before forming parts, which reduces the number of parts created in the inner tables of a `TimeSeries` table under a high rate of small remote-write requests. Since `async_insert` is enabled by default, remote-write requests are batched by default; add `async_insert=0` to the handler URL or disable the setting for the user to keep the previous synchronous behavior. A request is acknowledged only after the data is flushed to all inner tables of the `TimeSeries` table, regardless of the `wait_for_async_insert` setting, because the remote-write protocol treats an acknowledged write as durable. If the flush fails, the request returns an error instead of an acknowledgement, so the sender retries it. Deduplication on flush is forcibly disabled on this path (both `deduplicate_insert` and `async_insert_deduplicate`, since the former overrides the latter): a flushed block combines data from multiple remote-write requests, so its hash differs on every retry anyway, and the inner tables of the `TimeSeries` engine handle duplicates themselves. Verified manually with a local server and real remote-write requests: a request without settings goes through the asynchronous insert queue and the data is visible immediately after the acknowledgement; `async_insert=0` keeps the synchronous path; four concurrent requests are flushed as a single batch insert; a failing inner table (a `CHECK` constraint on an external `DATA` target table) returns HTTP 500 with no acknowledgement and no data written. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The Prometheus remote-write protocol now supports asynchronous inserts: data from multiple concurrent remote-write requests is batched before forming parts, following the `async_insert` setting (enabled by default; add `async_insert=0` to the handler URL to keep the synchronous behavior). A request is acknowledged only after the data is flushed to all inner tables of the target `TimeSeries` table. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115688&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115688](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115688+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not treat a cast to String from a type that can hold NULL as safe
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115294 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Code: 349. Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type` when a `has` or `notHas` predicate carries a NULL array element and the primary key is a `String`, `Array(String)` or `Map(String, String)`, and fixed wrong results when that element is a `Dynamic` or `Variant` holding NULL. The NULL is now dropped from the set during key analysis, as it already was for other key types. ### Description No related open issue. Reproduces on 26.7.4.55: ```sql CREATE TABLE a3 (k String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO a3 VALUES ('a'); SELECT count() FROM a3 WHERE has([CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(String)')], k); -- Code: 349. Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type. ``` `ENGINE = Memory` answers `0` for the same data, and key analysis raises the error, so no rewrite avoids it. `canBeSafelyCast` declared `Nullable(X) -> String` safe, but `String` cannot hold a NULL. `tryPrepareSetColumnsForIndex` trusts that and exits early through the non-accurate `castColumn`, which throws. Every other target answers "not safe" and routes to `castColumnAccurateOrNull`, which filters unrepresentable elements out; this pair never reached it. `Array` and `Map` inherit it by recursion. The switch made the same claim for `Dynamic` and `Variant`, which carry NULL in a discriminator. There it gave wrong results rather than an error: the NULL became `''`, entered the set index and pruned away rows keyed `''`. A `Nullable` target represents it, so those two stay safe against one. That routes more targets into `castColumnAccurateOrNull`, which refuses a target it cannot wrap in `Nullable`. All four guards over such a cast tested only the outer type, so a `Tuple(Array(String))` key passed and then raised `Code: 43`; the `EmbeddedRocksDB`/`KeeperMap`/`Redis` helper had no check at all. Each now asks the cast about the target, and that helper also strips the `LowCardinality` encoding, as the key-analysis guards did. Scalar, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality` and plain `Tuple` keys keep their pruning; a container key scans when its element is Nullable-nested. Both tests fail without this change and pass with it, 50/50 under randomization. Two of my open PRs touch this. #115294 is orthogonal but appends to the same test, so the second to merge rebases it. #112890 makes two of the same `canBeSafelyCast` changes without these guards, so alone it raises that `Code: 43` for a container key. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115647&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115647](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115647+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1872` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Docs: replace settings manifests with compact route contracts
signal.text: Remove all four generated settings manifests, which duplicated anchor routing and frequently caused conflicts. Runtime anchor redirects remain in the existing legacy-route JavaScript, while the small amount of generator-only state needed to keep page grouping stable now lives in compact route contracts under `ci/jobs/scripts/docs/autogenerate/settings-route-contracts`. The contracts preserve only prefix, matching mode, and destination page. They deliberately exclude anchor maps, setting counts, page statistics, and other regenerated data. The accompanying README documents why this state exists and when it changes. Verified locally against `master` at `fb44f2a90cb377aac169a59dccc615b8403ad26e`: - Session, format, server, and `MergeTree` generated pages, navigation, overviews, explorers, and anchor-only legacy JavaScript match the saved baseline byte-for-byte. - Existing anchor registries remain exact: session 1,334; format 303; server 526; `MergeTree` 360. - Route contracts exactly preserve the historical manifest routes: session 258; format 17; server 130; `MergeTree` 82. - All four focused `--check` runs pass, and `--write` recreates none of the manifests. - Fresh-process beta-and-experimental `--write` and `--check` pass without the manifests. - Link-checker alias injection, missing/malformed registry handling, stale-page reconciliation, and the no-remap guard pass. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Documentation (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not applicable. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115672&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115672](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115672+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1876` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Don't build a set to estimate its selectivity
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Bounded the cost of estimating the selectivity of `col IN (...)` from column statistics, which could add hundreds of milliseconds to the planning of a single query. The estimator no longer runs the subquery behind `col IN (subquery)` to fill a set it only needs one selectivity number from — an unbuilt set is skipped instead. For a set larger than the new `statistics_max_set_size_for_exact_selectivity_estimation` setting (default 10000), the selectivity is now derived from the size of the set and its bounding range. --- Some measurements on sf=100 could be found [here](https://clickhouse-inc.slack.com/archives/C02F2LML5UG/p1786527589000709?thread_ts=1786399008.205189&cid=C02F2LML5UG). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114389&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114389](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114389+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add a `bucketed` schema for `system.metric_log`: a single Map column with Enum keys and 128 buckets
signal.text: Adds a new `schema_type` option `bucketed` for `system.metric_log` (the default `wide` and the `transposed` schemas are unchanged): ```xml <metric_log> <schema_type>bucketed</schema_type> </metric_log> ``` With this schema, all profile events and current metrics are stored in a single `metrics` column of type `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)`, where the `Enum16` value is the global metric index and zero values are not stored (a lookup of a missing key in a `Map` returns `0`). The default table definition uses the bucketed `Map` serialization with a constant number of 128 buckets: ``` SETTINGS map_serialization_version = 'with_buckets', map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts = 'basic', max_buckets_in_map = 128, map_buckets_strategy = 'constant', map_buckets_min_avg_size = 0 ``` Parts created by inserts keep the basic serialization to avoid creating many small files on every flush; merged parts are always split into 128 buckets. Every metric is also exposed through an `ALIAS` column, e.g. `ProfileEvent_Query UInt64 ALIAS metrics['ProfileEvent_Query']`, so all queries, dashboards, and tests written for the `wide` schema continue to work. Reading a single metric goes through the `Map` key subcolumn (`metrics.key_ProfileEvent_Query`), which reads only the bucket containing the key: in a local test it reads ~100 times less data than reading the whole map (616 vs 60716 bytes on the same rows). Supporting changes: - `arrayElement` on a `Map` with `Enum` keys now accepts the string name of the enum value (`m['name']`): the index is cast to the key type, so an unknown name throws the `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM` exception, while a name that is in the `Enum` but absent from the map returns the default value. This previously threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. - The rewrite of `m['key']` to a key subcolumn in `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` now supports `Enum`-keyed maps indexed by the name of the enum value, so both the aliases and ad-hoc queries prune buckets. - System logs can declare additional default engine settings via `getDefaultEngineSettings`, merged with the `settings` from the server configuration when no custom `engine` is specified. - An unknown `metric_log.schema_type` value is now rejected with an error instead of silently disabling the table. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `bucketed` schema type for `system.metric_log`, which stores all metrics in a single `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)` column using the bucketed `Map` serialization with 128 buckets, plus a per-metric `ALIAS` column for compatibility: the table consists of a few columns instead of thousands, zero values are not stored, and reading a single metric reads only one of the 128 buckets. In addition, a `Map` with `Enum` keys can now be indexed by the string name of the enum value, e.g. `map['name']`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115380&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115380](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115380+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Supply `_sample_factor` to the per-part read path used by mutations and merges
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a mutation that references the `_sample_factor` virtual column failing mid-execution with `Unexpected const virtual column: _sample_factor` and leaving the mutation stuck. A mutation now reads it as `1`, the same value a query without `SAMPLE` returns. ### Description `_sample_factor` is registered with `VirtualsMaterializationPlace::Reader`, so a reader is expected to supply its value. `ReadFromMergeTree` publishes it into `shared_virtual_fields` and the normal read pool copies that map into every read task, which is why `SELECT` resolves it. The per-part path used by mutations and merges does not: `createMergeTreeSequentialSource` seeds only `_part_index` and `_part_starting_offset`, so `fillVirtualColumns` falls through to a throw. `ALTER TABLE t UPDATE u = _sample_factor WHERE ...` therefore starts, then fails per part with `Code 341` wrapping `Code 16`, and the mutation entry stays stuck. The fix seeds the field where the sibling already does. The value is `1` because no `SAMPLE` clause reaches this path: `used_sample_factor` is declared `1.0` and is overwritten only for an actual `SAMPLE` clause, which a mutation predicate cannot carry. It is a literal constant, identical on every replica, so it is safe on ReplicatedMergeTree and SharedMergeTree. The net change against master is 3 lines of source plus one test. This replaces the analysis-time rejection this PR previously carried, so the guard it added earlier is gone and `MutationsInterpreter.cpp` is now untouched. That guard decided column identity from raw AST identifier names, which cannot distinguish an `ALIAS` over a virtual column from an `ALIAS` over a real `Tuple`, because `ColumnsDescription` deliberately omits alias subcolumns. One of the six holes measured rejected `a Tuple(_table UInt8) ALIAS tup` over a real `tup`, which master and 26.7.2 both accept, so dropping the guard also removes that regression. Scope is `_sample_factor` only, which is what the issue reports. `_table` and `_database` derive from the local storage id, and a mutation persists what it reads, so seeding them could diverge replicas, while rejecting them for every MergeTree would be a new restriction. That design is filed separately, and their current mid-execution failure is unchanged here.

signal.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115614 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies nothing is scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it populates the cache inside its own job budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits, and still looks finished because `Finish Workflow` reports success. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days. #115614 has since raised the job cap to 1800s. This adds the other half, so an overrun is a failing step naming the cause instead of a job-level SIGTERM that leaves no result: - Population is bounded, covering every subprocess it starts and not only the clone: the S3 probes and the upload are AWS client subprocesses with retried socket deadlines of minutes, measured at 182s for one call and 557s for the upload. - The bound is the smaller of the configured 1200s and what the job actually has left, since an import-time check relates two configured numbers and holds however long the preamble ran. The job authenticates unconditionally first and `GHAuth.auth` has no deadline (311s to mint a token, still running at 420s for `gh auth login`); a preamble that left nothing now fails naming the elapsed time. Bounding `GHAuth.auth` is separate, as `runner.py`, `changelog_nightly.py` and `revert_ci_regressions.py` share it. - A reserve is held back for the checks after the upload. Each step may spend its whole deadline, so the confirmatory `head-object` on a refused conditional write could get one second, turning an ordinary concurrent-writer collision into a dropped matrix. - The clone is retried, since a population failure now fails the step, as the rest of the repo already assumes. The attempts share the budget; one deadline each would bound no total. Population failure fails the step rather than reporting `OK`, since dependants clone unauthenticated and cannot reach a private submodule. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115176&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115176](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115176+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
