signal.title: Keyed aggregations over huge constant-folded literals still pay a per-execution O(N) content-hash in the hash-table-stats cache key (bounded residual of #107643; ~9ms per execution for a 5M-element literal)
signal.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the situation There is a small, result-preserving win available here: bounding how many bytes of a constant may be hashed into the cache-key fingerprint (a ~30-line patch, below) removes the last per-execution cost that grows with a constant-folded literal's size from the aggregation hash-table-stats cache key. On the fixed build the key costs 89–93us regardless of literal size (vs 8.8ms at 5M elements / 35.3ms at 20M elements before), a plan with many keyed aggregations over large folded constants runs about 2x faster end to end, every smoke query returns byte-identical results (including a deliberately constructed collision pair), and peak memory is byte-identical. **Background — the parent finding.** The aggregation hash-table-statistics cache key introduced by merge `49dc83c610c4fb82ee468e61b7f82a1968123027` (PR #107643) serializes the aggregation's input plan subtree — including full constant column data — during query plan optimization, on every execution. That caused the `quantile_merge` +78.5% CI regression documented in the parent finding — filed as https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113037 — whose proposed patch has two parts: (1) skip the key entirely for keyless aggregations (the key is never consumable there), and (2) represent constants larger than 64 KiB in the hash-input-only stream by an identity fingerprint — marker + row count + **whole-column SipHash** — instead of their full binary data. **The residual (keyed case).** For *keyed* aggregations the key is still computed, and part (2)'s fingerprint calls `data.updateHashFast(column_hash)`, which for an array constant recurses into offsets and data and ends in a single hash update over the entire element buffer — every byte of the literal, per execution. The parent fix reduced the constant factor (full binary serialization → one hash pass) without removing the linear term. Per the investigation objective: the measured residual is ~9ms plan-optimize per execution for a 5M-element folded literal on the parent-fixed build, vs ~44ms unpatched and ~0.07ms on 26.6. The serialized stream exists only as SipHash input inside `calculateHashFromStep(const ITransformingStep &)` (`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp`), which is why the cost appears only on plan steps that do not preserve row count[^rowcount], and vanishes entirely when `collect_hash_table_stats_during_aggregation = 0` short-circuits `setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys`. Hash path: `serializeConstant` in `src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp` (the `updateHashFast` call sits at line 4165 at our base ref; the originally cited :4148 was the diff hunk header) → `ColumnArray::updateHashFast` (`src/Columns/ColumnArray.cpp:360-363`) → `ColumnVector::updateHashFast` (`src/Columns/ColumnVector.cpp:108-111`, one `hash.update(data.data(), size()*sizeof(T))`). **Linearity, measured** (parent-fixed local build at the `v26.7.1.1315-stable`-era base ref, arm64, `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` per execution): | Folded literal | Counter per execution (us, raw series) | Verified median (us) | | --- | --- | --- | | `range(1000000)` | 1792, 1853, 1840, 1830 | 1840 | | `range(5000000)` | 8797, 8835, 8746, 8792, 8794 | 8794 | | `range(20000000)` | 35625, 35277, 35171, 35256 | 35277 | Floor-subtracted cost is 1742.0 / 1743.1 / 1762.8 us per million elements at 1M/5M/20M (max deviation 0.77%), while the setting-off floor stays size-invariant ([79, 76, 74, 79, 79] us at 5M). An integer literal is narrowed by `FieldToDataType`, so `range(N)` folds to `Array(UInt32)` at 4 bytes/element: hashed content is 4/20/80 MB and implied throughput is 2.27–2.30 GB/s — consistent with a single-pass SipHash, i.e. the residual is linear in literal bytes at hash throughput, not a fixed overhead. **The fix.** A new registry cap, `max_constant_bytes_to_hash` (set to 1 MiB where the cache key is computed), makes `serializeConstant` write only the constant's *shape* once the constant exceeds the cap — marker, row count, data byte size, and a flag recording whether content was hashed — so the cost stops growing with the literal. Validation (parent-fixed baseline vs cap-fixed candidate, sole A→B code delta is the cap — verified by patch diffing): - Objective query (single keyed aggregation, 5M-element folded constant): plan-optimize counter [8912, 8745, 8874, 8935, 8934] → [93, 89, 92, 92, 91] us — 8.9ms → 0.09ms, two orders of magnitude. - Post-fix cost is size-invariant: 91.4us at 5M vs 91.8us at 20M elements — slope 0.027us per million elements against a pre-fix 1743us per million; exactly the linear term is removed and nothing more. - Amplifier `q_union16_20m` (sixteen keyed aggregations, each over its own distinct large folded array constant, each producing one row): wall verdict **improvement** in two interleaved sessions — ratio 0.4909, bounds [0.4476, 0.6457], and ratio 0.4913, bounds [0.4313, 0.566] (n=9/side each); causal counter [141750, 141497, 141676, 140992, 140930] → [1344, 1339, 1363, 1324, 1387] us. A 32-aggregation variant also roughly halves (ratios 0.5485 / 0.5288) but its verdicts are labelled unstable at this rig's variance. - Smoke: 14 queries, 100% result-hash equality — including a deliberately colliding pair, `range(2000000)` vs `arrayMap(y -> y + 1, range(2000000))`: same type, same element count, same byte size, different content, therefore sharing a shape-only key. Peak memory byte-identical on all three probe workloads. **Positioning against the culprit PR's intent.** PR #107643's own stated goal was to remove per-query overhead (the eager query-tree-to-AST conversion was "a noticeable cost during query analysis even though that AST is otherwise unused on the common `SELECT ... FROM <MergeTree>` path"). The one performance tradeoff its cloud benchmark report declared is unrelated to this mechanism: clickbench Q31 +11.9%, described there as "the expected flip side: preallocation can overshoot and cost cache locality when the estimate is off." Nothing in the PR discussion declares or prices a plan-optimization cost proportional to the size of a constant-folded literal. This residual therefore cuts *against* the PR's stated intent, and removing it is aligned with that intent — not a reversal of a deliberate tradeoff. **Disclosed costs of the fix:** - Above the cap, the cache key no longer distinguishes two constants that share type, element count and byte size; such plans share one hash-table-statistics entry. That entry supplies a preallocation size hint to the aggregator (`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:117-121`) — and, via `initDataVariantsWithSizeHint`, feeds the single-level→two-level pre-conversion decision — so a collision can mis-size a preallocation or flip that pre-conversion, but cannot change a query result. The colliding-pair smoke verifies this. - Bounded, not eliminated: the post-fix residual is 92us [89, 93] against a setting-off floor of 79us [74, 79] — non-overlapping, +16% (the key path still runs; the mechanism predicts exactly this). - Binary size +128 bytes (947296264 → 947296392). - On a sub-threshold plan whose code path is unchanged (eight keyed aggregations over ~8KB folded constants, below the 64KB fingerprint threshold), plan-optimize time was consistently a few tens of microseconds higher on the candidate — [828, 782, 788, 780] vs [857, 841, 830, 873] us, about +7 percent of a sub-millisecond time — most likely code layout in the recompiled translation units; far below wall-clock resolution. - No-effect controls clean: a keyed aggregation over a `numbers` source with no folded constant is inside-band in both sessions (ratios 1.0104 [0.9861, 1.0277] and 1.011 [0.9962, 1.0374]); a below-threshold constant is counter-indistinguishable ([132, 130, 134, 133] vs [130, 145, 130, 137] us); the `hash_table_sizes_stats` perf-test sweep shows ratios 0.9064–1.0429 with no query beyond run-to-run noise (4 of its queries need the external `hits_100m_single` dataset and were skipped, disclosed). ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? The linear per-execution term exists wherever the #107643 cache-key path serializes or hashes constant data for keyed aggregations: - Stock `v26.7.1.1315-stable` pays it as full constant serialization (~44ms per execution at 5M elements — the parent issue's keyed case). - A build carrying the parent fingerprint fix pays it as a whole-column hash (~9ms per execution at 5M elements — this issue). - `v26.6.1.1193-stable` is unaffected (~0.07ms). Measured builds: base ref `a6156303df65c307bdb8b66e9e9cc5637346a6b8` plus the parent patch (baseline, binary sha256 `e70346392b04328a18a1ace47e625f905b2191287f7967cd3b9e392eeeb1f0a4`) vs plus this patch (candidate, `ff69830ad339970a50b950caf11a2381845c669cce4c559038a3b54b4bc678e0`), both locally built, attested as 26.7.1.1. Current master was not measured. ### How to reproduce On any affected build, take a keyed (`GROUP BY`) aggregation whose plan contains a constant-folded array literal well above the 64 KiB fingerprint threshold (e.g. a folded `range(5000000)` — the parent issue's `quantile_merge` query with a grouping key is the original shape) and watch `QueryPlanOptimizeMicroseconds` per execution. 1. On the parent-fixed build the counter medians are 1840 / 8794 / 35277 us for 1M / 5M / 20M-element literals — linear in the literal. 2. Discriminator — `SET collect_hash_table_stats_during_aggregation = 0`: the counter drops to the 74–79us floor and becomes size-invariant, because `setAggregationHashTableCacheKeys` is short-circuited. 3. Discriminator — scale the literal: cost per million elements is flat (1742.0–1762.8 us floor-subtracted), i.e. a linear term, not fixed overhead. 4. On stock 26.7 (no parent fix) the same query shape pays the ~5x larger full-serialization cost (~44ms at 5M elements) through the same code path. Note: the single-aggregation objective query's wall-clock gain is **not** resolvable on our rig (ratios ~0.96, labelled unstable in both attempts) — its ~9ms gain is counter-level only. The wall-clock improvement was demonstrated on a synthetic amplifier (16 keyed aggregations over distinct large folded constants in one plan, `UNION`-combined) built to expose the same mechanism above wall-clock noise. ### Expected performance The cache-key cost for a keyed aggregation should be O(1) in the size of any folded literal in its subtree: with the cap, 89–93us at 5M elements and size-invariant to 20M (slope 0.027us per million elements vs 1743us per million without), against a 74–79us floor with the stats path disabled entirely. End to end, a many-aggregation plan over large folded constants runs ~2x faster (ratios 0.4909 / 0.4913 in two sessions); a single-aggregation query recovers ~9ms → ~0.09ms of plan-optimize time per execution, below wall-clock resolution for the query we measured. ### Related issues and pull requests - Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107643 — the residual persists (in reduced form) even with our parent-finding patch applied. - Parent finding: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113037 — aggregation hash-table-stats cache key serializes large constant-folded literals on every execution (`quantile_merge` +78.5%). Its patch covered the keyless-aggregation skip and constant fingerprinting; this issue is the remaining keyed case that patch left bounded but linear. - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113333 (open, groeneai) — implements the keyless-skip fix and closes #113037. Its description explicitly reserves this issue's topic: "Constant serialization is still costly for keyed aggregations, about 62 ms here, and is left to a separate fix." This issue is the problem statement for that separate fix. - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106137 — the plan-node hashing infrastructure that #107643 reuses (per the PR description). ### Additional context groeneai raised four objections on the #113037 thread that bear on this proposal; each is addressed with what we measured: 1. *"SerializedSetsRegistry ... not a serialization-policy holder, threshold would sit in the wrong layer."* — Since PR #106073 merged (2026-08-05), the registry does carry a cache-key serialization-policy flag: `bool for_cache_key` in `src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h`. On master this layer already holds exactly this kind of policy; the proposed cap fields would sit next to an existing one. 2. *"64 KiB is an unmotivated constant ... thresholds become settings unless justified."* — Conceded. We propose the threshold as a setting rather than a hard-coded constant. 3. *"updateHashFast is not universally implemented: ColumnBLOB, ColumnCompressed, ColumnLazy all throw ... would LOSE preallocation for plans that serialize fine today."* — Conceded for the 64 KiB–1 MiB band, where the fingerprint hashes content via `updateHashFast` while full serialization would have succeeded; that band is exactly the already-disclosed smoke coverage gap (see the validation caveats below). Above the 1 MiB cap the shape-only branch does not call `updateHashFast` at all. 4. *"Streaming it through a hashing write buffer removes the allocation with no cache-key identity change."* — Agreed on the allocation: streaming removes the 379MB allocation. It does not remove the O(N) serialize+hash term, which our gated numbers put at ~1.74ms per million elements (floor-subtracted 1742.0 / 1743.1 / 1762.8 us per million at 1M/5M/20M). The cap/fingerprint targets that linear term itself, which streaming cannot touch. The patch adds one field to `SerializedSetsRegistry` (`max_constant_bytes_to_hash`, default 0 = "always hash the whole content", so plan-shipping serialization is untouched) and sets it to 1 MiB at the single hash-input-only call site. Above the cap the fingerprint keeps the constant's shape only — marker, row count, data byte size, hashed-content flag. The touched code is the generic hash-input-only serialization stream, so every large constant in any such stream benefits, not only the triggering query's shape. 1 MiB of content hashing is ~0.2ms; the cap sits 8x–160x below every constant measured in this investigation, so it is not tuned to the benchmark. <details> <summary>Proposed patch (cumulative over the parent-finding patch): bound fingerprint content-hashing at 1 MiB — above the cap the cache key records only the constant's shape (validated: objective-query plan-opt 8.9ms → 0.09ms and size-invariant to 20M elements; amplifier wall ~2x, ratios 0.4909/0.4913; smoke incl. deliberate shape-collision pair 100% result equality; peak memory byte-identical)</summary> ```diff diff --git a/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp b/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp index f12b3152794..e3752bb42f9 100644 --- a/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp +++ b/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp @@ -4148,6 +4148,43 @@ static void serializeConstant(const IDataType & type, const IColumn & value, Wri "Cannot serialize non-constant column {} as constant", value.getName()); const auto & data = const_column->getDataColumn(); + + /// Hash-input-only streams (see SerializedSetsRegistry::max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint): + /// represent large constants by an identity fingerprint instead of their full binary data. + /// A constant-folded literal can be arbitrarily big (e.g. `range(5000000)` folds into a + /// 5M-element array), and serializing it in full on every query execution just to compute + /// a hash-table-stats cache key costs more than the aggregation it is meant to help. + /// The fingerprint keeps the key's identity (type is encoded by the caller; size and a + /// whole-column hash are written here) at a bounded cost. This stream is never deserialized. + if (registry.max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint + && data.byteSize() > registry.max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint) + { + const size_t data_bytes = data.byteSize(); + writeStringBinary("__constant_fingerprint", out); + writeVarUInt(data.size(), out); + writeVarUInt(data_bytes, out); + + /// Hashing the content is itself O(data_bytes): SipHash over a constant-folded + /// literal runs at a few GB/s, so a 40MB folded `range(5000000)` array still costs + /// ~9ms on EVERY execution of the query — the same linear per-execution cost this + /// fingerprint exists to remove, only with a smaller constant factor. Above + /// max_constant_bytes_to_hash keep the constant's shape only (its type is written by + /// the caller, its row count and data size just above), which is O(1) in the + /// literal's size. Two distinct constants that share a type and a shape then also + /// share a cache key; that key selects a hash-table SIZE HINT for preallocation, so a + /// collision can only mis-size a preallocation and can never change a query result. + const bool hash_content = !registry.max_constant_bytes_to_hash + || data_bytes <= registry.max_constant_bytes_to_hash; + writeVarUInt(hash_content ? 1 : 0, out); + if (hash_content) + { + SipHash column_hash; + data.updateHashFast(column_hash); + writeBinary(column_hash.get64(), out); + } + return; + } + type.getDefaultSerialization()->serializeBinary(data, 0, out, FormatSettings{}); } diff --git a/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h b/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h index 1413aa556da..4beb1f15618 100644 --- a/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h +++ b/src/Interpreters/SetSerialization.h @@ -15,6 +15,25 @@ struct SerializedSetsRegistry }; std::unordered_map<FutureSet::Hash, FutureSetPtr, Hashing> sets; + + /// When non-zero, constant column values whose data is larger than this many bytes are + /// serialized as an identity fingerprint (marker + row count + data size + a bounded + /// content hash) instead of full binary data (see serializeConstant in ActionsDAG.cpp). + /// Such a stream CANNOT be deserialized; this mode is only for streams that are used as + /// hash input (aggregation hash-table stats cache keys, see calculateHashTableCacheKeys.cpp), + /// mirroring how Set constants are represented by their precomputed hash there. + /// 0 (default) keeps full serialization for shipping plans between servers. + size_t max_constant_bytes_before_fingerprint = 0; + + /// Upper bound on how many bytes of a constant's data may be hashed INTO that fingerprint. + /// Writing the fingerprint is cheap, but hashing the column content is itself O(bytes): + /// a constant-folded literal is unbounded (`range(5000000)` folds into a ~40MB array + /// constant, `range(50000000)` into ~400MB), so a whole-column hash keeps a linear + /// per-execution cost in the plan-optimize path. signal.title: Enable the consecutive-keys cache for fixed-size aggregation keys
signal.text: The `keys128` and `keys256` aggregation methods had `consecutive_keys_optimization = false`, so aggregating data whose keys arrive in long runs of equal values (e.g. anything grouped by a fixed-size key that is a prefix of the table sort order) paid a full hash-and-probe per row. Enabling the existing `LastElementCache` for these methods (including the two-level variants) skips the hash table entirely within a run, at the cost of one wide key compare per row; the aggregator's adaptive hit-rate machinery already disables the cache on random keys, verified by a random-key `keys256` microbenchmark showing no regression (3.88 s baseline vs 3.82/3.88 s). On clustered keys (runs of ~200k equal `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` values, 400M rows) this saves ~10% of aggregation CPU. Session: ad94609b-7b39-4f96-af16-7947efc50974 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Aggregation by fixed-size keys of 17-32 bytes (the `keys128`/`keys256` methods, e.g. `GROUP BY` a `UUID` or a `Tuple(UInt64, UInt64)`) now uses the consecutive-keys cache, making aggregation of sorted or clustered data up to 10% faster; the cache disables itself adaptively on random keys. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115155&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115155](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115155+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: mergeTreeIndex table function ignores the source table's row policy
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A user restricted by a SELECT row policy can read the primary-key (and minmax-index) column values of the rows the policy hides, by calling `mergeTreeIndex(db, table)` instead of selecting from the table.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp:413`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp#L413) - the access check is grant-only; there is no row-policy lookup for `source_table->getStorageID()` before the primary-key values are exposed. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `StorageMergeTreeIndex::readImpl` ([`src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp:413`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp#L413)) checks only `AccessType::SELECT` on the source table and then streams primary-key granule values straight out of the parts. It never calls `Context::getRowPolicyFilter`, unlike its two siblings: `StorageMergeTreeTextIndex::readImpl` ([`src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeTextIndex.cpp:446`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeTextIndex.cpp#L446)) and, as of this PR, `StorageFromMergeTreeProjection::read` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/StorageFromMergeTreeProjection.cpp:51`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/MergeTree/StorageFromMergeTreeProjection.cpp#L51)). **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp:413`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeIndex.cpp#L413) — readImpl: grant-only access check, no row-policy lookup before streaming primary-key values - [`src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeTextIndex.cpp:446`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/StorageMergeTreeTextIndex.cpp#L446) — sibling that DOES enforce the row policy - the shape the fix should follow - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/StorageFromMergeTreeProjection.cpp:51`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/9c7ecedbfc68c/src/Storages/MergeTree/StorageFromMergeTreeProjection.cpp#L51) — the sibling this PR fixes **Impact:** Row-policy bypass. Any user holding plain SELECT on a table (the normal case for a row-policy-restricted user) can enumerate primary-key column values for every row, including rows the policy hides. With `index_granularity = 1` every row's key is exposed; at the default granularity every 8192nd row's key is. `with_minmax = true` additionally exposes per-part min/max of the key columns across hidden rows. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `9c7ecedbfc68c`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test: a row policy on the source table must not be bypassed by the mergeTreeIndex table function. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_mt_index_rp; DROP ROW POLICY IF EXISTS rp_mt_index ON t_mt_index_rp; CREATE TABLE t_mt_index_rp (id UInt64, department String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (department, id) SETTINGS index_granularity = 1; INSERT INTO t_mt_index_rp VALUES (1, 'engineering'), (2, 'finance'), (3, 'engineering'), (4, 'hr'); CREATE ROW POLICY rp_mt_index ON t_mt_index_rp FOR SELECT USING department = 'engineering' TO ALL; SELECT '-- base table honours the policy'; SELECT id, department FROM t_mt_index_rp ORDER BY id; SELECT '-- mergeTreeIndex must not expose primary key values of policy-hidden rows'; SELECT DISTINCT department FROM mergeTreeIndex(currentDatabase(), 't_mt_index_rp') ORDER BY department; -- { serverError ACCESS_DENIED } DROP ROW POLICY rp_mt_index ON t_mt_index_rp; DROP TABLE t_mt_index_rp; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` -- base table honours the policy 1 engineering 3 engineering -- mergeTreeIndex must not expose primary key values of policy-hidden rows ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` -- base table honours the policy 1 engineering 3 engineering -- mergeTreeIndex must not expose primary key values of policy-hidden rows engineering finance hr ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Mirror `StorageMergeTreeTextIndex::readImpl`: in `StorageMergeTreeIndex::readImpl`, after the `checkAccess`, fetch `context->getRowPolicyFilter(source_storage_id.getDatabaseName(), source_storage_id.getTableName(), RowPolicyFilterType::SELECT_FILTER)` and throw `ACCESS_DENIED` when it is set and not always-true (the index dump is per-granule, so the policy cannot be applied per row). </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `mergeTreeAnalyzeIndexes` and `mergeTreeCodecBlockCounts` were audited and expose no column values (part names, granule ranges, byte/codec counts only), so they are out of scope - but the granule ranges they report do reveal row counts of a policy-restricted table. Found during automated review of [PR #112329](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112329). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr112329_001` </details> cc @yariks5s @KochetovNicolai (from #112329) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115304 - Backported to: `26.7.6.5`, `26.6.4.10` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on constant-folded comparison under group_by_use_nulls + GROUPING SETS
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (server abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a constant-folded comparison appears in the SELECT list together with `group_by_use_nulls = 1` and `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 `group_by_use_nulls` promotes a `FunctionNode`'s declared result type to `Nullable` via `FunctionNode::wrap_with_nullable`, while the un-wrapped base function used for constant folding still returns the non-`Nullable` type. When such a node is constant-folded in `tryFoldFunctionToConstant` (`ActionsDAG.cpp`), the folded `Const(UInt8)` diverges from the declared `Nullable(UInt8)`, so the node result-type consistency check throws `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got Const(UInt8)`. In debug/sanitizer builds this aborts the server; release tolerates it (the check is an assert), and `group_by_use_nulls = 0` is unaffected. The fix reconciles the folded constant to the declared node result type in exactly this case (the declared type equals `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(base_result_type)`) instead of weakening the check. The strict `LOGICAL_ERROR` check is kept as a fallback for genuine mismatches. Regression test: `04545_group_by_use_nulls_grouping_sets_const_fold_equals` (the issue's repro plus a minimal variant). Found by the AST fuzzer. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110703&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110703](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110703+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

At a minimum, the following information should be added (but add more as needed). - Motivation: Why is this function, table engine, etc. useful to ClickHouse users? Sometimes people need to track table's changes via matirialized view. - Example use: A query or command. I used this to check is materialized view metrics work: ```sql CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS test; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS test.random_events; CREATE TABLE test.random_events ( id UUID, user_id UInt64, event_type LowCardinality(String), amount Float64, is_success UInt8, event_time DateTime, payload String ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (event_time, user_id); INSERT INTO test.random_events SELECT generateUUIDv4(), rand64() % 1000000, arrayElement(['click', 'view', 'purchase', 'login', 'logout'], 1 + rand() % 5), round(randCanonical() * 1000, 2), rand() % 2, now() - toIntervalSecond(rand() % 86400), concat('random_payload_', toString(rand64())) FROM numbers(1000); ``` ```sql CREATE TABLE test.random_events_hourly_stats ( event_type LowCardinality(String), event_hour DateTime, total_amount Float64, success_count UInt64, fail_count UInt64, event_count UInt64 ) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY (event_type, event_hour); CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW test.mv_hourly_stats TO test.random_events_hourly_stats AS SELECT event_type, toStartOfHour(event_time) AS event_hour, sum(amount) AS total_amount, countIf(is_success = 1) AS success_count, countIf(is_success = 0) AS fail_count, count() AS event_count FROM test.random_events GROUP BY event_type, event_hour; -- Backfill hourly stats INSERT INTO test.random_events_hourly_stats SELECT event_type, toStartOfHour(event_time) AS event_hour, sum(amount) AS total_amount, countIf(is_success = 1) AS success_count, countIf(is_success = 0) AS fail_count, count() AS event_count FROM test.random_events GROUP BY event_type, event_hour; -- Testing results SELECT * FROM test.random_events_hourly_stats ORDER BY event_hour DESC, event_type LIMIT 20; ``` Kinda optional stage: ```sql INSERT INTO test.random_events SELECT generateUUIDv4(), rand64() % 1000000, arrayElement(['click', 'view', 'purchase', 'login', 'logout'], 1 + rand() % 5), round(randCanonical() * 1000, 2), rand() % 2, now() - toIntervalSecond(rand() % 86400), concat('random_payload_', toString(rand64())) FROM numbers(1000000); signal.title: CI: refuse LLVM coverage verdicts on incomplete measurements, make coverage profiles kill-safe
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The `LLVM Coverage` gate fails a PR when total line coverage drops more than 0.3 pp below the master baseline. Both totals are merged from 21 per-shard `.profdata` artifacts that are deliberately `optional=True`, and nothing verified that either side had all of them. A shard profile can vanish while every check stays green (a corrupt `.profraw` aborts the producer merge, `-failure-mode=warn` silently discards a corrupt input, a zero-length `.profraw` is accepted silently). Both error directions occur: - A short PR side fails an unrelated PR. Observed twice in the last 60 days, both times the same missing file `it-amd_llvm_coverage_4_8.profdata` with all 21 shard jobs green: [PR 110186](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110186&sha=0b33f54bc8089ea3560397c589e93dc6aec92d47&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage) ("dropped 0.50 pp" on a 102-line PR) and [PR 105844](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105844&sha=66107bb44ab45a490e839225eb096e46204e5e86&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage). - A short master run writes a low baseline into the CI DB, so a later real regression passes. This direction produces a PASS and is invisible in any failure count. The invariant established here: a verdict comes only from two complete measurements. - Every coverage producer (functional, integration, unit) names its profile after its own artifact (`<artifact>.profdata`), so the filename carries the shard identity. Producer merges use `--failure-mode=any` and skip zero-length `.profraw` inputs: a shard with invalid data publishes nothing instead of a silently short profile. Artifacts stay `optional=True`, so a missing profile never reddens a green test job. - The `LLVM Coverage` job compares the expected file set against what arrived and merges an explicit file list instead of a `*.profdata` glob. On a missing or invalid shard it reports `SKIPPED` naming the shard, and withholds every comparative output: no verdict, no GitHub comment, no `llvm_coverage.info` artifact, no CI DB row. A genuine tooling failure (report generation) still stays RED. - Baseline completeness needs no metadata: the diff script already selects the first master ancestor that has an `llvm_coverage.info`, and after this change such an `.info` exists only for complete runs. (Transitional: for the first ~30 master commits after merge, pre-change ancestors are still selectable, which is exactly today's behaviour.) - Under coverage, the integration sequential test phase runs regardless of how many parallel tests failed (`MAX_FAILS_BEFORE_DROP`), so a green shard cannot silently publish a profile that is short by the whole sequential phase. - Root cause of the recurring shard 4/8 loss: `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` in merge mode writes the profile only at process exit, and integration tests `SIGKILL` servers on purpose; a kill inside that multi-second write leaves a half-written `.profraw` whose header makes `llvm-profdata` abort with `LLVM ERROR: out of memory` ([llvm/llvm-project#50970](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/50970), open since 2021). Coverage builds now compile with `-mllvm -runtime-counter-relocation` and run with `%c` (continuous mode): the counters are memory-mapped into the profile, which is valid at every instant, so a kill at any moment loses nothing and corrupts nothing. This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832, which establishes the same invariant via a completeness sidecar published next to `llvm_coverage.info`, a manifest fingerprint, and a two-pass baseline selector. Withholding the `.info` on incomplete runs makes the sidecar unnecessary, and the profile naming plus set check shrink to ~40 lines. Accepted residuals of the simpler design: a session-timeout-truncated shard can still publish a valid short profile, and on the rare day the coverage artifact manifest itself changes, verdicts are unreliable until master republishes. Not covered here (pre-existing, unchanged): the diagnostics of the diff-report script, addressed separately by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115225. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115623&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115623](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115623+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Convert the JOIN keys to the type of the values that they have in common
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/21794 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/21794 There is no type that is able to hold all the values of both `UInt64` and `Int64`, so a JOIN on such keys was rejected: ``` SELECT * FROM (SELECT number FROM numbers(10)) AS a INNER JOIN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10)) AS b ON a.number = b.number - 1 Code: 386. DB::Exception: There is no supertype for types UInt64, Int64 ... ``` But a JOIN does not need the least supertype. It is enough to convert both keys to the type of the values that they have in common - the most subtype, which is `UInt64` for this pair, holding the values from `0` to `9223372036854775807`. A value outside of this range is not equal to any value from the other side, so `accurateCastOrNull` converts it to NULL, and it does not match anything. This is applied to the equality conditions in the `ON` section, and to the `USING` section of an `INNER JOIN` or a `SEMI JOIN`, where the result contains only the matched values. It is not applied to: - the kinds of JOIN with `USING` that can emit unmatched rows (`LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `FULL`, `ANTI`), where the key is also a column of the result and can hold the unmatched values; - null-safe comparisons (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`), where NULL matches NULL, so the values converted to NULL would match each other; - the ASOF inequality (the last column in the `USING` list), which needs the order of the values, not only their equality; - a `Join` table engine whose stored key is not itself the common type, because its hash table is prebuilt over the original key values and cannot be converted - the opposite direction, where only the probe key has to be converted, is supported. A runtime filter is not built for such a JOIN, because a `NOT IN` filter over a set with NULLs would drop the rows that have to be preserved. Only the queries that were failing before are affected - the type inference is unchanged whenever the least supertype exists. It is implemented in the analyzer, which is enabled by default; with `enable_analyzer = 0` the old `TableJoin::inferJoinKeyCommonType` path still rejects such a JOIN, exactly as before. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow a JOIN on keys that have no common supertype, such as `UInt64` and `Int64`. Previously such a query was rejected with `There is no supertype for types UInt64, Int64`. Now the keys are converted to the type of the values that they have in common, and a value outside of this range does not match anything. This requires the analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112951&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112951](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112951+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix std::out_of_range when a space-filling curve is not a key column
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `std::out_of_range: map::at: key not found` when a `MergeTree` key expression contains a `mortonEncode` or `hilbertEncode` call that is not itself a key column, for example `ORDER BY mortonEncode(hilbertEncode(x, y), x, y)` or `PARTITION BY mortonEncode(x, y) % 4`. ### Description `KeyCondition::getAllSpaceFillingCurves` walks every action of the key-expression DAG and looks up each curve node in `key_columns` with `at()`. `key_columns` holds only top-level key columns, so a curve nested inside another expression is an intermediate node whose `result_name` is absent, and the lookup throws out of `KeyCondition`'s constructor. Such a table accepts `CREATE` and `INSERT`, then rejects almost every read. On released `26.7.4.14` with `ORDER BY mortonEncode(hilbertEncode(x, y), x, y)`, `SELECT *`, `SELECT count() WHERE x = 5` and `SELECT sum(y)` all fail with `Code: 1001` and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with `Code: 341`; only a bare `count()` works. Debug and sanitizer builds abort instead. It reproduces on `25.8.30.12` (LTS), `26.6.3.28` and `26.7.4.14`, so it is not new. A curve is only ever consumed through `key_column_pos` as a key column index, so one that is not a key column cannot participate in curve-aware key analysis at all. Rather than catch the failed lookup, the fix restricts the enumeration to curve nodes that are key columns, using the `key_columns.find` form already used at the five other lookups here. Line 1386 was the file's only unconditional `at()` on `key_columns`. Three construction sites reach that line and are all fixed: the primary/sorting key, the partition key, and minmax/set skip indexes. Nothing that worked before changes: for `ORDER BY mortonEncode(x, y)`, and for a nested curve that is also a key column, `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` is byte-identical before and after, so curve pruning is preserved. Found by the AST fuzzer on an unrelated PR that does not touch this code: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113022&sha=03db3c42bad3adf593a621b427aa706d7d81e966&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29. No related open issue found. Not addressed here: `INDEX i mortonEncode(x, y) TYPE minmax`, where the curve *is* the index key column, fails `Code: 10 NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` both before and after. There the lookup succeeds and the failure is downstream, a different defect. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1727` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Disable read-in-order when primary key selectivity is poor
signal.text: When the WHERE clause cannot use the primary key effectively (e.g., `LIKE '%...'`), the `optimize_read_in_order` optimization kills parallelism: each part is read by a single stream instead of many. This can make `ORDER BY` queries 4x slower than the same query without `ORDER BY`. Example on a 2.5B row table with `ORDER BY path` and `WHERE path LIKE '%stderr.log'`: - Without ORDER BY: ~9.5s - With ORDER BY (read-in-order): ~40s - With `optimize_read_in_order = 0`: ~9.6s The fix adds a runtime check in `ReadFromMergeTree::spreadMarkRanges`: if the primary key index selected more than a configurable fraction of all granules and there is no LIMIT, we fall back to parallel reading with per-stream `PartialSortingTransform` + `MergeSortingTransform`, so the output is still sorted as the `SortingStep` above expects. New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` controls the threshold. The default is 1.0, which preserves the previous behavior (never disable read-in-order based on primary key selectivity): the heuristic is opt-in until the default threshold is tuned against the performance report. Set it below 1.0 (e.g. 0.5) to enable the guard. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` that can disable the read-in-order optimization when the primary key selectivity is poor (more than the given fraction of granules selected), falling back to parallel reading with sorting. This avoids severe parallelism loss for queries like `SELECT ... WHERE path LIKE '%...' ORDER BY path`. The default 1.0 preserves the previous behavior; set a lower value (e.g. 0.5) to enable the heuristic. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` (Float, default 1.0): maximum ratio of selected to total primary key granules for `optimize_read_in_order` to stay enabled. When the ratio exceeds this value, read-in-order is disabled in favor of parallel reading with per-stream sorting. The default 1.0 preserves the old behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `CI Tests` fails on master for any PR touching `ci/`: `test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data` broken by the #115221 + #104631 combination
signal.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115221 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104631 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 ### Describe what's wrong `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py::test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data` fails on current master (verified on `590a91de69b`), so the `CI Tests` job is red for every pull request whose changes select it (anything touching `ci/`). The test (added in #115221, merged 2026-08-21 01:27 UTC) asserts that changing only `ci/defs/job_configs.py` or `ci/defs/defs.py` does not schedule `Build (arm_release)`. Meanwhile #104631 (merged 2026-08-20) added `Parser memory check` to the PR workflow with - `digest_config` including `./ci/defs/defs.py`, `./ci/defs/job_configs.py` and `./ci/workflows/pull_request.py`, and - `requires=[CLICKHOUSE_EXAMPLES]`, an artifact provided by `Build (arm_release)` (the `--build-examples` variant). So a registry-only edit makes `Parser memory check` affected, and the rescue pass in `_filter_unaffected_jobs` schedules `Build (arm_release)` to produce `CLICKHOUSE_EXAMPLES` — exactly the waste the new test pins against. Each PR was green on its own: #115221's branch predates #104631's merge, and #104631 could not run the not-yet-existing test. The combination on master is what breaks. First observed in #115036 (`CI Tests`, head `1c383b2ae00`): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=1c383b2ae000d256fc2e04e60b4b4b5ddab93b96&name_0=PR&name_1=CI%20Tests ### How to reproduce On master: ``` python3 -m pytest ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_scheduling.py::test_registry_edits_do_not_schedule_a_run_without_profile_data ``` Fails at `8518542d957` (the #115221 merge commit) and on current master; the test does not exist on its parent. Possible directions (either restores the invariant): drop the registry paths from `Parser memory check`'s `digest_config` (no other job digests the registry; its own script and `utils/parser-memory-profiler/` stay), or teach the rescue pass / the test about registry-digesting consumers of build artifacts.

signal.title: Make array membership functions compare a constant `FixedString` needle zero-padded
signal.text:
Make array membership functions compare a constant `FixedString` needle zero-padded ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `has`, `indexOf`, `indexOfAssumeSorted`, `countEqual`, `mapContainsKey` and `mapContainsValue` returning a wrong result for a constant `FixedString` argument. String comparison ignores a `FixedString`'s trailing NUL padding, so `toFixedString('V0', 3)` equals both `'V0'` and `'V0\0'`, but these functions matched only one of them, and which one depended on whether the element type was wrapped in `LowCardinality`. `countEqual` under-counted and `indexOf` could return the wrong position. For a `LowCardinality` element, also fixes a constant of a different type matching a value it does not equal (`1.5` matched `1`, `-1` matched `255`, a non-midnight `DateTime` matched a `Date`), and a constant `NULL` matching the dictionary's default value. ### Description String equality is zero-padded, so `toFixedString('V0', 3)` equals both `'V0'` and `'V0\0'`. These functions reduced the needle to one exact value and matched only the member equal to it, differently in `executeString`, `executeConst` and the `LowCardinality` shortcut. A wider needle such as `toFixedString('V0', 5)` dropped every row. Rows `['V0']`, `['V0\0']`, `['X']`: | | `Array(String)` | `Array(LowCardinality(String))` | `=` | |---|---|---|---| | `has` | `[1]` | `[0]` | `[0,1]` | | `countEqual`, both members in one row | 1 | 1 | 2 | | `indexOf`, both members in one row | 2 | 1 | 1 | The comparison is now zero-padded in `executeString` and `executeConst`, using the primitive from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104858, which settled these semantics for `equals`. The `LowCardinality` shortcut resolves the needle to one dictionary index and compares indices, so it now runs only when the needle provably denotes a single element value: the width relation for the string family, otherwise a cast round trip back to the needle's own type, separating a `DateTime` at midnight (matches a `Date`) from one that is not (matches nothing). A `Float` element is refused outright: the lookup is by byte identity while `+0.0 = -0.0` and `NaN != NaN`. Declining costs the index-comparison speedup when the needle type differs from the element type, so `array_index_low_cardinality_numbers` may move. Most new assertions carry an inline `arrayExists(x -> x = needle, v)` oracle with `optimize_rewrite_array_exists_to_has = 0`, so the expected value comes from `=`. Left for their own PRs: a non-constant `FixedString` argument, `hasAny`/`hasAll`, a `bloom_filter` or text index hashing only the padded needle, and `has(map, key)`, which strips `LowCardinality` before the shortcut and so follows the plain path.
Reference change in 01414_low_cardinality_nullable Four lines move from `1` to `0`: `has(u8, -1)`, `has(u16, -1)`, `has(u32, -1)` and `has(u64, -1)` on `Array(LowCardinality(Nullable(UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64)))`. Each column stores the wrapped value (`255`, `65535`, `4294967295`, `18446744073709551615`), for which `x = -1` is false, so `has` must not match. Four independent oracles agree on `0` at every width (`arrayExists` with `=`, `arrayFilter`, `indexOf`, `countEqual`), as does scalar `=`. The reference recorded the defect. The positive control `has(u8, 255)` still returns `1`, and the `UInt8` cell is now pinned against both its `=` oracle and its plain-array control in the new test. A negative needle still matches an unsigned element in the plain `Array(UInt32/UInt64)` spelling, which has no dictionary and so reaches the integral comparison directly; that comparison suppresses `-Wsign-compare`, so `-1` equals its unsigned twin at widths 32 and 64. That is a separate pre-existing defect, measured identical before and after this change, and left for its own PR.

signal.title: Do not expose uninitialized memory in query results
signal.text: Two places where uninitialized or stale memory could end up in the result of a query: - The buffer for a binary string literal (`b'...'`) is allocated for the worst case, `ceil(bits / 8)` bytes, but when the number of bits is not a multiple of eight fewer bytes are written, and the result was built from the size of the buffer rather than from the number of bytes written. So `SELECT hex(b'000000001')` returned `01` followed by a byte of uninitialized memory. - `LZ4::decompress` returned success without writing anything when the compressed block was empty while the caller expected a non-empty result, and the caller then handed out whatever was in the destination buffer. A third one, `formatRowNoNewline` stepping the position of a shared buffer back into the previous row, was in this pull request initially; it was fixed separately in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115669, which is already in `master`, so this branch now carries the version from `master`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115669 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Do not return uninitialized memory in the result of a binary string literal whose length is not a multiple of eight, and from the LZ4 decompressor when a compressed block has no body. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115704&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115704](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115704+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Lower KeeperTCPHandler 'Client has not sent any data' log from warning to info
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/18005 `KeeperTCPHandler` logs `Client has not sent any data` at `LOG_WARNING` when a connection is opened but no data is received (the `in->eof()` branch). The same message in the server's `TCPHandler` was lowered from warning to info in #18005, but `KeeperTCPHandler` — a separate copy of the same pattern — was never updated, so it still logs at warning. Any TCP health check against the Keeper client port trips this on every probe. In particular, the ClickHouse Keeper operator's default `tcpSocket` liveness probe opens and closes a connection to the client port every few seconds, producing a steady stream of warning-level lines. This brings `KeeperTCPHandler` in line with `TCPHandler`. The nearby `LOG_WARNING` for a genuine protocol-header read error is intentionally left unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ClickHouse Keeper now logs the "Client has not sent any data" event at `Information` level instead of `Warning`, matching the server's TCP handler. This avoids spurious warnings from TCP health-check probes (for example Kubernetes `tcpSocket` liveness probes) that open and immediately close a connection to the Keeper client port. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111217&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111217](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111217+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1867` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Reload a persisted `url` table with the storage its creation selected
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not fan out the single-row output of an aggregation without keys
signal.text: After `AggregatingStep`, the pipeline was unconditionally resized to `max_threads` output streams. For an aggregation with `GROUP BY` keys that is what enables downstream parallelism, but an aggregation without keys produces at most one row: fanning that single row out to `max_threads` streams cannot create any parallelism — the only chunk still goes to one stream — while every downstream step instantiates `max_threads` processors that are created, scheduled and profiled for nothing. `AggregatingStep::transformPipeline` now keeps a single output stream when `params.keys` is empty (the same way it already does when results must be produced in order of bucket number). For example, `EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT count() FROM t` loses the `Resize 1 → <max_threads>` node and the `× <max_threads>` fan-out of every subsequent transform (see the update of `00172_early_constant_folding`). This was found while profiling tiny instant PromQL stat queries of the shape `sum(a) / sum(b)` over `TimeSeries` tables, where the emitted SQL contains several keyless aggregations and the fan-out multiplied the pipeline size; the effect is generic and this change is independent of the PromQL transpiler. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115171 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): An aggregation without `GROUP BY` keys no longer fans its single-row output out to `max_threads` streams, so queries whose plan continues after such an aggregation get a much smaller pipeline (fewer processors to create, schedule and profile) without losing any parallelism.

signal.title: Fix analyzer conflict between a column alias and a table expression alias
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/79966 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/66143 The analyzer rejected queries where a column alias coincides with the alias of a table expression in the `FROM` section: ```sql SELECT number AS test_name FROM (SELECT * FROM numbers(1000)) AS test_name ``` ``` Code: 179. DB::Exception: Duplicate aliases test_name for table expressions in FROM section are not allowed. Try to register SELECT * FROM numbers(1000). Already registered number AS test_name. (MULTIPLE_EXPRESSIONS_FOR_ALIAS) ``` This is a regression from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/66143 (25.2): `QueryExpressionsAliasVisitor` started to speculatively register aliased short identifiers from expression sections (e.g. the projection `number AS test_name`) in the table expression alias map, because such an alias can transitively name a table expression. When a table expression in the `FROM` section has the same alias, its registration in `resolveQueryJoinTreeNode` collided with the speculative entry, and the query was rejected. The same conflict also affected aliases of `ARRAY JOIN` result columns and identifier aliases defined in the `WITH` section. Now the actual table expression takes over the alias in the table expression namespace, which matches the old analyzer behavior: a column alias and a table expression alias live in different namespaces, and for table lookups the alias from the `FROM` section wins. Genuine duplicate aliases between table expressions are still rejected by `TableExpressionsAliasVisitor`, which runs before this code. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the `MULTIPLE_EXPRESSIONS_FOR_ALIAS` error in queries where a column alias coincides with the alias of a table expression in the `FROM` section (an analyzer regression in version 25.2). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115714&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115714](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115714+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `to_utc_timestamp` and `from_utc_timestamp` are ~2.7x slower for `DateTime64` after the overflow fix
signal.text: The performance test `utc_timestamp_transform` shows that `to_utc_timestamp` and `from_utc_timestamp` on a `DateTime64` argument became ~2.7 times slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. The `DateTime` variants of the same queries did not regress, which points directly at the `DateTime64` overflow fix. Queries (from `tests/performance/utc_timestamp_transform.xml`, `test2` is `CREATE TABLE test2(d DateTime64) ENGINE Memory` with 10M rows): ```sql select count(1) from test2 where to_utc_timestamp(d, 'Etc/GMT+1') > '1990-01-01 12:00:00' SETTINGS max_threads=1 select count(1) from test2 where from_utc_timestamp(d, 'Etc/GMT+1') > '1990-01-01 12:00:00' SETTINGS max_threads=1 ``` Measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `to_utc_timestamp(DateTime64)` | 0.067 s | 0.182 s | **+172%** | | `from_utc_timestamp(DateTime64)` | 0.067 s | 0.182 s | **+172%** | The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit 3566f9010eaeca8ad8bdabf7dbd8cd536cdb2cdf on 2026-07-30, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. The overflow check is needed for correctness, but a 2.7x slowdown suggests it is done per row in a way that defeats vectorization or adds a per-row branch/exception path; it should be possible to keep saturating/checked behavior much cheaper (e.g. hoisting the timezone offset computation or checking bounds on the whole column). Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109738 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=3566f9010eae This is one of the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @groeneai

signal.title: Hide aws_external_id in DataLakeCatalog SHOW CREATE DATABASE
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114999 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Mask the `aws_external_id` setting of the `DataLakeCatalog` database engine in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` and `system.databases.engine_full`. It was previously printed in plaintext, unlike the other AWS credential settings. Closes: #114999 ### Description `aws_external_id` was missing from `DataLake::SETTINGS_TO_HIDE`, so any user able to run `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` or read `system.databases` saw it verbatim at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Every other credential setting of the engine was already masked. Root cause: `ASTSetQuery::formatImpl` consults that map to decide whether to print a masking rule instead of the value; the key was absent, so the fallthrough printed the secret. This adds the missing entry. Both surfaces share one seam (`StorageSystemDatabases` builds `engine_full` with the same formatter `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` uses), and the map also backs `ASTSetQuery::hasSecretParts`, so log masking is covered too. The stored metadata and replicated-DDL propagation format with secrets shown, so the database still authenticates after a restart. The codebase already classifies the value as a secret: `external_id` is a member of `s3_secret_keys` in `src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.h`, whose comment calls it the shared secret of the assume-role triple while `role_arn` and `role_session_name` are non-secret identifiers that stay visible. So the identical value was masked in the inline `s3()` form and leaked only here. `aws_role_arn` and `aws_role_session_name` are therefore left visible, and the new test pins them visible so a future over-masking change fails. Validation: new stateless test `05030_datalake_catalog_hide_aws_external_id.sh` asserts `[HIDDEN]` at the default and the true value still retrievable with `clickhouse-format --show_secrets`, so the fix redacts rather than destroys. It fails on master and passes here; 50 randomized runs of it and of the neighbouring `04401` pass. signal.title: Support the plan-based parallel replicas in automatic parallel replicas
signal.text: Automatic parallel replicas builds a plan with parallel replicas, finds the node that would sit at the top of the plan executed on the replicas, and instruments the corresponding node of the single-node plan to collect runtime dataflow statistics. `findTopNodeOfReplicasPlan` located that node by matching the branch that reads from the other replicas against `ReadFromParallelRemoteReplicasStep`. With `parallel_replicas_plan_based` that branch is a `ReadFromParallelReplicas` step, which ships a serialized plan fragment instead of a query. The rest of the plan is shaped exactly the same - a `Union` of the local branch and the branch reading from the other replicas - but the top node was never found, so no statistics were collected and automatic parallel replicas never enabled parallel replicas for any query. This recognizes both steps. Verified against a local server with `parallel_replicas_plan_based=1`: 10 of the 12 `*_autopr_*` stateless tests that fail with the plan-based implementation as the default now pass. The remaining two are left for a follow-up and keep the previous behaviour of skipping the optimization: - `04341_autopr_mode1_apply_join` - with join runtime filters the plan-based local branch carries an extra pass-through `Expression`, so the node hashes of the two plans differ and no match is found. - `03634_autopr_input_bytes_estimation_compact` - for a plain read the plan fragment is the reading step itself, which cannot estimate the number of bytes sent to the initiator. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112351 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Automatic parallel replicas can now collect runtime statistics and enable parallel replicas for supported queries when `parallel_replicas_plan_based` is enabled.

signal.title: Gate the release_base perf comparison on the delta to the previous master run
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115802 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115803 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115804 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115805 The `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, N/6)` checks compare each master commit against the build at the latest release branch point, so every performance change since that point accumulates in the report. With the absolute slower-count gate (more than `SLOWER_QUERIES_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 10` per shard), the check inevitably drifts into permanent red: shard `3/6` failed on all 198 master commits of the past week (28 accumulated slower queries), was red for the entire previous release cycle as well, and only went green for two weeks after the 26.7 branch cut reset the baseline. A permanently red check points at no specific commit and trains everyone to ignore it — meanwhile real regressions (see the linked issues) land silently because the per-commit `master_head` mode rarely exceeds 10 slower queries for a single PR. This PR changes the `release_base` gate to fail only on a large delta to the previous master commit: the job fetches the previous valid master run's result from S3 (walking `master_track_commits_sha`, skipping runs that produced no report or ended with errors) and fails when the slower count grew by more than `SLOWER_QUERIES_DELTA_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 5`. Red now blames the commit that introduced the regression and recovers on the next commit by itself. If no previous run can be found, the gate falls back to the old absolute threshold. The reported message is extended with the delta, e.g. `5 too long, 24 faster, 28 slower; delta vs prev master run (5ad58af3): +2`. The `master_head` mode keeps the absolute gate. The threshold is based on 10 days of master runs: run-to-run count-delta noise is p90 ≤ 3 per shard (max 3–7 outside of regression landings), while real regression landings showed +8..+16. Replayed over 58 real master runs of the always-red shard `3/6`: 57 turn green and the only `FAIL` lands exactly on the commit that introduced the `direct_dictionary` regression (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115803). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115821&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115821](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115821+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not merge over a gap containing an outdated part with a higher mutation version
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113864 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Part ... intersects previous part ... It is a bug or a result of manual intervention`) that makes a `MergeTree` table impossible to load: attaching it, and every later attempt to load it, fails with that exception (a server abort in debug and sanitizer builds). A merge could span a block gap holding an outdated part whose mutation version is higher than the merge result's, producing a pair of parts on disk that neither contain nor are disjoint from each other. Closes #113864. ### Description A merge is refused when the block gap it spans holds an outdated part the merge result would not cover. That check compared only the part **level**, while `MergeTreePartInfo::contains` requires both `level >=` and `mutation >=`. An outdated part left by a mutation has level 0, so the check could not see it and the merge produced an intersecting, mutually non-containing pair. Every later part load (`ATTACH TABLE`, or a server restart) then throws; in debug and sanitizer builds that exception aborts the server. Such a gap appears when parts owe different mutation stacks. In the reported case a mutation succeeded on one part (version 59) and threw on its neighbour (left at 45); once killed, the surrounding parts merged into `all_43_62_1_45`, which does not contain the intervening `all_57_57_0_59`. Later no-op merges carried that result to `all_43_62_5_45`, the name in the reported message. `getMaxLevelInBetween` now also accumulates the maximum mutation version over the gap and is renamed `getMaxLevelMutationInBetween`, and `canMergeParts` refuses the merge when that version exceeds `max(left.mutation, right.mutation)`. That is the pairwise maximum rather than the exact result version, which is only known later in `FutureMergedMutatedPart::assign`; since the exact version is a maximum over a superset of any adjacent pair, this can refuse a merge early but never admits one it should refuse. The refusal is non-fatal: the merge is deferred until `old_parts_lifetime` removes the outdated part. The replicated merge predicate has no such hole: it probes the gap with a synthetic part at `MAX_LEVEL`/`MAX_BLOCK_NUMBER`, which dominates on both terms. Validation: on a debug build the new test aborts the server without this change and passes with it; reverting only the added term reddens it while `02521_merge_over_gap` (the existing level-shape test) stays green. A slice of 261 merge/optimize/mutation tests shows no regressions, and the test passes 50/50. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113941&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113941](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113941+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `GradualResizeProcessor` to limit effective parallelism for GROUP BY on small data volumes
signal.text: When ClickHouse processes GROUP BY, it often overestimates the number of threads needed. With `max_threads = 64` but only a few thousand rows, all 64 `AggregatingTransform` instances get data, produce 64 partial hash tables, and the merge phase has to combine all of them — most nearly empty. This wastes time on merging overhead, which is especially noticeable for heavy aggregate states such as `uniq`, `uniqExact`, `groupArray`, etc. The new `GradualResizeProcessor` starts by pushing data to a single output port (or one port per split group when `min_outstreams_per_resize_after_split` applies), and activates all aggregation streams at once as soon as the configured row or byte threshold is crossed. For small datasets, only one aggregating thread receives data (or one per split group); for large datasets, all threads are used as before. New settings: - `min_rows_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` (default: `0`) - `min_bytes_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` (default: `0`) Both settings default to `0`, so the optimization is opt-in. Set either setting to a non-zero threshold to replace the pre-aggregation `StrictResize` with `GradualResize` for keyed `GROUP BY` queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add opt-in settings `min_rows_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` and `min_bytes_per_stream_for_gradual_resize` that can improve `GROUP BY` performance on small data volumes. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=99495&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/99495](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F99495+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
