signal.title: `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER` with literal shard/replica names makes two servers the same `Replicated` replica: LOGICAL_ERROR and crash loop (debug), permanently wedged database (release)
signal.text: 🕵️ ### Describe the bug A `Replicated` database created with `ON CLUSTER` and *literal* shard/replica names — instead of the `{shard}`/`{replica}` macros — registers every host in the cluster as the **same** replica. One of the servers then hits ``` Logical error: 'Ephemeral node /clickhouse/databases/<db>/replicas/s1|d1/active still exists after 45s, probably it's owned by someone else. ...' ``` and aborts (debug/sanitizer builds), re-aborting ~45 s after every restart. On release builds it does not abort, but the database becomes permanently unusable on **both** servers. The same misconfiguration is correctly rejected when the two `CREATE DATABASE` statements are run separately on each server: ``` Code: 253. DB::Exception: Replica d1 of shard s1 of replicated database at /clickhouse/databases/db already exists. Replica host ID: 'host:30301:<uuid>', current host ID: 'host:30302:<uuid>'. (REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS) ``` `ON CLUSTER` defeats that guard. A distributed `CREATE DATABASE` assigns **one database UUID to every host**, so on the second host `DatabaseReplicated::initDatabaseReplica` finds a `replica_path` whose stored `host_id` differs from its own but whose embedded UUID matches, takes the "same UUID, the interserver address must have changed" branch, overwrites `host_id` with its own and continues: ```cpp if (uuid_in_keeper != db_uuid) throw Exception(ErrorCodes::REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS, ...); // After restarting, InterserverIOAddress might change ... // If the UUID in the keeper is the same as the current server UUID, we will update the host_id in keeper current_zookeeper->set(replica_path, host_id, -1); ``` That branch is right for its intended case (the same server coming back under a new FQDN/port, when no other server is live), but here the other host is alive and holding `/replicas/s1|d1/active`. Both `DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker`s then fight over that ephemeral node, and the loser waits `3 * session_timeout_ms` in `zkutil::ZooKeeper::deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches` before raising `LOGICAL_ERROR`. Found by the `La Casa Del Dolor` CI job (amd_debug) on #94148: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=e43941717e2178c119882d2b41b874d625613dd3&name_0=PR The fuzzer's statement was ```sql CREATE DATABASE d0 ON CLUSTER 'allnodes' ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/d0', 's1', 'd1'); ``` ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes. Reproduced on master `26.8.1.1` (debug+UBSan, `0c8a8f100913887455521757dba3e4ec0e0fbc67`) and on the `26.8.1.1833` official release build. ### How to reproduce Two servers sharing one Keeper, both listed in a cluster. `session_timeout_ms` is lowered only to shorten the wait from 90 s to 15 s; the bug does not depend on it. `node1` (also runs Keeper), `config.xml`: ```xml <clickhouse> <tcp_port>30301</tcp_port> <http_port>30341</http_port> <interserver_http_port>30351</interserver_http_port> <path>/tmp/chA/data/</path> <zookeeper> <node><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>9181</port></node> <session_timeout_ms>5000</session_timeout_ms> </zookeeper> <distributed_ddl><path>/clickhouse/task_queue/ddl</path></distributed_ddl> <remote_servers> <two><shard> <replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>30301</port></replica> <replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>30302</port></replica> </shard></two> </remote_servers> <keeper_server> <tcp_port>9181</tcp_port> <server_id>1</server_id> <log_storage_path>/tmp/chA/data/coordination/log</log_storage_path> <snapshot_storage_path>/tmp/chA/data/coordination/snapshots</snapshot_storage_path> <raft_configuration><server><id>1</id><hostname>127.0.0.1</hostname><port>9234</port></server></raft_configuration> </keeper_server> </clickhouse> ``` `node2`: the same file with `tcp_port` 30302, `http_port` 30342, `interserver_http_port` 30352, `path` `/tmp/chB/data/` and no `<keeper_server>` section. Then, on either node, a single query: ```sql CREATE DATABASE dtest ON CLUSTER 'two' ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/dtest', 's1', 'd1'); ``` It reports success on both hosts: ``` 127.0.0.1 30301 0 1 1 127.0.0.1 30302 0 0 0 ``` 15 s later (`3 * session_timeout_ms`) one of the two servers aborts. Both servers end up with the same database UUID, and the single replica znode is owned by whichever server took it over last: ``` :) SELECT name, value FROM system.zookeeper WHERE path='/clickhouse/databases/dtest/replicas'; s1|d1 host:30302:4d9f5111-fa11-4ec2-b3c8-d3fbeb5091c7 -- same UUID as node1's `dtest` ``` **Debug/sanitizer builds** — the losing server aborts with signal 6. Because the metadata is already on disk, it comes up on restart, serves queries for 15 s and aborts again: a permanent crash loop. **Release builds** (verified on `26.8.1.1833`) — no abort, but: - the losing DDL worker retries forever, logging every ~20 s: `<Error> DDLWorker(dtest): Error on initialization of dtest: Code: 49. DB::Exception: Ephemeral node ... still exists after 15s` - `CREATE TABLE dtest.x (c0 Int) ENGINE = Null` **hangs indefinitely on both nodes**, including with `distributed_ddl_task_timeout=3`; the database accepts no DDL at all, on either server - the two servers keep taking `host_id` from each other, so the replica's registered address flips between them - `system.clusters` for the database shows a single host, so `ON CLUSTER` routing for that database is broken too `SELECT` and `SHOW TABLES` still work, and the rest of the server is unaffected — the damage is confined to that database, but it is not recoverable without manual Keeper/metadata surgery. ### Expected behavior `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER` with a replica name already held by a *different, live* server should fail with `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS`, exactly like the non-distributed path already does, and in no case should a user-reachable misconfiguration produce a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. ### Suggested fix **Not by rejecting `ON CLUSTER`.** Every use of it with a `Replicated` database in this repo pairs it with macros — `ON CLUSTER 'cluster' ENGINE=Replicated('/clickhouse/path/','{shard}','{replica}')` in `test_backup_restore_on_cluster`, and the same shape in `test_external_cluster`, `test_refreshable_mat_view_replicated`, `02859_replicated_db_name_zookeeper.sh` and others — so it is the normal way to provision such a database, and banning it would be a breaking change. It would also close only one of the entrances: the precondition is *two hosts holding the same database UUID*, which `ON CLUSTER` produces, but so does an explicit `CREATE DATABASE x UUID '...' ENGINE = Replicated(...)` run on both hosts, and so does restoring one backup onto two hosts. **The UUID match is being read as "this is me" when it only means "this is the same database".** Making the takeover conditional on the replica not being live fixes that, in `DatabaseReplicated::initDatabaseReplica`, right after the existing `uuid_in_keeper != db_uuid` throw: ```cpp /// The UUID matching only means "same database", not "same server": ON CLUSTER hands every host /// one db_uuid, so two hosts given the same replica name land here. Taking the replica over while /// the other host is alive leaves both DDL workers fighting for `<replica_path>/active`. String active_id; if (current_zookeeper->tryGet(fs::path(replica_path) / "active", active_id)) { if (active_id.ends_with(REPLICA_UNSYNCED_MARKER)) active_id.resize(active_id.size() - strlen(REPLICA_UNSYNCED_MARKER)); if (active_id != toString(ServerUUID::get())) throw Exception( ErrorCodes::REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS, "Replica {} of shard {} of replicated database at {} is active on another server " "(host ID: '{}'). If the database is created with ON CLUSTER, use the {{shard}} and " "{{replica}} macros instead of literal names.", replica_name, shard_name, zookeeper_path, replica_host_id); } ``` Comparing against our own `ServerUUID` is what keeps the case the branch was written for working: the same server restarting finds its own stale ephemeral node and still takes the replica over. **One race remains, and it is why the severity matters too.** With `ON CLUSTER` both hosts run the CREATE simultaneously, so both can see no `active` node yet and pass the check above. The loser should then get an ordinary error rather than a `LOGICAL_ERROR`: ```cpp // ZooKeeper.h / ZooKeeper.cpp - the default keeps today's behaviour for the other callers void deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches(const std::string & path, std::function<bool(const std::string &)> condition, int error_code = ErrorCodes::LOGICAL_ERROR); ``` with `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS` passed from `DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:181`. That leaves the five other callers (`ReplicatedMergeTreeRestartingThread`, `StorageKafka2`, `DDLWorker` ×2) untouched — though the same argument arguably applies to them, since "another server holds my `is_active` node" is a misconfiguration rather than a broken internal invariant anywhere it occurs. Optionally, as a usability layer rather than part of the fix: reject `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER c ENGINE = Replicated(path, shard, replica)` on the initiator when neither name contains a macro and `c` has more than one host. That catches this shape before anything is written to Keeper, with a message saying what to write instead. Together that is roughly 20 lines, plus a test — two servers are needed, so `tests/integration/test_replicated_database/`, whose fixtures already provide the topology. ### Error message and/or stacktrace From the CI job (amd_debug, 26.8.1.1): ``` <Fatal> : Logical error: 'Ephemeral node /clickhouse/databases/d0/replicas/s1|d1/active still exists after 45s, probably it's owned by someone else. Either session_timeout_ms in client's config is different from server's config or it's a bug. Node data: '4463091c-64a0-4f2a-bc0b-e2eafcb97be1''. Stack trace: src/Common/Exception.cpp:66:5: DB::abortOnFailedAssertion(...) src/Common/Exception.cpp:115:13: DB::Exception::handleErrorCode(...) src/Common/Exception.cpp:171:19: DB::Exception::Exception(DB::Exception::MessageMasked&&, int, bool) src/Common/ZooKeeper/ZooKeeper.cpp:1462:19: zkutil::ZooKeeper::deleteEphemeralNodeIfContentMatches(String const&, std::function<bool (String const&)>) src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:181:16: DB::DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker::initializeReplication() src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:121:13: DB::DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker::initializeMainThread() src/Interpreters/DDLWorker.cpp:1305:22: DB::DDLWorker::runMainThread() ``` Preceded by: ``` <Warning> ZooKeeper: Ephemeral node ('/clickhouse/databases/dtest/replicas/s1|d1/active') already exists but it isn't owned by us. Will wait until it disappears ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Four closed issues carry the same error string, none of them with this cause — listed so triage does not close this as a duplicate of one of them: - #68570 — same LOGICAL_ERROR in `DatabaseReplicated`, from a stress run. signal.title: RESTORE DATABASE ... AS ... corrupts/crashes views using FROM table AS alias FINAL,  other_table
signal.text: ### Company or project name Critical Manufacturing S.A. ### Describe what's wrong Restoring a database backup under a different name (`RESTORE DATABASE src AS dst FROM ...`) mishandles views whose `SELECT` uses a table alias immediately followed by `FINAL` in a multi-table (comma-joined) `FROM t1 AS a FINAL, t2 AS b`. This is valid, documented syntax (["When a table has an alias, FINAL must come after the alias, not before it"](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/from#final-modifier)), and views are created and queried correctly before any rename-restore. Depending on the query's complexity, this produces one of two failures only when the database is renamed during restore: 1. Silent alias drop (minimal repro below): the restored view's stored definition loses the alias(es) entirely, silently corrupting the view — it then fails when queried. 2. Hard crash (seen on a more complex, real production view with CTEs/multiple joins — full trace below): the restore itself fails with a `SYNTAX_ERROR` while ClickHouse tries to re-resolve the qualified table name for the rename. No issue occurs if the database is restored under its original name (no `AS `) or if the `CREATE VIEW` is executed directly (not via backup/restore) — pointing at the backup-restore-time table-name rewrite (`DB::BackupMetadataFinder::findTableInBackupImpl`) as the common cause, not the general SQL parser. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce Tested and reproducible in these versions: - 25.3.6.56 - 26.3.9.8 - **26.3.19.3** ``` CREATE DATABASE testdb; USE testdb; CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt32, val String) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t2 (id UInt32, label String) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (1, 'a'); INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (1, 'x'); CREATE VIEW v1 AS SELECT a.id, b.label FROM t1 AS a FINAL, t2 AS b WHERE a.id = b.id; -- Works fine so far: SELECT * FROM v1; BACKUP DATABASE testdb TO Disk('backups', 'repro_backup'); --Restoring under a DIFFERENT name silently drops both aliases from the view definition: RESTORE DATABASE testdb AS restoredtestdb FROM Disk('backups', 'repro_backup'); USE restoredtestdb; SHOW CREATE VIEW v1; -- Actual: -- FROM restoredtestdb.t1 -- FINAL, -- restoredtestdb.t2 -- WHERE a.id = b.id -- (aliases `a` and `b` are gone, but the WHERE clause still references them) SELECT * FROM v1; -- Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown expression identifier `a.id` in scope -- SELECT a.id, b.label FROM restoredtestdb.t1 FINAL, restoredtestdb.t2 WHERE a.id = b.id. -- Maybe you meant: ['t1.id']. (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) -- Restoring under the ORIGINAL name works correctly (no alias loss): DROP DATABASE testdb; RESTORE DATABASE testdb FROM Disk('backups', 'repro_backup'); USE testdb; SHOW CREATE VIEW v1; -- Actual: -- FROM testdb.t1 AS a -- FINAL, -- restoredtestdb.t2 AS b -- WHERE a.id = b.id -- (aliases `a` and `b` are present) SELECT * FROM v1; ``` ### Expected behavior Aliases are kept when restoring with a rename. Fix expected for 26.3 LTS. ### Error message and/or stacktrace Complete statements and error messages present as comments in the reproduction example. ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Version info - Resolved by: #115645 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1859` (included in `26.8` and later)

signal.title: Add a TOLERANCE clause to ASOF JOIN
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109034 `ASOF JOIN` matches the closest row however far away it is, so a trade can be matched against a quote from hours earlier. `TOLERANCE` bounds that distance: ```sql SELECT trades.time, trades.price, quotes.bid FROM trades ASOF LEFT JOIN quotes ON trades.symbol = quotes.symbol AND trades.time >= quotes.time TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND ``` The bound is inclusive. With `ASOF LEFT JOIN` a row whose closest match is out of tolerance is kept with default or `NULL` values on the right, following `join_use_nulls`, which is what `pandas.merge_asof(tolerance=...)` does. With `ASOF JOIN` it is dropped, like a row with no match at all. It can be written as an `INTERVAL`, or as a plain number in the units of the `ASOF` column. For a `DateTime64(3)` column `TOLERANCE 5000` and `TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND` are the same bound. ### Implementation notes The bound is converted into the units of the `ASOF` key once, during planning, so the join implementation compares it against key values directly with no per-probe conversion. `findAsof` already returns the closest match in the direction the inequality fixes, so if that one is out of bounds no other can be closer and the probe has no match. The interval unit is read from the result type rather than from the shape of the expression: `INTERVAL 5 SECOND` is written `toIntervalSecond(5)` but is constant folded during resolution into a constant whose value is `5` and whose type is `IntervalSecond`, so treating it as a bare number silently means five milliseconds against a `DateTime64(3)` key. ### Rejected rather than approximated - `MONTH`, `QUARTER` and `YEAR`, which are not fixed lengths of time. - An `INTERVAL` against an `ASOF` key that is not a date or time, where the unit would be undefined. - A bound finer than the key's resolution, such as `INTERVAL 1 MICROSECOND` against `DateTime64(3)`, which would otherwise round down to "exact matches only". - A negative bound, which nothing can satisfy. - `enable_analyzer = 0`, which builds `TableJoin` without the query tree the bound travels on and would silently ignore it. - `full_sorting_merge`, which matches through `IColumn::compareAt` and so has ordering but not distance. The planner falls back to another enabled algorithm; if only `full_sorting_merge` is enabled the query fails. Each of these silently returns matches further away than the query asked for if it is accepted instead, which is the failure this clause exists to prevent. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `TOLERANCE` clause to `ASOF JOIN`, bounding how far apart the left and the matched right value of the `ASOF` column may be, so that stale rows are not matched. The bound can be given as an `INTERVAL` or as a number in the units of the `ASOF` column, for example `ASOF LEFT JOIN quotes ON trades.symbol = quotes.symbol AND trades.time >= quotes.time TOLERANCE INTERVAL 5 SECOND`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115530&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115530](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115530+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not strand processors queued for removal in `ExecutingGraph`
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115625 Processor removal in `ExecutingGraph` recently became deferred: `updatePipeline` only records `update.to_remove` into a pending group, and `updateNode` retires that group once every processor in it reports `Finished`. Two paths leave a recorded group behind, so its processors stay in the pipeline until the whole query is destroyed: - `updatePipeline` records the group and then returns `Cancelled`, which makes `updateNode` return before it reaches the code that retires groups; - the retiring code handles a single group per prepared node, so a backlog can outlive the last `updateNode` call. This change retires every group that is ready instead of just one, and also retires them on the way out when `updatePipeline` does not return `Done`. This is what `Processors.UpdatePipelineMultipleCoordinatorsMultithreaded` caught on master — it cancels the executor while 16 coordinators are cycling, so one of them gets its removal stranded and an extra source is still alive at the end of the test: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b16561cc816cf56cadd0c35ed9ad48964ad7758d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%29 ``` src/Processors/tests/gtest_update_pipeline.cpp:504 Expected: (alive) <= (1u), actual: 2 vs 1 ``` The existing test only reproduces this rarely, so a deterministic one is added: `Processors.UpdatePipelineRemovalIsNotStrandedByCancellation` cancels the pipeline from inside `prepare`, so the `updatePipeline` that retires the source is exactly the one that observes the cancellation. It fails before this change and passes after it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115800&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115800](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115800+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix stale MATERIALIZED column values read through a chain while a mutation is pending
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100613 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50237 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99281 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115371 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115372 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115638 **Scope changed.** The staging half of this pull request — recomputing a chain of `MATERIALIZED` columns one dependency level at a time during a mutation — landed on master in the meantime via #103182, which also generalizes it to `APPLY PATCHES`, so all of it was dropped here. What remains is the read path, which master still gets wrong: the read set is closed in `AlterConversions`, and `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` keeps a single line of change, resolving `MATERIALIZED` defaults against the whole table instead of the read task's columns. The two defects that belong to the staging path are split out into #115371 and #115372. ## Problem With a mutation still pending, reading a `MATERIALIZED` column that reaches the updated column only through another `MATERIALIZED` column returns the stale on-disk value, while reading the whole chain returns the recomputed one: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, y Int32, m1 Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1, m2 Int32 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1, m3 Int32 MATERIALIZED m2 + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t (x, y) VALUES (10, 0); SYSTEM STOP MERGES t; SET alter_sync = 0, mutations_sync = 0, apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending ``` ``` SELECT m2 FROM t; -- 12 (stale; must be 22) SELECT m3 FROM t; -- 13 (stale; must be 23) SELECT x, m1, m2, m3 FROM t; -- 20 21 22 23 (correct) ``` - The result of a query depends on which columns it selects, so the same value read two ways disagrees. - The same happens for a `MATERIALIZED` column defined over a subcolumn (`m1 MATERIALIZED t.a + 1` with a pending `UPDATE t = ...`): `SELECT m1` returns the stale value unless the query happens to select `t` as well. - Selecting a `MATERIALIZED` column together with a column the mutation updates fails outright with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` whenever the first one's dependencies are not in the select list, even when that column has nothing to do with the mutation. - Once the mutation finishes, the values are correct — only the pending window is affected. ## Root cause Reading with `apply_mutations_on_fly` builds the pending commands into the read pipeline. `AlterConversions::addColumnsRequiredForMaterialized` decides which extra columns must be read so that the `MATERIALIZED` columns being selected can be recomputed, and it only looked one hop deep: ```cpp for (const auto & column_name : read_columns_set) if (default is MATERIALIZED) for (const auto & dependency : TreeRewriter(context).analyze(expression, source_columns)->requiredSourceColumns()) if (all_updated_columns.contains(dependency)) required_source_columns.insert(dependency); ``` For `m2 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1` the only dependency is `m1`, which is not in `all_updated_columns`, so nothing is added, `filterMutationCommands` drops the `UPDATE x` command as irrelevant to the read set, and `m2` is returned from disk. Two further details of the same analysis: - the default expression is not normalized with `replaceSubcolumnsToGetSubcolumnFunctionInQuery`, so `m MATERIALIZED t.a` is seen to depend on `t.a` rather than on `t`, and a pending `UPDATE t` is filtered out (or the analysis fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` when the subcolumn does not resolve against `source_columns`); - a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an `EPHEMERAL` column can never be recomputed outside `INSERT`, so analysing it against physical columns must be avoided rather than attempted. ## Solution Two sites, because the read set has two consumers that must agree. ### `AlterConversions::addColumnsRequiredForMaterialized` — close the read set 1. **Transitive closure.** A breadth-first walk seeded with the read columns replaces the single pass, so the `MATERIALIZED` columns in between are read too and the interpreter recomputes the whole chain instead of `filterMutationCommands` dropping the `UPDATE` as irrelevant. 2. **Only a column that is recalculated pulls in dependencies, and it pulls in all of them.** The walk asks of the column it visits whether the interpreter recalculates it, and if so takes its whole expression, because the stage that rewrites it evaluates that expression against the block — including the part reading a column no mutation touches (`c MATERIALIZED m1 + y`, where `y` is untouched). A column that keeps its stored value contributes nothing, so a chain whose value cannot change is not read. 3. **Subcolumn rewrite.** Dependencies are analysed after `replaceSubcolumnsToGetSubcolumnFunctionInQuery`, matching what `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` does before analysing the same expression. Without it `m MATERIALIZED t.a + 1` is seen to depend on `t.a` while `all_updated_columns` holds `t`; the names do not match and a pending `UPDATE t` is filtered out. This is a one-hop defect, independent of the chain. 4. **`EPHEMERAL` columns added to the analysis source list.** `getAllPhysical` excludes them, so analysing `me MATERIALIZED x + e` threw `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` inside this function. Measured on master, `SELECT me` with any pending `UPDATE` fails this way. Also a one-hop defect, and analysing every hop of a chain would have multiplied its reach. 5. **The `EPHEMERAL` test mirrors the interpreter's policy, and keeps a pass of its own.** `MutationsInterpreter` never recomputes a `MATERIALIZED` column that reads an `EPHEMERAL` one, so such a column is not treated as recalculable here either — the read set must not promise a recomputation the interpreter refuses. It cannot share the loop that looks for a changed dependency: that loop stops at the first one it finds, while this test quantifies over all of them, so interleaving them skips it exactly when a dependency is updated. 6. **Memoised lookups.** `getMutationSteps` runs per read task per part, so each default expression is analysed at most once per call and each reachability question answered at most once. ### `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` — resolve defaults against the whole table `available_columns` was serving two different roles: which `MATERIALIZED` columns need recalculating, and which columns their expressions may be resolved against. For a plain `UPDATE` the two coincide. A table carrying a `MATERIALIZED` column the mutation does not affect breaks the coincidence — its dependencies are legitimately outside the read set — and the analysis failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, taking the query with it: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, y Int32, m Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1, n Int32 MATERIALIZED y + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending SELECT m, n FROM t; -- Missing columns: 'y' while processing: 'y + 1' SELECT x, n FROM t; -- the same, and this one fails on master too ``` Deciding whether a column has to be recalculated must not require reading what it reads, so the default expressions are now resolved against every column of the table. Only an on-fly read has a narrow list: a materialising mutation passes `getNamesOfPhysical()`, so the only columns this adds there are virtual ones, which a `MATERIALIZED` default cannot reference — `CREATE` and `ALTER` both reject that. The list is built on first use. Copying it costs a node per column of the table, the loop needs it only for a `MATERIALIZED` column the task reads, and an on-fly read reaches it per part. Widening `need_materialized_analysis` instead would have been wrong: `validateUpdateColumns` runs at the end of the same block, so guarding the block would drop the check that rejects an `ALTER UPDATE` of a key or `MATERIALIZED` column on every table without `MATERIALIZED` columns. ### Taken from #115638 @Avogar tried an alternative on top of this branch in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115638 and asked for it to be moved here. It is in as of `4bec5ca8a1a`, applied verbatim — the test files this branch already carried are byte-identical in it, and `Settings::apply_on_fly_for_read` is kept. What it adds over the two sites above: - **`MaterializedColumnDependencies`** — the dependency graph over a table's `MATERIALIZED` columns, built once and shared by the read path and `MutationsInterpreter` instead of being derived separately in each, so the two can no longer disagree about how a dependency is spelled. This is also the graph @Avogar needs in #112717. - **The closure and the command filter now run to a fixed point.** `filterMutationCommands` puts the columns a surviving command reads into the read set, and one of those can itself be a `MATERIALIZED` column of a chain (`DELETE WHERE m2 > 100`), which can in turn keep an older command alive. Closing and filtering used to run once each, in that order, so a chain reached from a `DELETE` predicate or an `UPDATE` expression stayed stale. They now iterate until the set stops growing; it only grows and is bounded by the width of the table, so it terminates. - **A command may name a subcolumn as written (`t.a`)** while the read set is keyed on storage columns, which made every read of the table fail with `NO_SUCH_COLUMN_IN_TABLE`. Names now go through `getNameInStorage` on the way in. This one reproduces on master. - **One `buildMutationChainForRead`** shared by `getMutationSteps` and `getMutationActions`, instead of each recomputing the read set and the command filter. ### A `MATERIALIZED` column over an `ALIAS` column Also fixed here, in `aeda9610380`, because after the extraction there is exactly one place to do it. A `MATERIALIZED` default may read an `ALIAS` column, and that made **every** mutation on the table throw, including one updating a column the expression never mentions: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, z Int32, a Int32 ALIAS x + 100, m Int32 MATERIALIZED a + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t UPDATE z = 5 WHERE 1; -- Code: 47. Missing columns: 'a' while processing: 'a + 1' ... (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) ``` The list the default is analysed against is the physical one and an `ALIAS` is physical-excluded. Merely adding aliases to it would let `TreeRewriter` resolve the name, but the expression would then still read `a` at execution time and no part has such a column, so the recompute stage would fail on it instead. The reference is replaced by the expression it stands for, with `ReplaceAliasByExpressionMatcher` — the same visitor `IndexDescription::initExpressionInfo` uses so a skip index can reference an `ALIAS` column. `MaterializedColumnDependencies` hands the same expression to the dependency analysis and to the recompute stage, so one expansion reaches both; it runs before the subcolumn rewrite, so a subcolumn reached through an alias is normalised too. Unlike the `EPHEMERAL` case next to it there is no trade-off: `m` recalculates correctly from the stored `x`, and an `ALIAS` column is recomputed per query so it can never itself be stale. ### Not proposed for backport The change started as a narrow read-path fix, but with the dependency graph extracted into a new component shared by two subsystems it is no longer a good backport candidate, and it is not labelled for one. ### Coverage Regression test `04869_materialized_chain_on_fly_read` covers six cases, each measured individually against master `5bd006cd298`: - the plain chain read tail-only — returns the stale value; - the chain read next to the updated column, without the intermediate hop — throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, because the surviving command makes the interpreter analyse a default whose dependency is not in the read set; - one command assigning two columns, with the query reading the other assignment target — throws for the same reason, after the command is narrowed and loses the assignment the chain depends on; - a pending `DELETE` that keeps a command alive while the set of updated columns stays empty — returns the stale value, since the analysis is skipped entirely; - columns the mutation does not affect, read on their own and next to the updated column, and a recalculated column reading an untouched one — stale value or `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` depending on the select list; - the subcolumn default and the `EPHEMERAL`-derived column — stale value and `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` respectively. `04926_on_fly_mutation_read_set_closure` covers the cases the read-set closure loop repairs: the chain reached from a pending `DELETE` predicate, a subcolumn spelled as written in a command, and the cases that must not move. `05024_materialized_over_alias_column_mutation` covers the `ALIAS` case, measured both ways on a Debug build: without the expansion `UPDATE z = 5` and `UPDATE x = 20` both throw `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`; with it the first leaves `m` alone and the second gives `x, a, m = 20, 120, 121`, on the settled part and on the on-fly read alike. `05023_materialized_ephemeral_stale_warning` is unchanged and still passes. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed reading a table while a mutation is in progress: a `MATERIALIZED` column could return a stale value, and selecting one together with an updated column could fail with an error. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114561&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114561](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114561+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Reject a bare carriage return in HTTP header names and values
signal.text:
`HTTPHeaderFilter::checkAndNormalizeHeaders` rejected an embedded line feed (`
`) in HTTP header names and values, but not a bare carriage return (``). A lone `` also terminates a header line, so a value such as `tokenX-Injected: evil` could still smuggle a second header into an outgoing request (request/response splitting). This rejects `` alongside `
`, for both header names and values, in the shared filter. This covers the callers that route header names/values through `HTTPHeaderFilter` — the SQL-facing paths where headers are supplied per query: the `url` table function and engine, HTTP dictionaries, S3/Web configuration, and the DataLake/REST catalogs. Outbound HTTP clients that build headers without this filter (for example the AI providers and the BigQuery client, whose header values come from named collections, OAuth tokens, or DDL configuration) are not affected by this change; enforcing the same invariant at the shared HTTP send path for those clients is left to a separate follow-up. Deferred from #110313 to keep that pull request focused on refactoring. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110313 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reject a bare carriage return (``), in addition to a line feed (`
`), in HTTP header names and values that pass through the HTTP header filter. This closes an HTTP header injection (request/response splitting) gap for features that pass user-provided headers, such as the `url` table function and engine, HTTP dictionaries, and data lake catalogs. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1790` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Assign merges for all partitions at once for OPTIMIZE FINAL
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/46770 For a non-replicated `MergeTree` table, `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` without an explicit partition used to process partitions one by one: it selected and ran the merge for one partition, waited for it to finish, and only then moved on to the next one. On a table with many partitions this serialized all the work and only ever showed a single merge in `system.merges`. Now the per-partition merges are assigned and executed in parallel, so all partitions are merged at once. The degree of parallelism is bounded by the configured `background_pool_size` and reserves only currently available merge-executor capacity. This mirrors how `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::optimize` already assigns a merge per partition and then waits for all of them. Notes: - Tables inside an explicit transaction keep the sequential path, because parallel merges would otherwise share a single transaction object that is not made for concurrent use. - The wait for already-running merges inside `selectPartsToMerge` (the `OPTIMIZE FINAL` path) is now scoped to the current partition: merges in other partitions cannot prevent selecting all the parts of this one, and waiting for them would needlessly serialize the parallel assignment. Verified on a local build: on a table with 8 partitions, `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` now runs 8 merges concurrently (observed via `system.merges`) instead of one at a time, and every partition is still correctly merged into a single part (checked for `MergeTree`, `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL DEDUPLICATE`, and `ReplacingMergeTree`, plus the `optimize_skip_merged_partitions` / `optimize_throw_if_noop` no-op paths and two concurrent `OPTIMIZE FINAL` queries). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` on a non-replicated `MergeTree` table now assigns and runs the merges for all partitions at once instead of processing them one partition at a time. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109004&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109004](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109004+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not push sorting into Merge children across an order-breaking cast
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112931 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong `ORDER BY` and `DISTINCT` results, and a `CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE` error for aggregate functions, when reading a `Merge` table whose declared column type differs from a source table's type in a way that does not preserve sort order, for example `UInt64` over a source holding negative `Int64`. ### Description Related: #112931 `StorageMerge::getQueryProcessingStage` reports whatever stage its children report, so a `Distributed` child makes the shards apply the `ORDER BY` while the initiator only merges the sorted streams. `ReadFromMerge::convertAndFilterSourceStream` then casts each child's output to the declared types, and that cast lands *above* the child's own sort, so an order-breaking conversion reinterprets the values after they were sorted. The promise cannot be withdrawn, since the merging step was chosen from the stage, not from a sort property. It also enables DISTINCT-in-order, which in debug builds throws `Equal values are not contiguous within the range assumed to be sorted`. The fix refuses the delegation where it is issued: `getQueryProcessingStage` returns `FetchColumns` when a child's column type differs from the declared type un-order-preservingly, as it already does for `JOIN`. The flag is applied after the stage arithmetic, since `FetchColumns` is zero and `std::max` would erase the refusal. The type test must be order-preserving *and* injective, because it composes elementwise inside `Array`. Following `ToNumberMonotonicity`, it accepts integer widening that keeps the signedness or targets a signed type, adding `Nullable`, stripping `LowCardinality`, an `Enum` target at least as wide as the source, and `Array` over `Array` with an accepted element pair. Everything else is refused, including a narrower `Enum` target, which truncates and so reverses the order even where `contains` accepts the pair. A false "safe" gives silently wrong results; a false "unsafe" costs one pushdown. `Merge` derives such pairs itself via `getLeastSupertypeOrVariant`. Read-in-order needs no change: its monotonicity analysis already rejects the inserted `_CAST`. `Tuple`, `Map`, `StorageBuffer`, `StorageView`, `StorageMaterializedView` and `buildQueryTreeForShard` need their own fixes. Found by the AST fuzzer, which had retyped a `Merge` column to `IPv4` over `Int64` (2508-36d8, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112931&sha=581f5ddc3b2ce1429d9064179dad535fafea72a4&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29)). Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115455 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113242&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113242](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113242+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: The performance test `scalar` shows that a short (~0.1 s) analytical query with 8 scalar subqueries became ~20% slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. Query #0 from `tests/performance/scalar.xml` (8 scalar subqueries over `cdp_tags` feeding `multiIf(bitmapContains(...))` over `cdp_orders` with `PREWHERE`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `scalar #0` | 0.094 s | 0.113 s | **+20%** | The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit 1a969f3a2d697e0a4b86cb04d9fa69eef5271e7d on 2026-08-05, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. The suspected PR does not change execution of this query (it has no JOIN), so the cost is most likely added planning overhead — e.g. `considerEnablingParallelReplicas` / output-bytes estimation now running extra analysis for each of the scalar subqueries. At ~100 ms total runtime, per-query planning cost is the dominant term, so this likely affects all short queries with many scalar subqueries, not just this benchmark. signal.title: Avoid deep copy of AccessRights in getGrantQueriesImpl when it is only read
signal.text: ## What's Changed `getGrantQueriesImpl` used to unconditionally deep-copy the grantee's whole `AccessRights` tree: ```cpp AccessRights access = grantee.access; ``` `AccessRights` is a radix tree, and copying it is `O(number of nodes)`. For users with a huge number of per-table grants (e.g. tens of thousands), this deep copy becomes a serious bottleneck: it is executed on **every** `GRANT`/`REVOKE` (during serialization to `DiskAccessStorage`) and on every `SHOW GRANTS`. The tree is only *modified* when `final == true` (via `unionAccessFromRoles`, which calls `AccessRights::makeUnion`). In the common case (`final == false`) the tree is only read, so we can pass a read-only reference and avoid the deep copy entirely. ## Scope - `src/Interpreters/Access/InterpreterShowGrantsQuery.cpp` — avoid the deep copy when `final == false`. ## Motivation / observed impact On a production cluster (ClickHouse 26.6.1.1193), a user with ~11.6k per-table grants in one database: - A single `GRANT ... ON <table> TO <user>` took **5–28 seconds** on some replicas. - `system.query_log` showed the grant spending **99.9% of its time in user-space CPU**, with a `MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheckBytes` of up to **~500 MB**. - `system.trace_log` showed the hot spot was the recursive `Node::operator=` deep copy inside `serializeAccessEntity -> getGrantQueriesImpl`. - The same grant completed in **~100 ms** on replicas whose in-memory `AccessRights` tree was smaller, confirming the deep copy is the bottleneck. This change removes one of the three deep copies performed per grant (the one inside `getGrantQueriesImpl`). It is a safe, behavior-preserving optimization. ## Testing - Added `tests/queries/0_stateless/02536_grants_no_deepcopy.sql` + `.reference` verifying that `GRANT`, `SHOW GRANTS` and `REVOKE` behave identically. - Manual verification on the affected cluster: after applying the equivalent change, `SHOW GRANTS FOR <user>` completed in tens of milliseconds instead of seconds. ## Checklist **Changelog category (leave one):** Improvement **Changelog entry:** Avoid a deep copy of the AccessRights tree in getGrantQueriesImpl when it is only read, speeding up GRANT/REVOKE and SHOW GRANTS for users with many grants. **Unit tests pass.** **Documentation is not required** (internal implementation detail). Closes #115694 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115696&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115696](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115696+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: `GROUP BY` without aggregate functions is 23-30% slower on short string keys after the `HashSet` change
signal.text: The performance test `if_transform_strings_to_enum` shows that `GROUP BY` without aggregate functions over short string keys became 23-30% slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base. Queries (from `tests/performance/if_transform_strings_to_enum.xml`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | `SELECT transform(number, [2, 4, 6], ['google', 'yandex', 'yahoo'], 'other') as x FROM numbers(100000000) GROUP BY x FORMAT Null` | 0.670 s | 0.874 s | **+30%** | | `SELECT length(URL) > 1000 ? 'LONG' : 'SHORT' as x FROM hits_100m_single GROUP BY x FORMAT Null` | 0.096 s | 0.119 s | **+23%** | Both queries aggregate without aggregate functions over a low-cardinality string key, which is exactly the path switched to `HashSet`. The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit dddf61ccff5828bb6937cfe680874a04be35932f on 2026-08-19, flagged on both AMD and ARM, and has been flagged as `slower` in the `release_base` comparison on every master run since. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108862 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=dddf61ccff58 This is one of the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @nickitat

signal.title: `dictGet` with direct dictionaries is up to 2x slower after column-native IN/set constant handling
signal.text: The performance test `direct_dictionary` shows that `dictGet` with direct dictionaries became substantially slower on master compared to the 26.7 release base — 16 query variants regressed at once, up to 2x for simple-key lookups. Representative queries (from `tests/performance/direct_dictionary.xml`), measured in the master CI comparison against the 26.7 release base (ARM): | query | 26.7 base | master | change | |---|---|---|---| | simple key, `value_int`, 75k lookups | 0.220 s | 0.435 s | **+98%** | | simple key, tuple of 4 attributes, 75k lookups | 0.225 s | 0.440 s | **+96%** | | simple key, `value_decimal`, 50k lookups | 0.158 s | 0.296 s | **+88%** | | simple key, `value_string_nullable`, 50k lookups | 0.160 s | 0.297 s | **+86%** | | complex key, `value_string`, 50k lookups | 0.476 s | 0.631 s | **+33%** | | complex key, `value_int`, 75k lookups | 0.692 s | 0.910 s | **+32%** | ```sql WITH rand64() % toUInt64(75000) as key SELECT dictGet('default.simple_key_direct_dictionary', 'value_int', key) FROM system.numbers LIMIT 75000 FORMAT Null; ``` The regression first appeared in the per-commit (`master_head`) comparison at merge commit ce2fb4e26e8156e469449866f7d64b0e7de768ba on 2026-08-12, flagged on both AMD and ARM (16 query variants). A direct dictionary executes a source query per `dictGet` block and builds a set/filter from the requested keys, so it is plausible that the new column-native IN/set constant handling made that per-lookup path more expensive. Notably, on that commit the per-commit comparison showed exactly 10 slower queries per shard, one under the `SLOWER_QUERIES_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 10` gate (which is `> 10`), so the check stayed green and the regression landed silently. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113051 Report (ARM, vs release base): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=29cf83dac1355231265f4893603d31dfcfb577f1&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28arm_release%2C%20release_base%2C%203%2F6%29 Dashboard: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?scope=master&q=ce2fb4e26e81 This is the largest contributor to the accumulated regressions that currently keep the `Performance Comparison (arm_release, release_base, 3/6)` check permanently red on master (28 slower queries against a gate of 10). cc @yakov-olkhovskiy

signal.title: Report a clean error when a table expression has no columns to read
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101005 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `LOGICAL_ERROR: No available columns` when a query reads no columns from a table expression that has no columns at all, for example `SELECT count() FROM loop(db, tbl)` where `tbl` is an `Alias` table whose target was dropped, or a parameterized view. Such a query now fails with `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD` instead of aborting the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (`BuzzHouse (amd_msan)`, STID 3938-27bd, [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115586&sha=c2aff39bbb1c833322107a522af2fd6a316adc10&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29)). No related open issue. Reproducer, deterministic, no experimental settings: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (c0 Int32) ENGINE = Memory; CREATE TABLE a ENGINE = Alias(currentDatabase(), t); DROP TABLE t; SELECT count() FROM loop(currentDatabase(), 'a'); ``` Root cause. When a query needs no columns from a table expression, the planner synthesises a cheapest column to count rows. For a table or table function it calls `chooseSmallestColumnToReadFromStorage`, which, with no column sizes available, falls through to `ExpressionActions::getSmallestColumn` -- and that treats an empty column list as a logical error. An `Alias` whose target is gone reports column-less metadata by design, `StorageLoop` copies it onto itself, and the planner hands the empty list down. The sibling branch of the same `if (columns_names.empty())` block already guards its degenerate case with `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD "Cannot read from subquery with empty projection"`. This adds the missing counterpart to the storage branch. `getSmallestColumn`'s `LOGICAL_ERROR` stays as an internal assertion and becomes unreachable from this caller. The message is cause-neutral because a parameterized view has no columns by design, so naming a missing table would be wrong. Two further carriers that also aborted are covered: a bare parameterized view, and an `Alias` to a live one. Validation. Both directions on builds of the same revision, all four carriers: unpatched aborts with the CI stack, patched returns `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`. The new test aborts an unpatched server, so it cannot pass vacuously. Authorization ordering is unchanged and pinned by a test: without a grant the query still fails `ACCESS_DENIED` on both builds. Reading the alias directly, enumerating it in `system.tables`/`system.columns`, and `DESCRIBE` over the table function are unchanged; the existing `Alias` tests pass unmodified. 50 randomized runs, plus a matched before/after run of 399 planner, alias and table-function tests, show no new failure. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115716&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115716](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115716+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix wrong results of the partial aggregation strategy in distributed query plans
signal.text: The partial+merge aggregation strategy of `make_distributed_plan` rewrites a final aggregation into a partial `AggregatingStep` plus a memory-efficient `MergingAggregatedStep`. The memory-efficient merge consumes each input as a stream of two-level buckets in ascending order, but the rewrite kept `should_produce_results_in_order_of_bucket_number = false` on the partial step, so its multi-stream output was combined into the single exchange stream in arbitrary order. When a bucket arrived after the merge had already emitted it, the merge emitted it a second time: duplicated `GROUP BY` keys with split aggregate states (for ClickBench Q08, a wrong `COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)`). The fix, one commit each: - Make the row count estimation look through `LogicalExchangeStep`. The `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD` guard around it was needed when the exchange steps existed only in the private repo; since they are in the public repo, the guard only made every aggregation over a distributed read fall back to the Shuffle strategy in non-cloud builds (and masked this bug there). - Validate the bucket delivery order in `GroupingAggregatedTransform`: an unannounced late bucket now fails with a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception instead of silently duplicating groups. - Wait for delayed buckets in `GroupingAggregatedTransform` when the consumer needs the output in bucket order, and release the announcements of finished inputs. Covered by a gtest. - Build the partial step with `should_produce_results_in_order_of_bucket_number = true` when the merge is memory-efficient (`AggregatingStep::cloneAsPartial`). The partial aggregation then produces a single bucket-ordered stream per worker, the same contract the classic distributed path establishes on shards. Covered by a stateless test that reproduces the duplicated keys on the code without the fix (about 80% of single runs, 8 repetitions, 50k rows, ~0.5s). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix duplicated `GROUP BY` keys in the partial aggregation strategy of `make_distributed_plan`, and allow this strategy for aggregations over a distributed read. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114523&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114523](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114523+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1855` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Add early short-circuit evaluation for OR/AND in the analyzer to prevent unnecessary scalar subquery execution
signal.text: <!--- Disable AI PR formatting assistant: true --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): You can now enable early short-circuit folding for builtin `and` and `or` during analysis with the `enable_function_early_short_circuit` setting. This can skip executing dead single-row `count()` scalar subqueries while preserving normal type inference and semantic validation. Resolves #83017 ### Details When `enable_function_early_short_circuit` is enabled (and `short_circuit_function_evaluation` is not disabled), the analyzer detects decisive constants in builtin `and` / `or` expressions. The optimization is deliberately conservative. It is attempted only for expressions without outer-scope Identifier/Column dependencies and only for scalar subqueries of the statically single-row forms `SELECT count()` or `SELECT count(*)` without GROUP BY/window/HAVING/QUALIFY/LIMIT BY. All other scalar forms use normal analysis and execution. A dedicated temporary `QueryAnalyzer` resolves a clone in type-only mode using an isolated, cache-disabled scope. It never mutates the live resolver state. Scalar values are represented by non-constant type placeholders, and expressions containing aggregate/`arrayJoin` semantic carriers outside scalar-subquery boundaries are not replaced. Resolves #83017 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=83505&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/83505](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F83505+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1856` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Recursive CTE over MergeTree with parallel replicas: logical error `UNION query ... is not recursive` or infinite recursion
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe what's wrong When a recursive CTE reads from a `MergeTree` table and parallel replicas are enabled, the query breaks in one of two ways depending on how the CTE is used: 1. If the CTE is referenced from an `IN` subquery, the query fails with a logical error: `UNION query r is not recursive. (LOGICAL_ERROR)`. In debug and sanitizer builds this aborts the server (this is how it surfaced in a Stress test (arm_msan) CI run). 2. If the CTE is the top-level `FROM`, the recursion never converges and fails with `Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (1000) exceeded (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION)` on a 3-row table whose recursion should terminate after 3 iterations. Without parallel replicas the same queries return correct results. The logical error is thrown from `RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator` (`src/Processors/Sources/RecursiveCTESource.cpp:84`) because `collectTableNodesWithTemporaryTableName` finds no table node referencing the CTE's temporary table inside the union node. A recursive CTE with no table read inside it (e.g. `SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3`) works fine under the same settings, so the parallel replicas rewrite of the table read inside the CTE appears to replace or lose the recursive self-reference before `RecursiveCTESource` is built. The non-convergence in the second case points at the same root cause: the reference to the working table resolves incorrectly, so every iteration keeps producing rows. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on a recent master build (26.8.1.1). The involved code paths (`RecursiveCTESource`, parallel replicas planning) are the same in the latest releases. ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE t_pr_cte (n UInt64, p UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY n; INSERT INTO t_pr_cte VALUES (1, 0), (2, 1), (3, 2); -- Manifestation 1: logical error WITH RECURSIVE r AS ( SELECT n FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n = 1 UNION ALL SELECT t.n FROM t_pr_cte AS t INNER JOIN r ON t.p = r.n ) SELECT count() FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n IN (SELECT n FROM r) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'parallel_replicas', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1; -- Manifestation 2: infinite recursion WITH RECURSIVE r AS ( SELECT n FROM t_pr_cte WHERE n = 1 UNION ALL SELECT t.n FROM t_pr_cte AS t INNER JOIN r ON t.p = r.n ) SELECT count() FROM r SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'parallel_replicas', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1; ``` Removing the parallel replicas settings makes both queries return the correct result (`3`). ### Expected behavior Both queries return `3`, as they do without parallel replicas (or parallel replicas is not applied to the recursive CTE if it cannot handle it). ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: UNION query r is not recursive. (LOGICAL_ERROR) 4. src/Common/Exception.h:219:77: DB::Exception::Exception<String>(...) 5. src/Processors/Sources/RecursiveCTESource.cpp:84:19: DB::RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator::RecursiveCTEChunkGenerator(std::shared_ptr<DB::Block const>, std::shared_ptr<DB::IQueryTreeNode>) 6. DB::RecursiveCTESource::RecursiveCTESource(std::shared_ptr<DB::Block const>, std::shared_ptr<DB::IQueryTreeNode>) 7. DB::ReadFromRecursiveCTEStep::initializePipeline(DB::QueryPipelineBuilder&, DB::BuildQueryPipelineSettings const&) 8. src/Processors/QueryPlan/ISourceStep.cpp:20:5: DB::ISourceStep::updatePipeline(...) 9. src/Processors/QueryPlan/QueryPlan.cpp:271:47: DB::QueryPlan::buildQueryPipeline(...) 10. src/Interpreters/InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer.cpp:429:34: DB::InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer::buildQueryPipeline() ``` And for the second manifestation: ``` Code: 306. DB::Exception: Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (1000) exceeded, during evaluation of r. Consider raising max_recursive_cte_evaluation_depth setting: While executing RecursiveCTESource. (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION) ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115619 Related: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115619&sha=452c119a225d1107c28037a0c371d692306cd2de&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29 ### Additional context Found while investigating a Stress test (arm_msan) failure of the pull request above: the stress runner replayed a test query containing a recursive CTE with randomized parallel replicas settings and the server aborted on the logical error. The test was rewritten to avoid the recursive CTE, so the pull request only removed the trigger; the underlying bug is unrelated to its changes.

signal.title: Log tolerated connection failures to remote MySQL/PostgreSQL databases as warnings instead of errors
signal.text: Fix CI upgrade test failure: Example failing report — Upgrade check (amd_release) on the unrelated PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108255: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108255&sha=28ca539bd4bf66de37e388238de45d840bc30c52&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 (`Error message in clickhouse-server.log (see upgrade_error_messages.txt)` with the `getTablesIterator` line above; the report shows green now because the check passed on a later rerun — which is exactly the flaky-victim pattern). **Problem.** A `DatabasePostgreSQL` or `DatabaseMySQL` pointed at an unreachable server writes the connection failure to the server log at `<Error>` level on code paths that explicitly tolerate and retry the failure. A temporarily unavailable remote server is a normal operational state on these paths, yet it floods the log with error-level messages. Concretely: - every `system.tables` / `system.columns` scan that touches the database logs an error (`DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator`: `Code: 614. DB::Exception: ... Connection to ... failed`); - the background cleaner logs one more error every rescheduling cycle; - `ATTACH DATABASE ... ENGINE = MySQL(...)` logs three error lines for a single tolerated probe failure. This also trips the Upgrade check (which fails on any unexpected error message in `clickhouse-server.log`) on unrelated PRs: the stateless test `04210_show_remote_databases_in_system_tables` (added in #104416) leaves `PostgreSQL`/`MySQL` databases pointed at the unroutable `192.0.2.1` during the check's restart window, and since #109082 made remote databases visible to `system.tables` scans by default, the check failed on 137 distinct PRs in 14 days, and 0 times on master. **Root cause.** Seven log sites report a caught-and-tolerated (or caught-and-propagated) connection failure at error level: the catches in `DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator` (kept non-throwing so `system.tables` scans do not fail) and `DatabasePostgreSQL::removeOutdatedTables` (the cleaner reschedules and continues) use `tryLogCurrentException` with the default `LogsLevel::error`; the same for the `DatabaseMySQL` constructor catch on `ATTACH` and `DatabaseMySQL::getCreateTableQueryImpl` with `throw_on_error = false`; and the connection-pool layers (`mysqlxx::Pool::allocConnection`, `mysqlxx::PoolWithFailover::get`, `postgres::PoolWithFailover::get`) log at error level before propagating the exception to the caller — who is the one deciding how severe the failure actually is. **Fix.** Downgrade those seven sites to warning. Exception propagation is unchanged everywhere: a non-tolerated failure (e.g. `CREATE DATABASE` with an unreachable host) still reaches the client as an error through the normal query-error path. The new test `04506_remote_database_unreachable_no_error_log` attaches `PostgreSQL` and `MySQL` databases pointing at an unreachable host, exercises the tolerated paths (attach probe, `system.tables` scan, background cleaner), and asserts through `system.text_log` that each path produced a warning (proving the failure path fired) and no error-level lines at all for the corresponding queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe the situation ```sql CREATE TABLE test (s String) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO test SELECT rand() % 100 = 12 ? '' : randomString(100) FROM numbers_mt(100000000); ``` ```sql SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE length(s) > 0; -- 0.027 sec. SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE notEmpty(s); -- 0.765 sec. SELECT avg(length(s)) FROM test WHERE s != ''; -- 0.719 sec. ``` The reason for this difference in performance is the following: SELECT expression needs to calculate `length(s)`. If this expression is not already available after `WHERE`, it will request the source column, `s`, be present in the pipeline after filtering. This will lead to filtering `s` and copying the values that passed the filter. However, the function `length` does not throw exceptions, is easy to calculate, and it reduces the data volume, so it will be beneficial to calculate it early in the pipeline if its source column is not needed later in the pipeline. Essentially, we can "push up" the calculation of `length(s)` before filtering, so that we will not need to filter its argument, `s`, which was needed only for the calculation of this function. I'd expect it for a few functions, `length`, `empty`, `notEmpty`, comparisons with empty strings or arrays, and probably even `substring`. ### Which ClickHouse versions are affected? . ### How to reproduce . ### Expected performance _No response_ ### Additional context Don't be confused with "optimization for subcolumns" and "lazy reading," which are other optimizations. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #106199 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1857` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix double free when finalizing -State aggregates under looping combinators
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash (double free) that could happen when finalizing an aggregate function with the `-State` combinator nested under a looping combinator (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), for example `groupArrayStateResample`, if a memory limit was reached during finalization. ### Description Reported on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 (unrelated to that PR). Found by the Stress test (amd_debug): a segfault in `Aggregator::prepareChunkAndFillWithoutKey`, reached from `ConvertingAggregatedToChunksTransform::initialize`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110975&sha=838d0b61235b06939c8acd923ebd396f51cf5b10&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 Root cause: the `-State` combinator transfers its result by aliasing the raw aggregate state pointer into a `ColumnAggregateFunction` (`AggregateFunctionState::insertResultInto` -> `getData().push_back(place)`); ownership passes to the column. `Aggregator::insertAggregatesIntoColumns` relies on this transfer being atomic per place: on an exception it destroys the whole place exactly once. A looping combinator nested over `-State` aliases many sub-states one at a time; the `push_back` into the column's pointer array can reallocate and, being memory-tracked, throw `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` mid-loop. The already-transferred sub-states are then freed once by the aggregator's full `destroy()` and again by `~ColumnAggregateFunction`, i.e. a double free. Reproducer (crashes without the fix, returns a memory-limit error with it): ```sql SELECT arrayMap(x -> finalizeAggregation(x), state) FROM (SELECT groupArrayStateResample(0, 1048576, 1)(number, number % 20) AS state FROM numbers(100000)) SETTINGS max_memory_usage = 150000000, max_rows_to_read = 0; ``` Fix: reserve the destination columns before the transfer loop so the aliasing `push_back`s cannot reallocate (and therefore cannot throw) once a transfer has started. `ColumnAggregateFunction` used the no-op `IColumn::reserve`, so a real `reserve()`/`capacity()` over its state-pointer array is added. For `-Map`, the (possibly variable-width) key inserts are moved into their own loop before the value transfer, keeping the throwing work out of the aliasing loop. Reserving happens before any aliasing, so a throw there is harmless. The transfer loop is now non-throwing at the point of aliasing, restoring the atomic-per-place contract; results are unchanged. The fix covers all three looping transfer combinators (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), which share the aliasing path; non-looping combinators delegate a single call and are already atomic. The added stateless test reproduces the crash deterministically via `-Resample` (empty buckets keep memory low until the finalization transfer, so a memory limit reliably lands the throw mid-transfer). `-ForEach` and `-Map` build their sub-states eagerly during aggregation, so they are not deterministically reproducible under a memory limit, but are fixed as the same class via the shared transfer path.
