signal.title: Fix `Files metadata is empty` logical error on the object storage queue read path
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/93009 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Logical error: 'Files metadata is empty'` when reading from, altering, or flushing an `S3Queue`/`AzureQueue` table whose metadata handle is gone: concurrently with a `DROP`/`DETACH`, after a failed `startup`, or after a failed `DROP`. Such a table now reports `TABLE_IS_DROPPED` instead. `SYSTEM FLUSH OBJECT STORAGE QUEUE` on such a table no longer crashes the server. ### Description `StorageObjectStorageQueue::getTableMetadata` threw `LOGICAL_ERROR` whenever `files_metadata` was null, and `createFileIterator` calls it first. Plan optimization reaches it via `ReadFromObjectStorageQueue::applyFilters`, so an ordinary `SELECT` aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds (7 occurrences in 90 days, 4 unrelated PRs, 0 on master). Three reachable states leave an addressable table with a null handle: * a concurrent `DROP`/`DETACH`: the storage is shut down before any exclusive lock is taken, and for an Atomic database none is taken at all, while a `SELECT` holds only `lockForShare`; * a failed `startup`: the catalog entry is created first, and never rolled back; * a failed `DROP`: the database does fallible disk work before detaching (the #93009 route). The handle was also a plain `shared_ptr` with no synchronisation, unlike the twelve other members of that class, and `waitForPathToBeProcessed` read it with no null check, which segfaulted. The fix guards it with the existing class mutex and gives every operation one snapshot it owns for its whole duration, so a handle observed non-null cannot become null halfway through. `getTableMetadata` is removed rather than reimplemented on the accessor: it returned a reference into the object the snapshot owns, which a snapshot local to the accessor would leave dangling. Its seven callers each take their own. Where the state is legitimate the code reports `TABLE_IS_DROPPED`, matching `IStorage`; the background streaming path returns instead, a null handle there meaning shutdown. Such a table now reports a clear error; it does **not** become usable again, since recovery is a `DatabaseAtomic`/`InterpreterDropQuery` concern for every engine, out of scope here. All three reproduce on unpatched master with a stack frame-for-frame identical to the CI report, the concurrent-teardown one with no fault injection (8/8). Three integration tests cover them: pristine master reports 1 failure, the fix 18 passes, 30/30 repeats green.

signal.title: Automatic LowCardinality serialization based on uniq statistics
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85145 --> This PR adds automatic `LowCardinality` serialization for `MergeTree`, analogous to the existing automatic `Sparse` serialization. A `String` or `FixedString` column whose declared type is **not** `LowCardinality` can now be stored on disk in dictionary-encoded form when it has a `uniq` statistic with a low cardinality estimate. The encoding is transparent: the column keeps its declared data type, flows through the query pipeline as a (non-native) `ColumnLowCardinality`, and is materialized to a full column at the boundaries that require it. **Motivation:** save disk space and read I/O for low-cardinality string columns without requiring users to declare the column type as `LowCardinality(...)`. **How it works** - A new per-part serialization kind `LOW_CARDINALITY` (shown as `LowCardinality` in `system.parts_columns.serialization_kind`). - The decision is made at write time from the **existing** `uniq` statistic — there are **no changes to statistics serialization**. In `MergeTreeDataWriter`, a `String`/`FixedString` column whose `uniq` estimate does not exceed the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (default `0` = disabled), and which was not already chosen for `Sparse`, is stored with `SerializationLowCardinality`. The column must therefore declare `STATISTICS(uniq)` and have `materialize_statistics_on_insert` enabled. - A new `is_native` flag on `ColumnLowCardinality` makes `getDataType` report the nested type, so the "column class matches data type" invariant holds while such a column flows through the pipeline. It is materialized to a full column in `removeSpecialRepresentations` (aggregation, joins, squashing, blocks), in the merge-input step of `IMergingAlgorithm`, in the sorting and sparse-removing transforms, and in `IFunction`. The `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` pass skips columns stored as non-native `LowCardinality`, since the dictionary encoding does not expose the data type's regular subcolumns. - The kind is independent of sparse serialization: `SerializationInfo` entries for eligible columns are created in the writer, in merges, in mutations and in the per-table serialization hints even when `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization = 1` disables `Sparse` entirely. **Notes** - Opt-in: disabled by default and requires an explicit `uniq` statistic, so existing tables are unaffected. Requires `allow_experimental_statistics`. - Reading a subcolumn of an encoded column (for example `s.size`) is not supported and reports `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`: the subcolumn's streams do not exist in a dictionary-encoded part. Making it read the full column and extract the subcolumn in memory needs a dedicated serialization and is left for a separate change. - Extracts and reimplements the automatic `LowCardinality` part of the draft #85145 against current `master`, without the statistics-serialization refactoring. That refactoring is still unmerged (#85145 and #109128 are open drafts). Validated locally with a server built from this branch: kind selection for `Wide` and `Compact` parts, `String` and `FixedString`, query correctness, functions, `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT BY`/window functions, joins, `IN` subqueries, `INSERT SELECT`, `UNION ALL`, `OPTIMIZE FINAL` (LowCardinality preserved through merges), mutations, `ALTER RENAME`/`MODIFY COLUMN`, `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, `PREWHERE`, input/output formats with and without `allow_special_serialization_kinds_in_output_formats`, and tables with mixed `Default` and `LowCardinality` active parts. The three tests also pass with `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization` forced to `0.0` and `1.0`, with `enable_block_offset_column`/`enable_block_number_column`, with compact parts, and over repeated fully randomized runs. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added automatic `LowCardinality` serialization: a `String`/`FixedString` column that has a `uniq` statistic and low cardinality can be stored in dictionary-encoded form on disk while keeping its declared data type. Controlled by the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (disabled by default). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107436&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107436](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107436+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: ReplicatedMergeTree replica becomes permanently readonly (Code 122) when power loss reverts an applied ALTER's local metadata commit; force_restore_data / RESTART REPLICA / RESTORE REPLICA all fail to recover
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse ### Describe what's wrong When a `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica applies an `ALTER` (its `/replicas/<r>/metadata_version` znode is durably advanced in [Zoo]Keeper) but the local side of that commit — the rename that replaces `metadata/<db>/<table>.sql` — is reverted by a power loss, the replica can never start again: `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread` fails initialization with `Code: 122` `Table columns structure in ZooKeeper is different from local table structure` and logs `Initialization failed, table will remain readonly`. The state is permanent across restarts, and none of the documented recovery paths repair it: | Recovery attempt | Result | |---|---| | restart the server | same `Code: 122`, still readonly | | `SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA t` | still readonly | | `flags/force_restore_data` + restart | still readonly (the flag only skips part sanity checks) | | `SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA t` | refuses: `Replica path is present at ... - nothing to restore` | The only way out is `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA` plus re-creating the replica (or hand-editing the `.sql` file to match ZooKeeper). The window is real on default settings: the `ALTER`'s local metadata commit is `writeMetadataFile` of an fsynced `.sql.tmp` (`fsync_metadata = 1` covers only the file content) followed by `DatabaseAtomic::commitAlterTable` doing `renameExchange`/`replaceFile` with no fsync of the file or parent directory — the same never-made-durable commit rename described in #111348, and the code itself carries `/// NOTE: replica will be lost if server crashes before the following rename` right at that spot. On ext4 the rename becomes durable only when the journal happens to commit, so a power cut within that interval rolls the local file back to the pre-`ALTER` structure while the replica's own `metadata_version` znode (updated durably in Keeper as part of applying the `ALTER_METADATA` entry) stays advanced. On the next start the replica's recorded metadata version claims the new structure while the local file carries the old one, and the attach thread refuses. A normal lagging replica (killed before applying the `ALTER`) recovers fine — its local structure and its `metadata_version` znode are consistently old, so the queued `ALTER_METADATA` entry replays. The brick needs exactly the torn state this unfsynced rename produces: znode ahead, local file behind. Since initialization refuses before the queue is even loaded, the `ALTER_METADATA` replay that would repair the structure never gets a chance to run. Secondary effects observed while the replica sits in this state: its `/replicas/<r>/parts` set keeps hundreds of stale entries for parts that no longer exist locally (the startup fetch-or-remove reconciliation also never runs), and the broken local parts accumulate in `detached/`. Observed organically first: a 3-replica cluster under a concurrent INSERT/mutation/DDL workload where one replica's data directory sat on a dm-flakey device that lost power (drop_writes + remount) while the other replicas and Keeper stayed durable — 2 of 5 such runs on 26.8 ended with the recovered replica permanently readonly with `Code: 122`. The deterministic reproduction below simulates only the rename rollback, which is what the device power loss does by itself. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — 26.8.1.1708 (official master build), deterministic with the reproduction below; also observed under real device power loss. ### How to reproduce Two `ReplicatedMergeTree` replicas (`r0`, `r1`) of one table over one Keeper, each server with its own data directory: ```sql -- on both replicas: CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, val UInt64, part UInt8) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/t', '{replica}') PARTITION BY part ORDER BY id; -- on r0: INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number, 0 FROM numbers(100); ``` 1. Save a copy of r1's `metadata/default/t.sql`. 2. `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c UInt32` (on either replica); wait until r1's `t.sql` contains the new column (the `ALTER_METADATA` entry applied; r1's `/replicas/r1/metadata_version` znode advanced). 3. Kill r1's server (`kill -9` — any crash). 4. Write the saved pre-`ALTER` content back into r1's `metadata/default/t.sql`. This simulates the power-loss rollback of the never-fsynced commit rename (#111348's mechanism); under a real device power cut inside the filesystem journal window this step happens by itself. 5. Start r1. r1 logs `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread: Initialization failed, table will remain readonly. Error: Code: 122. DB::Exception: Table columns structure in ZooKeeper is different from local table structure` and `system.replicas.is_readonly` stays `1` forever. `SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA t`, the `flags/force_restore_data` flag and `SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA t` all fail as in the table above. A control run without step 4 recovers to `is_readonly = 0` immediately. ### Expected behavior An applied `ALTER` whose local metadata commit was lost to power loss leaves the replica in a state its own queue already knows how to repair — the replica's structure is simply behind ZooKeeper's. The replica should reconcile the local metadata from ZooKeeper (or reapply the `ALTER_METADATA` diff) instead of refusing initialization forever, or at minimum `force_restore_data` / `SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA` should cover this state. Alternatively, making the metadata commit rename durable (fsync the parent directory when `fsync_metadata` is enabled) closes the window at its source. ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` <Error> default.t (ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread): Initialization failed, table will remain readonly. Error: Code: 122. DB::Exception: Table columns structure in ZooKeeper is different from local table structure. Local columns: ... ``` `SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA t`: ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Replica path is present at /clickhouse/tables/t/replicas/r1 - nothing to restore. If you are sure that metadata is lost and that replica path contains some garbage, then use SYSTEM DROP REPLICA query first.. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` ### Additional context Related but distinct open reports of the same unfsynced-commit-rename mechanism with different consequences: #111348 (table-level `DROP`/`RENAME`/`EXCHANGE` on an Atomic database silently revert) and #111802 (`ON CLUSTER` DDL marked finished in Keeper while one host's local effect is lost, never retried). This report is the `ReplicatedMergeTree` column-`ALTER` flavor, where the outcome is not a silent revert but a replica that permanently refuses to initialize, with no working documented recovery short of dropping and re-creating the replica.
